Que nos fils soient comme des plantes qui croissent dans leur jeunesse ; que nos filles soient comme des pierres d’angle, polies à la manière d’un palais –Psaume 144:12.

La vision de tout parent pieux est de voir ses enfants grandir jusqu’à l’âge adulte et devenir matures. Nous voulons que nos enfants développent des convictions bibliques qui guideront leur vie et leur permettront de ne plus dépendre de la direction de leurs parents.

Telle était la vision de tout père juif. Pour célébrer le passage de son enfant à la responsabilité personnelle, on organisait une cérémonie appelée bar mitzvah pour les garçons et bat mitzvah pour les filles. Traditionnellement, elle avait lieu à l’âge de treize ans. Bar mitzvah signifie « fils du commandement » et bat mitzvah, « fille du commandement ». Après la bar mitzvah, on considérait qu’un fils était « sous la loi » et responsable de ses propres actes. Avant cet événement, ses parents étaient tenus responsables de ses actes.

La plupart d’entre nous ne sont pas d’origine juive ; toutefois, notre Seigneur Jésus l’était. À l’âge de douze ans, nous le trouvons assis dans le temple, en conversation avec les docteurs, les écoutant et leur posant des questions. Tous ceux qui l’entendaient étaient étonnés de son intelligence et de ses réponses. (voir Luc 2:47) Jésus manifestait une maturité remarquable à l’âge de douze ans. Même ses parents en étaient étonnés. Oui, il était divin, et pourtant, en tant qu’être humain, il a montré qu’une maturité précoce était possible avec les bonnes valeurs et les bonnes disciplines.

L’adolescence est une période de transition. Les adolescents passent de l’enfance à l’âge adulte, de la dépendance envers leurs parents à l’apprentissage de l’autonomie. Cette transition est un processus que les parents comme l’enfant doivent comprendre. Trop de liberté trop tôt peut rendre l’enfant insécurisé et l’amener à faire de mauvais choix aux conséquences durables. Trop peu de liberté peut étouffer le développement du caractère de l’enfant et devenir un terrain fertile pour la rébellion.

L’adolescence est une période de croissance. Tout comme une plante a besoin d’une culture attentive tout au long de son cycle de vie, un enfant a besoin d’être guidé continuellement pendant son adolescence. Après l’épisode de Jésus au temple, nous lisons : Et il descendit avec eux, et vint à Nazareth, et leur était soumis… –Luc 2:51. Nous examinerons certaines choses que les parents peuvent faire pour favoriser la maturité de leurs enfants, mais considérons d’abord plusieurs relations fondamentales à une maturité saine.

Heureux le peuple qui est dans une telle situation ; oui, heureux le peuple dont l’Éternel est le Dieu –Psaume 144:15.

La relation avec les parents

La relation entre le parent et l’enfant pendant l’adolescence est en grande partie la récolte de ce qui a été semé dans cette relation durant les années formatrices de l’enfance. À moins qu’une crise spirituelle majeure ne transforme radicalement la relation — comme la conversion évangélique du parent ou de l’enfant —, nous, parents, récoltons pendant l’adolescence de l’enfant ce que nous avons semé durant son enfance.

Élever des adolescents est une expérience enrichissante si une relation de base saine a été établie tout au long de l’enfance. Si le parent a été présent physiquement et émotionnellement ; si le parent et l’enfant ont communiqué ouvertement et librement ; et si le parent a maintenu avec amour son rôle d’autorité et de contrôle, alors les fondations d’une relation plus mature pendant l’adolescence ont été posées.

En l’absence de ce type de relation avec les parents, l’enfant qui entre dans l’adolescence cherchera à combler ce vide par d’autres relations. Le plus souvent, si la relation avec les parents fait défaut, l’enfant cherchera à combler ce vide par des relations avec ses pairs. Les pairs sont de bons amis, mais ils remplacent mal un parent. Nous avons été créés pour vivre en relation avec autrui. Les adolescents, en particulier, aspirent à trouver un sentiment d’importance dans leurs relations.

Tout adolescent recherche deux choses dans sa relation avec ses parents : l’identité et l’affirmation. Deux questions brûlantes habitent le cœur de tout adolescent : « Qui suis-je ? » et « Est-ce que je vais bien ? ».

Le facteur identitaire

Quand les enfants sont jeunes, ils adoptent l’identité de leur famille. En grandissant et en devenant adolescents, ils commencent à se voir comme autre chose que simplement le fils de papa. Ils commencent à se forger une identité propre. Ce mouvement vers « être moi-même » devient manifeste dans beaucoup de leurs choix, par exemple :

  • Leur façon de s’habiller
  • Leur choix de musique
  • Leur choix d’amis
  • Le choix de servir ou non le Dieu de leurs parents
  • Le choix de fréquenter ou non l’église où ils ont grandi

Il est vrai que d’autres influences peuvent affecter les choix d’un adolescent dans ces domaines, mais, dans l’ensemble, ces choix reflètent la relation entre l’enfant et le parent. Lorsque le parent a exercé une influence positive sur l’enfant, celui-ci sera plus enclin à adopter les valeurs de son parent.

Lorsque la relation avec les parents s’est détériorée ou n’a jamais été entretenue, ou si elle n’a été qu’une relation de maître à esclave, l’enfant cherchera à s’identifier à quelqu’un d’autre qu’à son parent. Cela se manifestera par des choix vestimentaires, musicaux, amicaux et d’activités que le parent n’approuvera pas. C’est souvent ce qu’on appelle la « rébellion adolescente ».

La « rébellion adolescente » est-elle toujours la faute du parent ? Non, mais si vous ne vous engagez pas activement à bâtir et à entretenir une relation avec votre adolescent, il est probable que cela arrive. Il est important de noter qu’il y a un rebelle dans le cœur de chaque personne. Dans mon dernier article, j’ai souligné l’importance de confronter cet esprit rebelle lorsque nos enfants sont jeunes et influençables.

Cet esprit rebelle ne sera pas entièrement vaincu tant qu’il ne sera pas soumis à Dieu par une expérience de conversion évangélique. Seule l’œuvre de la grâce de Dieu dans le cœur peut dompter la rébellion innée contre Dieu et l’autorité parentale.

Connaissez le cœur de votre enfant et cherchez à le conduire à se soumettre avec amour au Seigneur Jésus-Christ. C’est uniquement dans une relation avec Jésus-Christ que nos enfants peuvent trouver leur identité véritable et durable. L’autorité parentale joue un rôle dans la formation et le contrôle de nos enfants lorsqu’ils sont jeunes. À mesure qu’ils grandissent et deviennent adultes, nous comprenons que l’autorité parentale a ses limites et que nos enfants ont besoin d’être guidés par une influence qui nous dépasse.

Il n’est jamais trop tard pour construire un pont relationnel. Si vous avez le sentiment d’avoir échoué dans votre relation avec vos enfants, il n’est jamais trop tard pour les appeler auprès de vous et chercher humblement à rétablir ce qui manque. Même si vos enfants ont quitté la maison, je peux vous assurer qu’ils aspirent à une relation avec leur mère et leur père.

Le facteur de l’affirmation

Tout adolescent aspire à être valorisé par ses parents, surtout par son père. Vous pouvez valoriser votre adolescent en recherchant et en reconnaissant les traits de caractère positifs. La critique corrective d’un parent envers son enfant a sa place, mais une critique qui rabaisse n’est pas constructive ; elle est destructrice. À chaque remarque critique devraient correspondre plusieurs compliments positifs. En d’autres termes, vous gagnez le droit de critiquer ce qui ne va pas en bénissant ce qui va bien.

Vous pouvez valoriser votre adolescent en le traitant avec dignité et respect. Vous pouvez lui demander : « Qu’en penses-tu ? » ou « Que crois-tu que nous devrions faire ? ». En cherchant à connaître le point de vue de votre fils ou de votre fille, vous ne renoncez pas à votre responsabilité parentale. En réalité, vous l’aidez à « grandir dans sa jeunesse » en l’amenant à réfléchir comme un adulte.

Vous pouvez valoriser votre adolescent en le traitant avec une courtoisie élémentaire. De simples expressions comme « s’il te plaît » et « merci », « je suis désolé », « excuse-moi », « au revoir », « passe une bonne journée », « conduis prudemment » et « que Dieu te bénisse » expriment à votre adolescent qu’il a de la valeur et qu’il compte. Si ces simples marques de courtoisie sont courantes chez vous, vos enfants vous les rendront. Pensez à ce que vous ressentez quand quelqu’un vous dit : « Oh, excusez-moi, je suis désolé. » Vous éprouvez un sentiment de respect, de valeur et de dignité. C’est un cadeau simple que tout parent peut offrir à son enfant.

Vous pouvez valoriser votre adolescent en lui confiant des responsabilités. J’ai grandi dans une ferme laitière. Nous avions de nombreuses occasions de développer notre caractère et nos compétences. Je me souviens d’un jour où j’avais 16 ans : mon père avait besoin qu’on construise un mur en blocs de béton dans la grange. Je me suis proposé pour le faire. Mon père m’a fourni les blocs et le mortier et m’a mis au travail. Ensuite, je me suis débrouillé seul. Ai-je construit un mur d’allure professionnelle ? Non, mais j’étais assez fier du résultat et ce mur a tenu de nombreuses années. Mon père m’a fait confiance pour accomplir un travail d’homme, et je l’ai fait.

Valoriser, ce n’est pas flatter. La flatterie consiste en des louanges qui ne sont pas sincères et souvent pas vraies. Valoriser, c’est reconnaître et encourager le bien que l’on voit chez l’autre. J’ai rencontré des hommes adultes qui pleuraient amèrement parce qu’ils n’avaient jamais reçu d’affirmation de la part de leur père. Même Jésus a reçu l’approbation de son Père, lorsque celui-ci a dit : « Celui-ci est mon Fils bien-aimé, en qui j’ai mis toute mon affection. »

(2) La relation avec Dieu

Notre première responsabilité en matière d’évangélisation concerne nos enfants. Si nous ne pouvons pas évangéliser nos enfants, comment pouvons-nous espérer en gagner d’autres au Seigneur ? Nous avons un avantage particulier pour communiquer notre foi à nos enfants : nous vivons avec eux. Ils peuvent observer, et observent effectivement, comment notre foi se traduit dans la vie quotidienne. Cela devrait être la preuve la plus convaincante de la validité de notre foi.

Malheureusement, la manière dont les parents vivent leur foi — ou plutôt ne la vivent pas — peut devenir une énorme pierre d’achoppement pour leurs enfants. Nos enfants remarquent parfaitement toute incohérence dans notre profession de foi chrétienne.

À l’inverse, si nos enfants voient la puissance de Dieu à l’œuvre dans nos vies, s’ils voient leurs parents manifester une foi en Dieu qui les soutient dans les moments difficiles, s’ils voient leurs parents se reposer paisiblement dans le Seigneur et si Jésus-Christ est exalté et adoré au foyer, ils seront convaincus de faire du Dieu de leurs parents leur Dieu.

C’est la réalité de l’Évangile vécue au quotidien qui constitue la preuve la plus convaincante de la validité de notre foi. Nos enfants devraient être les premiers témoins de l’œuvre de transformation de l’Évangile dans nos cœurs.

Comment un parent conduit-il son enfant au salut ? Le salut est une œuvre de Dieu ; toutefois, Dieu se sert d’instruments humains pour accomplir son œuvre. Les parents jouent un rôle majeur pour conduire leurs enfants à Christ. Soyez attentifs aux signes de conviction. Si un enfant est silencieux et renfermé, ou irritable et agité, ou agressif et provocateur, il se peut que l’Esprit de Dieu soit à l’œuvre dans son cœur.

Espérons que vous avez entretenu une relation qui vous permet de sonder son cœur et de le conduire doucement à Jésus afin qu’il reçoive le pardon et la purification. La conversion de la plupart de nos enfants a été amorcée par un parent. Nous avons reconnu les signes de conviction et les avons conduits à la contrition et à la repentance, puis à recevoir le salut par la foi en Christ.

Le début de l’adolescence est une période idéale pour qu’un enfant remette sa vie à Jésus, s’il ne l’a pas déjà fait. Lorsque la rébellion active s’installe, un adolescent fait souvent des choix qui entraînent une récolte douloureuse et parfois des conséquences irréversibles. Une vie consacrée au service de Dieu est la seule vie qui apporte bénédiction et épanouissement.

La relation avec l’Église

Il existe une autre relation qui a une influence déterminante sur la formation de la vie et des convictions d’un adolescent : celle avec l’église locale. C’est à travers notre expérience du culte et des relations au sein de l’église locale que nous acquérons notre sentiment d’identité et notre compréhension de la réalité de la foi chrétienne. Après la relation avec les parents, c’est l’influence la plus importante dans la vie d’un adolescent.

Il est important de célébrer le culte dans une église qui présente l’Évangile comme une relation avec Dieu qui transforme, par la foi en Jésus. Il est également important que la vie de l’église soit faite de relations chaleureuses et aimantes au sein d’une communauté unie.

J’en parle parce que certains parents croient à tort qu’ils peuvent offrir à leurs enfants toute la direction spirituelle et toutes les relations dont ils ont besoin. Cela peut sembler fonctionner lorsque les enfants sont petits et tout près d’eux, mais à mesure qu’ils grandissent et deviennent adultes, ils chercheront un réseau de relations plus vaste. L’église locale et la communauté des églises qui lui sont associées fournissent cette base plus large de communion fraternelle.

Il est important de fréquenter une église que vous pouvez soutenir et dont vous pouvez encourager vos enfants à soutenir le ministère. Beaucoup d’enfants ont abandonné la foi parce que leur mère et leur père ne soutenaient pas l’église qu’ils fréquentaient. Il vaut bien mieux partir et trouver une église que vous pouvez soutenir que de rester dans une église en vous opposant constamment à elle.

Je ne préconise pas de passer d’une église à l’autre. Il est important pour les enfants, en particulier vos adolescents, que la vie de l’église soit stable. Trouvez une église où vous vous sentez à l’aise, si possible pendant que vos enfants sont encore jeunes, et restez-y. Il existe toujours des exceptions liées à la logistique, et vos enfants s’y adapteront, mais, dans l’ensemble, une vie d’église stable produit des jeunes qui ont un fort sentiment d’identité et de vocation.

Comme les flèches dans la main d’un homme puissant, ainsi sont les enfants de la jeunesse –Psaume 127:4. Ce verset nous rappelle que nos enfants constituent une puissante défense contre l’ennemi. S’ils sont bien aiguisés (formés) et bien équilibrés (instruits aux disciplines), nos enfants pourront nous survivre, tant par leur longévité que par leur utilité. Lorsque vous lâcherez la flèche, vos enfants iront en des lieux, dans le temps et dans le monde, que vous ne verrez jamais. Heureux l’homme qui en a rempli son carquois ! Ils ne seront pas confus, quand ils parleront avec des ennemis à la porte –Psaume 127:5.

As a young man I remember hearing a popular slogan about faith: “Faith begins when reason ends.” As a young Christian, I thought it was a great life slogan. As I mature in my walk with Jesus, I look back on this particular slogan and shake my head. I can think of no better way to misrepresent faith than by claiming it exists apart from reason.

One simple reason for rejecting this view is because it misrepresents faith. A quick search on Google turns up this definition of faith: “complete trust or confidence in someone or something.” We use this definition all the time. I might tell you I have faith in my wife, I have faith in my employer to give me a paycheck, or I have no faith in alcohol to give me a good time. This is the same way the Bible defines faith.

Hebrews 11:1 affirms that faith is “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” Biblical faith is simply a state of mind that has confidence and trust in the Lord. I have confidence that I will one day walk on the new Earth, and I have confidence that the Holy Spirit is working in the hearts of Christians. My confidence is based on, not apart from, reason. The more Jesus shows himself trustworthy, the more I trust (have confidence in) Him.

One aspect of Christ’s dependability is His word. The Old Testament was written by prophets and leaders who correctly predicted future events and ruled nations. The New Testament was written by Apostles or people that were closely associated with the apostles. We have more manuscripts of the Bible than any other work in antiquity. The Bible gives an honest portrayal of its heroes and correctly describes ancient leaders and places. In short, I trust in the Bible because it stands alone above all other books in terms of its authorship, preservation, honesty, and accuracy. The more I read it and read about it, the more my faith—and trust—increases.

Luke bases his whole Gospel on the premise that more knowledge gives more faith. He begins his book with this introduction: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled [or been surely believed] among us, just as they were handed down to us by those who from the first were eyewitnesses and servants of the word. With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught. –Luke 1:1-4. (NIV)

The apostle Paul argues that faith in God is so grounded in reality that no one has a legitimate claim against God’s existence. He writes, The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse –Romans 1:18-20. (NIV)

Knowledge of nature builds my faith in Jesus. Scripture teaches that God created all life in six days, that there was a global flood, and that animals produce after their own kind. All across our earth, the rocks cry out their testimony of the global flood. People have uncovered billions of fossils—mostly marine animals—in rock layers that were laid down by water. Animals too, live out what the Bible teaches about kinds. We can observe animals changing all around us. They change sizes, colors, and eating habits. Fish in caves lose their ability to see. Birds’ beaks adjust to the environment. In all this intricate change, all animals exist within the Biblical framework of their own kind. Sharks remain sharks; frogs remain frogs; iguanas remain iguanas; and gibbons remain gibbons. The more I learn and observe about nature, the more my faith (confidence) increases.

In some discussions of faith, it is natural for the words of Jesus to come up. After His resurrection, Jesus visits Thomas and tells him, …Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed –John 20:29. (ESV) From this, it is tempting to define faith as “believing without seeing.” That would be missing the point. I’m not claiming any superiority to Thomas, but he should have believed without seeing Jesus. All the evidence pointed to it. First, his good friends, who had proved themselves trustworthy, said Jesus was alive. Second, Jesus had plainly said He would be resurrected (see Matthew 16:21). Third, Jesus had already proven He was divine by His ability to raise the dead, control the weather, heal the sick, and multiply food. Thomas had all he needed to believe Jesus rose from the dead. Yet, he went against all reasoning and said he needed more evidence.

When confronted with the resurrected Christ, Thomas repented of his disbelief and followed Christ into martyrdom. Unfortunately, the spirit of disbelief in the face of evidence still lingers in our world. Atheists claim, in spite of all evidence to the contrary, that life can come from nothing. They claim, without any evidence, that fish turned into frogs. They blindly cling to various theories such as: The Big Bang, Punctuated Equilibrium, and Descent with Modification. They have NO workable evidence, yet they still claim to base all their thoughts on observable, repeatable reality. Christians, who with good intentions, tell them that faith begins where reason ends, unwittingly play right into their hands. This world does not need a social media definition of faith. They need to see faith for what it is: confidence in the living God based firmly in reason.

Saat masih muda, saya ingat pernah mendengar slogan populer tentang iman: “Iman dimulai ketika akal berakhir.” Sebagai orang Kristen muda, saya pikir itu slogan hidup yang hebat. Seiring saya bertumbuh dewasa dalam perjalanan saya bersama Yesus, saya mengenang slogan khusus ini dan menggelengkan kepala. Saya tidak dapat memikirkan cara yang lebih baik untuk menggambarkan iman secara keliru selain dengan mengklaim bahwa iman ada terpisah dari akal.

Salah satu alasan sederhana untuk menolak pandangan ini adalah karena pandangan tersebut menggambarkan iman secara keliru. Pencarian singkat di Google menampilkan definisi iman berikut: “kepercayaan atau keyakinan penuh kepada seseorang atau sesuatu.” Kita selalu menggunakan definisi ini. Saya mungkin mengatakan kepada Anda bahwa saya memiliki kepercayaan kepada istri saya, saya percaya kepada atasan saya untuk memberi saya gaji, atau saya tidak percaya bahwa alkohol akan membuat saya bersenang-senang. Alkitab mendefinisikan iman dengan cara yang sama.

Ibrani 11:1 menegaskan bahwa iman adalah “dasar dari segala sesuatu yang kita harapkan dan bukti dari segala sesuatu yang tidak kita lihat.” Iman alkitabiah hanyalah keadaan pikiran yang memiliki keyakinan dan kepercayaan kepada Tuhan. Saya memiliki keyakinan bahwa suatu hari nanti saya akan berjalan di bumi yang baru, dan saya memiliki keyakinan bahwa Roh Kudus bekerja dalam hati orang-orang Kristen. Keyakinan saya didasarkan pada akal, bukan terpisah dari akal. Semakin Yesus menunjukkan bahwa Ia dapat dipercaya, semakin saya percaya (memiliki keyakinan kepada)-Nya.

Salah satu aspek dari sifat Kristus yang dapat diandalkan adalah firman-Nya. Perjanjian Lama ditulis oleh para nabi dan pemimpin yang meramalkan peristiwa-peristiwa masa depan dengan tepat dan memerintah bangsa-bangsa. Perjanjian Baru ditulis oleh para rasul atau orang-orang yang memiliki hubungan erat dengan para rasul. Kita memiliki lebih banyak manuskrip Alkitab daripada karya mana pun dari zaman kuno. Alkitab menggambarkan para pahlawannya dengan jujur dan menjelaskan para pemimpin serta tempat-tempat kuno dengan tepat. Singkatnya, saya percaya kepada Alkitab karena dalam hal kepengarangan, pelestarian, kejujuran, dan ketepatannya, Alkitab tiada tandingannya di antara semua kitab. Semakin banyak saya membacanya dan membaca tentangnya, semakin bertambah iman—dan kepercayaan—saya.

Lukas mendasarkan seluruh Injilnya pada premis bahwa semakin banyak pengetahuan, semakin besar iman. Ia memulai kitabnya dengan pengantar ini: Banyak orang telah berusaha menyusun kisah tentang hal-hal yang telah digenapi [atau telah diyakini dengan teguh] di antara kita, sebagaimana disampaikan kepada kita oleh mereka yang sejak awal adalah saksi mata dan pelayan firman. Karena itu, setelah saya sendiri menyelidiki segala sesuatu dengan saksama sejak awal, saya juga memutuskan untuk menulis kisah yang teratur bagimu, hai Teofilus yang mulia, supaya engkau dapat mengetahui kepastian dari hal-hal yang telah diajarkan kepadamu. –Lukas 1:1-4. (NIV)

Rasul Paulus berpendapat bahwa iman kepada Allah begitu berlandaskan kenyataan sehingga tidak seorang pun memiliki alasan yang sah untuk menyangkal keberadaan Allah. Ia menulis, Murka Allah sedang dinyatakan dari surga terhadap segala kefasikan dan kelaliman manusia, yang menindas kebenaran dengan kelaliman mereka, karena apa yang dapat diketahui tentang Allah sudah jelas bagi mereka, sebab Allah telah menyatakannya kepada mereka. Sebab sejak penciptaan dunia, sifat-sifat-Nya yang tidak kelihatan—kuasa-Nya yang kekal dan keilahian-Nya—telah terlihat dengan jelas, karena dipahami melalui segala sesuatu yang telah diciptakan, sehingga manusia tidak dapat berdalih –Roma 1:18-20. (NIV)

Pengetahuan tentang alam membangun iman saya kepada Yesus. Kitab Suci mengajarkan bahwa Allah menciptakan seluruh kehidupan dalam enam hari, bahwa pernah terjadi air bah global, dan bahwa hewan berkembang biak menurut jenisnya. Di seluruh bumi kita, bebatuan menyuarakan kesaksiannya tentang air bah global. Orang-orang telah menemukan miliaran fosil—yang sebagian besar adalah hewan laut—di lapisan batuan yang terbentuk oleh air. Hewan juga memperlihatkan apa yang diajarkan Alkitab tentang jenis-jenis. Kita dapat mengamati hewan berubah di sekeliling kita. Ukuran, warna, dan kebiasaan makan mereka berubah. Ikan di gua kehilangan kemampuan untuk melihat. Paruh burung menyesuaikan diri dengan lingkungan. Di tengah semua perubahan yang rumit ini, semua hewan tetap berada dalam kerangka alkitabiah tentang jenisnya masing-masing. Hiu tetaplah hiu; katak tetaplah katak; iguana tetaplah iguana; dan owa tetaplah owa. Semakin banyak saya belajar tentang alam dan mengamatinya, semakin bertambah iman (keyakinan) saya.

Dalam beberapa pembahasan tentang iman, wajar jika perkataan Yesus muncul. Setelah kebangkitan-Nya, Yesus menemui Tomas dan berkata kepadanya, …Apakah engkau percaya karena engkau telah melihat Aku? Berbahagialah mereka yang tidak melihat, namun percaya –Yohanes 20:29. (ESV) Dari sini, kita mungkin tergoda untuk mendefinisikan iman sebagai “percaya tanpa melihat.” Itu berarti tidak memahami maksudnya. Saya tidak mengklaim lebih unggul daripada Tomas, tetapi ia seharusnya percaya tanpa melihat Yesus. Semua bukti mengarah pada hal itu. Pertama, sahabat-sahabat baiknya, yang telah terbukti dapat dipercaya, mengatakan bahwa Yesus hidup. Kedua, Yesus telah dengan jelas mengatakan bahwa Ia akan dibangkitkan (lihat Matius 16:21). Ketiga, Yesus telah membuktikan bahwa Ia ilahi melalui kuasa-Nya untuk membangkitkan orang mati, mengendalikan cuaca, menyembuhkan orang sakit, dan melipatgandakan makanan. Tomas memiliki semua yang ia perlukan untuk percaya bahwa Yesus bangkit dari antara orang mati. Namun, ia bertindak bertentangan dengan segala penalaran dan berkata bahwa ia membutuhkan lebih banyak bukti.

Ketika berhadapan dengan Kristus yang telah bangkit, Tomas bertobat dari ketidakpercayaannya dan mengikuti Kristus sampai mati sebagai martir. Sayangnya, semangat tidak percaya meskipun ada bukti masih bertahan di dunia kita. Kaum ateis mengklaim, meskipun semua bukti menunjukkan sebaliknya, bahwa kehidupan dapat muncul dari ketiadaan. Mereka mengklaim, tanpa bukti apa pun, bahwa ikan berubah menjadi katak. Mereka secara membabi buta berpegang pada berbagai teori seperti: Dentuman Besar, Keseimbangan Bersela, dan Keturunan dengan Modifikasi. Mereka sama sekali TIDAK memiliki bukti yang dapat digunakan, tetapi tetap mengklaim bahwa semua pemikiran mereka didasarkan pada kenyataan yang dapat diamati dan diulangi. Orang-orang Kristen yang dengan niat baik mengatakan kepada mereka bahwa iman dimulai ketika akal berakhir, tanpa sadar justru membantu mereka. Dunia ini tidak membutuhkan definisi iman dari media sosial. Mereka perlu melihat iman sebagaimana adanya: keyakinan kepada Allah yang hidup, yang berlandaskan kuat pada akal.

As I mature in my walk with Jesus, I look back on this particular slogan and shake my head. I can think of no better way to misrepresent faith than by claiming it exists apart from reason.

One simple reason for rejecting this view is because it misrepresents faith. A quick search on Google turns up this definition of faith: “complete trust or confidence in someone or something.” We use this definition all the time. I might tell you I have faith in my wife, I have faith in my employer to give me a paycheck, or I have no faith in alcohol to give me a good time. This is the same way the Bible defines faith.

Hebrews 11:1 affirms that faith is “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” Biblical faith is simply a state of mind that has confidence and trust in the Lord. I have confidence that I will one day walk on the new Earth, and I have confidence that the Holy Spirit is working in the hearts of Christians. My confidence is based on, not apart from, reason. The more Jesus shows himself trustworthy, the more I trust (have confidence in) Him.

One aspect of Christ’s dependability is His word. The Old Testament was written by prophets and leaders who correctly predicted future events and ruled nations. The New Testament was written by Apostles or people that were closely associated with the apostles. We have more manuscripts of the Bible than any other work in antiquity. The Bible gives an honest portrayal of its heroes and correctly describes ancient leaders and places. In short, I trust in the Bible because it stands alone above all other books in terms of its authorship, preservation, honesty, and accuracy. The more I read it and read about it, the more my faith—and trust—increases.

Luke bases his whole Gospel on the premise that more knowledge gives more faith. He begins his book with this introduction: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled [or been surely believed] among us, just as they were handed down to us by those who from the first were eyewitnesses and servants of the word. With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught. –Luke 1:1-4. (NIV)

The apostle Paul argues that faith in God is so grounded in reality that no one has a legitimate claim against God’s existence. He writes, The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse –Romans 1:18-20. (NIV)

Knowledge of nature builds my faith in Jesus. Scripture teaches that God created all life in six days, that there was a global flood, and that animals produce after their own kind. All across our earth, the rocks cry out their testimony of the global flood. People have uncovered billions of fossils—mostly marine animals—in rock layers that were laid down by water. Animals too, live out what the Bible teaches about kinds. We can observe animals changing all around us. They change sizes, colors, and eating habits. Fish in caves lose their ability to see. Birds’ beaks adjust to the environment. In all this intricate change, all animals exist within the Biblical framework of their own kind. Sharks remain sharks; frogs remain frogs; iguanas remain iguanas; and gibbons remain gibbons. The more I learn and observe about nature, the more my faith (confidence) increases.

In some discussions of faith, it is natural for the words of Jesus to come up. After His resurrection, Jesus visits Thomas and tells him, …Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed –John 20:29. (ESV) From this, it is tempting to define faith as “believing without seeing.” That would be missing the point. I’m not claiming any superiority to Thomas, but he should have believed without seeing Jesus. All the evidence pointed to it. First, his good friends, who had proved themselves trustworthy, said Jesus was alive. Second, Jesus had plainly said He would be resurrected (see Matthew 16:21). Third, Jesus had already proven He was divine by His ability to raise the dead, control the weather, heal the sick, and multiply food. Thomas had all he needed to believe Jesus rose from the dead. Yet, he went against all reasoning and said he needed more evidence.

When confronted with the resurrected Christ, Thomas repented of his disbelief and followed Christ into martyrdom. Unfortunately, the spirit of disbelief in the face of evidence still lingers in our world. Atheists claim, in spite of all evidence to the contrary, that life can come from nothing. They claim, without any evidence, that fish turned into frogs. They blindly cling to various theories such as: The Big Bang, Punctuated Equilibrium, and Descent with Modification. They have NO workable evidence, yet they still claim to base all their thoughts on observable, repeatable reality. Christians, who with good intentions, tell them that faith begins where reason ends, unwittingly play right into their hands. This world does not need a social media definition of faith. They need to see faith for what it is: confidence in the living God based firmly in reason.

Nikiwa kijana, nakumbuka nikisikia kauli mbiu maarufu kuhusu imani: “Imani huanza pale akili inapokoma.” Nikiwa Mkristo mchanga, nilifikiri hiyo ilikuwa kauli mbiu nzuri ya maisha. Ninapokomaa katika mwenendo wangu pamoja na Yesu, ninaitazama kauli mbiu hii na kutikisa kichwa. Siwezi kufikiria njia bora zaidi ya kupotosha maana ya imani kuliko kudai kwamba ipo bila akili.

Sababu moja rahisi ya kukataa mtazamo huu ni kwamba unapotosha maana ya imani. Utafutaji wa haraka kwenye Google unaonyesha ufafanuzi huu wa imani: “kumwamini au kumtumaini mtu au kitu kikamilifu.” Tunatumia ufafanuzi huu kila wakati. Ninaweza kukuambia nina imani na mke wangu, nina imani kwamba mwajiri wangu atanilipa mshahara, au sina imani kwamba pombe itanifanya nijisikie vizuri. Hivi ndivyo Biblia pia inavyofafanua imani.

Waebrania 11:1 inathibitisha kwamba imani ni “uhakika wa mambo yatarajiwayo na bayana ya mambo yasiyoonekana.” Imani ya kibiblia ni hali ya moyo tu yenye uhakika na kumtumaini Bwana. Nina uhakika kwamba siku moja nitatembea katika dunia mpya, na nina uhakika kwamba Roho Mtakatifu anafanya kazi katika mioyo ya Wakristo. Uhakika wangu unatokana na akili, si bila akili. Kadiri Yesu anavyojidhihirisha kuwa mwaminifu zaidi, ndivyo ninavyomtumaini zaidi (kuwa na uhakika naye).

Sehemu moja ya uaminifu wa Kristo ni neno lake. Agano la Kale liliandikwa na manabii na viongozi waliotabiri kwa usahihi matukio ya wakati ujao na kutawala mataifa. Agano Jipya liliandikwa na mitume au watu waliokuwa na uhusiano wa karibu na mitume. Tuna nakala za hati za Biblia nyingi kuliko za kazi nyingine yoyote ya kale. Biblia inasimulia kwa uaminifu kuhusu mashujaa wake na inaeleza kwa usahihi viongozi na maeneo ya kale. Kwa kifupi, ninaitumaini Biblia kwa sababu inajitokeza juu ya vitabu vingine vyote kwa upande wa waandishi wake, uhifadhi wake, uaminifu wake na usahihi wake. Kadiri ninavyoisoma na kusoma kuihusu, ndivyo imani yangu—na tumaini langu—vinavyoongezeka.

Luka anaijenga Injili yake yote juu ya dhana kwamba maarifa zaidi huleta imani zaidi. Anaanza kitabu chake kwa utangulizi huu: Wengi wamejitahidi kuandika habari za mambo yaliyotimizwa [au yaliyoaminiwa kwa hakika] kati yetu, kama tulivyokabidhiwa na wale ambao tangu mwanzo walikuwa mashahidi wa kuyaona na watumishi wa lile Neno. Kwa hiyo, mimi nami, kwa kuwa nimechunguza kila kitu kwa uangalifu tangu mwanzo, nimeona vema kukuandikia wewe pia, mtukufu Theofilo, habari hizo kwa utaratibu, ili upate kujua hakika ya mambo yale uliyoelekezwa. –Luka 1:1-4. (NIV)

Mtume Paulo anasema kwamba imani katika Mungu imejikita sana katika uhalisi kiasi kwamba hakuna mtu aliye na dai halali dhidi ya kuwepo kwa Mungu. Anaandika, Hasira ya Mungu inafunuliwa kutoka mbinguni juu ya uasi wote wa Mungu na udhalimu wa watu, ambao kwa udhalimu wao wanaikandamiza kweli, kwa kuwa yale yanayoweza kujulikana kuhusu Mungu yako wazi kwao, kwa sababu Mungu amewadhihirishia. Kwa maana tangu kuumbwa kwa ulimwengu, sifa zake zisizoonekana—uweza wake wa milele na asili yake ya Uungu—zimeonekana waziwazi, zikieleweka kutokana na vitu vilivyoumbwa, ili watu wasiwe na udhuru –Warumi 1:18-20. (NIV)

Maarifa ya ulimwengu wa asili hujenga imani yangu katika Yesu. Maandiko yanafundisha kwamba Mungu aliumba viumbe vyote katika siku sita, kwamba kulitokea gharika ya dunia nzima, na kwamba wanyama huzaa kulingana na aina zao. Kote duniani, miamba inatoa ushuhuda wake kuhusu gharika ya dunia nzima. Watu wamegundua mabilioni ya visukuku—hasa wanyama wa baharini—katika tabaka za miamba zilizowekwa na maji. Wanyama pia huishi kulingana na kile Biblia inachofundisha kuhusu aina. Tunaweza kuona wanyama wakibadilika kotekote. Wanabadilika ukubwa, rangi na tabia za kula. Samaki wanaoishi mapangoni hupoteza uwezo wao wa kuona. Midomo ya ndege hubadilika kulingana na mazingira. Katika mabadiliko haya yote tata, wanyama wote wapo ndani ya mfumo wa kibiblia wa aina zao wenyewe. Papa hubaki papa; vyura hubaki vyura; iguana hubaki iguana; na giboni hubaki giboni. Kadiri ninavyojifunza na kutazama ulimwengu wa asili, ndivyo imani yangu (uhakika wangu) inavyoongezeka.

Katika baadhi ya mijadala kuhusu imani, ni kawaida maneno ya Yesu kutajwa. Baada ya kufufuka kwake, Yesu anamtembelea Tomaso na kumwambia, …Je, umeamini kwa sababu umeniona? Heri wale ambao hawakuona, lakini wakaamini –Yohana 20:29. (ESV) Kutokana na maneno haya, ni rahisi kujaribiwa kufafanua imani kuwa “kuamini bila kuona.” Hilo lingekuwa kukosa hoja. Sidai kuwa bora kuliko Tomaso, lakini alipaswa kuamini bila kumwona Yesu. Ushahidi wote ulionyesha hivyo. Kwanza, marafiki zake wazuri, waliokuwa wamejithibitisha kuwa waaminifu, walisema Yesu alikuwa hai. Pili, Yesu alikuwa amesema wazi kwamba angefufuliwa (tazama Mathayo 16:21). Tatu, Yesu alikuwa tayari amethibitisha kuwa yeye ni wa Uungu kwa uwezo wake wa kuwafufua wafu, kudhibiti hali ya hewa, kuponya wagonjwa na kuzidisha chakula. Tomaso alikuwa na kila kitu alichohitaji kuamini kwamba Yesu alifufuka kutoka kwa wafu. Hata hivyo, alikwenda kinyume na mantiki yote na kusema alihitaji ushahidi zaidi.

Alipokutana na Kristo aliyefufuka, Tomaso alitubu kutokuamini kwake na kumfuata Kristo hadi kufa kishahidi. Kwa bahati mbaya, roho ya kutokuamini licha ya ushahidi bado imeenea katika ulimwengu wetu. Watu wasiomwamini Mungu hudai, licha ya ushahidi wote unaopingana na dai hilo, kwamba uhai unaweza kutokea kutoka pasipo kitu. Wanadai, bila ushahidi wowote, kwamba samaki waligeuka kuwa vyura. Wanang'ang'ania kwa upofu nadharia mbalimbali kama vile: Nadharia ya Mlipuko Mkubwa, Usawaziko wa Vipindi vya Ghafla, na Ukoo wenye Mabadiliko. Hawana USHahidi wowote unaoweza kutumika, lakini bado hudai kwamba mawazo yao yote yanategemea uhalisi unaoweza kuangaliwa na kurudiwa. Wakristo ambao, wakiwa na nia njema, huwaambia kwamba imani huanza pale akili inapokoma, bila kujua wanawasaidia. Ulimwengu huu hauhitaji ufafanuzi wa imani wa mitandao ya kijamii. Unahitaji kuona imani jinsi ilivyo: uhakika katika Mungu aliye hai, uliojengwa imara juu ya akili.

Many people ask, “Is listening to secular music a sin? Is there anything wrong with CCM (Christian Contemporary Music)? Is it okay for Christians to listen to rap, rock, country, pop, or rhythm and blues?” For the sake of this article, I am going to refer to all the music listed above as “secular” music.

Should Christians only listen to “A cappella” music? Music is compelling, and it can have a significant effect on how we live our lives. Music influences us negatively or positively. We should ask the question, “Does the music that I listen to draw me closer to God, or does it push me away from Him and closer to Satan?”

The primary purpose of music is to worship (the expression of reverence and adoration to something or someone). Yet at times we as believers still fail in listening to good wholesome music. This is a problem since most secular music is evil and promotes things that God hates.

Secular music is very catchy and addicting. The flesh would rather listen to secular music than to godly music. This type of music negatively influences the mind and is not profitable. If the song encourages evil, promotes worldliness, gives you bad thoughts, changes your actions for the wrong, and influences your speech for the wrong, we should not be listening to it. When it comes to music, we can comfortably lie to ourselves in this area. Have you lied to yourself? Have you said, “God is OK with this type of music,” yet deep down in your heart, you know He is convicting you, and that He is NOT OK with it?

Secular music is often sensual. The meaning of sensual is “of arousing gratification of the senses and physical.” Is the music that we listen to sensual? Does it put our mind in a state of just going with the beat? How do our bodies want to respond when we listen to such music? If our bodies swing with the rhythm of the music, it is not honoring to the Lord; it is not bringing glory to His name; it is not putting our mind and body in a position to worship the Lord.

We always worship something when we listen to music. If we are concentrating on music that is not of God, we are worshiping our flesh, the world, or even the devil. Usually, music like CCM tends to draw attention to ourselves and not to God. Music like this is very sensual. Can we truly worship God when we listen to this type of music?

CCM is a genre of modern popular music in which the lyrics are focused on matters concerned with the Christian faith. It formed as those affected by the 1960s’ “Jesus movement” revival began to express themselves with a more contemporary style of music. Before that, it was hymns and other gospel songs that were prevalent in the church at the time. Whether we know it or not, much of the CCM adds a pulsating beat (syncopation) at a place that it is not naturally supposed to be. The pulsating beat that is relevant in CCM does not appeal to the spirit of man in worship, rather, it appeals to the flesh. The type of music that appeals to the flesh is not of God but is of the devil. Today, CCM is a term that is used to refer to pop, rock, or praise & worship styles of rhythm and beat, so long as the lyrics fall under the definition of CCM.

Philippians tells us that we are supposed to think on … whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

Secular music does not pass the Philippians 4:8 test. Most secular music has lyrics that are impure, while all of it has a rhythm or beat that is against God’s order. The devil uses it all to influence people to sin or to think about sin. It will affect you in some way. Is the influence of the music that we listen to good or bad? For example, if we are concentrating on music that affects our thoughts or lifestyle in the wrong way, then it is a negative influence that we must put out of our lives.

The Hebrews started the tradition of using music without accompaniment after the fall of the second temple in 70 A.D., at which time instruments were not allowed during a period of mourning after the fall. Throughout history up until The Renaissance, instrumental music was mostly associated with dancing and merry making. As one could not have too much fun in places of worship, this kind of amusing music was not popular with religious leaders.

A cappella is an Italian phrase which means “in the style of the chapel”. It was initially used to refer to music that was sung in a chapel or small worship space without accompanying instruments, as opposed to a large church where an organ usually attended vocal music. The term has since come to mean any music sung without accompaniment, whether sacred (religious) or secular (non-religious). A cappella music can be sung by a large choir, a small group, or as a solo.

In Orthodox and Conservative Jewish congregations, the tradition of singing mostly A cappella still exists. In these synagogues, it is customary for a cantor to chant or sing an authoritative text from the scriptures which the congregation responds to in kind. The only instruments used might be a pitch pipe to give everyone a starting note or a ram’s horn on a special occasion or a holiday.

The early church developed the tradition of A cappella singing from the Hebrews’ Jewish tradition, chanting psalms, or other scriptures and using a cantor as a leader. Gregorian chant was the dominant form of church music starting around 590 A.D. It is a single, simple, melodic line half-spoken, half-sung in a free rhythmic style. In the early church, instrumental music was associated with the sinful outside world and was considered a negative influence.

The tradition of unaccompanied sacred vocal music continued during The Renaissance. Although instruments sometimes doubled or substituted for a vocal line, vocal music mostly stood on its own. The sound of a choir of voices in a chapel with excellent acoustics had a particularly ethereal effect.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was one of the most significant composers of The Renaissance in Italy, writing hundreds of masses and motets for the church. ‘The Palestrina Style,’ as it is called, was a sophisticated A cappella form using many voices singing with different music and text coming in at different times. This was called polyphonic, as opposed to homophonic, which means one melodic line sung together or in the same rhythm.

The Apostle Paul writes, Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; –Ephesians 5:19. Does that sound like making music with instruments? Or does it rather seem like singing praises to God from the heart?

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them –Acts 16:25. When Paul and Silas were in prison, and they were in stocks singing at midnight, I don’t believe that they were singing to bring glory to themselves. They were singing to bring glory to God the Father. The result of them giving God the glory is quite astounding. There was an earthquake, the foundations of the prison shook, the doors flew open, and everyone’s prison bands broke. At the end of this happening, the jailor came trembling before Paul and Silas and asked: “What must I do to be saved?”

Colossians also tells us that we should Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Do we let psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs teach us, admonish us, and encourage us?

I wonder what hymn Jesus sang with His disciples at the last supper before He went out to the Mount of Olives. I doubt that they were singing to themselves. I believe they were singing to their heavenly Father.

Pure and holy music is a blessing from the Lord. It is such a beautifully powerful thing that we should not take for granted. Sometimes God uses it to speak to us. I firmly believe that all Christians need to be listening to godly music throughout the week, not just on Sunday. It helps me stay calm, be encouraged, and keep my mind on the Lord. When my mind is on the Lord, I can go through the day blest.

We need to discipline ourselves with the things of God. We also need to get rid of things in our life that we know God is not pleased with. Godly music (music that draws our spirit and mind to the things that are from God) is the type of music that believers should listen to. Worship is what it boils down to, do we worship God or something else?

Jesus says, But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him –John 4:23.

So, let us sing in sincere worship to our Creator, let us give God the glory for the voices that He has given us, and let us sing and listen to godly, wholesome songs to our God.

Mange spør: «Er det synd å lytte til verdslig musikk? Er det noe galt med CCM (kristen samtidsmusikk)? Er det greit for kristne å lytte til rap, rock, country, pop eller rhythm and blues?» I denne artikkelen kommer jeg til å omtale all musikken som er nevnt ovenfor, som «verdslig» musikk.

Bør kristne bare lytte til musikk «a cappella»? Musikk har stor tiltrekningskraft, og den kan ha stor innvirkning på hvordan vi lever livene våre. Musikk påvirker oss negativt eller positivt. Vi bør stille spørsmålet: «Fører musikken jeg lytter til meg nærmere Gud, eller skyver den meg bort fra ham og nærmere Satan?»

Musikkens fremste formål er å tilbe (å uttrykke ærbødighet og hengivenhet overfor noe eller noen). Likevel hender det at vi som troende ikke klarer å lytte til god og sunn musikk. Dette er et problem, siden det meste av den verdslige musikken er ond og fremmer ting Gud hater.

Verdslig musikk er svært fengende og vanedannende. Kjødet vil heller lytte til verdslig musikk enn til gudfryktig musikk. Denne typen musikk påvirker sinnet negativt og er ikke til gagn. Hvis sangen oppmuntrer til ondskap, fremmer verdslighet, gir deg dårlige tanker, får deg til å handle galt og påvirker måten du snakker på i negativ retning, bør vi ikke lytte til den. Når det gjelder musikk, kan vi lett lyve for oss selv på dette området. Har du løyet for deg selv? Har du sagt: «Gud synes det er greit med denne typen musikk», selv om du innerst inne vet at han overbeviser deg om synd, og at han IKKE synes det er greit?

Verdslig musikk er ofte sanselig. Sanselig betyr «noe som vekker tilfredsstillelse av sansene og det fysiske». Er musikken vi lytter til sanselig? Får den sinnet vårt til bare å følge rytmen? Hvordan ønsker kroppene våre å reagere når vi lytter til slik musikk? Hvis kroppene våre svaier med musikkens rytme, ærer det ikke Herren; det herliggjør ikke hans navn; det stiller ikke sinnet og kroppen vår i en posisjon der vi kan tilbe Herren.

Vi tilber alltid noe når vi lytter til musikk. Hvis vi konsentrerer oss om musikk som ikke er av Gud, tilber vi kjødet, verden eller til og med djevelen. CCM-musikk har gjerne en tendens til å rette oppmerksomheten mot oss selv og ikke mot Gud. Slik musikk er svært sanselig. Kan vi virkelig tilbe Gud når vi lytter til denne typen musikk?

CCM er en sjanger innen moderne populærmusikk der tekstene handler om temaer knyttet til den kristne tro. Den oppsto da mennesker som ble påvirket av vekkelsen i «Jesusbevegelsen» på 1960-tallet, begynte å uttrykke seg med en mer moderne musikkstil. Før den tid var det salmer og andre gospelsanger som var utbredt i kirken. Enten vi vet det eller ikke, legger mye av CCM-musikken til en pulserende rytme (synkopering) på steder der det ikke faller naturlig. Den pulserende rytmen som kjennetegner CCM, appellerer ikke til menneskets ånd i tilbedelsen, men til kjødet. Musikk som appellerer til kjødet, er ikke av Gud, men av djevelen. I dag brukes CCM som en betegnelse på pop-, rock- eller lovsangs- og tilbedelsesstiler med bestemte rytmer og takter, så lenge tekstene faller innenfor definisjonen av CCM.

Filipperbrevet forteller oss at vi skal tenke på … alt som er sant, alt som er verdig, alt som er rett, alt som er rent, alt som er elskelig, alt som fortjener ros, alt som er en dyd, og alt som er verdt å prise – Filipperne 4:8.

Verdslig musikk består ikke Filipperne 4:8-prøven. Det meste av den verdslige musikken har urene tekster, mens all slik musikk har en rytme eller takt som strider mot Guds orden. Djevelen bruker den til å påvirke mennesker til å synde eller tenke på synd. Den vil påvirke deg på en eller annen måte. Er musikkens påvirkning på oss god eller dårlig? Hvis vi for eksempel konsentrerer oss om musikk som påvirker tankene våre eller livsstilen vår i feil retning, er den en negativ påvirkning som vi må fjerne fra livet vårt.

Hebreerne begynte tradisjonen med å bruke musikk uten akkompagnement etter at det andre tempelet falt i år 70 e.Kr. Da var instrumenter ikke tillatt i en sorgperiode etter templets fall. Gjennom historien fram til renessansen var instrumentalmusikk for det meste knyttet til dans og festligheter. Siden man ikke skulle more seg for mye på steder for tilbedelse, var denne typen underholdningsmusikk ikke populær blant religiøse ledere.

A cappella er et italiensk uttrykk som betyr «i kapellstil». Opprinnelig ble det brukt om musikk som ble sunget i et kapell eller et lite gudstjenesterom uten instrumentakkompagnement, til forskjell fra en stor kirke der et orgel vanligvis akkompagnerte vokalmusikken. Siden har uttrykket fått betydningen all musikk som synges uten akkompagnement, enten den er hellig (religiøs) eller verdslig (ikke-religiøs). A cappella-musikk kan synges av et stort kor, en liten gruppe eller som solo.

I ortodokse og konservative jødiske menigheter lever tradisjonen med hovedsakelig a cappella-sang fortsatt. I disse synagogene er det vanlig at en kantor messer eller synger en autoritativ tekst fra skriftene, som menigheten svarer på med sang. De eneste instrumentene som brukes, kan være en stemmegaffel for å gi alle en starttone eller et bukkehorn ved en spesiell anledning eller høytid.

Den tidlige kirken utviklet tradisjonen med a cappella-sang fra hebreernes jødiske tradisjon, der man messet salmer eller andre skriftsteder og brukte en kantor som leder. Gregoriansk sang var den dominerende formen for kirkemusikk fra omkring år 590 e.Kr. Den består av én enkel melodilinje, halvt talt og halvt sunget i en fri rytmisk stil. I den tidlige kirken var instrumentalmusikk forbundet med den syndige verden utenfor og ble sett på som en negativ påvirkning.

Tradisjonen med hellig vokalmusikk uten akkompagnement fortsatte under renessansen. Selv om instrumenter av og til doblet eller erstattet en vokalstemme, sto vokalmusikken stort sett på egne ben. Lyden av et kor som sang i et kapell med fremragende akustikk, hadde en særlig overjordisk virkning.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina var en av de mest betydningsfulle komponistene i Italia under renessansen, og skrev hundrevis av messer og motetter for kirken. «Palestrina-stilen», som den kalles, var en sofistikert a cappella-form der mange stemmer sang forskjellige melodier og tekster som kom inn på ulike tidspunkter. Dette ble kalt polyfoni, i motsetning til homofoni, som betyr at én melodilinje synges samlet eller i samme rytme.

Apostelen Paulus skriver: Tal til hverandre med salmer og hymner og åndelige sanger, syng og spill for Herren i hjertet deres – Efeserne 5:19. Høres dette ut som å lage musikk med instrumenter? Eller virker det snarere som om vi synger lovsanger til Gud av hjertet?

Ved midnatt ba Paulus og Silas og sang lovsanger til Gud, og fangene hørte på dem – Apostlenes gjerninger 16:25. Da Paulus og Silas satt i fengsel, fastlenket, og sang ved midnatt, tror jeg ikke at de sang for å gi seg selv ære. De sang for å gi Gud Fader ære. Resultatet av at de ga Gud æren, er ganske forbløffende. Det kom et jordskjelv, fengselets grunnvoller ristet, dørene sprang opp, og alle fanglenkene løsnet. Da dette hadde skjedd, kom fangevokteren skjelvende fram for Paulus og Silas og spurte: «Hva må jeg gjøre for å bli frelst?»

Kolosserbrevet forteller oss også at vi skal La Kristi ord bo rikelig blant dere, så dere med all visdom kan undervise og rettlede hverandre med salmer, hymner og åndelige sanger, og synge for Gud med takknemlighet i hjertet – Kolosserne 3:16. Lar vi salmer, hymner og åndelige sanger undervise, rettlede og oppmuntre oss?

Jeg lurer på hvilken salme Jesus sang sammen med disiplene ved det siste måltidet, før han dro ut til Oljeberget. Jeg tviler på at de sang for seg selv. Jeg tror de sang til sin himmelske Far.

Ren og hellig musikk er en velsignelse fra Herren. Den er noe så vakkert og kraftfullt at vi ikke bør ta den for gitt. Noen ganger bruker Gud den til å tale til oss. Jeg tror fullt og fast at alle kristne trenger å lytte til gudfryktig musikk gjennom hele uken, ikke bare på søndag. Det hjelper meg å holde meg rolig, bli oppmuntret og holde tankene mine rettet mot Herren. Når tankene mine er rettet mot Herren, kan jeg gå velsignet gjennom dagen.

Vi må disiplinere oss selv med det som hører Gud til. Vi må også kvitte oss med ting i livet vårt som vi vet ikke behager Gud. Gudfryktig musikk (musikk som retter ånden og sinnet vårt mot det som er fra Gud) er den typen musikk troende bør lytte til. Det koker ned til tilbedelse: Tilber vi Gud eller noe annet?

Jesus sier: Men den time kommer, ja, den er nå, da de sanne tilbedere skal tilbe Faderen i ånd og sannhet. For slike tilbedere vil Faderen ha – Johannes 4:23.

La oss derfor synge i oppriktig tilbedelse til vår Skaper, gi Gud æren for stemmene han har gitt oss, og synge og lytte til gudfryktige, sunne sanger til vår Gud.

A verse that has always caught my attention, one that has caused my spine to tingle is found in Matthew chapter seven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? –Matthew 7:22.

Jesus gives us a picture of a large group of people standing before Him on Judgment Day. They thought they lived their lives for Him. They were gifted people—prophesying, casting out devils, and doing many wonderful things in the name of Jesus—they seemed like good Christians. However, in the next verse we read that Jesus will say to them that He never knew them. Jesus even tells them to depart from Him. He sends them to hell, forever.

I remember an account that reminds me of these verses. Years ago, I was working for a steel joist company. It was a normal Friday morning, we were working hard, as was required of each of us. The line boss came out and announced a meeting with the whole plant after the shift was over. We all wondered what the meeting was about. We asked around but it seemed that no one knew. After the shift, we all stood in a large circle and waited for the boss. He soon entered the room with another man. It was the manager of the whole company. Prior to these men coming in, we were all talking casually with each other, there was laughter and loud voices. The boss had a large stack of envelopes, and I heard a buzz go around about bonus checks. Everyone looked excited, except for the boss.

Then the boss started talking, “We have been watching all of you very closely over the past four weeks. We have been looking at your work ethic, how hard you try, and whether you’re on time. We have been looking at many different areas. Your supervisors will give each of you an envelope with your name on it. Do not open this letter until you are off the premises. When you do open it, you will find some instructions. For most, it will say to return to work at the normal time on Monday. But for 27 of you, it will say that you are fired. For those included in that number, we did not like what we saw during our time of evaluation, so we decided that we need to release you from your employment here.”

You could hear a pin drop. Fear was seen on every face. I remember wishing I had worked harder, been more involved. I regretted taking my job for granted. It was a terrible feeling, I had worked there for years, but did that matter?

I wasn’t fired that day, but 27 others were. They thought they had done enough. They thought they were safe since they had put in their time. But they were wrong, and now nothing could be done. It was over.

What about us? Do we gauge our walk with God based on eternity? Do we wonder what will happen on the day of judgement? How can we know?

Jesus says a few verses earlier that we will know each other by our fruits. There is much talk in the Word of God about fruit. We know what type of tree one is, by examining its fruit. When we first moved to Haiti, we didn’t know what kinds of trees were there. I remember looking up at a large tree on our property and wondering what kind it was. Then something gave it away. There were small avocados hanging from its branches. In the church today, it seems that people do not want to talk about this. But I assure you that we should talk about it before it is forever too late. Looking back, we would have loved to talk about this at the factory before that day when some of the employees were fired.

So, what is the fruit of a Christian? We know that being a good person and dressing in a certain way are not determining factors of a godly life. It is not the church we attend, the family we were born into, our culture, or the color of our skin. Many would agree that these things are not what identifies us as Christians. Some may think that the fruit of a Christian is being a good, morally upright, and loving citizen of society. There are many people who are law-abiding citizens, loving and peaceful, taking care of their own needs and the needs of others. Yet it is still possible for them to do all these good things and still go to hell.

We hear the world (and some in the church) proclaiming loudly that it’s only the heart that matters. We know they are saying this so they can excuse the lack of visible fruit. Even though their outside is bad, they want people to think that their heart is good, and that that’s all that really matters.

They are correct about the heart being important. You can’t change or fix anything simply by putting on a form when the heart is still selfish and wicked. However, they are wrong about the heart being good and the outside being bad. This is impossible. Jesus says, Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:26.

You cannot have a clean heart and a sinful appearance. However, on the flip side, you can have a clean appearance and yet still have an ungodly heart. So how do we tell? What is this fruit that Jesus is talking about?

We will talk about the fruit of the Spirit shortly, but first I would like to talk about something else that I believe defines a Christian. Something that can separate the sheep from the wolves, even if they both appear to be the same.

A desire to serve Jesus. When God converts a person’s soul, that individual is a new creature, and desires to serve God with his whole being. That person does not need to be forced to do what pleases God. There is much talk today in the church about structure and rules, however, this was not always the case. So why is this such a big issue today? Maybe there are unconverted people in the church. Perhaps people are too independent and do not want to be told what to do. You can tell a church member to dress modestly, but if their heart is not changed, you will face problems. They will try to be as worldly as they can, and still be within the ‘law’ of the church. Or they will simply refuse to do it and the church soon gives in and no longer requires their people to dress and live modestly. Should the church need to force its people to be modest? Should the church need to force its people to be Christ-like? Absolutely not. When a soul has been redeemed and transformed by the blood of Christ, that person, in return, will, because of his changed nature, live a sacrificial life for Him. We obey His commandments with grateful hearts!

For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous –1 John 5:3.

A heart that has not been made new by God’s Spirit will not passionately desire to live for God. One can religiously go to church—many unbelievers attend church services regularly. One can dress right and act right, but if their heart does not pant after the things of God, these things will have no profit. Much of what they do is to receive the praise of men, not the glory of God. It is no wonder that many churches of today are accepting drift.

It is a beautiful thing to see someone truly desire to live for God. They desire to seek the face of their Creator, their Savior. They live for the Kingdom, for the brotherhood. To obey God and serve Him is a necessity; it is the only thing that really matters to them. Their ‘all’ truly is on the altar. They love reading the Word and spending time alone with God. Their desires and their will have been sacrificed on the altar of their God.

People have told me that we need to give a new Christian some room. “Some room for what?” I ask. Some room for sin… for carnality? Absolutely not. Every example in the Bible says differently. Every conversion brought a tremendous change, a new creature. Many people confuse ‘grace to learn and to grow’ in the faith as an ‘excuse for sin’. The Scriptures define new Christians… As newborn babes, and commands each of us to desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby: –1 Peter 2:2. So new Christians don’t need space to continue for a time in their ungodly ways, but they do need space to grow …in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man –Luke 2:52.

When someone comes declaring they have been converted, it is easy to find out. We simply go over some scriptures that explain practical, foundational doctrines like non-conformity, non-resistance, and such like. Some see it as God’s Word and soak it in. Many folks sit in astonishment as I read such verses to them—Scripture verses they have never heard before. Usually they simply believe what they just heard from God’s word, and it changes them. That is a Christian who wants to be taught, who wants to be discipled. They tend to come with a teachable attitude asking questions about that which they have read in God’s Word and don’t understand.

But what about so many others? They hear the same scriptures and they argue—they argue with the Bible and the person sharing the Scripture with them, but ultimately, they are arguing with God. They will usually admit that it’s what the Bible says but they want to know why it says that. They are not wanting to change their life for God. They want to be a Christian, yes, but they also want to live how they want. They do not desire to obey God. We can continue working with them, but it is clear: their heart pants after the things of the world and the pleasures of this life.

Picture with me a man living 1,000 years ago. He is locked in a dungeon, where everything is as black as coal. It is musty and stinks. He has been arrested for preaching the gospel. His ankles and wrists are raw and bloody from the large, heavy chains that keep him bound in the tiny cell. He’s claustrophobic, weary, and worn. His back is bloody. His aching limbs have been stretched to the breaking point. He talks to God, but God does not answer. He pleads for deliverance but hears nothing in return. He thinks back on his life, his faith. Then he wonders the dreaded thought: “God, are you there? Are you real?” Silence. His faith is being tried to the extreme. He knows that if he continues to hold to his beliefs, a fire awaits him. Why? Why die for a God that allows him to go through this agony? Why die for a God that will not speak? “My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me?”

Now picture this man… is you.

Do we really believe in God, a God who’s not seen and often not heard? If our faith does not exist, then God will not exist when we really need Him.

God wants us to put all our faith in Him, all the time. We walk by faith, NOT by sight… even when things are going well. When we find ourselves in terrible times, God is still near, leading us and giving us courage to go on! We are used to simply trusting in Him, in His word.

For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry? –Luke 23:31.

God loves a heart that is turned toward Him, fully yielded, and surrendered. He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him!

Do we have the fruit of the Spirit of God? Do we act like Christians? Do we look like Christians?

I was asked to preach for a large church that I had never been to before. I went with my family and sat while the seats filled up with hundreds of people. I was amazed at how these people were dressed. There were short miniskirts and skimpy tops, much worldly fashion and style. The service began and I realized quickly that this was not a good place for my family, so I took them home and returned by myself. The rock music was still going, and the dancing was pushing my limits. After two hours it was time for the message. I stood and told the large crowd that I was the new President of America. Laughter filled the auditorium. I then asked them if they believed me. “No!” they shouted. I asked why they didn’t believe me, and they responded with different answers. One yelled, “You don’t look or dress like the president!” Another said, “You wouldn’t be here if you were the president!” Yet another said that I didn’t sound like the president. I told them that I didn’t understand. I asked how they can say that they are Christians—They don’t look like it! They don’t act like it! They don’t sound like it!—Yet everyone believes them!

It seems that we judge everything by its fruit, except for Christians. For Christians we are expected to judge by what they claim. This world thinks they can simply imagine what Jesus wants and then please Him in any way they personally choose. However, the Bible is clear: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them –Matthew 7:16-20.

The Bible says that …the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance… –Galatians 5:22-23. Are these the things that people see when they look at you and I? I know it is easy to justify not having one or more of these fruits by saying, “I’m working on it,” or “I’m praying about it.” Jesus does not say that this fruit is something that Christians should work to attain. He simply says that these are the fruits, or product, of the indwelling Spirit of God. If we pursue worldly ambitions, or if we desire to fit in with the world, we cannot expect this fruit to be evident in our lives. I believe this is the fruit of a suffering man, a person that has been giving his all, and desires to give his all to the Lamb that was slain.

Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire –Matthew 7:19.

When we give something our all, whether it’s our work, our school, or raising a family, it feels good—it is fulfilling. When we serve God with all our being, the same is true. There is a very rewarding feeling, a feeling of peace that passes all understanding.
