제 마음을 늘 사로잡고 등골이 오싹해지게 하는 구절이 마태복음 7장에 나옵니다. 그날에 많은 사람이 내게 이르되, 주여, 주여, 우리가 주의 이름으로 예언하지 아니하였나이까? 주의 이름으로 마귀들을 쫓아내지 아니하였나이까? 주의 이름으로 많은 놀라운 일을 행하지 아니하였나이까? 하리라 –마태복음 7:22.

예수님께서는 심판 날에 그분 앞에 서 있는 많은 사람의 모습을 우리에게 보여 주십니다. 그들은 자신들이 그분을 위해 살아왔다고 생각했습니다. 그들은 은사를 받은 사람들이었습니다. 예수님의 이름으로 예언하고, 마귀들을 쫓아내고, 많은 놀라운 일을 했으니 좋은 그리스도인처럼 보였습니다. 그러나 바로 다음 절에서 예수님께서는 그들에게 자신이 그들을 전혀 알지 못했다고 말씀하실 것임을 읽습니다. 예수님께서는 그들에게 자신에게서 떠나라고까지 하십니다. 그분은 그들을 영원히 지옥으로 보내십니다.

이 구절들을 떠올리게 하는 한 가지 일이 기억납니다. 여러 해 전, 저는 철골 장선 회사에서 일했습니다. 평범한 금요일 아침이었고, 우리 각자에게 요구된 대로 열심히 일하고 있었습니다. 작업반장이 나와서 근무가 끝난 뒤 공장 전체 직원 회의가 있을 것이라고 알렸습니다. 우리는 무슨 회의인지 궁금해했습니다. 여기저기 물어보았지만 아는 사람이 없는 듯했습니다. 근무가 끝난 뒤 우리는 모두 큰 원을 이루어 서서 반장을 기다렸습니다. 곧 반장이 다른 남자 한 명과 함께 방에 들어왔습니다. 회사 전체의 관리자였습니다. 두 사람이 들어오기 전까지 우리는 서로 편하게 이야기하고 있었고, 웃음소리와 큰 목소리가 오갔습니다. 반장은 봉투를 한 무더기 들고 있었는데, 보너스 수표에 관한 수군거림이 퍼지는 소리가 들렸습니다. 반장을 제외한 모두가 들뜬 표정이었습니다.

그러자 반장이 말하기 시작했습니다. “지난 4주 동안 여러분 모두를 아주 면밀히 지켜보았습니다. 여러분의 직업 윤리와 얼마나 열심히 일하는지, 제시간에 출근하는지를 살펴보았습니다. 여러 가지 측면을 검토했습니다. 각자의 상사가 여러분 이름이 적힌 봉투를 하나씩 건네줄 것입니다. 구내를 벗어나기 전까지는 이 편지를 열지 마십시오. 열어 보면 몇 가지 지시가 적혀 있을 것입니다. 대부분은 월요일에 평소 시간에 출근하라는 내용일 것입니다. 하지만 27명에게는 해고되었다는 내용이 적혀 있을 것입니다. 그 27명은 평가 기간에 보여 준 모습이 마음에 들지 않아, 이곳에서 고용 관계를 끝내기로 했습니다.”

핀 하나 떨어지는 소리도 들릴 만큼 조용했습니다. 모든 얼굴에 두려움이 역력했습니다. 더 열심히 일하고, 더 적극적으로 참여했어야 했다는 생각이 났습니다. 제 일자리를 당연한 것으로 여긴 것을 후회했습니다. 끔찍한 기분이었습니다. 그곳에서 여러 해 일했지만, 그게 무슨 의미가 있었겠습니까?

저는 그날 해고되지 않았지만, 다른 27명은 해고되었습니다. 그들은 자신들이 충분히 했다고 생각했습니다. 정해진 기간 동안 일했으니 안전하다고 생각했습니다. 하지만 그들은 틀렸고, 이제는 아무것도 할 수 없었습니다. 모든 것이 끝났습니다.

우리는 어떻습니까? 영원을 기준으로 하나님과 동행하는 삶을 살펴봅니까? 심판 날에 무슨 일이 일어날지 생각해 봅니까? 우리는 어떻게 알 수 있습니까?

예수님께서는 몇 절 앞에서 열매로 서로를 알게 될 것이라고 말씀하십니다. 하나님의 말씀에는 열매에 관한 이야기가 많이 나옵니다. 우리는 열매를 살펴봄으로 어떤 나무인지 압니다. 처음 아이티로 이사 왔을 때, 우리는 그곳에 어떤 종류의 나무들이 있는지 몰랐습니다. 집터에 있는 큰 나무를 올려다보며 무슨 나무인지 궁금해했던 기억이 납니다. 그러다 그 나무의 정체를 알게 해 주는 것이 보였습니다. 가지에 작은 아보카도가 매달려 있었습니다. 오늘날 교회에서는 사람들이 이 이야기를 하고 싶어 하지 않는 것 같습니다. 그러나 너무 늦어 영원히 돌이킬 수 없게 되기 전에 이 이야기를 해야 한다고 저는 분명히 말씀드립니다. 돌이켜보면, 공장에서 직원 몇 명이 해고되기 전날 이 이야기를 나누었더라면 얼마나 좋았을까 싶습니다.

그렇다면 그리스도인의 열매는 무엇입니까? 선한 사람이 되는 것과 특정한 방식으로 옷을 입는 것이 경건한 삶을 결정하는 요소가 아니라는 점은 압니다. 우리가 다니는 교회나 태어난 가정, 문화, 피부색도 결정 요소가 아닙니다. 많은 사람도 이런 것들이 우리를 그리스도인으로 규정하지 않는다는 데 동의할 것입니다. 어떤 사람들은 그리스도인의 열매란 선하고 도덕적으로 올바르며 사회를 사랑하는 시민이 되는 것이라고 생각할지도 모릅니다. 법을 지키고, 사랑과 평화를 실천하며, 자신과 다른 사람의 필요를 돌보는 사람은 많습니다. 하지만 그들이 이런 좋은 일을 모두 하면서도 여전히 지옥에 갈 가능성은 있습니다.

세상 사람들과 교회 안의 일부 사람들이 마음만 중요하다고 큰 소리로 주장하는 것을 듣습니다. 그들이 그렇게 말하는 것은 눈에 보이는 열매가 없는 것을 변명하려는 것임을 압니다. 겉모습은 좋지 않더라도 마음은 선하다고, 그리고 그것만이 정말 중요하다고 사람들이 생각하기를 바랍니다.

마음이 중요하다는 그들의 말은 옳습니다. 마음이 여전히 이기적이고 사악한데 겉모양만 갖춘다고 해서 어떤 것을 바꾸거나 바로잡을 수는 없습니다. 그러나 마음은 선하고 겉모습은 나쁘다는 말은 틀렸습니다. 그것은 불가능합니다. 예수님께서는 말씀하십니다. 눈먼 바리새인아, 먼저 잔과 대접의 안을 깨끗하게 하여라. 그러면 겉도 깨끗해질 것이다 –마태복음 23:26.

마음은 깨끗한데 외모는 죄악된 상태일 수 없습니다. 반대로, 겉모습은 깨끗해 보여도 마음은 여전히 경건하지 않을 수 있습니다. 그렇다면 우리는 어떻게 분별합니까? 예수님께서 말씀하시는 이 열매는 무엇입니까?

곧 성령의 열매에 대해 이야기하겠지만, 먼저 그리스도인을 규정한다고 제가 믿는 다른 한 가지에 대해 말씀드리고 싶습니다. 서로 똑같아 보이더라도 양과 이리를 구별해 줄 수 있는 것입니다.

예수님을 섬기려는 열망. 하나님께서 한 사람의 영혼을 회심시키시면, 그 사람은 새로운 피조물이 되어 온 존재를 다해 하나님을 섬기기를 열망합니다. 하나님을 기쁘시게 하는 일을 억지로 시킬 필요가 없습니다. 오늘날 교회에서는 조직과 규칙에 관한 이야기가 많이 나오지만, 언제나 그랬던 것은 아닙니다. 그렇다면 오늘날에는 왜 이것이 이렇게 큰 문제가 되었습니까? 교회 안에 회심하지 않은 사람들이 있기 때문일지도 모릅니다. 사람들이 지나치게 독립적이어서 지시받기를 원하지 않는 것일 수도 있습니다. 교회 구성원에게 단정하게 옷을 입으라고 말할 수는 있지만, 마음이 변화되지 않았다면 문제가 생길 것입니다. 그들은 교회의 ‘규칙’ 안에 머물면서도 최대한 세상 사람처럼 행동하려고 할 것입니다. 아니면 그냥 거부할 것이고, 교회는 곧 양보하여 더는 교인들에게 단정하게 옷 입고 살라고 요구하지 않을 것입니다. 교회가 교인들에게 단정하라고 강요해야 합니까? 교회가 교인들에게 그리스도처럼 되라고 강요해야 합니까? 결코 그렇지 않습니다. 한 영혼이 그리스도의 피로 구속받고 변화되면, 그 사람은 변화된 본성으로 말미암아 그분을 위해 희생하는 삶을 살게 됩니다. 우리는 감사하는 마음으로 그분의 계명에 순종합니다!

하나님을 사랑한다는 것은 곧 그분의 계명들을 지키는 것이며, 그분의 계명들은 무거운 짐이 아닙니다 –요한일서 5:3.

하나님의 영으로 새롭게 된 마음이 아니라면 하나님을 위해 살고자 하는 뜨거운 열망이 생기지 않습니다. 종교적인 마음으로 교회에 다닐 수는 있습니다. 믿지 않는 사람 중에도 정기적으로 예배에 참석하는 이들이 많습니다. 올바르게 옷을 입고 올바르게 행동할 수도 있지만, 마음이 하나님의 일을 간절히 사모하지 않는다면 그런 것들은 아무 유익이 없습니다. 그들이 하는 일의 상당 부분은 하나님의 영광이 아니라 사람들의 칭찬을 받기 위한 것입니다. 오늘날 많은 교회가 세상의 흐름을 받아들이는 것도 놀랄 일이 아닙니다.

누군가가 진정으로 하나님을 위해 살기를 열망하는 모습을 보는 것은 아름다운 일입니다. 그들은 창조주이자 구원자이신 하나님의 얼굴을 구하기를 열망합니다. 하나님 나라와 형제 공동체를 위해 삽니다. 하나님께 순종하고 그분을 섬기는 일은 반드시 해야 할 일이며, 그들에게 정말 중요한 것은 그것뿐입니다. 그들의 ‘모든 것’이 참으로 제단 위에 놓여 있습니다. 그들은 말씀 읽기를 사랑하고 하나님과 단둘이 시간을 보내는 것을 사랑합니다. 그들의 소원과 뜻은 그들의 하나님께 드리는 제단 위에 희생되었습니다.

새 그리스도인에게 여유를 주어야 한다고 말하는 사람들이 있습니다. “무엇을 위한 여유입니까?” 하고 제가 묻습니다. 죄를 위한 여유, 육적인 삶을 위한 여유입니까? 결코 그렇지 않습니다. 성경에 나오는 모든 본보기는 그와 다릅니다. 모든 회심은 엄청난 변화, 새로운 피조물이 되는 일을 가져왔습니다. 많은 사람이 믿음 안에서 ‘배우고 성장할 은혜’를 ‘죄를 위한 변명’으로 혼동합니다. 성경은 새 그리스도인들을 이렇게 묘사합니다. 갓난아이들처럼, 그리고 우리 각자에게 이렇게 명합니다. 말씀의 순전한 젖을 사모하십시오. 이는 그 젖으로 말미암아 자라게 하려는 것입니다 –베드로전서 2:2. 그러므로 새 그리스도인에게는 경건하지 않은 삶의 방식을 한동안 계속할 여유가 필요한 것이 아니라, …지혜와 키가 자라 가며 하나님과 사람에게 더욱 사랑스러워져 가는 데 필요한 여유가 필요합니다 –누가복음 2:52.

누군가 회심했다고 말하며 찾아오면 쉽게 알아볼 수 있습니다. 비순응, 비저항주의 등과 같은 실천적이고 기초적인 교리를 설명하는 성경 구절을 함께 살펴보면 됩니다. 어떤 이들은 그것을 하나님의 말씀으로 받아들여 마음에 깊이 새깁니다. 제가 그런 구절들을 읽어 주면, 처음 듣는 성경 말씀이라며 놀라는 사람들이 많습니다. 대개 그들은 방금 하나님의 말씀에서 들은 내용을 그대로 믿고, 그 말씀은 그들을 변화시킵니다. 그런 사람은 가르침받기를 원하고 제자 훈련을 받기를 원하는 그리스도인입니다. 그들은 배우려는 태도로 찾아와 하나님의 말씀에서 읽었지만 이해하지 못한 내용에 대해 질문하는 경향이 있습니다.

그러나 그 밖의 많은 사람은 어떻습니까? 그들은 같은 성경 말씀을 듣고 논쟁합니다. 성경과 그 말씀을 전하는 사람과 논쟁하지만, 결국 하나님과 논쟁하는 것입니다. 보통 그들은 성경이 그렇게 말한다는 점은 인정하지만, 왜 그렇게 말하는지 알고 싶어 합니다. 그들은 하나님을 위해 자신의 삶을 바꾸고 싶어 하지 않습니다. 그리스도인이 되고 싶기는 하지만, 자신이 원하는 대로 살고 싶기도 합니다. 그들은 하나님께 순종하기를 바라지 않습니다. 계속 그들을 돕기 위해 애쓸 수는 있지만, 그들의 마음이 세상의 일과 이생의 쾌락을 간절히 좇는다는 점은 분명합니다.

천 년 전을 살았던 한 남자를 함께 그려 보십시오. 그는 지하 감옥에 갇혀 있습니다. 그곳은 석탄처럼 온통 캄캄합니다. 곰팡내가 나고 악취가 풍깁니다. 그는 복음을 전했다는 이유로 체포되었습니다. 작고 비좁은 감방에 그를 묶어 둔 크고 무거운 사슬에 발목과 손목이 쓸려 살갗이 벗겨지고 피가 납니다. 그는 폐쇄 공포에 시달리고 지쳤으며 기진맥진해 있습니다. 등은 피투성이입니다. 아픈 팔다리는 부러질 지경까지 늘어났습니다. 하나님께 기도하지만 하나님께서는 응답하지 않으십니다. 구해 달라고 간청하지만 아무런 대답도 듣지 못합니다. 그는 자신의 삶과 믿음을 되돌아봅니다. 그러다 두려운 생각을 합니다. “하나님, 거기 계십니까? 정말 계십니까?” 침묵입니다. 그의 믿음은 극한의 시험을 받고 있습니다. 믿음을 계속 지키면 자신을 기다리는 것은 불길이라는 사실을 압니다. 왜입니까? 그가 이런 고통을 겪도록 내버려 두시는 하나님을 위해 왜 죽어야 합니까? 말씀하지 않으시는 하나님을 위해 왜 죽어야 합니까? “나의 하나님, 나의 하나님, 어찌하여 나를 버리셨나이까?”

이제 이 남자가… 바로 여러분이라고 상상해 보십시오.

우리는 보이지 않으시고 자주 응답하지도 않으시는 하나님을 정말 믿습니까? 우리에게 믿음이 없다면, 정작 하나님이 절실히 필요할 때 하나님께서는 우리에게 계시지 않을 것입니다.

하나님께서는 우리가 언제나 온전히 그분을 믿기를 바라십니다. 우리는 보는 것으로가 아니라 믿음으로 걷습니다… 일이 잘 풀릴 때에도 그렇습니다. 끔찍한 시기를 맞이할 때에도 하나님께서는 여전히 가까이 계시며, 우리를 이끄시고 계속 나아갈 용기를 주십니다! 우리는 그분과 그분의 말씀을 그저 신뢰하는 데 익숙합니다.

푸른 나무에도 이런 일을 하거든 마른 나무에는 무슨 일이 일어나겠느냐? –누가복음 23:31.

하나님께서는 자신을 향하고 온전히 내어 드린 마음, 자신에게 복종하는 마음을 사랑하십니다. 그분은 부지런히 자신을 찾는 이들에게 상을 주시는 분입니다!

우리에게 하나님의 영의 열매가 있습니까? 우리는 그리스도인처럼 행동합니까? 그리스도인처럼 보입니까?

제가 한 번도 가 본 적 없는 큰 교회에서 설교해 달라는 부탁을 받았습니다. 가족과 함께 가서 수백 명이 자리를 채우는 동안 앉아 있었습니다. 사람들의 옷차림에 놀랐습니다. 짧은 미니스커트와 노출이 심한 상의, 세상적인 유행과 스타일이 많이 보였습니다. 예배가 시작되고 얼마 지나지 않아 가족이 머물기에는 좋은 곳이 아니라는 것을 깨달아, 가족을 집에 데려다준 뒤 저 혼자 돌아왔습니다. 록 음악은 계속 흘러나왔고, 춤은 제가 감당할 수 있는 선을 넘고 있었습니다. 두 시간이 지나 설교할 때가 되었습니다. 저는 일어서서 군중에게 제가 미국의 새 대통령이라고 말했습니다. 강당은 웃음소리로 가득 찼습니다. 그런 다음 그들에게 제 말을 믿느냐고 물었습니다. “아니요!” 하고 그들이 외쳤습니다. 왜 믿지 않느냐고 묻자 여러 가지 대답이 나왔습니다. 한 사람이 “대통령처럼 보이지도 않고 옷차림도 그렇지 않잖아요!”라고 외쳤습니다. 또 다른 사람은 “대통령이라면 여기에 오지 않았을 겁니다!”라고 말했습니다. 또 다른 사람은 제가 대통령처럼 말하지 않는다고 했습니다. 저는 이해가 되지 않는다고 말했습니다. 그들에게 그리스도인이라고 하는 이유를 물었습니다. 그리스도인처럼 보이지 않습니다! 그리스도인처럼 행동하지 않습니다! 그리스도인처럼 말하지 않습니다! 그런데도 모두가 그들을 믿습니다!

그리스도인만 빼고 모든 것을 열매로 판단하는 것 같습니다. 그리스도인에 대해서는 그들이 스스로 주장하는 말로 판단해야 한다고 여깁니다. 세상은 예수님께서 원하시는 것을 마음대로 상상한 다음, 각자 원하는 방식으로 그분을 기쁘시게 할 수 있다고 생각합니다. 그러나 성경은 분명히 말씀합니다. 그들의 열매로 그들을 알게 될 것입니다. 가시나무에서 포도를, 엉겅퀴에서 무화과를 거두겠습니까? 이와 같이 좋은 나무마다 좋은 열매를 맺고, 못된 나무는 나쁜 열매를 맺습니다. 좋은 나무가 나쁜 열매를 맺을 수 없고, 못된 나무가 좋은 열매를 맺을 수 없습니다. 좋은 열매를 맺지 않는 나무마다 찍혀 불에 던져집니다. 그러므로 그들의 열매로 그들을 알게 될 것입니다 –마태복음 7:16-20.

성경은 …성령의 열매는 사랑과 기쁨과 화평과 오래 참음과 친절과 선함과 믿음과 온유와 절제입니다… –갈라디아서 5:22-23.라고 말씀합니다. 사람들이 여러분과 저를 볼 때 이런 모습을 봅니까? 이런 열매 중 하나 이상이 없는 것을 “노력하고 있어요” 또는 “그 문제를 두고 기도하고 있어요”라고 말하며 정당화하기 쉽다는 것을 압니다. 예수님께서는 이 열매가 그리스도인들이 얻기 위해 노력해야 하는 것이라고 말씀하지 않으십니다. 그저 이것이 하나님의 영이 내주하시는 데서 나오는 열매, 곧 결과라고 말씀하십니다. 세상적인 야망을 좇거나 세상에 어울리기를 원한다면, 우리 삶에서 이런 열매가 드러나리라고 기대할 수 없습니다. 저는 이것이 고난을 겪는 사람의 열매, 모든 것을 바쳤고 죽임당하신 어린양께 자신의 모든 것을 드리기를 열망하는 사람의 열매라고 믿습니다.

좋은 열매를 맺지 않는 나무마다 찍혀 불에 던져집니다 –마태복음 7:19.

일이든 학교든 가정을 꾸리는 일이든, 어떤 일에 온 힘을 다하면 기분이 좋고 보람을 느낍니다. 온 존재를 다해 하나님을 섬길 때도 마찬가지입니다. 모든 이해를 뛰어넘는 평안, 참으로 큰 보람을 느낍니다.

Greetings in the name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. We are trusting that each of you as our readers are doing well and continuing to trust the Lord. The pandemic has created a bit of a backlog for us, along with some personal issues we have been working through, so this issue is coming to you somewhat behind schedule. Our apologies…. We plan to get the next issue printed within the next several months to get back on track.

In the last issue’s editorial, I wrote about an obscure news article which revealed that many folks across the world were surprised by the positive outcomes they were experiencing through the need to stay at home during the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic. They were enjoying family time. They were finding camaraderie in facing this challenge together. They were finding excitement in the adventure of discovering new ways to function and survive. And they were finding renewed vision and purpose in life.

However, as time has passed, this seems to have been short-lived by all who did not have a deeper level of stability in their lives. After a varying amount of time has elapsed for many folks, reality has begun to set in. Some have lost their jobs. Some have lost loved ones. Some have gone through a time of sickness. Many have been starved for fellowship with other human beings. For the elderly living in nursing homes and assisted-living facilities, and those requiring hospitalization, life has become a very lonely existence indeed, since most of these places have not allowed visitors to enter their doors.

The world is trying to find any way possible to cope and survive. There are phone conference lines. There are chat lines. There are webinars geared towards the issue. Many are doing their part to fill the gaps that this pandemic has created in the lives of the people around them.

As we step back to gain a clearer perspective of the unfolding events brought about by the pandemic, the last number of months have been a time of change and uncertainty for most. There’s the economic future, “Is my job secure?” “What about my bills?” “What about my housing?” Then there’s the greatly politicized nature of numerous issues—race inequality, conspiracy theories about the pandemic, and the government mandates regarding our response to the virus pandemic. Add to this the polarization in our country regarding politics—who is telling the truth on issues, and who will be the best option to lead the country after the upcoming election.

Despite everything else that is going on, the virus and its effects seem to be on everyone’s mind. On August 15, 2020 there was an article published by CNN, written by Ryan Prior, titled: “1 IN 4 YOUNG PEOPLE ARE REPORTING SUICIDAL THOUGHTS”. For those wanting to read the article, it can be found here:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

This article recognizes that there were positive effects during the onset of the pandemic and the resulting stay-at-home orders. This article goes on to say that as time has passed this event is different than most past events, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, and even the circumstances of 9/11. Most of these events have been localized and brief in their destructive effects, while the Covid-19 pandemic has dragged on for so long that it is becoming a way of life—with no end in sight, and its beginning is fading into our forgetful past.

According to the news article, the CDC has published data from a survey which was conducted to determine the outcome of the negative effects of the pandemic. Following are some facts as presented in the article:

  • Suicidal ideation is up among young people since last year
  • As many as one in four people ages 18 through 24 having seriously considered suicide in the 30 days preceding the survey (researchers surveyed 5,412 adults in the US between June 24 and 30.)
  • In the general US population … 11% of adults surveyed had seriously considered suicide in the past 30 days before they completed the survey.
  • The number of Americans reporting anxiety symptoms is three times the number at this same time last year, the CDC said.
  • The results reflect a nation increasingly on edge.

How sad it is to ponder this reality. As I read this news article, I had to wonder whether the percentages are the same for the church as they are for the world. A verse of scripture came to mind: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable –1 Corinthians 15:19. As Christians…

  • …we have HOPE!
  • …we have HOPE IN CHRIST!!
  • …we have HOPE both IN THIS LIFE and FOR ETERNITY!!!

Considering all this we should have a smile on our faces, hope in our hearts, and an encouraging word on our lips for all with whom we come in contact. Let’s be especially observant as we interact with the people around us—family, friend, and even the stranger. Who knows, maybe the neighbor next door is feeling all alone and discouraged. Or perhaps our best friend from church has been struggling with a burden that seems more than they can bear. As we pray, we can ask God to bring people to our minds that would be blessed by our assistance of one sort or another. We never know when our smile or encouraging word will help make a change in someone’s eternal welfare.

Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another. For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:1-5.

There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able… –1 Corinthians 10:13.

My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience –James 1:2-3.

In these verses, I see a number of things that God wants us to use to live by.

  1. God will not allow us to be tempted above that which we are able to endure. This is according to His fact, not according to our feeling.
  2. Each of us WILL fall into temptations, but as we see God’s sovereignty involved in our trials, we can rest as we “count it all joy”.
  3. When it seems that our faith is being tried and tested, sometimes seemingly almost to the breaking point, we can rest assured that God is in the middle of it and that He is up to something according to His will.
  4. God will allow burdens into each of our lives and He expects each of us to “bear our own burdens”.
  5. God will allow our fellow man to go through times of difficulty, during which God expects us to see our struggling brother or sister and do whatever we can to help ease the burden—through prayer, words of encouragement, or deeds of assistance.

In closing, I will leave you with several verses that Paul wrote to the church of Galatia. And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. –Galatians 6:9-10. As strangers and pilgrims here on this earth, let’s not lose sight of our Eternal Home, our Sympathetic Savior, our Sovereign God, and our Abba Father.

Hilsen i vår Herre og frelser Jesu Kristi navn. Vi håper at det står bra til med hver og en av dere som leser oss, og at dere fortsetter å sette deres lit til Herren. Pandemien har ført til at vi har kommet litt på etterskudd, sammen med noen personlige utfordringer som vi har arbeidet oss gjennom, så dette nummeret kommer til dere noe senere enn planlagt. Vi beklager…. Vi planlegger å få trykt neste nummer i løpet av de neste månedene, slik at vi kommer à jour igjen.

I lederartikkelen i forrige nummer skrev jeg om en lite omtalt nyhetsartikkel som viste at mange mennesker verden over ble overrasket over de positive virkningene de opplevde da de måtte holde seg hjemme i begynnelsen av Covid-19-pandemien. De nøt tiden sammen med familien. De fant fellesskap i å møte denne utfordringen sammen. De opplevde spenningen ved å finne nye måter å fungere og overleve på. Og de fant fornyet visjon og mening i livet.

Men etter hvert som tiden har gått, ser dette ut til å ha vært kortvarig for alle som ikke hadde en dypere grad av stabilitet i livet. Etter at det har gått ulikt lang tid for mange, har virkeligheten begynt å synke inn. Noen har mistet jobben. Noen har mistet sine nærmeste. Noen har vært syke en periode. Mange har savnet fellesskap med andre mennesker. For eldre som bor på sykehjem og omsorgsboliger, og for dem som trenger sykehusinnleggelse, har livet virkelig blitt en svært ensom tilværelse, ettersom de fleste slike steder ikke har tillatt besøkende å komme inn.

Verden prøver å finne alle mulige måter å takle situasjonen på og overleve. Det finnes telefonkonferanser. Det finnes chattetjenester. Det finnes webinarer rettet mot dette temaet. Mange gjør sitt for å fylle tomrommene pandemien har skapt i livene til menneskene rundt dem.

Når vi tar et skritt tilbake for å få et klarere perspektiv på hendelsene som utspiller seg som følge av pandemien, ser vi at de siste månedene har vært en tid preget av forandring og usikkerhet for de fleste. Så er det den økonomiske framtiden: «Er jobben min trygg?» «Hva med regningene mine?» «Hva med boligen min?» I tillegg kommer den sterkt politiserte karakteren ved en rekke spørsmål – raseulikhet, konspirasjonsteorier om pandemien og myndighetenes påbud om hvordan vi skal forholde oss til viruspandemien. Legg til polariseringen i landet vårt når det gjelder politikk – hvem som snakker sant i ulike saker, og hvem som vil være best egnet til å lede landet etter det kommende valget.

Til tross for alt annet som skjer, ser viruset og virkningene av det ut til å oppta alles tanker. 15. august 2020 publiserte CNN en artikkel skrevet av Ryan Prior, med tittelen: «1 AV 4 UNGE MELDER OM SELVMORDSTANKER». De som vil lese artikkelen, finner den her:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

Artikkelen erkjenner at det var positive virkninger da pandemien brøt ut og påbudene om å holde seg hjemme ble innført. Videre sier den at denne hendelsen er annerledes enn de fleste tidligere hendelser, som tornadoer, orkaner, jordskjelv og til og med omstendighetene rundt 11. september 2001. De fleste av disse hendelsene har vært lokale og kortvarige i sine ødeleggende virkninger, mens Covid-19-pandemien har trukket ut så lenge at den er i ferd med å bli en livsstil – uten noen ende i sikte, og begynnelsen på den er i ferd med å forsvinne inn i vår glemsomme fortid.

Ifølge nyhetsartikkelen har CDC publisert data fra en undersøkelse som ble gjennomført for å fastslå omfanget av pandemiens negative virkninger. Her er noen fakta slik de presenteres i artikkelen:

  • Selvmordstanker blant unge har økt siden i fjor
  • Så mange som én av fire personer i alderen 18 til 24 år hadde seriøst vurdert selvmord i løpet av de 30 dagene før undersøkelsen (forskerne spurte 5 412 voksne i USA mellom 24. og 30. juni.)
  • I den generelle befolkningen i USA … hadde 11 % av de voksne som ble spurt, seriøst vurdert selvmord i løpet av de 30 dagene før de svarte på undersøkelsen.
  • Antallet amerikanere som rapporterer symptomer på angst, er tre ganger så høyt som på samme tid i fjor, sa CDC.
  • Resultatene gjenspeiler en nasjon som blir stadig mer urolig.

Så trist det er å tenke på denne virkeligheten. Da jeg leste denne nyhetsartikkelen, måtte jeg undre meg på om prosentandelene er de samme i kirken som i verden. Et bibelvers kom meg i hu: Hvis vi bare har håp om Kristus i dette livet, er vi de ynkeligste av alle mennesker –1. Korinter 15:19. Som kristne …

  • … har vi HÅP!
  • … har vi HÅP I KRISTUS!!
  • … har vi HÅP både I DETTE LIVET og I EVIGHETEN!!!

Når vi tenker på alt dette, bør vi ha et smil om munnen, håp i hjertet og et oppmuntrende ord på leppene for alle vi møter. La oss være særlig oppmerksomme når vi samhandler med menneskene rundt oss – familie, venner og til og med fremmede. Hvem vet, kanskje naboen føler seg helt alene og motløs. Eller kanskje vår beste venn i kirken har strevd med en byrde som synes større enn vedkommende kan bære. Når vi ber, kan vi be Gud om å minne oss på mennesker som vil bli velsignet av at vi hjelper dem på den ene eller andre måten. Vi vet aldri når smilet eller det oppmuntrende ordet vårt vil bidra til å forandre noens evige ve og vel.

Brødre, om et menneske blir grepet i et feiltrinn, skal dere som er åndelige, hjelpe ham til rette i en mild ånd. Men pass deg selv, så ikke også du blir fristet. Bær byrdene for hverandre, og oppfyll på den måten Kristi lov. Den som tror at han er noe, enda han ingenting er, bedrar seg selv. Enhver må prøve sin egen gjerning. Da kan han være stolt av det han selv har gjort, uten å sammenligne seg med andre. For enhver skal bære sin egen bør –Galaterne 6:1-5.

Dere har ikke møtt noen prøvelse som ikke er menneskelig. Gud er trofast, og han skal ikke la dere bli prøvet over evne … –1. Korinter 10:13.

Mine søsken, vær glade når dere møter alle slags prøvelser. For dere vet at når troen deres blir prøvet, skaper det utholdenhet –Jakob 1:2-3.

I disse versene ser jeg flere ting Gud vil at vi skal leve etter.

  1. Gud vil ikke la oss bli fristet mer enn vi kan tåle. Dette bygger på hans faktum, ikke på hvordan vi føler det.
  2. Hver og en av oss VIL møte fristelser, men når vi ser Guds suverenitet virksom i prøvelsene våre, kan vi finne ro mens vi «regner alt som glede».
  3. Når det synes som om troen vår blir prøvet og testet, noen ganger tilsynelatende nesten til bristepunktet, kan vi være trygge på at Gud er midt i det, og at han gjør noe etter sin vilje.
  4. Gud vil la byrder komme inn i livet til hver og en av oss, og han forventer at hver og en av oss skal «bære sin egen byrde».
  5. Gud vil la våre medmennesker gå gjennom vanskelige tider, og da forventer Gud at vi ser vår bror eller søster som strever, og gjør alt vi kan for å lette byrden – gjennom bønn, oppmuntrende ord eller praktisk hjelp.

Avslutningsvis vil jeg etterlate dere med noen vers Paulus skrev til menigheten i Galatia. La oss ikke bli trette av å gjøre det gode. Når tiden er inne, skal vi høste, bare vi ikke gir opp. Så la oss gjøre godt mot alle så lenge det er tid, og mest mot dem som er våre søsken i troen. –Galaterne 6:9-10. Som fremmede og pilegrimer her på jorden må vi ikke miste vårt evige hjem, vår medfølende frelser, vår suverene Gud og vår Abba Far av syne.

It is August 2020, over four months since the coronavirus pandemic started, and it is still affecting our lives. People are still getting sick. The government and its decisions continue to be at the center of a lot of our conversations. The cause and cure are ongoing topics. The difference between those that believe the coronavirus to be a real threat and those that believe it to be primarily an agenda of political nature are becoming more distinct as this virus slowly makes its way through our communities, churches, and society as a whole.

The mandates being issued by the governors of many of our states are forcing God’s people to make decisions on issues we have not faced before. At what point does the government cross the line of interfering in our religious freedoms by putting in place mandates that will affect how we do church? How should we relate to the differences among us concerning the mandates? Should we or should we not follow them? What should our attitude be towards those in authority when we feel that they are doing things that are politically motivated? What should we do with all the “unbelievable things” that are being passed around, even from well-meaning Christians from what they would consider to be very valid and from legitimate sources? What should we do with the many, what seem to be, “conspiracy theories” that are being propagated and peddled from one person to another in such a manner that makes it hard to refute them? I, in no way, am going to attempt to answer how a church should relate to the specific mandates but would like to address some concerning attitudes and other responses that have been observed throughout our plain communities.

One of the most concerning issues is the attitude that people have had and are having toward the government. In 1 Peter, the apostle Peter calls us to “honor the king” and the Apostle Paul admonishes us in Romans 13 to be “subject to the higher Powers, for there is no power but of God”. The word honour, as used in 1 Peter 2, in reference to the king, means to “prize” or to “fix valuation upon.” A verse like this and others would indicate that when we speak of our government and, for that matter, others, our attitude should be one of respect. The words and the tone of voice we use should reflect that commitment. Our choice of words and the tone we use will speak volumes. They reflect our attitude.

I personally believe that we as the plain community have done a lot of damage to our “light” and “witness” by refusing to wear the mask in required public settings. But God looks deeper than our actions and we should too. The remarks like “no one will tell me I have to wear that thing” and others similar to that have their roots in a “lack of respect.” God clearly tells us, though we may not be able to always obey in every situation, respect and honor is always to be seen and heard in our attitudes and speech.

The apostle Paul is a good example of one who had a heart to honor those in authority and repented when he failed to do so. When Ananias the high priest asked the ones by him to smite him, he called the high priest a “whited wall”. When told that he had reviled the high priest, he was very quick to apologize for his wrong even though the high priest was wrong in asking them to hit him. It might remind us of the little saying, “Two wrongs do not make a right.”

Having a bad attitude because the government is making what we think are wrong decisions will not bring about right! As we find our way through these mandates, let’s make sure we do not sin against those in authority by speaking about them in a disrespectful manner. Let us repent of any bad attitudes and make sure our heart is in a position to honor and then the words and tone we use will convey the same.

Another area that is extremely hard to know how to respond to is that of all the negative information that is floating around surrounding Covid–19. Many of the plain community tend to distrust the government’s way of handling the situation. Because of this we are quick to believe and pass on negative information as fact. How do we know what is true and what is not? We need to be so careful, even when the information comes from what we believe to be a reliable source, because the more this negative information is passed along, the more folks will distrust the government. Case in point, there have been numerous deaths that were not directly connected to Covid–19; however, it was reported that Covid–19 was marked on the death certificate as being the cause of these deaths. After fact checking some of these supposed cases, it was found that some of these reports were not true. Since several reports have been verified as untrue, I no longer know what to believe. I think we should all be very careful what we do with the information we come across and do all we can to verify the information before passing it on as fact. If it is hard to believe, it is all the more important to check the facts or not pass it on until it has been proven.

Throughout this time period it seems that the conspiracy theories have just escalated. A lot of speculation surrounds the origin of Covid–19, the possible underlying motives, and secrecies the government has in how they are handling the whole Covid–19 dilemma. How do we know if the many propagated theories are true? If they are true, how will that affect the way I live for the other kingdom now? Will it change the way I live? Will it somehow help me prepare for these supposed difficulties that are coming?

In Luke 21, we have a verse talking about future events: “Men’s hearts failing them for fear of things that are coming on the earth.” Are we going to respond to the future in faith or in fear? The media proclaims Covid–19 to be a very dangerous, infectious virus. This perception has caused many in our world to start buying and hoarding for fear of things coming on the face of the earth. We now have articles and theories being peddled by many that seemingly will cause fear of the government and what they are planning to do and ultimately men’s hearts will fail for fear.

The Apostle Peter said that …God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7. Whether these claims are true or not, the Bible still calls us in Philippians to think on …whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report… –Philippians 4:8. To spend even a little time following these theories will have a negative and spiritually draining effect on our lives and the lives around us. Thinking about them not only promotes fear but also makes it even more difficult to respect and honor the government. In reality, some or many of these things may not even be true. As Christians we try to be a peaceful and trusting people, yet this tends to make us vulnerable to be quite gullible. We are quite willing to believe negative claims, allegations, and theories without checking the facts to see whether they could even be true or not. My appeal would be to continue to seek those things that are above, to think on the things that are noble and virtuous.

As believers, we are facing another challenge. The unity within our groups is being challenged in ways it has not been before. We differ in thought on how much the government should interfere in our services. Should we even be having church if the governor would rather that we would not? What about the wearing of masks in our services? Some feel one way and others think differently. These mandates and how we should respond to them can be quite controversial! Now, as much as ever before, we need to extend lots of grace as we sort these things through with each other. We must give some room to each other to understand and relate to it a bit differently. We need much grace with one another and dare not allow these things to become a point of contention. I believe God wants to use these difficulties to draw us closer to Him and each other, but the enemy of our souls is doing his best to have it destroy our love and commitment to each other. Let us seek peace and ensue it!

Dit is Augustus 2020, meer as vier maande sedert die koronaviruspandemie begin het, en dit beïnvloed steeds ons lewens. Mense word steeds siek. Die regering en sy besluite bly die middelpunt van baie van ons gesprekke. Die oorsaak en genesing is voortdurende gespreksonderwerpe. Die verskil tussen dié wat glo dat die koronavirus ’n werklike bedreiging is en dié wat glo dat dit hoofsaaklik ’n politieke agenda is, word al duideliker namate hierdie virus stadig deur ons gemeenskappe, kerke en die samelewing as geheel versprei.

Die verpligte maatreëls wat deur die goewerneurs van baie van ons deelstate uitgevaardig word, dwing God se volk om besluite te neem oor sake waarmee ons nog nie voorheen te doen gehad het nie. Op watter punt oorskry die regering die grens en meng dit in met ons godsdiensvryheid deur maatreëls in te stel wat ’n uitwerking sal hê op hoe ons kerk hou? Hoe behoort ons die meningsverskille onder ons oor die maatreëls te hanteer? Moet ons dit volg of nie? Wat behoort ons houding te wees teenoor dié in gesagsposisies wanneer ons voel dat hulle dinge doen wat deur politieke motiewe gedryf word? Wat moet ons doen met al die “ongelooflike dinge” wat rondgestuur word, selfs deur goedbedoelende Christene, vanuit bronne wat hulle as baie geldig en betroubaar beskou? Wat moet ons doen met die talle sogenaamde “samesweringsteorieë” wat versprei en van een persoon na ’n ander aangegee word op so ’n manier dat dit moeilik is om hulle te weerlê? Ek gaan glad nie probeer antwoord hoe ’n kerk op die spesifieke maatreëls moet reageer nie, maar wil graag aandag gee aan sommige kommerwekkende houdings en ander reaksies wat in ons eenvoudige gemeenskappe waargeneem is.

Een van die sake wat die meeste kommer wek, is die houding wat mense teenoor die regering gehad het en steeds het. In 1 Petrus roep die apostel Petrus ons op om “die koning te eer”, en die apostel Paulus vermaan ons in Romeine 13 om “aan die hoër magte onderdanig te wees, want daar is geen mag behalwe van God nie”. Die woord “eer”, soos dit in 1 Petrus 2 met verwysing na die koning gebruik word, beteken om hom “op prys te stel” of “waarde toe te ken”. ’n Vers soos hierdie en ander dui daarop dat ons houding respekvol behoort te wees wanneer ons oor ons regering praat en, wat dit betref, ook oor ander mense. Die woorde en stemtoon wat ons gebruik, behoort van daardie verbintenis te getuig. Ons woordkeuse en stemtoon spreek boekdele. Dit weerspieël ons houding.

Ek glo persoonlik dat ons as die eenvoudige gemeenskap baie skade aan ons “lig” en “getuienis” aangerig het deur te weier om die masker te dra in openbare plekke waar dit vereis word. Maar God kyk dieper as ons dade, en ons behoort dit ook te doen. Opmerkings soos “niemand gaan vir my sê ek moet daardie ding dra nie” en soortgelyke uitsprake spruit uit ’n “gebrek aan respek”. God sê duidelik vir ons dat respek en eerbied altyd in ons houding en spraak sigbaar en hoorbaar moet wees, al kan ons dalk nie in elke situasie altyd gehoorsaam wees nie.

Die apostel Paulus is ’n goeie voorbeeld van iemand wat ’n hart gehad het om dié in gesagsposisies te eer en berou getoon het wanneer hy daarin gefaal het. Toe Ananias, die hoëpriester, dié wat by hom gestaan het, vra om Paulus te slaan, het hy die hoëpriester ’n “witgekalkte muur” genoem. Toe hy hoor dat hy die hoëpriester beledig het, was hy baie gou om vir sy verkeerde optrede om verskoning te vra, al was die hoëpriester verkeerd toe hy hulle gevra het om Paulus te slaan. Dit herinner ons dalk aan die bekende sêding: “Twee verkeerde dinge maak nie een reg nie.”

’n Slegte houding omdat die regering besluite neem wat ons dink verkeerd is, sal nie die regte uitwerking hê nie! Terwyl ons ons pad deur hierdie maatreëls vind, moet ons sorg dat ons nie teen dié in gesagsposisies sondig deur op ’n oneerbiedige manier oor hulle te praat nie. Laat ons berou hê oor enige slegte houdings en seker maak dat ons hart ingestel is daarop om eer te betoon; dan sal die woorde en stemtoon wat ons gebruik dieselfde oordra.

’n Ander saak waarop dit uiters moeilik is om te weet hoe om te reageer, is al die negatiewe inligting wat oor Covid–19 die rondte doen. Baie in die eenvoudige gemeenskap is geneig om die regering se hantering van die situasie te wantrou. Daarom glo en versprei ons gou negatiewe inligting asof dit feite is. Hoe weet ons wat waar is en wat nie? Ons moet baie versigtig wees, selfs wanneer die inligting kom van ’n bron wat ons as betroubaar beskou, want hoe meer hierdie negatiewe inligting versprei word, hoe meer mense sal die regering wantrou. ’n Voorbeeld hiervan: daar was talle sterftes wat nie direk met Covid–19 verband gehou het nie; tog is daar berig dat Covid–19 as die oorsaak van dié sterftes op die doodsertifikaat aangedui is. Nadat sommige van hierdie beweerde gevalle nagegaan is, is bevind dat sommige van hierdie berigte nie waar was nie. Aangesien verskeie berigte as onwaar bevestig is, weet ek nie meer wat om te glo nie. Ek dink ons behoort almal baie versigtig te wees met wat ons doen met die inligting wat ons teëkom, en alles in ons vermoë te doen om die inligting te verifieer voordat ons dit as feit versprei. As dit moeilik is om te glo, is dit des te belangriker om die feite na te gaan, of om dit nie aan te stuur voordat dit bewys is nie.

Dit lyk asof die samesweringsteorieë in hierdie tydperk net toegeneem het. Daar is baie spekulasie oor die oorsprong van Covid–19, moontlike onderliggende motiewe en geheime wat die regering het oor hoe hulle die hele Covid–19-dilemma hanteer. Hoe weet ons of die talle teorieë wat versprei word waar is? As hulle waar is, hoe sal dit die manier waarop ek nou vir die ander koninkryk leef, beïnvloed? Sal dit die manier waarop ek leef, verander? Sal dit my op die een of ander manier help om my voor te berei op hierdie beweerde moeilikhede wat aan die kom is?

In Lukas 21 is daar ’n vers oor toekomstige gebeure: “Die mense se harte sal beswyk van vrees vir die dinge wat oor die aarde kom.” Gaan ons die toekoms met geloof of met vrees tegemoet? Die media verkondig dat Covid–19 ’n baie gevaarlike, aansteeklike virus is. Hierdie siening het baie mense in ons wêreld laat begin koop en opgaar uit vrees vir dinge wat oor die aarde sal kom. Nou word daar artikels en teorieë deur baie mense versprei wat blykbaar vrees vir die regering en sy beoogde optrede sal aanwakker, en uiteindelik sal mense se harte van vrees beswyk.

Die apostel Petrus het gesê dat …God ons nie ’n gees van vreesagtigheid gegee het nie, maar van krag en liefde en selfbeheersing –2 Timoteus 1:7. Of hierdie bewerings waar is of nie, die Bybel roep ons steeds in Filippense op om te dink aan …alles wat waar is, alles wat eerbaar is, alles wat reg is, alles wat rein is, alles wat lieflik is, alles wat lof verdien… –Filippense 4:8. Selfs ’n bietjie tyd daaraan om hierdie teorieë te volg, sal ’n negatiewe, geestelik uitputtende uitwerking op ons lewens en die lewens van dié om ons hê. Om daaroor te dink, bevorder nie net vrees nie, maar maak dit ook nog moeiliker om die regering te respekteer en te eer. In werklikheid is sommige of baie van hierdie dinge dalk nie eens waar nie. As Christene probeer ons om ’n vreedsame en vertrouende volk te wees, maar dit maak ons dikwels kwesbaar en nogal goedgelowig. Ons is baie bereid om negatiewe bewerings, aantygings en teorieë te glo sonder om die feite na te gaan om te sien of dit hoegenaamd waar kan wees. My pleidooi is dat ons moet aanhou soek na die dinge daarbo, en moet dink aan die dinge wat edel en deugsaam is.

As gelowiges staan ons voor nog ’n uitdaging. Die eenheid binne ons groepe word op maniere getoets wat dit nog nooit tevore was nie. Ons verskil van mening oor hoeveel die regering by ons eredienste behoort in te meng. Moet ons enigsins kerk hou as die goewerneur liewer wil hê ons moet dit nie doen nie? Wat van die dra van maskers tydens ons eredienste? Sommige voel op een manier en ander dink anders. Hierdie maatreëls en hoe ons daarop behoort te reageer, kan nogal omstrede wees! Nou, meer as ooit tevore, moet ons baie genade aan mekaar betoon terwyl ons hierdie sake saam deurwerk. Ons moet mekaar ruimte gee om dit ’n bietjie anders te verstaan en daarop te reageer. Ons het baie genade met mekaar nodig en durf nie toelaat dat hierdie dinge ’n twispunt word nie. Ek glo God wil hierdie moeilikhede gebruik om ons nader aan Hom en aan mekaar te bring, maar die vyand van ons siele doen sy bes om dit ons liefde en verbondenheid aan mekaar te laat vernietig. Laat ons die vrede soek en dit najaag!

That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace –Psalm 144:12.

The vision of every godly parent is to see their children grow into mature adulthood. We want our children to develop biblical convictions that will govern their lives and allow them to become independent of parental guidance.

This was the vision of every Jewish father. To celebrate their child’s transition to personal responsibility, a ceremony was held called bar mitzvah for boys, and bat mitzvah for girls. This was traditionally done at the age of thirteen. Bar mitzvah means “a son of the commandment” and bat mitzvah “a daughter of the commandment”. After bar mitzvah a son was considered to be “under the law” and responsible for his own actions. Prior to this event, his parents were accountable for his actions.

Most of us are not of Jewish descent; however, our Lord Jesus was. We find him at the age of twelve sitting in the temple visiting with the doctors, both hearing them and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. (see Luke 2:47) Jesus demonstrated an amazing level of maturity at the age of twelve. Even his parents were amazed. Yes, he was divine, yet as a human he demonstrated the potential for early maturity given the right set of values and disciplines.

The teen years are transitional years. Teens are transitioning from childhood to adulthood; from being dependent on parents to learning to be independent. This transition is a process that must be understood by both the parents and the child. Too much freedom too soon, can leave the child feeling insecure and can result in bad choices that can have life-long consequences. Too little freedom can squelch a child’s character growth and can become fertile ground for rebellion.

The teen years are growing years. Just as a plant needs diligent cultivation throughout its life cycle, so a child needs ongoing direction throughout his teen years. After Jesus’ episode in the temple we read, And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them… –Luke 2:51. We will look at some things that parents can do to nurture maturity in their children, but first we will consider several relationships that are foundational to healthy maturity.

Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the LORD –Psalm 144:15.

Parental relationship

The relationship between the parent and the child in the teen years is largely a reaping of what that relationship was throughout the formative years of childhood. Unless there is a major spiritual crisis that dynamically changes the relationship—such as an evangelical conversion on the part of either the parent or the child—we (as parents) reap during the child’s teen years that which we have sown during their childhood.

Raising teens is a rewarding experience if there has been a healthy foundational relationship established throughout childhood. If the parent has been physically and emotionally present; if the parent and child have been communicating openly and freely; and if the parent has lovingly maintained the role of authority and control, then a foundation has been laid for a more mature level of relating during the teen years.

In the absence of this kind of parental relationship, the child entering the teen years will try to fill this void with other relationships. Most often, if a parental relationship is lacking, a child will seek to fill that void through relationships with their peers. Peers are great friends but are a poor substitute for a parent. We have been created to be relational. Teens especially crave significance through relationship.

There are two things that every teen is looking for in parental relationship. One is identity and the other is affirmation. Two burning questions in the heart of every teen are “Who am I?” and “Am I OK?”.

The identity factor

When children are young, they assume their family identity. As children grow into adolescence and become more independent, they begin to view themselves as someone more than merely Dad’s son. They begin to develop an identity of their own. This movement toward “being my own person” becomes evident in many of the choices that they make such as:

  • How they dress
  • Their choice of music
  • Their choice of friends
  • Whether or not they choose to serve their parent’s God
  • Whether or not they choose to worship in the church of their upbringing

Admittedly, there are other influences that can affect a teen’s choices in these areas, but for the most part these choices reflect the relationship between the child and the parent. Where the parent has exerted a positive influence on the child, that child will be more inclined to adopt the values of the parent.

When the parental relationship has broken down or has never been nurtured, or if the relationship has been nothing more than a master/slave relationship, that child will seek to identify with someone other than the parent. This will manifest itself in choices of dress, music, friends, and activities that the parent will not approve of. This is often called “teenage rebellion”.

Is “teenage rebellion” always the fault of the parent? No, but if you are not actively involved in building and maintaining a relationship with your teen, it is likely to happen. It is important to note that there is a rebel in the heart of every person. In my last article I stressed the importance of confronting that rebel spirit when our children are young and impressionable.

This rebel spirit will not be fully conquered until it is surrendered to God through an evangelical conversion experience. Only a work of the grace of God upon the heart can subdue the inborn rebellion against God and parental authority.

Know the heart of your child and seek to lead them into loving submission to the Lord Jesus Christ. Only in a relationship with Jesus Christ can our children find their true and lasting identity. Parental authority has a place in shaping and controlling our children when they are young. As our children grow into adulthood, we come to realize that parental authority has limitations and our children need to be controlled by an influence beyond ourselves.

It is never too late to build a relational bridge. If you are feeling that you have failed in your relationship with your children, it’s never too late to call them to your side and humbly seek to restore what is missing. Even if your children are gone from home, I can assure you that they long for a relationship with mom and dad.

The affirmation factor

Every teen longs to be affirmed by their parents, especially their father. You can affirm your teen by looking for and acknowledging positive character traits. There is a place for corrective criticism from parent to child, but criticism that demeans is not constructive; it’s destructive. For every critical comment you should have several positive compliments. In other words, you earn the right to criticize what is wrong by blessing what is right.

You can affirm your teen by treating them with dignity and respect. You can ask, “How do you feel about…?” Or “What do you think we should do…?” You are not surrendering your parental responsibility by probing your son’s or daughter’s mind for their perspective. You are actually causing them to be “grown up in their youth” by forcing them to think as adults.

You can affirm your teen by treating him with common courtesy. Simple things like “please” and “thank you”,” I’m sorry”, “pardon me”, “good bye”, “have a good day”, “drive safely”, and “God bless you”, expresses worth and value to your teen. If these simple courtesies are common in your home your children will return them to you. Think about how you feel when someone says to you, “Oh, excuse me, I’m sorry.” You feel a sense of respect, value, and dignity. That is a simple gift that every parent can give to his child.

You can affirm your teen by entrusting him with responsibility. I grew up on a dairy farm. We had plenty of opportunity to develop character and skills. I remember one day when I was 16 years of age, my dad needed a concrete block wall built out in the barn. I volunteered for the job. Dad provided the blocks and the mortar and got me started. Then I was on my own. Did I build a professional-looking wall? No, but I was quite proud of the outcome and that wall lasted for many years. Dad trusted me to do a man’s job and I did it.

Affirming is not flattery. Flattery is praise that is not sincere and often is not true. Affirming is recognizing and encouraging the good that you see in another. I have encountered grown men who have wept bitterly because they had never received affirmation from their father. Even Jesus received affirmation from His Father when His Father said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

(2) Relationship with God

Our first responsibility in evangelization is to our children. If we cannot evangelize our children, how can we expect to win others to the Lord? We have a distinct advantage in relating our faith to our children in that we are living with our children. They can and do observe how our faith is lived out in everyday life. This should be the most convincing evidence for the validity of our faith.

Unfortunately, how parents live out their faith, or rather fail to live out their faith, can become a huge stumbling block to their children. Our children are keenly aware of any inconsistency in our Christian profession.

Conversely, if our children see that the power of God is evident in our lives, if they see their parents demonstrating faith in God that carries them through difficult times, if they see their parents demonstrating a graceful rest in the Lord, and if, in the home Jesus Christ is exalted and worshipped, they will be convinced to make their parents’ God, their God.

It is the reality of the gospel lived out in daily life that is the most convincing evidence for the validity of our faith. Our children should be our first witnesses to the transformational work of the gospel in our hearts.

How does a parent lead his child to salvation? Salvation is a work of God; however, God uses human instrumentality to accomplish His work. Parents play a major role in leading their children to Christ. Be aware of evidence of conviction. If a child is quiet and withdrawn, or irritable and restless, or belligerent and defiant, it may be that the spirit of God is working in their heart.

Hopefully, you have nurtured a relationship that allows you to probe their heart and gently lead them to Jesus for forgiveness and cleansing. Most of our children’s conversions were initiated by a parent. We recognized signs of conviction and lead them to brokenness and repentance and to receive salvation through faith in Christ.

The early teen years are an ideal time for a child to surrender his/her life to Jesus if he has not already done so. When active rebellion sets in, a teen often makes choices that lead to painful reaping and sometimes irrevocable consequences. A life of dedicated service to God is the only life of blessing and fulfilment.

Relationship with the church

There is one more relationship that dramatically affects the formation of a teen’s life and convictions and that is the local church. We gain both our sense of identity and our understanding of the reality of the Christian faith through our experience of worship and relationship within the local church. After parental relationship, this is the next most significant influence in a teen’s life.

It is important that we worship in a church that presents the gospel as a transformational relationship with God through faith in Jesus. It is also important that our church life consists of warm, loving relationships in a close–knit community.

The reason that I mention this is that some parents have the mistaken idea that they can provide all the spiritual direction and relationships that their children need. This may seem to work when the children are small and close at hand, but as our children grow into adulthood, they will seek a broader world of relationships. The local church and community of associated churches provides this broader base of fellowship.

It is important to worship in a church that you can support and that you can encourage your children to support. Many children have been lost to the faith because mom and dad were not supportive of the church where they were worshipping. It is far better to move on and find a church that you can support than to stay in a church and be in a state of constant opposition.

I am not encouraging church hopping. It is important to children, especially your teens, that there is stability in church life. Find a church that you are comfortable with, hopefully while your children are young, and stick with it. There are always logistical exceptions and your children will adapt to these, but for the most part a stable church life produces youth who have a strong sense of identity and purpose.

As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth –Psalm 127:4. This verse reminds us that our children are a mighty defense against the enemy. If properly honed (trained) and balanced (taught disciplines) our children will have the potential to outlive us both in years and in usefulness. When you release the arrow your children will go places both in time and in the world that you will never see. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate –Psalm 127:5.

Dat ons seuns mag wees soos plante wat in hulle jeug grootword; dat ons dogters mag wees soos hoekstene, gepoleer na die voorbeeld van ’n paleis – Psalm 144:12.

Die visie van elke godvresende ouer is om te sien hoe hul kinders tot volwassenheid groei. Ons wil hê dat ons kinders Bybelse oortuigings ontwikkel wat hul lewe sal rig en hulle in staat sal stel om onafhanklik van ouerlike leiding te word.

Dit was die visie van elke Joodse vader. Om die oorgang van hul kind na persoonlike verantwoordelikheid te vier, is ’n seremonie gehou wat vir seuns bar mitswa en vir meisies bat mitswa genoem is. Dit is tradisioneel op die ouderdom van dertien gedoen. Bar mitswa beteken “’n seun van die gebod” en bat mitswa “’n dogter van die gebod”. Ná bar mitswa is ’n seun beskou as iemand wat “onder die wet” was en verantwoordelik vir sy eie dade. Voor hierdie geleentheid was sy ouers verantwoordelik vir sy dade.

Die meeste van ons is nie van Joodse afkoms nie; ons Here Jesus was egter. Ons vind Hom op twaalfjarige leeftyd in die tempel, waar Hy met die leermeesters praat, na hulle luister en hulle vrae stel. En almal wat Hom gehoor het, was verbaas oor sy insig en antwoorde. (sien Lukas 2:47) Jesus het op twaalfjarige leeftyd ’n verstommende mate van volwassenheid getoon. Selfs sy ouers was verbaas. Ja, Hy was Goddelik, maar as mens het Hy die potensiaal vir vroeë volwassenheid getoon, mits die regte waardes en dissipline teenwoordig is.

Die tienerjare is oorgangsjare. Tieners beweeg van kinderjare na volwassenheid; van afhanklikheid van ouers na leer om onafhanklik te wees. Hierdie oorgang is ’n proses wat sowel die ouers as die kind moet verstaan. Te veel vryheid te gou kan die kind onseker laat voel en lei tot swak keuses met lewenslange gevolge. Te min vryheid kan ’n kind se karaktergroei smoor en ’n vrugbare teelaarde vir opstand word.

Die tienerjare is jare van groei. Net soos ’n plant gedurende sy hele lewensiklus noukeurige versorging nodig het, het ’n kind deur sy tienerjare heen voortdurende leiding nodig. Ná Jesus se gebeurtenis in die tempel lees ons: En Hy het saam met hulle afgegaan en na Nasaret gekom, en was aan hulle onderdanig… – Lukas 2:51. Ons gaan kyk na ’n paar dinge wat ouers kan doen om volwassenheid by hul kinders te bevorder, maar eers sal ons verskeie verhoudings oorweeg wat die grondslag vir gesonde volwassenheid vorm.

Gelukkig is dié volk met wie dit so gesteld is; ja, gelukkig is dié volk wie se God die HERE is – Psalm 144:15.

Verhouding met ouers

Die verhouding tussen die ouer en die kind gedurende die tienerjare is grootliks die oes van wat daardie verhouding gedurende die vormingsjare van die kinderjare was. Tensy daar ’n groot geestelike krisis is wat die verhouding ingrypend verander—soos ’n evangeliese bekering by die ouer of die kind—maai ons (as ouers) gedurende die kind se tienerjare dit wat ons gedurende hul kinderjare gesaai het.

Om tieners groot te maak, is ’n lonende ervaring as daar gedurende die kinderjare ’n gesonde grondslagverhouding gevestig is. As die ouer fisies en emosioneel teenwoordig was; as die ouer en kind openlik en vrylik gekommunikeer het; en as die ouer die rol van gesag en beheer liefdevol gehandhaaf het, is die grondslag gelê vir ’n meer volwasse manier van omgaan gedurende die tienerjare.

As hierdie soort ouer-kind-verhouding ontbreek, sal die kind wat die tienerjare betree, probeer om hierdie leemte met ander verhoudings te vul. Meestal sal ’n kind, as ’n ouer-kind-verhouding ontbreek, probeer om daardie leemte deur verhoudings met hul portuurgroep te vul. Portuurs is goeie vriende, maar ’n swak plaasvervanger vir ’n ouer. Ons is geskep om verhoudings te hê. Tieners smag veral na betekenisvolheid deur verhoudings.

Daar is twee dinge waarna elke tiener in ’n verhouding met hul ouers soek. Die een is identiteit en die ander is bevestiging. Twee brandende vrae in die hart van elke tiener is: “Wie is ek?” en “Is ek oukei?”.

Die identiteitsfaktor

Wanneer kinders jonk is, neem hulle hul gesin se identiteit aan. Namate kinders adolessensie bereik en meer onafhanklik word, begin hulle hulself beskou as iemand wat meer is as bloot Pa se seun. Hulle begin ’n eie identiteit ontwikkel. Hierdie beweging in die rigting van “om my eie mens te wees” word duidelik in baie van die keuses wat hulle maak, soos:

  • Hoe hulle aantrek
  • Hul keuse van musiek
  • Hul keuse van vriende
  • Of hulle kies om hul ouers se God te dien of nie
  • Of hulle kies om in die kerk waarin hulle grootgeword het, te aanbid of nie

Daar is ongetwyfeld ander invloede wat ’n tiener se keuses op hierdie gebiede kan beïnvloed, maar meestal weerspieël hierdie keuses die verhouding tussen die kind en die ouer. Waar die ouer ’n positiewe invloed op die kind uitgeoefen het, sal daardie kind eerder die ouer se waardes aanneem.

Wanneer die ouer-kind-verhouding verbrokkel het of nooit gekoester is nie, of as die verhouding niks meer as ’n meester/slaaf-verhouding was nie, sal die kind probeer om met iemand anders as die ouer te identifiseer. Dit sal sigbaar word in keuses van kleredrag, musiek, vriende en aktiwiteite wat die ouer nie sal goedkeur nie. Dit word dikwels “tieneropstand” genoem.

Is “tieneropstand” altyd die ouer se skuld? Nee, maar as jy nie aktief betrokke is by die bou en instandhouding van ’n verhouding met jou tiener nie, sal dit waarskynlik gebeur. Dit is belangrik om daarop te let dat daar in elke mens se hart ’n rebel is. In my vorige artikel het ek die belangrikheid beklemtoon daarvan om daardie rebelse gees te konfronteer wanneer ons kinders jonk en ontvanklik is.

Hierdie rebelse gees sal nie ten volle oorwin word voordat dit deur ’n evangeliese bekering aan God oorgegee word nie. Slegs ’n werk van God se genade in die hart kan die ingebore opstand teen God en ouerlike gesag bedwing.

Ken die hart van jou kind en probeer om hom of haar tot liefdevolle onderwerping aan die Here Jesus Christus te lei. Slegs in ’n verhouding met Jesus Christus kan ons kinders hul ware en blywende identiteit vind. Ouerlike gesag het ’n plek daarin om ons kinders te vorm en te beheer wanneer hulle jonk is. Namate ons kinders volwassenheid bereik, besef ons dat ouerlike gesag beperkings het en dat ons kinders deur ’n invloed buite onsself beheer moet word.

Dit is nooit te laat om ’n brug van verbondenheid te bou nie. As jy voel dat jy in jou verhouding met jou kinders misluk het, is dit nooit te laat om hulle nader te roep en nederig te probeer herstel wat ontbreek nie. Selfs as jou kinders nie meer tuis woon nie, kan ek jou verseker dat hulle na ’n verhouding met Ma en Pa verlang.

Die bevestigingsfaktor

Elke tiener verlang daarna om deur hul ouers, veral hul vader, bevestig te word. Jy kan jou tiener bevestig deur na positiewe karaktereienskappe te soek en dit te erken. Daar is ’n plek vir teregwysende kritiek van ouer tot kind, maar kritiek wat verneder, is nie opbouend nie; dit is afbrekend. Vir elke kritiese opmerking behoort jy verskeie positiewe komplimente te hê. Met ander woorde, jy verdien die reg om te kritiseer wat verkeerd is deur dit wat reg is, te seën.

Jy kan jou tiener bevestig deur hom of haar met waardigheid en respek te behandel. Jy kan vra: “Hoe voel jy oor…?” Of: “Wat dink jy behoort ons te doen…?” Jy gee nie jou ouerlike verantwoordelikheid prys deur jou seun of dogter se mening te ondersoek nie. Jy help hulle eintlik om “in hul jeug groot te word” deur hulle te dwing om soos volwassenes te dink.

Jy kan jou tiener bevestig deur hom met gewone hoflikheid te behandel. Eenvoudige dinge soos “asseblief” en “dankie”, “ek is jammer”, “verskoon my”, “totsiens”, “geniet jou dag”, “ry veilig” en “God seën jou” spreek jou tiener se waarde en betekenis uit. As hierdie eenvoudige hoflikheidsvorme algemeen in jou huis voorkom, sal jou kinders dit aan jou terugbetoon. Dink aan hoe jy voel wanneer iemand vir jou sê: “O, verskoon my, ek is jammer.” Jy voel gerespekteer, gewaardeer en waardig. Dit is ’n eenvoudige geskenk wat elke ouer aan sy kind kan gee.

Jy kan jou tiener bevestig deur hom verantwoordelikheid toe te vertrou. Ek het op ’n melkplaas grootgeword. Ons het volop geleenthede gehad om karakter en vaardighede te ontwikkel. Ek onthou een dag toe ek 16 jaar oud was; my pa moes ’n muur van betonblokke in die skuur laat bou. Ek het aangebied om dit te doen. Pa het die blokke en sement voorsien en my aan die gang gehelp. Daarna was ek op my eie. Het ek ’n muur gebou wat professioneel gelyk het? Nee, maar ek was nogal trots op die resultaat, en daardie muur het baie jare gehou. Pa het my vertrou om ’n man se werk te doen, en ek het dit gedoen.

Bevestiging is nie vleiery nie. Vleiery is lof wat nie opreg is nie en dikwels nie waar is nie. Bevestiging is om die goeie wat jy in iemand anders sien, raak te sien en aan te moedig. Ek het volwasse mans teëgekom wat bitterlik gehuil het omdat hulle nooit bevestiging van hul vader ontvang het nie. Selfs Jesus het bevestiging van sy Vader ontvang toe sy Vader gesê het: “Dit is my geliefde Seun in wie Ek ’n welbehae het.”

(2) Verhouding met God

Ons eerste verantwoordelikheid in evangelisasie is teenoor ons kinders. As ons nie ons kinders kan evangeliseer nie, hoe kan ons verwag om ander vir die Here te wen? Ons het ’n besondere voordeel wanneer ons ons geloof aan ons kinders oordra, omdat ons saam met hulle woon. Hulle kan sien, en sien inderdaad, hoe ons geloof in die alledaagse lewe uitgeleef word. Dit behoort die mees oortuigende bewys van die geldigheid van ons geloof te wees.

Ongelukkig kan die manier waarop ouers hul geloof uitleef, of eerder versuim om dit uit te leef, ’n groot struikelblok vir hul kinders word. Ons kinders is besonder bewus van enige teenstrydigheid in ons Christelike belydenis.

Omgekeerd, as ons kinders sien dat God se krag in ons lewe duidelik is, as hulle sien hoe hul ouers geloof in God toon wat hulle deur moeilike tye dra, as hulle sien hoe hul ouers ’n rustige rus in die Here toon, en as Jesus Christus in die huis verheerlik en aanbid word, sal hulle oortuig word om hul ouers se God hul God te maak.

Die werklikheid van die evangelie wat in die daaglikse lewe uitgeleef word, is die mees oortuigende bewys van die geldigheid van ons geloof. Ons kinders behoort die eerste getuies te wees van die transformerende werk van die evangelie in ons harte.

Hoe lei ’n ouer sy kind tot redding? Redding is ’n werk van God; God gebruik egter menslike instrumente om sy werk te volbring. Ouers speel ’n groot rol daarin om hul kinders na Christus te lei. Wees bedag op tekens van oortuiging. As ’n kind stil en teruggetrokke, of prikkelbaar en rusteloos, of strydlustig en uitdagend is, kan dit wees dat die Gees van God in hul hart werk.

Hopelik het jy ’n verhouding gekoester wat jou in staat stel om hul hart te peil en hulle sagkens na Jesus te lei vir vergifnis en reiniging. Die bekering van die meeste van ons kinders is deur ’n ouer aan die gang gesit. Ons het tekens van oortuiging herken en hulle gelei tot berou en bekering, en om redding deur geloof in Christus te ontvang.

Die vroeë tienerjare is ’n ideale tyd vir ’n kind om sy/haar lewe aan Jesus oor te gee as hy dit nog nie gedoen het nie. Wanneer aktiewe opstand begin, maak ’n tiener dikwels keuses wat tot ’n pynlike oes en soms onomkeerbare gevolge lei. ’n Lewe van toegewyde diens aan God is die enigste lewe van seën en vervulling.

Verhouding met die kerk

Daar is nog ’n verhouding wat ’n tiener se lewe en oortuigings ingrypend beïnvloed: die plaaslike kerk. Ons verkry sowel ons identiteitsbesef as ons begrip van die werklikheid van die Christelike geloof deur ons ervaring van aanbidding en verhoudings binne die plaaslike kerk. Ná die ouer-kind-verhouding is dit die volgende belangrikste invloed in ’n tiener se lewe.

Dit is belangrik dat ons aanbid in ’n kerk wat die evangelie aanbied as ’n transformerende verhouding met God deur geloof in Jesus. Dit is ook belangrik dat ons kerklewe bestaan uit warm, liefdevolle verhoudings in ’n hegte gemeenskap.

Ek noem dit omdat sommige ouers die verkeerde idee het dat hulle al die geestelike leiding en verhoudings kan voorsien wat hul kinders nodig het. Dit lyk dalk of dit werk wanneer die kinders klein en naby is, maar namate ons kinders volwassenheid bereik, sal hulle ’n breër wêreld van verhoudings soek. Die plaaslike kerk en die gemeenskap van kerke waarmee dit verbonde is, bied hierdie breër grondslag vir gemeenskap.

Dit is belangrik om te aanbid in ’n kerk wat jy kan ondersteun en waarin jy jou kinders kan aanmoedig om betrokke te wees. Baie kinders het die geloof verloor omdat Ma en Pa nie die kerk ondersteun het waar hulle aanbid het nie. Dit is baie beter om aan te beweeg en ’n kerk te vind wat jy kan ondersteun as om in ’n kerk te bly en voortdurend daarteen gekant te wees.

Ek moedig nie kerkwisseling aan nie. Dit is vir kinders, veral jou tieners, belangrik dat daar stabiliteit in die kerklewe is. Vind ’n kerk waarby jy tuis voel, hopelik terwyl jou kinders nog jonk is, en bly daar. Daar is altyd praktiese uitsonderings, en jou kinders sal daarby aanpas, maar oor die algemeen lei ’n stabiele kerklewe tot jongmense met ’n sterk identiteitsbesef en doelgerigtheid.

Soos pyle in die hand van ’n held, so is die seuns van die jeug – Psalm 127:4. Hierdie vers herinner ons daaraan dat ons kinders ’n kragtige verdediging teen die vyand is. As hulle behoorlik geslyp (opgelei) en gebalanseer (dissiplines geleer) word, sal ons kinders die potensiaal hê om ons te oorleef, sowel in lewensjare as in bruikbaarheid. Wanneer jy die pyl loslaat, sal jou kinders plekke bereik, sowel deur die tyd as in die wêreld, wat jy nooit sal sien nie. Gelukkig is die man wat sy pylkoker vol daarvan het; hulle sal nie beskaamd staan nie, maar met die vyande spreek in die poort – Psalm 127:5.
