Many people ask, “Is listening to secular music a sin? Is there anything wrong with CCM (Christian Contemporary Music)? Is it okay for Christians to listen to rap, rock, country, pop, or rhythm and blues?” For the sake of this article, I am going to refer to all the music listed above as “secular” music.

Should Christians only listen to “A cappella” music? Music is compelling, and it can have a significant effect on how we live our lives. Music influences us negatively or positively. We should ask the question, “Does the music that I listen to draw me closer to God, or does it push me away from Him and closer to Satan?”

The primary purpose of music is to worship (the expression of reverence and adoration to something or someone). Yet at times we as believers still fail in listening to good wholesome music. This is a problem since most secular music is evil and promotes things that God hates.

Secular music is very catchy and addicting. The flesh would rather listen to secular music than to godly music. This type of music negatively influences the mind and is not profitable. If the song encourages evil, promotes worldliness, gives you bad thoughts, changes your actions for the wrong, and influences your speech for the wrong, we should not be listening to it. When it comes to music, we can comfortably lie to ourselves in this area. Have you lied to yourself? Have you said, “God is OK with this type of music,” yet deep down in your heart, you know He is convicting you, and that He is NOT OK with it?

Secular music is often sensual. The meaning of sensual is “of arousing gratification of the senses and physical.” Is the music that we listen to sensual? Does it put our mind in a state of just going with the beat? How do our bodies want to respond when we listen to such music? If our bodies swing with the rhythm of the music, it is not honoring to the Lord; it is not bringing glory to His name; it is not putting our mind and body in a position to worship the Lord.

We always worship something when we listen to music. If we are concentrating on music that is not of God, we are worshiping our flesh, the world, or even the devil. Usually, music like CCM tends to draw attention to ourselves and not to God. Music like this is very sensual. Can we truly worship God when we listen to this type of music?

CCM is a genre of modern popular music in which the lyrics are focused on matters concerned with the Christian faith. It formed as those affected by the 1960s’ “Jesus movement” revival began to express themselves with a more contemporary style of music. Before that, it was hymns and other gospel songs that were prevalent in the church at the time. Whether we know it or not, much of the CCM adds a pulsating beat (syncopation) at a place that it is not naturally supposed to be. The pulsating beat that is relevant in CCM does not appeal to the spirit of man in worship, rather, it appeals to the flesh. The type of music that appeals to the flesh is not of God but is of the devil. Today, CCM is a term that is used to refer to pop, rock, or praise & worship styles of rhythm and beat, so long as the lyrics fall under the definition of CCM.

Philippians tells us that we are supposed to think on … whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

Secular music does not pass the Philippians 4:8 test. Most secular music has lyrics that are impure, while all of it has a rhythm or beat that is against God’s order. The devil uses it all to influence people to sin or to think about sin. It will affect you in some way. Is the influence of the music that we listen to good or bad? For example, if we are concentrating on music that affects our thoughts or lifestyle in the wrong way, then it is a negative influence that we must put out of our lives.

The Hebrews started the tradition of using music without accompaniment after the fall of the second temple in 70 A.D., at which time instruments were not allowed during a period of mourning after the fall. Throughout history up until The Renaissance, instrumental music was mostly associated with dancing and merry making. As one could not have too much fun in places of worship, this kind of amusing music was not popular with religious leaders.

A cappella is an Italian phrase which means “in the style of the chapel”. It was initially used to refer to music that was sung in a chapel or small worship space without accompanying instruments, as opposed to a large church where an organ usually attended vocal music. The term has since come to mean any music sung without accompaniment, whether sacred (religious) or secular (non-religious). A cappella music can be sung by a large choir, a small group, or as a solo.

In Orthodox and Conservative Jewish congregations, the tradition of singing mostly A cappella still exists. In these synagogues, it is customary for a cantor to chant or sing an authoritative text from the scriptures which the congregation responds to in kind. The only instruments used might be a pitch pipe to give everyone a starting note or a ram’s horn on a special occasion or a holiday.

The early church developed the tradition of A cappella singing from the Hebrews’ Jewish tradition, chanting psalms, or other scriptures and using a cantor as a leader. Gregorian chant was the dominant form of church music starting around 590 A.D. It is a single, simple, melodic line half-spoken, half-sung in a free rhythmic style. In the early church, instrumental music was associated with the sinful outside world and was considered a negative influence.

The tradition of unaccompanied sacred vocal music continued during The Renaissance. Although instruments sometimes doubled or substituted for a vocal line, vocal music mostly stood on its own. The sound of a choir of voices in a chapel with excellent acoustics had a particularly ethereal effect.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was one of the most significant composers of The Renaissance in Italy, writing hundreds of masses and motets for the church. ‘The Palestrina Style,’ as it is called, was a sophisticated A cappella form using many voices singing with different music and text coming in at different times. This was called polyphonic, as opposed to homophonic, which means one melodic line sung together or in the same rhythm.

The Apostle Paul writes, Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; –Ephesians 5:19. Does that sound like making music with instruments? Or does it rather seem like singing praises to God from the heart?

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them –Acts 16:25. When Paul and Silas were in prison, and they were in stocks singing at midnight, I don’t believe that they were singing to bring glory to themselves. They were singing to bring glory to God the Father. The result of them giving God the glory is quite astounding. There was an earthquake, the foundations of the prison shook, the doors flew open, and everyone’s prison bands broke. At the end of this happening, the jailor came trembling before Paul and Silas and asked: “What must I do to be saved?”

Colossians also tells us that we should Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Do we let psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs teach us, admonish us, and encourage us?

I wonder what hymn Jesus sang with His disciples at the last supper before He went out to the Mount of Olives. I doubt that they were singing to themselves. I believe they were singing to their heavenly Father.

Pure and holy music is a blessing from the Lord. It is such a beautifully powerful thing that we should not take for granted. Sometimes God uses it to speak to us. I firmly believe that all Christians need to be listening to godly music throughout the week, not just on Sunday. It helps me stay calm, be encouraged, and keep my mind on the Lord. When my mind is on the Lord, I can go through the day blest.

We need to discipline ourselves with the things of God. We also need to get rid of things in our life that we know God is not pleased with. Godly music (music that draws our spirit and mind to the things that are from God) is the type of music that believers should listen to. Worship is what it boils down to, do we worship God or something else?

Jesus says, But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him –John 4:23.

So, let us sing in sincere worship to our Creator, let us give God the glory for the voices that He has given us, and let us sing and listen to godly, wholesome songs to our God.

M많은 사람이 이렇게 묻습니다. “세속 음악을 듣는 것은 죄인가요? CCM(크리스천 현대 음악)에 문제가 있나요? 그리스도인이 랩, 록, 컨트리, 팝, 리듬 앤 블루스를 들어도 괜찮나요?” 이 글에서는 앞서 나열한 모든 음악을 ‘세속’ 음악이라고 부르겠습니다.

그리스도인은 ‘아카펠라’ 음악만 들어야 할까요? 음악은 사람을 사로잡으며 우리가 살아가는 방식에 큰 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다. 음악은 우리에게 부정적으로든 긍정적으로든 영향을 줍니다. 우리는 “내가 듣는 음악은 나를 하나님께 더 가까이 이끄는가, 아니면 하나님에게서 멀어져 사탄에게 더 가까이 가게 하는가?”라고 물어야 합니다.

음악의 주된 목적은 예배하는 것입니다(어떤 것이나 누군가에게 경의와 찬양을 표현하는 것). 하지만 때때로 우리 믿는 사람들은 여전히 선하고 건전한 음악을 듣지 못합니다. 이는 문제입니다. 세속 음악의 대부분은 악하며 하나님께서 미워하시는 것들을 조장하기 때문입니다.

세속 음악은 매우 귀에 잘 들어오고 중독성이 있습니다. 육신은 경건한 음악보다 세속 음악을 듣고 싶어 합니다. 이런 종류의 음악은 마음에 부정적인 영향을 주며 유익하지 않습니다. 노래가 악을 부추기거나 세속적인 것을 조장하거나 나쁜 생각을 하게 하거나 행동을 그릇된 방향으로 바꾸거나 말을 잘못된 방향으로 이끈다면, 우리는 그것을 듣지 말아야 합니다. 음악에 관해서는 이 문제에서 스스로에게 거짓말을 쉽게 할 수 있습니다. 여러분은 스스로를 속인 적이 있습니까? “하나님께서는 이런 음악을 괜찮게 여기셔”라고 말하면서도, 마음 깊은 곳에서는 하나님께서 여러분의 양심을 찌르시며 그것을 괜찮게 여기지 않으신다는 것을 알고 있지는 않습니까?

세속 음악은 흔히 관능적입니다. 관능적이라는 말은 “감각과 육체에 만족을 불러일으키는 것”을 뜻합니다. 우리가 듣는 음악은 관능적입니까? 그 음악은 우리 마음을 그저 박자에 몸을 맡기는 상태로 만듭니까? 그런 음악을 들을 때 우리 몸은 어떻게 반응하고 싶어 합니까? 우리 몸이 음악의 리듬에 맞춰 흔들린다면, 그것은 주님께 영광을 돌리는 일이 아닙니다. 그분의 이름을 영화롭게 하지도 않으며, 우리의 마음과 몸을 주님께 예배드리는 자세로 두지도 않습니다.

음악을 들을 때 우리는 언제나 무엇인가를 예배합니다. 하나님께 속하지 않은 음악에 집중한다면, 우리는 우리의 육신이나 세상, 심지어 마귀를 예배하는 것입니다. 대개 CCM 같은 음악은 하나님이 아니라 우리 자신에게 주의를 돌리게 하는 경향이 있습니다. 이런 음악은 매우 관능적입니다. 이런 종류의 음악을 들으면서 참으로 하나님께 예배드릴 수 있습니까?

CCM은 가사가 기독교 신앙과 관련된 주제에 초점을 둔 현대 대중음악의 한 장르입니다. 1960년대 ‘예수 운동’ 부흥의 영향을 받은 사람들이 보다 현대적인 음악 형식으로 자신을 표현하기 시작하면서 형성되었습니다. 그 이전에는 당시 교회에서 찬송가와 다른 복음성가가 널리 불렸습니다. 우리가 알든 모르든, CCM의 많은 곡에는 원래 들어가서는 안 될 곳에 박동감 있는 비트(당김음)가 더해집니다. CCM에서 두드러지는 이 박동감 있는 비트는 예배하는 인간의 영에 호소하기보다 육신에 호소합니다. 육신에 호소하는 음악은 하나님께 속한 것이 아니라 마귀에게 속한 것입니다. 오늘날 CCM이라는 말은 가사가 CCM의 정의에 해당하기만 하면 팝, 록, 또는 찬양과 경배 스타일의 리듬과 비트를 가리키는 데 쓰입니다.

빌립보서는 우리가 … 무엇이든지 참되며, 무엇이든지 정직하며, 무엇이든지 의로우며, 무엇이든지 순결하며, 무엇이든지 사랑받을 만하며, 무엇이든지 칭찬할 만하며, 무슨 덕이 있든지 무슨 칭찬이 있든지 이것들을 생각하라 –빌립보서 4:8.고 말합니다.

세속 음악은 빌립보서 4:8의 기준을 통과하지 못합니다. 세속 음악의 대부분은 불순한 가사를 담고 있으며, 세속 음악은 모두 하나님의 질서에 어긋나는 리듬이나 박자를 지닙니다. 마귀는 그것을 모두 사용하여 사람들을 죄짓게 하거나 죄를 생각하게 합니다. 그것은 어떤 식으로든 여러분에게 영향을 미칠 것입니다. 우리가 듣는 음악의 영향은 좋은 것입니까, 나쁜 것입니까? 예를 들어, 우리의 생각이나 생활 방식을 그릇된 방향으로 이끄는 음악에 집중하고 있다면, 그것은 우리 삶에서 제거해야 할 부정적인 영향입니다.

히브리인들은 서기 70년 제2성전이 무너진 뒤 반주 없이 음악을 부르는 전통을 시작했습니다. 성전이 무너진 뒤 애도하는 기간에는 악기 사용이 허용되지 않았기 때문입니다. 역사적으로 르네상스 시대에 이르기까지 기악은 주로 춤과 잔치와 관련이 있었습니다. 예배 장소에서는 지나치게 즐길 수 없었으므로, 이런 오락성 음악은 종교 지도자들에게 인기가 없었습니다.

아카펠라는 “예배당 양식으로”라는 뜻의 이탈리아어 표현입니다. 처음에는 대형 교회에서 오르간이 보통 성악을 반주한 것과 달리, 예배당이나 작은 예배 공간에서 악기 반주 없이 부르는 음악을 가리키는 말로 쓰였습니다. 그 뒤 이 말은 종교적인 음악이든 세속적인 음악이든, 반주 없이 부르는 모든 음악을 뜻하게 되었습니다. 아카펠라 음악은 대규모 합창단이나 소규모 그룹이 부를 수도 있고, 독창으로 부를 수도 있습니다.

정교회 유대교와 보수파 유대교 회중에는 주로 아카펠라로 노래하는 전통이 지금도 남아 있습니다. 이런 회당에서는 선창자가 성경의 권위 있는 본문을 낭송하거나 노래하고 회중이 이에 화답하는 것이 관례입니다. 사용되는 악기는 모두가 시작 음을 잡도록 돕는 음고 파이프나 특별한 날 또는 명절에 쓰는 숫양의 뿔 나팔 정도일 수 있습니다.

초대 교회는 히브리인의 유대교 전통에서 아카펠라 노래를 받아들여, 시편이나 다른 성경을 낭송하고 선창자를 인도자로 세우는 전통을 발전시켰습니다. 그레고리오 성가는 서기 590년경부터 교회 음악의 지배적인 형식이었습니다. 이는 자유로운 리듬으로 반쯤 말하고 반쯤 노래하는, 하나의 단순한 선율선으로 이루어져 있습니다. 초대 교회에서는 기악이 죄 많은 외부 세계와 연관되어 부정적인 영향으로 여겨졌습니다.

반주 없는 종교 성악의 전통은 르네상스 시대에도 이어졌습니다. 악기가 때로는 성악 선율을 겹쳐 연주하거나 대신하기도 했지만, 성악은 대체로 독립적으로 이루어졌습니다. 음향이 뛰어난 예배당에서 울리는 합창단의 목소리는 특히 천상의 듯한 효과를 냈습니다.

조반니 피에를루이지 다 팔레스트리나는 이탈리아 르네상스 시대의 가장 중요한 작곡가 가운데 한 사람으로, 교회를 위해 수백 곡의 미사곡과 모테트를 썼습니다. ‘팔레스트리나 양식’이라 불리는 것은 여러 성부가 서로 다른 음악과 가사로 각기 다른 시점에 노래하는 세련된 아카펠라 형식이었습니다. 이는 다성음악이라 불렸으며, 하나의 선율선을 함께 또는 같은 리듬으로 노래하는 단성음악과 대조됩니다.

사도 바울은 이렇게 씁니다. 시와 찬송과 영적인 노래로 서로 말하고, 너희 마음으로 주님께 노래하며 찬송하라 –에베소서 5:19. 이것은 악기로 음악을 만드는 것처럼 들립니까? 아니면 마음으로 하나님께 찬양을 노래하는 것처럼 들립니까?

한밤중에 바울과 실라가 기도하고 하나님께 찬송을 부르니 죄수들이 들었더라 –사도행전 16:25. 바울과 실라가 감옥에 갇혀 차꼬에 채인 채 한밤중에 노래했을 때, 자신들에게 영광을 돌리려고 노래한 것은 아니라고 생각합니다. 하나님 아버지께 영광을 돌리려고 노래했습니다. 하나님께 영광을 돌린 결과는 참으로 놀라웠습니다. 지진이 일어나 감옥의 기초가 흔들리고 문들이 활짝 열렸으며, 모든 죄수의 결박이 풀렸습니다. 이 일이 일어난 뒤 간수가 떨며 바울과 실라 앞에 와서 물었습니다. “제가 구원을 받으려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?”

골로새서도 우리에게 이렇게 말합니다. 그리스도의 말씀이 너희 속에 풍성히 거하게 하여 모든 지혜로 서로 가르치고 권면하며, 시와 찬송과 영적인 노래를 부르고 너희 마음에 은혜로 주님께 노래하라 –골로새서 3:16. 우리는 시와 찬송과 영적인 노래가 우리를 가르치고 권면하며 격려하게 하고 있습니까?

예수님께서 감람산으로 나가시기 전 마지막 만찬에서 제자들과 어떤 찬송을 부르셨을지 궁금합니다. 그들이 자신들을 위해 노래했다고는 생각하지 않습니다. 하늘 아버지께 노래했다고 믿습니다.

순결하고 거룩한 음악은 주님께서 주시는 복입니다. 그것은 참으로 아름답고 능력 있는 것이므로 당연하게 여겨서는 안 됩니다. 때때로 하나님께서는 음악을 통해 우리에게 말씀하십니다. 저는 모든 그리스도인이 일요일만이 아니라 한 주 내내 경건한 음악을 들어야 한다고 굳게 믿습니다. 음악은 제가 평온을 유지하고, 격려를 얻으며, 마음을 주님께 두는 데 도움을 줍니다. 마음을 주님께 두면, 하루를 복되게 보낼 수 있습니다.

우리는 하나님의 일들로 자신을 훈련해야 합니다. 또한 하나님께서 기뻐하지 않으신다는 것을 아는 것들을 삶에서 없애야 합니다. 경건한 음악, 곧 우리의 영과 마음을 하나님께 속한 것들로 향하게 하는 음악은 믿는 사람들이 들어야 할 음악입니다. 결국 핵심은 예배입니다. 우리는 하나님을 예배합니까, 아니면 다른 무엇을 예배합니까?

예수님께서는 말씀하십니다. 그러나 참되게 예배하는 자들이 영과 진리로 아버지께 예배할 때가 오나니 곧 지금이라. 아버지께서는 자기에게 이렇게 예배하는 자들을 찾으시느니라 –요한복음 4:23.

그러므로 창조주께 진실한 예배로 노래합시다. 하나님께서 우리에게 주신 목소리로 하나님께 영광을 돌립시다. 하나님께 경건하고 건전한 노래를 부르고, 그런 노래를 들읍시다.

A verse that has always caught my attention, one that has caused my spine to tingle is found in Matthew chapter seven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? –Matthew 7:22.

Jesus gives us a picture of a large group of people standing before Him on Judgment Day. They thought they lived their lives for Him. They were gifted people—prophesying, casting out devils, and doing many wonderful things in the name of Jesus—they seemed like good Christians. However, in the next verse we read that Jesus will say to them that He never knew them. Jesus even tells them to depart from Him. He sends them to hell, forever.

I remember an account that reminds me of these verses. Years ago, I was working for a steel joist company. It was a normal Friday morning, we were working hard, as was required of each of us. The line boss came out and announced a meeting with the whole plant after the shift was over. We all wondered what the meeting was about. We asked around but it seemed that no one knew. After the shift, we all stood in a large circle and waited for the boss. He soon entered the room with another man. It was the manager of the whole company. Prior to these men coming in, we were all talking casually with each other, there was laughter and loud voices. The boss had a large stack of envelopes, and I heard a buzz go around about bonus checks. Everyone looked excited, except for the boss.

Then the boss started talking, “We have been watching all of you very closely over the past four weeks. We have been looking at your work ethic, how hard you try, and whether you’re on time. We have been looking at many different areas. Your supervisors will give each of you an envelope with your name on it. Do not open this letter until you are off the premises. When you do open it, you will find some instructions. For most, it will say to return to work at the normal time on Monday. But for 27 of you, it will say that you are fired. For those included in that number, we did not like what we saw during our time of evaluation, so we decided that we need to release you from your employment here.”

You could hear a pin drop. Fear was seen on every face. I remember wishing I had worked harder, been more involved. I regretted taking my job for granted. It was a terrible feeling, I had worked there for years, but did that matter?

I wasn’t fired that day, but 27 others were. They thought they had done enough. They thought they were safe since they had put in their time. But they were wrong, and now nothing could be done. It was over.

What about us? Do we gauge our walk with God based on eternity? Do we wonder what will happen on the day of judgement? How can we know?

Jesus says a few verses earlier that we will know each other by our fruits. There is much talk in the Word of God about fruit. We know what type of tree one is, by examining its fruit. When we first moved to Haiti, we didn’t know what kinds of trees were there. I remember looking up at a large tree on our property and wondering what kind it was. Then something gave it away. There were small avocados hanging from its branches. In the church today, it seems that people do not want to talk about this. But I assure you that we should talk about it before it is forever too late. Looking back, we would have loved to talk about this at the factory before that day when some of the employees were fired.

So, what is the fruit of a Christian? We know that being a good person and dressing in a certain way are not determining factors of a godly life. It is not the church we attend, the family we were born into, our culture, or the color of our skin. Many would agree that these things are not what identifies us as Christians. Some may think that the fruit of a Christian is being a good, morally upright, and loving citizen of society. There are many people who are law-abiding citizens, loving and peaceful, taking care of their own needs and the needs of others. Yet it is still possible for them to do all these good things and still go to hell.

We hear the world (and some in the church) proclaiming loudly that it’s only the heart that matters. We know they are saying this so they can excuse the lack of visible fruit. Even though their outside is bad, they want people to think that their heart is good, and that that’s all that really matters.

They are correct about the heart being important. You can’t change or fix anything simply by putting on a form when the heart is still selfish and wicked. However, they are wrong about the heart being good and the outside being bad. This is impossible. Jesus says, Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:26.

You cannot have a clean heart and a sinful appearance. However, on the flip side, you can have a clean appearance and yet still have an ungodly heart. So how do we tell? What is this fruit that Jesus is talking about?

We will talk about the fruit of the Spirit shortly, but first I would like to talk about something else that I believe defines a Christian. Something that can separate the sheep from the wolves, even if they both appear to be the same.

A desire to serve Jesus. When God converts a person’s soul, that individual is a new creature, and desires to serve God with his whole being. That person does not need to be forced to do what pleases God. There is much talk today in the church about structure and rules, however, this was not always the case. So why is this such a big issue today? Maybe there are unconverted people in the church. Perhaps people are too independent and do not want to be told what to do. You can tell a church member to dress modestly, but if their heart is not changed, you will face problems. They will try to be as worldly as they can, and still be within the ‘law’ of the church. Or they will simply refuse to do it and the church soon gives in and no longer requires their people to dress and live modestly. Should the church need to force its people to be modest? Should the church need to force its people to be Christ-like? Absolutely not. When a soul has been redeemed and transformed by the blood of Christ, that person, in return, will, because of his changed nature, live a sacrificial life for Him. We obey His commandments with grateful hearts!

For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous –1 John 5:3.

A heart that has not been made new by God’s Spirit will not passionately desire to live for God. One can religiously go to church—many unbelievers attend church services regularly. One can dress right and act right, but if their heart does not pant after the things of God, these things will have no profit. Much of what they do is to receive the praise of men, not the glory of God. It is no wonder that many churches of today are accepting drift.

It is a beautiful thing to see someone truly desire to live for God. They desire to seek the face of their Creator, their Savior. They live for the Kingdom, for the brotherhood. To obey God and serve Him is a necessity; it is the only thing that really matters to them. Their ‘all’ truly is on the altar. They love reading the Word and spending time alone with God. Their desires and their will have been sacrificed on the altar of their God.

People have told me that we need to give a new Christian some room. “Some room for what?” I ask. Some room for sin… for carnality? Absolutely not. Every example in the Bible says differently. Every conversion brought a tremendous change, a new creature. Many people confuse ‘grace to learn and to grow’ in the faith as an ‘excuse for sin’. The Scriptures define new Christians… As newborn babes, and commands each of us to desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby: –1 Peter 2:2. So new Christians don’t need space to continue for a time in their ungodly ways, but they do need space to grow …in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man –Luke 2:52.

When someone comes declaring they have been converted, it is easy to find out. We simply go over some scriptures that explain practical, foundational doctrines like non-conformity, non-resistance, and such like. Some see it as God’s Word and soak it in. Many folks sit in astonishment as I read such verses to them—Scripture verses they have never heard before. Usually they simply believe what they just heard from God’s word, and it changes them. That is a Christian who wants to be taught, who wants to be discipled. They tend to come with a teachable attitude asking questions about that which they have read in God’s Word and don’t understand.

But what about so many others? They hear the same scriptures and they argue—they argue with the Bible and the person sharing the Scripture with them, but ultimately, they are arguing with God. They will usually admit that it’s what the Bible says but they want to know why it says that. They are not wanting to change their life for God. They want to be a Christian, yes, but they also want to live how they want. They do not desire to obey God. We can continue working with them, but it is clear: their heart pants after the things of the world and the pleasures of this life.

Picture with me a man living 1,000 years ago. He is locked in a dungeon, where everything is as black as coal. It is musty and stinks. He has been arrested for preaching the gospel. His ankles and wrists are raw and bloody from the large, heavy chains that keep him bound in the tiny cell. He’s claustrophobic, weary, and worn. His back is bloody. His aching limbs have been stretched to the breaking point. He talks to God, but God does not answer. He pleads for deliverance but hears nothing in return. He thinks back on his life, his faith. Then he wonders the dreaded thought: “God, are you there? Are you real?” Silence. His faith is being tried to the extreme. He knows that if he continues to hold to his beliefs, a fire awaits him. Why? Why die for a God that allows him to go through this agony? Why die for a God that will not speak? “My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me?”

Now picture this man… is you.

Do we really believe in God, a God who’s not seen and often not heard? If our faith does not exist, then God will not exist when we really need Him.

God wants us to put all our faith in Him, all the time. We walk by faith, NOT by sight… even when things are going well. When we find ourselves in terrible times, God is still near, leading us and giving us courage to go on! We are used to simply trusting in Him, in His word.

For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry? –Luke 23:31.

God loves a heart that is turned toward Him, fully yielded, and surrendered. He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him!

Do we have the fruit of the Spirit of God? Do we act like Christians? Do we look like Christians?

I was asked to preach for a large church that I had never been to before. I went with my family and sat while the seats filled up with hundreds of people. I was amazed at how these people were dressed. There were short miniskirts and skimpy tops, much worldly fashion and style. The service began and I realized quickly that this was not a good place for my family, so I took them home and returned by myself. The rock music was still going, and the dancing was pushing my limits. After two hours it was time for the message. I stood and told the large crowd that I was the new President of America. Laughter filled the auditorium. I then asked them if they believed me. “No!” they shouted. I asked why they didn’t believe me, and they responded with different answers. One yelled, “You don’t look or dress like the president!” Another said, “You wouldn’t be here if you were the president!” Yet another said that I didn’t sound like the president. I told them that I didn’t understand. I asked how they can say that they are Christians—They don’t look like it! They don’t act like it! They don’t sound like it!—Yet everyone believes them!

It seems that we judge everything by its fruit, except for Christians. For Christians we are expected to judge by what they claim. This world thinks they can simply imagine what Jesus wants and then please Him in any way they personally choose. However, the Bible is clear: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them –Matthew 7:16-20.

The Bible says that …the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance… –Galatians 5:22-23. Are these the things that people see when they look at you and I? I know it is easy to justify not having one or more of these fruits by saying, “I’m working on it,” or “I’m praying about it.” Jesus does not say that this fruit is something that Christians should work to attain. He simply says that these are the fruits, or product, of the indwelling Spirit of God. If we pursue worldly ambitions, or if we desire to fit in with the world, we cannot expect this fruit to be evident in our lives. I believe this is the fruit of a suffering man, a person that has been giving his all, and desires to give his all to the Lamb that was slain.

Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire –Matthew 7:19.

When we give something our all, whether it’s our work, our school, or raising a family, it feels good—it is fulfilling. When we serve God with all our being, the same is true. There is a very rewarding feeling, a feeling of peace that passes all understanding.

Um versículo que sempre chamou minha atenção, que me fez sentir um arrepio na espinha, encontra-se no capítulo sete de Mateus. Muitos me dirão naquele dia: Senhor, Senhor, não profetizamos nós em teu nome? E em teu nome não expulsamos demônios? E em teu nome não fizemos muitas maravilhas? –Mateus 7:22.

Jesus nos apresenta a imagem de um grande grupo de pessoas diante dele no Dia do Juízo. Elas pensavam que viviam para ele. Eram pessoas dotadas de dons — profetizavam, expulsavam demônios e faziam muitas coisas maravilhosas em nome de Jesus — pareciam bons cristãos. No entanto, no versículo seguinte, lemos que Jesus lhes dirá que nunca as conheceu. Jesus chega a dizer-lhes que se afastem dele. Ele as envia para o inferno, para sempre.

Lembro-me de um episódio que me faz pensar nesses versículos. Anos atrás, eu trabalhava em uma empresa de vigas de aço. Era uma manhã de sexta-feira comum; trabalhávamos arduamente, como era exigido de cada um de nós. O chefe da linha veio e anunciou uma reunião com toda a fábrica depois do fim do turno. Todos nos perguntávamos do que se tratava a reunião. Perguntamos por aí, mas parecia que ninguém sabia. Depois do turno, todos ficamos em um grande círculo, esperando o chefe. Logo ele entrou na sala com outro homem. Era o gerente de toda a empresa. Antes de esses homens entrarem, conversávamos descontraidamente; havia risadas e vozes altas. O chefe tinha uma grande pilha de envelopes, e ouvi um burburinho sobre cheques de bônus. Todos pareciam empolgados, menos o chefe.

Então o chefe começou a falar: “Temos observado todos vocês muito de perto nas últimas quatro semanas. Temos avaliado sua ética de trabalho, o quanto se esforçam e se chegam no horário. Observamos muitos aspectos diferentes. Seus supervisores entregarão a cada um de vocês um envelope com seu nome. Não abram esta carta até saírem das instalações. Quando a abrirem, encontrarão algumas instruções. Para a maioria, estará escrito que devem voltar ao trabalho no horário normal na segunda-feira. Mas, para 27 de vocês, estará escrito que foram demitidos. Quanto aos que fazem parte desse número, não gostamos do que vimos durante o período de avaliação e, por isso, decidimos que precisamos dispensá-los do emprego aqui.”

Era possível ouvir um alfinete cair. O medo estava estampado em todos os rostos. Lembro-me de desejar ter trabalhado mais, ter me envolvido mais. Arrependi-me de ter dado meu emprego como garantido. Era uma sensação terrível; eu trabalhava ali havia anos, mas será que isso importava?

Não fui demitido naquele dia, mas outras 27 pessoas foram. Elas achavam que tinham feito o suficiente. Pensavam que estavam seguras por terem cumprido seu tempo de serviço. Mas estavam erradas, e agora nada podia ser feito. Tudo tinha acabado.

E quanto a nós? Avaliamos nossa caminhada com Deus à luz da eternidade? Perguntamo-nos o que acontecerá no dia do juízo? Como podemos saber?

Jesus diz, alguns versículos antes, que conheceremos uns aos outros pelos frutos. A Palavra de Deus fala muito sobre frutos. Sabemos que tipo de árvore é uma ao examinar seus frutos. Quando nos mudamos para o Haiti, não sabíamos que tipos de árvores havia ali. Lembro-me de olhar para uma árvore grande em nossa propriedade e me perguntar de que tipo era. Então algo a identificou. Havia pequenos abacates pendurados em seus galhos. Hoje, na igreja, parece que as pessoas não querem falar sobre isso. Mas garanto que devemos falar sobre isso antes que seja tarde demais para sempre. Olhando para trás, gostaríamos muito de ter conversado sobre isso na fábrica antes daquele dia em que alguns funcionários foram demitidos.

Então, qual é o fruto de um cristão? Sabemos que ser uma boa pessoa e vestir-se de determinada maneira não são fatores que determinam uma vida piedosa. Não é a igreja que frequentamos, a família em que nascemos, nossa cultura ou a cor da nossa pele. Muitos concordariam que essas coisas não são o que nos identifica como cristãos. Alguns podem pensar que o fruto de um cristão é ser um bom cidadão da sociedade, moralmente correto e amoroso. Há muitas pessoas que respeitam as leis, são amorosas e pacíficas e cuidam das próprias necessidades e das necessidades dos outros. Ainda assim, é possível que façam todas essas coisas boas e acabem no inferno.

Ouvimos o mundo (e alguns na igreja) proclamar em voz alta que só o coração importa. Sabemos que dizem isso para poder justificar a falta de frutos visíveis. Embora sua aparência exterior seja ruim, querem que as pessoas pensem que seu coração é bom e que isso é tudo o que realmente importa.

Estão certos ao dizer que o coração é importante. Não se pode mudar ou consertar nada simplesmente assumindo uma aparência, quando o coração continua egoísta e perverso. No entanto, estão errados ao dizer que o coração é bom e a aparência exterior é ruim. Isso é impossível. Jesus diz: Fariseu cego, limpa primeiro o interior do copo e do prato, para que também o exterior fique limpo –Mateus 23:26.

Não se pode ter um coração limpo e uma aparência pecaminosa. No entanto, por outro lado, é possível ter uma aparência limpa e ainda assim um coração ímpio. Então, como podemos distinguir? Qual é esse fruto de que Jesus está falando?

Falaremos em breve sobre o fruto do Espírito, mas primeiro gostaria de falar sobre outra coisa que acredito definir um cristão. Algo que pode separar as ovelhas dos lobos, mesmo que ambos pareçam iguais.

O desejo de servir a Jesus. Quando Deus converte a alma de uma pessoa, essa pessoa se torna uma nova criatura e deseja servir a Deus com todo o seu ser. Não é preciso forçá-la a fazer o que agrada a Deus. Hoje se fala muito na igreja sobre estrutura e regras; no entanto, nem sempre foi assim. Então, por que isso é uma questão tão importante hoje? Talvez haja pessoas não convertidas na igreja. Talvez as pessoas sejam independentes demais e não queiram que lhes digam o que fazer. Pode-se dizer a um membro da igreja que se vista com modéstia, mas, se seu coração não for transformado, haverá problemas. Ele tentará ser o mais mundano possível e ainda assim permanecer dentro da “lei” da igreja. Ou simplesmente se recusará a fazê-lo, e logo a igreja cederá e deixará de exigir que seus membros se vistam e vivam com modéstia. A igreja deveria precisar forçar seus membros a serem modestos? A igreja deveria precisar forçá-los a ser semelhantes a Cristo? De modo algum. Quando uma alma é redimida e transformada pelo sangue de Cristo, essa pessoa, por sua vez, viverá uma vida de sacrifício por ele, devido à sua natureza transformada. Obedecemos aos seus mandamentos com corações agradecidos!

Porque este é o amor de Deus: que guardemos os seus mandamentos; e os seus mandamentos não são pesados –1 João 5:3.

Um coração que não foi renovado pelo Espírito de Deus não desejará ardentemente viver para Deus. Alguém pode ir à igreja por hábito religioso — muitos incrédulos frequentam regularmente os cultos. Alguém pode se vestir e se comportar corretamente, mas, se seu coração não anseia pelas coisas de Deus, essas coisas não terão proveito algum. Muito do que fazem é para receber o louvor dos homens, e não a glória de Deus. Não é de admirar que muitas igrejas de hoje aceitem o desvio.

É uma coisa linda ver alguém que realmente deseja viver para Deus. Essa pessoa deseja buscar a face de seu Criador, seu Salvador. Vive pelo Reino, pela irmandade. Obedecer a Deus e servi-lo é uma necessidade; é a única coisa que realmente importa para ela. Seu “tudo” está verdadeiramente no altar. Ela ama ler a Palavra e passar tempo a sós com Deus. Seus desejos e sua vontade foram sacrificados no altar de seu Deus.

Já me disseram que precisamos dar um pouco de espaço ao novo cristão. “Espaço para quê?”, pergunto. Espaço para pecar… para a carnalidade? De modo algum. Todos os exemplos na Bíblia dizem o contrário. Cada conversão trouxe uma mudança tremenda, uma nova criatura. Muitos confundem “graça para aprender e crescer” na fé com uma “desculpa para pecar”. As Escrituras descrevem os novos cristãos como recém-nascidos e ordenam que cada um de nós deseje o leite genuíno da palavra, para que por ele cresça: –1 Pedro 2:2. Portanto, os novos cristãos não precisam de espaço para continuar por algum tempo em seus caminhos ímpios, mas precisam de espaço para crescer …em sabedoria e estatura, e em graça diante de Deus e dos homens –Lucas 2:52.

Quando alguém aparece declarando que foi convertido, é fácil descobrir. Simplesmente analisamos algumas passagens que explicam doutrinas práticas e fundamentais, como a não conformidade, a não resistência e outras semelhantes. Alguns reconhecem que é a Palavra de Deus e absorvem o que ela diz. Muitas pessoas ficam espantadas enquanto leio para elas versículos assim — passagens das Escrituras que nunca tinham ouvido antes. Em geral, simplesmente creem no que acabaram de ouvir da Palavra de Deus, e isso as transforma. Esse é um cristão que quer ser ensinado, que quer ser discipulado. Essas pessoas costumam vir com uma atitude receptiva ao ensino, fazendo perguntas sobre aquilo que leram na Palavra de Deus e não entenderam.

Mas e tantos outros? Ouvem as mesmas passagens e discutem — discutem com a Bíblia e com a pessoa que compartilha as Escrituras com eles, mas, no fim das contas, estão discutindo com Deus. Em geral, admitem que é isso o que a Bíblia diz, mas querem saber por que ela diz isso. Não querem mudar de vida para Deus. Querem ser cristãos, sim, mas também querem viver como bem entendem. Não desejam obedecer a Deus. Podemos continuar trabalhando com eles, mas é evidente: seu coração anseia pelas coisas do mundo e pelos prazeres desta vida.

Imagine comigo um homem que viveu há 1.000 anos. Ele está trancado em uma masmorra, onde tudo é negro como carvão. O ar é mofado e fedorento. Ele foi preso por pregar o evangelho. Seus tornozelos e pulsos estão em carne viva e ensanguentados por causa das grandes e pesadas correntes que o mantêm preso na minúscula cela. Ele é claustrofóbico, está exausto e abatido. Suas costas estão ensanguentadas. Seus membros doloridos foram esticados até quase se romperem. Ele fala com Deus, mas Deus não responde. Implora por libertação, mas não recebe resposta. Pensa em sua vida, em sua fé. Então lhe ocorre o pensamento terrível: “Deus, estás aí? És real?” Silêncio. Sua fé está sendo provada ao extremo. Ele sabe que, se continuar firme em suas convicções, uma fogueira o espera. Por quê? Por que morrer por um Deus que permite que ele passe por essa agonia? Por que morrer por um Deus que não fala? “Deus meu, Deus meu, por que me desamparaste?”

Agora imagine esse homem… esse homem é você.

Será que realmente cremos em Deus, um Deus que não é visto e muitas vezes não é ouvido? Se nossa fé não existir, então Deus não existirá quando realmente precisarmos dele.

Deus quer que depositemos toda a nossa fé nele, o tempo todo. Andamos pela fé, NÃO pelo que vemos… mesmo quando as coisas vão bem. Quando nos encontramos em tempos terríveis, Deus continua perto, guiando-nos e dando-nos coragem para seguir em frente! Estamos acostumados simplesmente a confiar nele, em sua palavra.

Pois, se fazem estas coisas com a árvore verde, o que acontecerá com a seca? –Lucas 23:31.

Deus ama um coração voltado para ele, plenamente dedicado e rendido. Ele é galardoador dos que diligentemente o buscam!

Temos o fruto do Espírito de Deus? Agimos como cristãos? Parecemos cristãos?

Pediriam-me que pregasse em uma grande igreja onde eu nunca tinha estado. Fui com minha família e me sentei enquanto os assentos se enchiam de centenas de pessoas. Fiquei espantado com a maneira como aquelas pessoas se vestiam. Havia minissaias curtas e blusas muito reveladoras, muita moda e estilo mundanos. O culto começou e logo percebi que aquele não era um bom lugar para minha família, então levei-os para casa e voltei sozinho. A música rock continuava tocando, e a dança estava testando meus limites. Depois de duas horas, chegou a hora da mensagem. Levantei-me e disse à multidão que eu era o novo presidente dos Estados Unidos. Risadas encheram o auditório. Então perguntei se acreditavam em mim. “Não!”, gritaram. Perguntei por que não acreditavam, e responderam com diferentes motivos. Alguém gritou: “Você não parece nem se veste como o presidente!” Outra pessoa disse: “Se você fosse o presidente, não estaria aqui!” Outra ainda disse que eu não falava como o presidente. Disse-lhes que não entendia. Perguntei como podiam dizer que eram cristãos — não pareciam cristãos! Não agiam como cristãos! Não falavam como cristãos! — e, ainda assim, todos acreditavam neles!

Parece que julgamos tudo pelos seus frutos, exceto os cristãos. Quanto aos cristãos, espera-se que julguemos pelo que afirmam ser. Este mundo pensa que pode simplesmente imaginar o que Jesus quer e, depois, agradá-lo da maneira que cada um escolher. No entanto, a Bíblia é clara: Pelos seus frutos os conhecereis. Colhem-se uvas dos espinheiros, ou figos dos abrolhos? Assim, toda árvore boa produz bons frutos; porém a árvore corrupta produz frutos maus. Uma árvore boa não pode produzir frutos maus, nem uma árvore corrupta pode produzir bons frutos. Toda árvore que não produz bons frutos é cortada e lançada no fogo. Portanto, pelos seus frutos os conhecereis –Mateus 7:16-20.

A Bíblia diz que …o fruto do Espírito é amor, alegria, paz, longanimidade, benignidade, bondade, fé, mansidão, domínio próprio… –Gálatas 5:22-23. São essas as coisas que as pessoas veem quando olham para você e para mim? Sei que é fácil justificar a falta de um ou mais desses frutos dizendo: “Estou trabalhando nisso” ou “Estou orando por isso”. Jesus não diz que esse fruto é algo que os cristãos devem se esforçar para alcançar. Ele simplesmente diz que esses são os frutos, ou o produto, do Espírito de Deus que habita em nós. Se buscarmos ambições mundanas ou desejarmos nos encaixar no mundo, não podemos esperar que esse fruto seja evidente em nossa vida. Creio que esse é o fruto de um homem que sofre, de alguém que deu tudo de si e deseja dar tudo de si ao Cordeiro que foi morto.

Toda árvore que não produz bons frutos é cortada e lançada no fogo –Mateus 7:19.

Quando nos dedicamos inteiramente a algo, seja ao trabalho, aos estudos ou à criação de uma família, isso nos faz bem — é gratificante. O mesmo acontece quando servimos a Deus com todo o nosso ser. Há uma sensação muito gratificante, uma paz que excede todo o entendimento.

Many people ask, “Is listening to secular music a sin? Is there anything wrong with CCM (Christian Contemporary Music)? Is it okay for Christians to listen to rap, rock, country, pop, or rhythm and blues?” For the sake of this article, I am going to refer to all the music listed above as “secular” music.

Should Christians only listen to “A cappella” music? Music is compelling, and it can have a significant effect on how we live our lives. Music influences us negatively or positively. We should ask the question, “Does the music that I listen to draw me closer to God, or does it push me away from Him and closer to Satan?”

The primary purpose of music is to worship (the expression of reverence and adoration to something or someone). Yet at times we as believers still fail in listening to good wholesome music. This is a problem since most secular music is evil and promotes things that God hates.

Secular music is very catchy and addicting. The flesh would rather listen to secular music than to godly music. This type of music negatively influences the mind and is not profitable. If the song encourages evil, promotes worldliness, gives you bad thoughts, changes your actions for the wrong, and influences your speech for the wrong, we should not be listening to it. When it comes to music, we can comfortably lie to ourselves in this area. Have you lied to yourself? Have you said, “God is OK with this type of music,” yet deep down in your heart, you know He is convicting you, and that He is NOT OK with it?

Secular music is often sensual. The meaning of sensual is “of arousing gratification of the senses and physical.” Is the music that we listen to sensual? Does it put our mind in a state of just going with the beat? How do our bodies want to respond when we listen to such music? If our bodies swing with the rhythm of the music, it is not honoring to the Lord; it is not bringing glory to His name; it is not putting our mind and body in a position to worship the Lord.

We always worship something when we listen to music. If we are concentrating on music that is not of God, we are worshiping our flesh, the world, or even the devil. Usually, music like CCM tends to draw attention to ourselves and not to God. Music like this is very sensual. Can we truly worship God when we listen to this type of music?

CCM is a genre of modern popular music in which the lyrics are focused on matters concerned with the Christian faith. It formed as those affected by the 1960s’ “Jesus movement” revival began to express themselves with a more contemporary style of music. Before that, it was hymns and other gospel songs that were prevalent in the church at the time. Whether we know it or not, much of the CCM adds a pulsating beat (syncopation) at a place that it is not naturally supposed to be. The pulsating beat that is relevant in CCM does not appeal to the spirit of man in worship, rather, it appeals to the flesh. The type of music that appeals to the flesh is not of God but is of the devil. Today, CCM is a term that is used to refer to pop, rock, or praise & worship styles of rhythm and beat, so long as the lyrics fall under the definition of CCM.

Philippians tells us that we are supposed to think on … whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

Secular music does not pass the Philippians 4:8 test. Most secular music has lyrics that are impure, while all of it has a rhythm or beat that is against God’s order. The devil uses it all to influence people to sin or to think about sin. It will affect you in some way. Is the influence of the music that we listen to good or bad? For example, if we are concentrating on music that affects our thoughts or lifestyle in the wrong way, then it is a negative influence that we must put out of our lives.

The Hebrews started the tradition of using music without accompaniment after the fall of the second temple in 70 A.D., at which time instruments were not allowed during a period of mourning after the fall. Throughout history up until The Renaissance, instrumental music was mostly associated with dancing and merry making. As one could not have too much fun in places of worship, this kind of amusing music was not popular with religious leaders.

A cappella is an Italian phrase which means “in the style of the chapel”. It was initially used to refer to music that was sung in a chapel or small worship space without accompanying instruments, as opposed to a large church where an organ usually attended vocal music. The term has since come to mean any music sung without accompaniment, whether sacred (religious) or secular (non-religious). A cappella music can be sung by a large choir, a small group, or as a solo.

In Orthodox and Conservative Jewish congregations, the tradition of singing mostly A cappella still exists. In these synagogues, it is customary for a cantor to chant or sing an authoritative text from the scriptures which the congregation responds to in kind. The only instruments used might be a pitch pipe to give everyone a starting note or a ram’s horn on a special occasion or a holiday.

The early church developed the tradition of A cappella singing from the Hebrews’ Jewish tradition, chanting psalms, or other scriptures and using a cantor as a leader. Gregorian chant was the dominant form of church music starting around 590 A.D. It is a single, simple, melodic line half-spoken, half-sung in a free rhythmic style. In the early church, instrumental music was associated with the sinful outside world and was considered a negative influence.

The tradition of unaccompanied sacred vocal music continued during The Renaissance. Although instruments sometimes doubled or substituted for a vocal line, vocal music mostly stood on its own. The sound of a choir of voices in a chapel with excellent acoustics had a particularly ethereal effect.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was one of the most significant composers of The Renaissance in Italy, writing hundreds of masses and motets for the church. ‘The Palestrina Style,’ as it is called, was a sophisticated A cappella form using many voices singing with different music and text coming in at different times. This was called polyphonic, as opposed to homophonic, which means one melodic line sung together or in the same rhythm.

The Apostle Paul writes, Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; –Ephesians 5:19. Does that sound like making music with instruments? Or does it rather seem like singing praises to God from the heart?

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them –Acts 16:25. When Paul and Silas were in prison, and they were in stocks singing at midnight, I don’t believe that they were singing to bring glory to themselves. They were singing to bring glory to God the Father. The result of them giving God the glory is quite astounding. There was an earthquake, the foundations of the prison shook, the doors flew open, and everyone’s prison bands broke. At the end of this happening, the jailor came trembling before Paul and Silas and asked: “What must I do to be saved?”

Colossians also tells us that we should Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Do we let psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs teach us, admonish us, and encourage us?

I wonder what hymn Jesus sang with His disciples at the last supper before He went out to the Mount of Olives. I doubt that they were singing to themselves. I believe they were singing to their heavenly Father.

Pure and holy music is a blessing from the Lord. It is such a beautifully powerful thing that we should not take for granted. Sometimes God uses it to speak to us. I firmly believe that all Christians need to be listening to godly music throughout the week, not just on Sunday. It helps me stay calm, be encouraged, and keep my mind on the Lord. When my mind is on the Lord, I can go through the day blest.

We need to discipline ourselves with the things of God. We also need to get rid of things in our life that we know God is not pleased with. Godly music (music that draws our spirit and mind to the things that are from God) is the type of music that believers should listen to. Worship is what it boils down to, do we worship God or something else?

Jesus says, But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him –John 4:23.

So, let us sing in sincere worship to our Creator, let us give God the glory for the voices that He has given us, and let us sing and listen to godly, wholesome songs to our God.

Muchas personas preguntan: «¿Escuchar música secular es pecado? ¿Hay algo de malo en la música cristiana contemporánea (CCM)? ¿Está bien que los cristianos escuchen rap, rock, música country, pop o rhythm and blues?». Para los fines de este artículo, me referiré a toda la música mencionada arriba como música «secular».

¿Deberían los cristianos escuchar únicamente música «a capela»? La música es poderosa y puede tener un efecto significativo en la manera en que vivimos. La música nos influye de forma negativa o positiva. Deberíamos preguntarnos: «¿La música que escucho me acerca más a Dios o me aleja de Él y me acerca más a Satanás?».

El propósito principal de la música es adorar (expresar reverencia y adoración a algo o a alguien). Sin embargo, a veces nosotros, como creyentes, seguimos fallando al escuchar música buena y sana. Esto es un problema, ya que la mayor parte de la música secular es malvada y promueve cosas que Dios aborrece.

La música secular es muy pegadiza y adictiva. La carne preferiría escuchar música secular antes que música piadosa. Este tipo de música influye negativamente en la mente y no es provechosa. Si una canción fomenta el mal, promueve la mundanalidad, te inspira malos pensamientos, cambia tus acciones para mal e influye negativamente en tu manera de hablar, no deberíamos escucharla. Cuando se trata de música, podemos mentirnos cómodamente a nosotros mismos en este aspecto. ¿Te has mentido a ti mismo? ¿Has dicho: «A Dios le parece bien este tipo de música», aunque en lo profundo de tu corazón sabes que Él te está convenciendo de lo contrario y que NO le parece bien?

La música secular suele ser sensual. Sensual significa «que suscita la satisfacción de los sentidos y lo físico». ¿Es sensual la música que escuchamos? ¿Hace que nuestra mente simplemente se deje llevar por el ritmo? ¿Cómo quieren responder nuestros cuerpos cuando escuchamos esa música? Si nuestros cuerpos se balancean con el ritmo de la música, eso no honra al Señor; no glorifica Su nombre; no coloca nuestra mente y nuestro cuerpo en una disposición para adorar al Señor.

Siempre adoramos algo cuando escuchamos música. Si nos concentramos en música que no es de Dios, adoramos nuestra carne, al mundo o incluso al diablo. Por lo general, la música como la CCM tiende a centrar la atención en nosotros mismos y no en Dios. Este tipo de música es muy sensual. ¿Podemos verdaderamente adorar a Dios cuando escuchamos este tipo de música?

La CCM es un género de música popular moderna cuyas letras se centran en asuntos relacionados con la fe cristiana. Surgió cuando quienes se vieron afectados por el avivamiento del «movimiento de Jesús» de la década de 1960 empezaron a expresarse con un estilo musical más contemporáneo. Antes de eso, en la iglesia de la época predominaban los himnos y otras canciones góspel. Lo sepamos o no, gran parte de la CCM añade un ritmo pulsante (síncopa) en un lugar donde no debería estar de forma natural. El ritmo pulsante propio de la CCM no apela al espíritu del ser humano en la adoración, sino a la carne. El tipo de música que apela a la carne no es de Dios, sino del diablo. Hoy en día, CCM es un término que se usa para referirse a estilos de pop, rock o alabanza y adoración con determinados ritmos, siempre que las letras correspondan a la definición de CCM.

Filipenses nos dice que debemos pensar en … todo lo verdadero, todo lo honesto, todo lo justo, todo lo puro, todo lo amable, todo lo que es de buen nombre; si hay alguna virtud y si algo merece alabanza, en esto pensad –Filipenses 4:8.

La música secular no supera la prueba de Filipenses 4:8. La mayor parte de la música secular tiene letras impuras, y toda ella tiene un ritmo o compás contrario al orden de Dios. El diablo usa toda esa música para influir en las personas a pecar o a pensar en el pecado. Te afectará de alguna manera. ¿Es buena o mala la influencia de la música que escuchamos? Por ejemplo, si nos concentramos en música que afecta negativamente nuestros pensamientos o nuestro estilo de vida, entonces es una influencia negativa que debemos eliminar de nuestra vida.

Los hebreos comenzaron la tradición de usar música sin acompañamiento después de la caída del segundo templo, en el año 70 d. C.; en ese momento no se permitían instrumentos durante el período de duelo posterior a la caída. A lo largo de la historia, hasta el Renacimiento, la música instrumental se asociaba principalmente con el baile y la diversión. Como no se podía disfrutar demasiado en los lugares de culto, este tipo de música recreativa no era popular entre los líderes religiosos.

A capela es una expresión italiana que significa «al estilo de la capilla». Al principio se usaba para referirse a la música que se cantaba en una capilla o en un pequeño espacio de culto sin instrumentos de acompañamiento, a diferencia de una iglesia grande, donde un órgano solía acompañar la música vocal. Desde entonces, el término ha llegado a significar cualquier música cantada sin acompañamiento, ya sea sagrada (religiosa) o secular (no religiosa). La música a capela puede ser interpretada por un coro grande, un grupo pequeño o una sola persona.

En las congregaciones judías ortodoxas y conservadoras aún existe la tradición de cantar principalmente a capela. En estas sinagogas, es costumbre que un cantor recite o cante un texto autorizado de las Escrituras, al que la congregación responde de la misma manera. Los únicos instrumentos que se usan podrían ser un diapasón para dar a todos una nota inicial, o un cuerno de carnero en una ocasión especial o festividad.

La iglesia primitiva desarrolló la tradición del canto a capela a partir de la tradición judía de los hebreos: entonaban salmos u otros pasajes de las Escrituras y usaban a un cantor como guía. El canto gregoriano fue la forma predominante de música eclesiástica a partir de aproximadamente el año 590 d. C. Consiste en una sola línea melódica sencilla, mitad hablada y mitad cantada, en un estilo rítmico libre. En la iglesia primitiva, la música instrumental se asociaba con el mundo pecaminoso exterior y se consideraba una influencia negativa.

La tradición de la música vocal sacra sin acompañamiento continuó durante el Renacimiento. Aunque a veces los instrumentos duplicaban o sustituían una línea vocal, la música vocal se sostenía principalmente por sí sola. El sonido de un coro de voces en una capilla con una acústica excelente producía un efecto particularmente etéreo.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina fue uno de los compositores más importantes del Renacimiento en Italia, y escribió cientos de misas y motetes para la iglesia. El «estilo palestriniano», como se lo llama, era una forma sofisticada de música a capela que utilizaba muchas voces que cantaban distintas melodías y textos, los cuales comenzaban en momentos diferentes. Se llamaba polifónica, en oposición a homofónica, que significa una sola línea melódica cantada al unísono o con el mismo ritmo.

El apóstol Pablo escribe: Hablando entre vosotros con salmos, con himnos y cánticos espirituales, cantando y alabando al Señor en vuestro corazón; –Efesios 5:19. ¿Suena eso como hacer música con instrumentos? ¿O más bien parece que se trata de cantar alabanzas a Dios desde el corazón?

A medianoche, Pablo y Silas oraban y cantaban himnos a Dios, y los presos los oían –Hechos 16:25. Cuando Pablo y Silas estaban en la cárcel, sujetos con cepos y cantando a medianoche, no creo que cantaran para glorificarse a sí mismos. Cantaban para glorificar a Dios Padre. El resultado de darle gloria a Dios fue asombroso. Hubo un terremoto, los cimientos de la cárcel temblaron, las puertas se abrieron de golpe y se soltaron las cadenas de todos los presos. Al final de todo esto, el carcelero se acercó temblando a Pablo y Silas y preguntó: «¿Qué debo hacer para ser salvo?».

Colosenses también nos dice que debemos La palabra de Cristo more en abundancia en vosotros, enseñándoos y exhortándoos unos a otros con toda sabiduría, con salmos e himnos y cánticos espirituales, cantando con gracia en vuestros corazones al Señor –Colosenses 3:16. ¿Permitimos que los salmos, los himnos y los cánticos espirituales nos enseñen, nos exhorten y nos animen?

Me pregunto qué himno cantó Jesús con sus discípulos en la última cena, antes de salir al monte de los Olivos. Dudo que cantaran para sí mismos. Creo que cantaban a su Padre celestial.

La música pura y santa es una bendición del Señor. Es algo tan hermoso y poderoso que no deberíamos darlo por sentado. A veces Dios la usa para hablarnos. Creo firmemente que todos los cristianos necesitan escuchar música piadosa durante toda la semana, no solo el domingo. Me ayuda a mantener la calma, me anima y mantiene mi mente puesta en el Señor. Cuando tengo la mente puesta en el Señor, puedo pasar el día con bendición.

Necesitamos disciplinarnos en las cosas de Dios. También necesitamos deshacernos de las cosas de nuestra vida que sabemos que no agradan a Dios. La música piadosa (música que dirige nuestro espíritu y nuestra mente hacia las cosas que provienen de Dios) es el tipo de música que los creyentes deberían escuchar. En definitiva, todo se reduce a la adoración: ¿adoramos a Dios o a otra cosa?

Jesús dice: Pero la hora viene, y ahora es, cuando los verdaderos adoradores adorarán al Padre en espíritu y en verdad; porque también el Padre busca a tales que le adoren –Juan 4:23.

Así que cantemos en sincera adoración a nuestro Creador, demos a Dios la gloria por las voces que nos ha dado y cantemos y escuchemos canciones piadosas y sanas para nuestro Dios.

A verse that has always caught my attention, one that has caused my spine to tingle is found in Matthew chapter seven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? –Matthew 7:22.

Jesus gives us a picture of a large group of people standing before Him on Judgment Day. They thought they lived their lives for Him. They were gifted people—prophesying, casting out devils, and doing many wonderful things in the name of Jesus—they seemed like good Christians. However, in the next verse we read that Jesus will say to them that He never knew them. Jesus even tells them to depart from Him. He sends them to hell, forever.

I remember an account that reminds me of these verses. Years ago, I was working for a steel joist company. It was a normal Friday morning, we were working hard, as was required of each of us. The line boss came out and announced a meeting with the whole plant after the shift was over. We all wondered what the meeting was about. We asked around but it seemed that no one knew. After the shift, we all stood in a large circle and waited for the boss. He soon entered the room with another man. It was the manager of the whole company. Prior to these men coming in, we were all talking casually with each other, there was laughter and loud voices. The boss had a large stack of envelopes, and I heard a buzz go around about bonus checks. Everyone looked excited, except for the boss.

Then the boss started talking, “We have been watching all of you very closely over the past four weeks. We have been looking at your work ethic, how hard you try, and whether you’re on time. We have been looking at many different areas. Your supervisors will give each of you an envelope with your name on it. Do not open this letter until you are off the premises. When you do open it, you will find some instructions. For most, it will say to return to work at the normal time on Monday. But for 27 of you, it will say that you are fired. For those included in that number, we did not like what we saw during our time of evaluation, so we decided that we need to release you from your employment here.”

You could hear a pin drop. Fear was seen on every face. I remember wishing I had worked harder, been more involved. I regretted taking my job for granted. It was a terrible feeling, I had worked there for years, but did that matter?

I wasn’t fired that day, but 27 others were. They thought they had done enough. They thought they were safe since they had put in their time. But they were wrong, and now nothing could be done. It was over.

What about us? Do we gauge our walk with God based on eternity? Do we wonder what will happen on the day of judgement? How can we know?

Jesus says a few verses earlier that we will know each other by our fruits. There is much talk in the Word of God about fruit. We know what type of tree one is, by examining its fruit. When we first moved to Haiti, we didn’t know what kinds of trees were there. I remember looking up at a large tree on our property and wondering what kind it was. Then something gave it away. There were small avocados hanging from its branches. In the church today, it seems that people do not want to talk about this. But I assure you that we should talk about it before it is forever too late. Looking back, we would have loved to talk about this at the factory before that day when some of the employees were fired.

So, what is the fruit of a Christian? We know that being a good person and dressing in a certain way are not determining factors of a godly life. It is not the church we attend, the family we were born into, our culture, or the color of our skin. Many would agree that these things are not what identifies us as Christians. Some may think that the fruit of a Christian is being a good, morally upright, and loving citizen of society. There are many people who are law-abiding citizens, loving and peaceful, taking care of their own needs and the needs of others. Yet it is still possible for them to do all these good things and still go to hell.

We hear the world (and some in the church) proclaiming loudly that it’s only the heart that matters. We know they are saying this so they can excuse the lack of visible fruit. Even though their outside is bad, they want people to think that their heart is good, and that that’s all that really matters.

They are correct about the heart being important. You can’t change or fix anything simply by putting on a form when the heart is still selfish and wicked. However, they are wrong about the heart being good and the outside being bad. This is impossible. Jesus says, Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also –Matthew 23:26.

You cannot have a clean heart and a sinful appearance. However, on the flip side, you can have a clean appearance and yet still have an ungodly heart. So how do we tell? What is this fruit that Jesus is talking about?

We will talk about the fruit of the Spirit shortly, but first I would like to talk about something else that I believe defines a Christian. Something that can separate the sheep from the wolves, even if they both appear to be the same.

A desire to serve Jesus. When God converts a person’s soul, that individual is a new creature, and desires to serve God with his whole being. That person does not need to be forced to do what pleases God. There is much talk today in the church about structure and rules, however, this was not always the case. So why is this such a big issue today? Maybe there are unconverted people in the church. Perhaps people are too independent and do not want to be told what to do. You can tell a church member to dress modestly, but if their heart is not changed, you will face problems. They will try to be as worldly as they can, and still be within the ‘law’ of the church. Or they will simply refuse to do it and the church soon gives in and no longer requires their people to dress and live modestly. Should the church need to force its people to be modest? Should the church need to force its people to be Christ-like? Absolutely not. When a soul has been redeemed and transformed by the blood of Christ, that person, in return, will, because of his changed nature, live a sacrificial life for Him. We obey His commandments with grateful hearts!

For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous –1 John 5:3.

A heart that has not been made new by God’s Spirit will not passionately desire to live for God. One can religiously go to church—many unbelievers attend church services regularly. One can dress right and act right, but if their heart does not pant after the things of God, these things will have no profit. Much of what they do is to receive the praise of men, not the glory of God. It is no wonder that many churches of today are accepting drift.

It is a beautiful thing to see someone truly desire to live for God. They desire to seek the face of their Creator, their Savior. They live for the Kingdom, for the brotherhood. To obey God and serve Him is a necessity; it is the only thing that really matters to them. Their ‘all’ truly is on the altar. They love reading the Word and spending time alone with God. Their desires and their will have been sacrificed on the altar of their God.

People have told me that we need to give a new Christian some room. “Some room for what?” I ask. Some room for sin… for carnality? Absolutely not. Every example in the Bible says differently. Every conversion brought a tremendous change, a new creature. Many people confuse ‘grace to learn and to grow’ in the faith as an ‘excuse for sin’. The Scriptures define new Christians… As newborn babes, and commands each of us to desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby: –1 Peter 2:2. So new Christians don’t need space to continue for a time in their ungodly ways, but they do need space to grow …in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man –Luke 2:52.

When someone comes declaring they have been converted, it is easy to find out. We simply go over some scriptures that explain practical, foundational doctrines like non-conformity, non-resistance, and such like. Some see it as God’s Word and soak it in. Many folks sit in astonishment as I read such verses to them—Scripture verses they have never heard before. Usually they simply believe what they just heard from God’s word, and it changes them. That is a Christian who wants to be taught, who wants to be discipled. They tend to come with a teachable attitude asking questions about that which they have read in God’s Word and don’t understand.

But what about so many others? They hear the same scriptures and they argue—they argue with the Bible and the person sharing the Scripture with them, but ultimately, they are arguing with God. They will usually admit that it’s what the Bible says but they want to know why it says that. They are not wanting to change their life for God. They want to be a Christian, yes, but they also want to live how they want. They do not desire to obey God. We can continue working with them, but it is clear: their heart pants after the things of the world and the pleasures of this life.

Picture with me a man living 1,000 years ago. He is locked in a dungeon, where everything is as black as coal. It is musty and stinks. He has been arrested for preaching the gospel. His ankles and wrists are raw and bloody from the large, heavy chains that keep him bound in the tiny cell. He’s claustrophobic, weary, and worn. His back is bloody. His aching limbs have been stretched to the breaking point. He talks to God, but God does not answer. He pleads for deliverance but hears nothing in return. He thinks back on his life, his faith. Then he wonders the dreaded thought: “God, are you there? Are you real?” Silence. His faith is being tried to the extreme. He knows that if he continues to hold to his beliefs, a fire awaits him. Why? Why die for a God that allows him to go through this agony? Why die for a God that will not speak? “My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me?”

Now picture this man… is you.

Do we really believe in God, a God who’s not seen and often not heard? If our faith does not exist, then God will not exist when we really need Him.

God wants us to put all our faith in Him, all the time. We walk by faith, NOT by sight… even when things are going well. When we find ourselves in terrible times, God is still near, leading us and giving us courage to go on! We are used to simply trusting in Him, in His word.

For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry? –Luke 23:31.

God loves a heart that is turned toward Him, fully yielded, and surrendered. He is a rewarder of them that diligently seek Him!

Do we have the fruit of the Spirit of God? Do we act like Christians? Do we look like Christians?

I was asked to preach for a large church that I had never been to before. I went with my family and sat while the seats filled up with hundreds of people. I was amazed at how these people were dressed. There were short miniskirts and skimpy tops, much worldly fashion and style. The service began and I realized quickly that this was not a good place for my family, so I took them home and returned by myself. The rock music was still going, and the dancing was pushing my limits. After two hours it was time for the message. I stood and told the large crowd that I was the new President of America. Laughter filled the auditorium. I then asked them if they believed me. “No!” they shouted. I asked why they didn’t believe me, and they responded with different answers. One yelled, “You don’t look or dress like the president!” Another said, “You wouldn’t be here if you were the president!” Yet another said that I didn’t sound like the president. I told them that I didn’t understand. I asked how they can say that they are Christians—They don’t look like it! They don’t act like it! They don’t sound like it!—Yet everyone believes them!

It seems that we judge everything by its fruit, except for Christians. For Christians we are expected to judge by what they claim. This world thinks they can simply imagine what Jesus wants and then please Him in any way they personally choose. However, the Bible is clear: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them –Matthew 7:16-20.

The Bible says that …the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance… –Galatians 5:22-23. Are these the things that people see when they look at you and I? I know it is easy to justify not having one or more of these fruits by saying, “I’m working on it,” or “I’m praying about it.” Jesus does not say that this fruit is something that Christians should work to attain. He simply says that these are the fruits, or product, of the indwelling Spirit of God. If we pursue worldly ambitions, or if we desire to fit in with the world, we cannot expect this fruit to be evident in our lives. I believe this is the fruit of a suffering man, a person that has been giving his all, and desires to give his all to the Lamb that was slain.

Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire –Matthew 7:19.

When we give something our all, whether it’s our work, our school, or raising a family, it feels good—it is fulfilling. When we serve God with all our being, the same is true. There is a very rewarding feeling, a feeling of peace that passes all understanding.
