’n Vers wat nog altyd my aandag getrek het, en my hoendervleis gegee het, staan in Matteus hoofstuk sewe. Baie sal in daardie dag vir My sê: Here, Here, het ons nie in u Naam geprofeteer en in u Naam duiwels uitgedryf en in u Naam baie wonders gedoen nie? –Matteus 7:22.

Jesus gee vir ons ’n beeld van ’n groot groep mense wat op die Oordeelsdag voor Hom staan. Hulle het gedink dat hulle hul lewens vir Hom geleef het. Hulle was begaafde mense—hulle het geprofeteer, duiwels uitgedryf en baie wonderlike dinge in Jesus se Naam gedoen—dit het gelyk asof hulle goeie Christene was. In die volgende vers lees ons egter dat Jesus vir hulle sal sê dat Hy hulle nooit geken het nie. Jesus sê selfs vir hulle om van Hom af weg te gaan. Hy stuur hulle vir ewig hel toe.

Ek onthou ’n voorval wat my aan hierdie verse herinner. Jare gelede het ek vir ’n vervaardiger van staalbalkwerk gewerk. Dit was ’n gewone Vrydagoggend; ons het hard gewerk, soos daar van elkeen van ons verwag is. Die lynbaas het uitgekom en aangekondig dat daar ná die skof ’n vergadering met die hele fabriek sou wees. Ons het almal gewonder waaroor die vergadering gaan. Ons het rondgevra, maar dit het gelyk asof niemand geweet het nie. Ná die skof het ons almal in ’n groot kring gestaan en vir die baas gewag. Hy het gou saam met ’n ander man die vertrek binnegekom. Dit was die bestuurder van die hele maatskappy. Voordat hierdie mans ingekom het, het ons almal rustig met mekaar gesels; daar was gelag en harde stemme. Die baas het ’n groot stapel koeverte gehad, en ek het ’n gegons oor bonusstrokies gehoor. Almal het opgewonde gelyk, behalwe die baas.

Toe begin die baas praat: “Ons het julle almal die afgelope vier weke baie fyn dopgehou. Ons het gekyk na julle werksetiek, hoe hard julle probeer en of julle betyds is. Ons het na baie verskillende dinge gekyk. Julle toesighouers sal vir elkeen van julle ’n koevert met julle naam daarop gee. Moenie hierdie brief oopmaak voordat julle die perseel verlaat het nie. Wanneer julle dit oopmaak, sal julle ’n paar instruksies daarin vind. Vir die meeste sal daar staan dat hulle Maandag op die gewone tyd moet terugkom werk toe. Maar vir 27 van julle sal daar staan dat julle afgedank is. Wat diegene betref wat onder daardie getal val: ons het nie gehou van wat ons tydens ons beoordeling gesien het nie, en daarom het ons besluit dat ons julle hier uit diens moet stel.”

Jy kon ’n speld hoor val. Vrees was op elke gesig te sien. Ek onthou dat ek gewens het ek het harder gewerk en meer betrokke geraak. Ek was spyt dat ek my werk as vanselfsprekend aanvaar het. Dit was ’n verskriklike gevoel. Ek het jare lank daar gewerk, maar het dit saak gemaak?

Ek is daardie dag nie afgedank nie, maar 27 ander mense is. Hulle het gedink hulle het genoeg gedoen. Hulle het gedink hulle is veilig omdat hulle hul tyd ingewerk het. Maar hulle was verkeerd, en nou kon niks meer gedoen word nie. Dit was verby.

Wat van ons? Meet ons ons wandel met God aan die hand van die ewigheid? Wonder ons wat op die oordeelsdag gaan gebeur? Hoe kan ons weet?

Jesus sê ’n paar verse vroeër dat ons mekaar aan ons vrugte sal ken. God se Woord praat baie oor vrugte. Ons weet watter soort boom dit is deur na sy vrugte te kyk. Toe ons die eerste keer na Haïti verhuis het, het ons nie geweet watter soorte bome daar was nie. Ek onthou dat ek opgekyk het na ’n groot boom op ons eiendom en gewonder het watter soort boom dit was. Toe het iets dit verklap. Daar het klein avokado’s aan sy takke gehang. In die kerk vandag lyk dit asof mense nie hieroor wil praat nie. Maar ek verseker julle dat ons hieroor moet praat voordat dit vir ewig te laat is. As ons terugdink, sou ons graag hieroor by die fabriek wou gepraat het voordat sommige werknemers daardie dag afgedank is.

Wat is ’n Christen se vrug dan? Ons weet dat om ’n goeie mens te wees en op ’n bepaalde manier aan te trek nie bepalende faktore van ’n godvrugtige lewe is nie. Dit is nie die kerk waarheen ons gaan, die gesin waarin ons gebore is, ons kultuur of ons velkleur nie. Baie sal saamstem dat hierdie dinge nie bepaal of ons as Christene herken word nie. Sommige dink dalk dat ’n Christen se vrug daarin bestaan om ’n goeie, sedelik regskape en liefdevolle burger van die samelewing te wees. Daar is baie mense wat wetsgehoorsame burgers is, liefdevol en vredeliewend is en na hul eie behoeftes en dié van ander omsien. Tog is dit steeds moontlik dat hulle al hierdie goeie dinge doen en steeds hel toe gaan.

Ons hoor hoe die wêreld (en sommige in die kerk) luidkeels verkondig dat net die hart saak maak. Ons weet hulle sê dit sodat hulle die gebrek aan sigbare vrug kan verskoon. Al lyk hulle uiterlik sleg, wil hulle hê mense moet dink dat hulle hart goed is en dat dit al is wat werklik saak maak.

Hulle is reg dat die hart belangrik is. Jy kan niks verander of regmaak bloot deur ’n uiterlike vorm aan te neem terwyl die hart nog selfsugtig en boos is nie. Hulle is egter verkeerd dat die hart goed en die uiterlike sleg kan wees. Dit is onmoontlik. Jesus sê: Blinde Fariseër, reinig eers die binnekant van die beker en die skottel, sodat die buitekant daarvan ook rein kan wees. –Matteus 23:26.

Jy kan nie ’n rein hart en ’n sondige voorkoms hê nie. Aan die ander kant kan jy egter ’n rein voorkoms hê en steeds ’n goddelose hart hê. Hoe kan ons dit dan uitken? Wat is hierdie vrug waarvan Jesus praat?

Ons sal binnekort oor die vrug van die Gees praat, maar eers wil ek praat oor iets anders wat, na my mening, ’n Christen kenmerk. Iets wat die skape van die wolwe kan onderskei, selfs al lyk hulle albei dieselfde.

’n Begeerte om Jesus te dien. Wanneer God ’n mens se siel bekeer, is daardie mens ’n nuwe skepsel en begeer hy om God met sy hele wese te dien. Daardie mens hoef nie gedwing te word om te doen wat God behaag nie. Daar word vandag baie in die kerk oor struktuur en reëls gepraat, maar dit was nie altyd so nie. Waarom is dit dan vandag so ’n groot kwessie? Miskien is daar onbekeerde mense in die kerk. Dalk is mense te onafhanklik en wil hulle nie voorgesê word wat om te doen nie. Jy kan vir ’n kerklidmaat sê om beskeie aan te trek, maar as sy hart nie verander is nie, sal jy probleme ondervind. Hulle sal probeer om so wêrelds moontlik te wees en tog binne die ‘wet’ van die kerk te bly. Of hulle sal eenvoudig weier om dit te doen, en die kerk sal gou ingee en nie meer van sy mense vereis om beskeie aan te trek en te lewe nie. Behoort die kerk sy mense te moet dwing om beskeie te wees? Behoort die kerk sy mense te moet dwing om soos Christus te wees? Beslis nie. Wanneer ’n siel deur die bloed van Christus verlos en verander is, sal daardie mens as gevolg van sy veranderde natuur op sy beurt ’n lewe van selfopoffering vir Hom lei. Ons gehoorsaam sy gebooie met dankbare harte!

Want dit is die liefde tot God, dat ons sy gebooie bewaar; en sy gebooie is nie swaar nie. –1 Johannes 5:3.

’n Hart wat nie deur God se Gees nuut gemaak is nie, sal nie vurig begeer om vir God te lewe nie. ’n Mens kan godsdienstig kerk toe gaan—baie ongelowiges woon gereeld kerkdienste by. ’n Mens kan reg aantrek en reg optree, maar as sy hart nie na die dinge van God smag nie, sal hierdie dinge geen nut hê nie. Baie van wat hulle doen, is om die lof van mense te ontvang, nie die eer van God nie. Dit is geen wonder dat baie kerke van vandag afdwaling aanvaar nie.

Dit is ’n pragtige ding om iemand te sien wat waarlik begeer om vir God te lewe. Hulle begeer om die aangesig van hul Skepper, hul Verlosser, te soek. Hulle lewe vir die Koninkryk, vir die broederskap. Om God te gehoorsaam en Hom te dien is ’n noodsaaklikheid; dit is die enigste ding wat werklik vir hulle saak maak. Hulle het waarlik alles op die altaar gelê. Hulle hou daarvan om die Woord te lees en tyd alleen saam met God deur te bring. Hulle begeertes en hul wil is op die altaar van hul God geoffer.

Mense het vir my gesê dat ons ’n nuwe Christen ’n bietjie ruimte moet gee. “Ruimte waarvoor?” vra ek. Ruimte vir sonde… vir vleeslikheid? Beslis nie. Elke voorbeeld in die Bybel sê iets anders. Elke bekering het ’n geweldige verandering teweeggebring, ’n nuwe skepsel. Baie mense verwar ‘genade om in die geloof te leer en te groei’ met ’n ‘verskoning vir sonde’. Die Skrif beskryf nuwe Christene as pasgebore kindertjies en beveel elkeen van ons om na die onvervalste melk van die woord te verlang, sodat julle daardeur kan opgroei: –1 Petrus 2:2. Nuwe Christene het dus nie ruimte nodig om ’n tyd lank met hul goddelose weë voort te gaan nie, maar hulle het wel ruimte nodig om te groei …in wysheid en grootte en in genade by God en die mense. –Lukas 2:52.

Wanneer iemand kom verklaar dat hy bekeer is, is dit maklik om uit te vind. Ons gaan eenvoudig deur ’n paar Skrifgedeeltes wat praktiese, grondliggende leerstellings soos nie-gelykvormigheid, nie-weerstand en dergelike verduidelik. Sommige sien dit as God se Woord en neem dit ter harte. Baie mense sit verbaas wanneer ek sulke verse vir hulle voorlees—Skrifverse waarvan hulle nog nooit tevore gehoor het nie. Gewoonlik glo hulle eenvoudig wat hulle so pas uit God se Woord gehoor het, en dit verander hulle. So iemand is ’n Christen wat geleer wil word, wat ’n dissipel wil wees. Hulle kom dikwels met ’n leerbare gesindheid en vra vrae oor wat hulle in God se Woord gelees het en nie verstaan nie.

Maar wat van soveel ander? Hulle hoor dieselfde Skrifgedeeltes en stry—hulle stry met die Bybel en met die persoon wat die Skrif met hulle deel, maar uiteindelik stry hulle met God. Gewoonlik erken hulle dat dit is wat die Bybel sê, maar hulle wil weet waarom dit dit sê. Hulle wil nie hul lewe vir God verander nie. Hulle wil wel Christene wees, maar hulle wil ook lewe soos hulle wil. Hulle begeer nie om God te gehoorsaam nie. Ons kan aanhou om met hulle te werk, maar dit is duidelik: hul hart smag na die dinge van die wêreld en die genietinge van hierdie lewe.

Stel jou saam met my ’n man voor wat 1 000 jaar gelede geleef het. Hy is toegesluit in ’n kerker waar alles pikswart is. Dit is muf en stink. Hy is in hegtenis geneem omdat hy die evangelie verkondig het. Sy enkels en polse is rou en bebloed van die groot, swaar kettings wat hom in die klein sel vasgebind hou. Hy is klaustrofobies, moeg en uitgeput. Sy rug is bebloed. Sy pynlike ledemate is tot op die breekpunt gerek. Hy praat met God, maar God antwoord nie. Hy smeek om bevryding, maar hoor geen antwoord nie. Hy dink terug aan sy lewe, sy geloof. Dan kom die gevreesde gedagte by hom op: “God, is U daar? Is U werklik?” Stilte. Sy geloof word tot die uiterste beproef. Hy weet dat ’n vuur hom wag as hy aanhou om by sy oortuigings te bly. Waarom? Waarom sterf vir ’n God wat toelaat dat hy hierdie foltering deurmaak? Waarom sterf vir ’n God wat nie wil praat nie? “My God, my God, waarom het U My verlaat?”

Stel jou nou hierdie man voor… dit is jy.

Glo ons werklik in God, ’n God wat ons nie kan sien nie en dikwels nie hoor nie? As ons geloof nie bestaan nie, sal God nie daar wees wanneer ons Hom werklik nodig het nie.

God wil hê dat ons te alle tye al ons geloof in Hom stel. Ons wandel deur geloof, NIE deur aanskouing nie… selfs wanneer dit goed gaan. Wanneer ons onsself in verskriklike tye bevind, is God steeds naby, lei Hy ons en gee Hy ons moed om voort te gaan! Ons is gewoond daaraan om eenvoudig op Hom, op sy woord, te vertrou.

Want as hulle hierdie dinge aan die groen hout doen, wat sal met die droë gebeur? –Lukas 23:31.

God het ’n hart lief wat op Hom gerig, volkome aan Hom toegewy en oorgegee is. Hy beloon dié wat Hom ywerig soek!

Het ons die vrug van God se Gees? Tree ons soos Christene op? Lyk ons soos Christene?

Ek is gevra om by ’n groot kerk te preek waar ek nog nooit voorheen was nie. Ek het saam met my gesin gegaan en gesit terwyl die sitplekke met honderde mense vol geraak het. Ek was verbaas oor hoe hierdie mense aangetrek was. Daar was kort minirokkies en onthullende toppies, baie wêreldse modes en style. Die diens het begin en ek het gou besef dat dit nie ’n goeie plek vir my gesin was nie. Daarom het ek hulle huis toe geneem en alleen teruggekeer. Die rockmusiek het steeds gespeel, en die dansery het my perke getoets. Ná twee uur het dit tyd geword vir die boodskap. Ek het opgestaan en vir die groot skare gesê dat ek die nuwe president van Amerika was. Die gehoorsaal het vol gelag geword. Toe vra ek hulle of hulle my glo. “Nee!” het hulle geskree. Ek het gevra waarom hulle my nie glo nie, en hulle het verskillende antwoorde gegee. Een het geskree: “Jy lyk of trek nie soos die president aan nie!” ’n Ander een het gesê: “Jy sou nie hier wees as jy die president was nie!” Nog iemand het gesê dat ek nie soos die president klink nie. Ek het vir hulle gesê dat ek dit nie verstaan nie. Ek het gevra hoe hulle kan sê dat hulle Christene is—Hulle lyk nie soos Christene nie! Hulle tree nie soos Christene op nie! Hulle klink nie soos Christene nie!—en tog glo almal hulle!

Dit lyk asof ons alles aan die hand van die vrug daarvan beoordeel, behalwe Christene. Van Christene word daar verwag dat ons hulle moet beoordeel op grond van wat hulle beweer. Hierdie wêreld dink dat hulle bloot kan uitdink wat Jesus wil hê en Hom dan op enige manier wat hulle persoonlik verkies, behaag. Die Bybel is egter duidelik: Aan hulle vrugte sal julle hulle ken. Pluk ’n mens druiwe van dorings of vye van distels? So bring elke goeie boom goeie vrugte voort, maar ’n slegte boom bring slegte vrugte voort. ’n Goeie boom kan nie slegte vrugte voortbring nie, en ’n slegte boom kan nie goeie vrugte voortbring nie. Elke boom wat nie goeie vrugte voortbring nie, word uitgekap en in die vuur gegooi. So sal julle hulle dan aan hul vrugte ken. –Matteus 7:16-20.

Die Bybel sê: …die vrug van die Gees is liefde, blydskap, vrede, lankmoedigheid, vriendelikheid, goedhartigheid, getrouheid, sagmoedigheid, selfbeheersing… –Galasiërs 5:22-23. Is dit die dinge wat mense sien wanneer hulle na jou en my kyk? Ek weet dit is maklik om die afwesigheid van een of meer van hierdie vrugte te regverdig deur te sê: “Ek werk daaraan,” of “Ek bid daaroor.” Jesus sê nie dat Christene moet werk om hierdie vrug te verkry nie. Hy sê eenvoudig dat dit die vrugte, of die produk, van die inwonende Gees van God is. As ons wêreldse ambisies nastreef, of as ons begeer om by die wêreld in te pas, kan ons nie verwag dat hierdie vrug in ons lewens sigbaar sal wees nie. Ek glo dat dit die vrug is van ’n lydende mens, iemand wat alles gegee het en begeer om alles te gee aan die Lam wat geslag is.

Elke boom wat nie goeie vrugte voortbring nie, word uitgekap en in die vuur gegooi. –Matteus 7:19.

Wanneer ons alles gee vir iets—of dit nou ons werk, ons skool of die grootmaak van ’n gesin is—voel dit goed; dit gee vervulling. Dieselfde geld wanneer ons God met ons hele wese dien. Dit bring ’n baie bevredigende gevoel, ’n vrede wat alle verstand te bowe gaan.

Greetings in the name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. We are trusting that each of you as our readers are doing well and continuing to trust the Lord. The pandemic has created a bit of a backlog for us, along with some personal issues we have been working through, so this issue is coming to you somewhat behind schedule. Our apologies…. We plan to get the next issue printed within the next several months to get back on track.

In the last issue’s editorial, I wrote about an obscure news article which revealed that many folks across the world were surprised by the positive outcomes they were experiencing through the need to stay at home during the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic. They were enjoying family time. They were finding camaraderie in facing this challenge together. They were finding excitement in the adventure of discovering new ways to function and survive. And they were finding renewed vision and purpose in life.

However, as time has passed, this seems to have been short-lived by all who did not have a deeper level of stability in their lives. After a varying amount of time has elapsed for many folks, reality has begun to set in. Some have lost their jobs. Some have lost loved ones. Some have gone through a time of sickness. Many have been starved for fellowship with other human beings. For the elderly living in nursing homes and assisted-living facilities, and those requiring hospitalization, life has become a very lonely existence indeed, since most of these places have not allowed visitors to enter their doors.

The world is trying to find any way possible to cope and survive. There are phone conference lines. There are chat lines. There are webinars geared towards the issue. Many are doing their part to fill the gaps that this pandemic has created in the lives of the people around them.

As we step back to gain a clearer perspective of the unfolding events brought about by the pandemic, the last number of months have been a time of change and uncertainty for most. There’s the economic future, “Is my job secure?” “What about my bills?” “What about my housing?” Then there’s the greatly politicized nature of numerous issues—race inequality, conspiracy theories about the pandemic, and the government mandates regarding our response to the virus pandemic. Add to this the polarization in our country regarding politics—who is telling the truth on issues, and who will be the best option to lead the country after the upcoming election.

Despite everything else that is going on, the virus and its effects seem to be on everyone’s mind. On August 15, 2020 there was an article published by CNN, written by Ryan Prior, titled: “1 IN 4 YOUNG PEOPLE ARE REPORTING SUICIDAL THOUGHTS”. For those wanting to read the article, it can be found here:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

This article recognizes that there were positive effects during the onset of the pandemic and the resulting stay-at-home orders. This article goes on to say that as time has passed this event is different than most past events, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, and even the circumstances of 9/11. Most of these events have been localized and brief in their destructive effects, while the Covid-19 pandemic has dragged on for so long that it is becoming a way of life—with no end in sight, and its beginning is fading into our forgetful past.

According to the news article, the CDC has published data from a survey which was conducted to determine the outcome of the negative effects of the pandemic. Following are some facts as presented in the article:

  • Suicidal ideation is up among young people since last year
  • As many as one in four people ages 18 through 24 having seriously considered suicide in the 30 days preceding the survey (researchers surveyed 5,412 adults in the US between June 24 and 30.)
  • In the general US population … 11% of adults surveyed had seriously considered suicide in the past 30 days before they completed the survey.
  • The number of Americans reporting anxiety symptoms is three times the number at this same time last year, the CDC said.
  • The results reflect a nation increasingly on edge.

How sad it is to ponder this reality. As I read this news article, I had to wonder whether the percentages are the same for the church as they are for the world. A verse of scripture came to mind: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable –1 Corinthians 15:19. As Christians…

  • …we have HOPE!
  • …we have HOPE IN CHRIST!!
  • …we have HOPE both IN THIS LIFE and FOR ETERNITY!!!

Considering all this we should have a smile on our faces, hope in our hearts, and an encouraging word on our lips for all with whom we come in contact. Let’s be especially observant as we interact with the people around us—family, friend, and even the stranger. Who knows, maybe the neighbor next door is feeling all alone and discouraged. Or perhaps our best friend from church has been struggling with a burden that seems more than they can bear. As we pray, we can ask God to bring people to our minds that would be blessed by our assistance of one sort or another. We never know when our smile or encouraging word will help make a change in someone’s eternal welfare.

Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another. For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:1-5.

There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able… –1 Corinthians 10:13.

My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience –James 1:2-3.

In these verses, I see a number of things that God wants us to use to live by.

  1. God will not allow us to be tempted above that which we are able to endure. This is according to His fact, not according to our feeling.
  2. Each of us WILL fall into temptations, but as we see God’s sovereignty involved in our trials, we can rest as we “count it all joy”.
  3. When it seems that our faith is being tried and tested, sometimes seemingly almost to the breaking point, we can rest assured that God is in the middle of it and that He is up to something according to His will.
  4. God will allow burdens into each of our lives and He expects each of us to “bear our own burdens”.
  5. God will allow our fellow man to go through times of difficulty, during which God expects us to see our struggling brother or sister and do whatever we can to help ease the burden—through prayer, words of encouragement, or deeds of assistance.

In closing, I will leave you with several verses that Paul wrote to the church of Galatia. And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. –Galatians 6:9-10. As strangers and pilgrims here on this earth, let’s not lose sight of our Eternal Home, our Sympathetic Savior, our Sovereign God, and our Abba Father.

Saludos en el nombre de nuestro Señor y Salvador Jesucristo. Confiamos en que cada uno de ustedes, nuestros lectores, se encuentre bien y siga confiando en el Señor. La pandemia nos ha ocasionado cierto retraso, junto con algunos asuntos personales que hemos estado resolviendo, así que este número les llega con algo de demora. Les pedimos disculpas…. Tenemos previsto imprimir el próximo número dentro de los próximos meses para retomar el ritmo habitual.

En el editorial del número anterior, escribí sobre un artículo de noticias poco conocido que revelaba que muchas personas de todo el mundo se habían sorprendido por los resultados positivos que experimentaban al tener que quedarse en casa durante el comienzo de la pandemia de COVID-19. Disfrutaban del tiempo en familia. Encontraban compañerismo al afrontar juntos este desafío. Se entusiasmaban con la aventura de descubrir nuevas maneras de funcionar y sobrevivir. Y encontraban una visión y un propósito renovados en la vida.

Sin embargo, con el paso del tiempo, esto parece haber durado poco para todos los que no tenían un nivel más profundo de estabilidad en sus vidas. Para muchas personas, después de transcurrido un período de tiempo variable, la realidad ha comenzado a imponerse. Algunos han perdido el trabajo. Algunos han perdido a seres queridos. Algunos han pasado por un período de enfermedad. Muchos han sufrido por la falta de compañía de otros seres humanos. Para las personas mayores que viven en residencias de ancianos y centros de vida asistida, y para quienes necesitan ser hospitalizados, la vida se ha convertido, sin duda, en una existencia muy solitaria, ya que la mayoría de estos lugares no ha permitido que entren visitantes.

El mundo está intentando encontrar cualquier manera posible de sobrellevar la situación y sobrevivir. Hay líneas para conferencias telefónicas. Hay chats. Hay seminarios web dedicados al tema. Muchos están haciendo su parte para llenar los vacíos que esta pandemia ha creado en la vida de quienes los rodean.

Al tomar distancia para obtener una perspectiva más clara de los acontecimientos que se van desarrollando a raíz de la pandemia, los últimos meses han sido un período de cambio e incertidumbre para la mayoría. Está el futuro económico: «¿Tengo un empleo seguro?», «¿Qué pasa con mis cuentas?», «¿Qué pasa con mi vivienda?». Luego está la naturaleza sumamente politizada de numerosos asuntos: la desigualdad racial, las teorías conspirativas sobre la pandemia y las medidas obligatorias del gobierno con respecto a nuestra respuesta a la pandemia del virus. A esto se suma la polarización política en nuestro país: quién dice la verdad sobre los distintos asuntos y quién será la mejor opción para dirigir el país después de las próximas elecciones.

A pesar de todo lo demás que está ocurriendo, parece que todos tienen en mente el virus y sus efectos. El 15 de agosto de 2020, CNN publicó un artículo escrito por Ryan Prior y titulado: «1 DE CADA 4 JÓVENES AFIRMA TENER PENSAMIENTOS SUICIDAS». Quienes deseen leer el artículo pueden encontrarlo aquí:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

Este artículo reconoce que hubo efectos positivos durante el inicio de la pandemia y las consiguientes órdenes de quedarse en casa. Continúa diciendo que, con el paso del tiempo, este acontecimiento es distinto de la mayoría de los sucesos del pasado, como los tornados, los huracanes, los terremotos e incluso las circunstancias del 11 de septiembre de 2001. La mayoría de estos sucesos han sido localizados y breves en sus efectos destructivos, mientras que la pandemia de COVID-19 se ha prolongado tanto que se está convirtiendo en una forma de vida, sin un final a la vista, y su comienzo se va desvaneciendo en nuestro pasado olvidadizo.

Según el artículo de noticias, los CDC han publicado datos de una encuesta realizada para determinar los efectos negativos de la pandemia. A continuación, algunos datos tal como se presentan en el artículo:

  • Los pensamientos suicidas han aumentado entre los jóvenes desde el año pasado
  • Hasta una de cada cuatro personas de entre 18 y 24 años había considerado seriamente el suicidio en los 30 días anteriores a la encuesta (los investigadores encuestaron a 5.412 adultos en EE. UU. entre el 24 y el 30 de junio).
  • En la población general de EE. UU. … el 11 % de los adultos encuestados había considerado seriamente el suicidio en los 30 días anteriores a completar la encuesta.
  • El número de estadounidenses que informan tener síntomas de ansiedad es tres veces mayor que en esta misma época del año pasado, dijeron los CDC.
  • Los resultados reflejan una nación cada vez más inquieta.

Qué triste es reflexionar sobre esta realidad. Al leer este artículo de noticias, no pude evitar preguntarme si los porcentajes son los mismos en la iglesia que en el mundo. Me vino a la mente un versículo de las Escrituras: Si solamente en esta vida esperamos en Cristo, somos los más dignos de lástima de todos los hombres –1 Corintios 15:19. Como cristianos…

  • …¡tenemos ESPERANZA!
  • …¡¡tenemos ESPERANZA EN CRISTO!!
  • …¡¡¡tenemos ESPERANZA tanto EN ESTA VIDA como PARA LA ETERNIDAD!!!

Al considerar todo esto, deberíamos tener una sonrisa en el rostro, esperanza en el corazón y una palabra de aliento en los labios para todos aquellos con quienes nos relacionamos. Seamos especialmente observadores al interactuar con las personas que nos rodean: familiares, amigos e incluso desconocidos. Quién sabe, quizá nuestro vecino de al lado se sienta completamente solo y desanimado. O tal vez nuestro mejor amigo de la iglesia esté luchando con una carga que parece más de lo que puede soportar. Al orar, podemos pedirle a Dios que traiga a nuestra mente a personas que se beneficiarían de que las ayudáramos de una u otra manera. Nunca sabemos cuándo nuestra sonrisa o una palabra de aliento ayudará a cambiar el destino eterno de alguien.

Hermanos, si alguno fuere sorprendido en alguna falta, vosotros que sois espirituales, restaurad al tal con espíritu de mansedumbre, considerándote a ti mismo, no sea que tú también seas tentado. Sobrellevad los unos las cargas de los otros, y cumplid así la ley de Cristo. Porque si alguno se cree ser algo, no siendo nada, a sí mismo se engaña. Así que cada uno someta a prueba su propia obra, y entonces tendrá motivo de gloriarse solo respecto de sí mismo, y no en otro. Porque cada uno llevará su propia carga –Gálatas 6:1-5.

No os ha sobrevenido ninguna tentación que no sea humana; pero fiel es Dios, que no permitirá que seáis tentados más de lo que podéis soportar… –1 Corintios 10:13.

Hermanos míos, tened por sumo gozo cuando os halléis en diversas pruebas, sabiendo que la prueba de vuestra fe produce paciencia –Santiago 1:2-3.

En estos versículos veo varias cosas que Dios quiere que pongamos en práctica en nuestra vida.

  1. Dios no permitirá que seamos tentados más allá de lo que podemos soportar. Esto se basa en Su hecho, no en lo que sentimos.
  2. Cada uno de nosotros caerá en tentaciones, pero al ver la soberanía de Dios presente en nuestras pruebas, podemos descansar mientras «lo tenemos por sumo gozo».
  3. Cuando parece que nuestra fe está siendo puesta a prueba, a veces aparentemente casi hasta el punto de quebrarse, podemos tener la seguridad de que Dios está en medio de ello y de que está obrando algo conforme a Su voluntad.
  4. Dios permitirá que haya cargas en la vida de cada uno de nosotros y espera que cada uno de nosotros «lleve su propia carga».
  5. Dios permitirá que nuestros semejantes pasen por momentos difíciles, durante los cuales espera que veamos a nuestro hermano o hermana en dificultades y hagamos todo lo que podamos para aliviar su carga, mediante la oración, palabras de aliento o acciones de ayuda.

Para terminar, les dejo varios versículos que Pablo escribió a la iglesia de Galacia. No nos cansemos, pues, de hacer el bien; porque a su tiempo cosecharemos, si no desmayamos. Así que, según tengamos oportunidad, hagamos bien a todos, y mayormente a los de la familia de la fe. –Gálatas 6:9-10. Como extranjeros y peregrinos aquí en la tierra, no perdamos de vista nuestro Hogar eterno, nuestro Salvador compasivo, nuestro Dios soberano y nuestro Padre Abba.

It is August 2020, over four months since the coronavirus pandemic started, and it is still affecting our lives. People are still getting sick. The government and its decisions continue to be at the center of a lot of our conversations. The cause and cure are ongoing topics. The difference between those that believe the coronavirus to be a real threat and those that believe it to be primarily an agenda of political nature are becoming more distinct as this virus slowly makes its way through our communities, churches, and society as a whole.

The mandates being issued by the governors of many of our states are forcing God’s people to make decisions on issues we have not faced before. At what point does the government cross the line of interfering in our religious freedoms by putting in place mandates that will affect how we do church? How should we relate to the differences among us concerning the mandates? Should we or should we not follow them? What should our attitude be towards those in authority when we feel that they are doing things that are politically motivated? What should we do with all the “unbelievable things” that are being passed around, even from well-meaning Christians from what they would consider to be very valid and from legitimate sources? What should we do with the many, what seem to be, “conspiracy theories” that are being propagated and peddled from one person to another in such a manner that makes it hard to refute them? I, in no way, am going to attempt to answer how a church should relate to the specific mandates but would like to address some concerning attitudes and other responses that have been observed throughout our plain communities.

One of the most concerning issues is the attitude that people have had and are having toward the government. In 1 Peter, the apostle Peter calls us to “honor the king” and the Apostle Paul admonishes us in Romans 13 to be “subject to the higher Powers, for there is no power but of God”. The word honour, as used in 1 Peter 2, in reference to the king, means to “prize” or to “fix valuation upon.” A verse like this and others would indicate that when we speak of our government and, for that matter, others, our attitude should be one of respect. The words and the tone of voice we use should reflect that commitment. Our choice of words and the tone we use will speak volumes. They reflect our attitude.

I personally believe that we as the plain community have done a lot of damage to our “light” and “witness” by refusing to wear the mask in required public settings. But God looks deeper than our actions and we should too. The remarks like “no one will tell me I have to wear that thing” and others similar to that have their roots in a “lack of respect.” God clearly tells us, though we may not be able to always obey in every situation, respect and honor is always to be seen and heard in our attitudes and speech.

The apostle Paul is a good example of one who had a heart to honor those in authority and repented when he failed to do so. When Ananias the high priest asked the ones by him to smite him, he called the high priest a “whited wall”. When told that he had reviled the high priest, he was very quick to apologize for his wrong even though the high priest was wrong in asking them to hit him. It might remind us of the little saying, “Two wrongs do not make a right.”

Having a bad attitude because the government is making what we think are wrong decisions will not bring about right! As we find our way through these mandates, let’s make sure we do not sin against those in authority by speaking about them in a disrespectful manner. Let us repent of any bad attitudes and make sure our heart is in a position to honor and then the words and tone we use will convey the same.

Another area that is extremely hard to know how to respond to is that of all the negative information that is floating around surrounding Covid–19. Many of the plain community tend to distrust the government’s way of handling the situation. Because of this we are quick to believe and pass on negative information as fact. How do we know what is true and what is not? We need to be so careful, even when the information comes from what we believe to be a reliable source, because the more this negative information is passed along, the more folks will distrust the government. Case in point, there have been numerous deaths that were not directly connected to Covid–19; however, it was reported that Covid–19 was marked on the death certificate as being the cause of these deaths. After fact checking some of these supposed cases, it was found that some of these reports were not true. Since several reports have been verified as untrue, I no longer know what to believe. I think we should all be very careful what we do with the information we come across and do all we can to verify the information before passing it on as fact. If it is hard to believe, it is all the more important to check the facts or not pass it on until it has been proven.

Throughout this time period it seems that the conspiracy theories have just escalated. A lot of speculation surrounds the origin of Covid–19, the possible underlying motives, and secrecies the government has in how they are handling the whole Covid–19 dilemma. How do we know if the many propagated theories are true? If they are true, how will that affect the way I live for the other kingdom now? Will it change the way I live? Will it somehow help me prepare for these supposed difficulties that are coming?

In Luke 21, we have a verse talking about future events: “Men’s hearts failing them for fear of things that are coming on the earth.” Are we going to respond to the future in faith or in fear? The media proclaims Covid–19 to be a very dangerous, infectious virus. This perception has caused many in our world to start buying and hoarding for fear of things coming on the face of the earth. We now have articles and theories being peddled by many that seemingly will cause fear of the government and what they are planning to do and ultimately men’s hearts will fail for fear.

The Apostle Peter said that …God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7. Whether these claims are true or not, the Bible still calls us in Philippians to think on …whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report… –Philippians 4:8. To spend even a little time following these theories will have a negative and spiritually draining effect on our lives and the lives around us. Thinking about them not only promotes fear but also makes it even more difficult to respect and honor the government. In reality, some or many of these things may not even be true. As Christians we try to be a peaceful and trusting people, yet this tends to make us vulnerable to be quite gullible. We are quite willing to believe negative claims, allegations, and theories without checking the facts to see whether they could even be true or not. My appeal would be to continue to seek those things that are above, to think on the things that are noble and virtuous.

As believers, we are facing another challenge. The unity within our groups is being challenged in ways it has not been before. We differ in thought on how much the government should interfere in our services. Should we even be having church if the governor would rather that we would not? What about the wearing of masks in our services? Some feel one way and others think differently. These mandates and how we should respond to them can be quite controversial! Now, as much as ever before, we need to extend lots of grace as we sort these things through with each other. We must give some room to each other to understand and relate to it a bit differently. We need much grace with one another and dare not allow these things to become a point of contention. I believe God wants to use these difficulties to draw us closer to Him and each other, but the enemy of our souls is doing his best to have it destroy our love and commitment to each other. Let us seek peace and ensue it!

È agosto 2020, sono passati più di quattro mesi dall’inizio della pandemia di coronavirus e continua a influenzare le nostre vite. Le persone continuano ad ammalarsi. Il governo e le sue decisioni restano al centro di molte delle nostre conversazioni. Le cause e la cura continuano a essere argomenti di discussione. La differenza tra coloro che considerano il coronavirus una minaccia reale e coloro che lo ritengono principalmente parte di un programma di natura politica diventa sempre più marcata, mentre questo virus si fa lentamente strada nelle nostre comunità, nelle nostre chiese e nella società nel suo insieme.

Le disposizioni emanate dai governatori di molti dei nostri Stati costringono il popolo di Dio a prendere decisioni su questioni che non avevamo mai affrontato prima. Fino a che punto il governo oltrepassa il limite e interferisce con le nostre libertà religiose imponendo disposizioni che influiranno sul modo in cui celebriamo il culto? Come dovremmo rapportarci alle nostre differenze riguardo a queste disposizioni? Dovremmo seguirle oppure no? Quale dovrebbe essere il nostro atteggiamento verso chi è in autorità quando riteniamo che agisca per motivi politici? Che cosa dovremmo fare di tutte le «cose incredibili» che vengono diffuse, anche da cristiani benintenzionati, attraverso fonti che essi considerano molto valide e legittime? Che cosa dovremmo fare delle tante cosiddette «teorie del complotto» che vengono propagate e fatte circolare da una persona all’altra in modo tale che è difficile confutarle? Non intendo in alcun modo tentare di rispondere alla domanda su come una chiesa dovrebbe rapportarsi alle specifiche disposizioni, ma vorrei affrontare alcuni atteggiamenti preoccupanti e altre reazioni che sono stati osservati nelle nostre comunità anabattiste tradizionaliste.

Una delle questioni più preoccupanti è l’atteggiamento che le persone hanno avuto e continuano ad avere nei confronti del governo. In 1 Pietro, l’apostolo Pietro ci esorta a «onorare il re» e l’apostolo Paolo, in Romani 13, ci ammonisce a essere «sottomessi alle autorità superiori, perché non vi è autorità se non da parte di Dio». La parola «onorare», usata in 1 Pietro 2 in riferimento al re, significa «stimare» o «attribuire valore». Questo versetto e altri indicano che, quando parliamo del nostro governo e, del resto, anche degli altri, il nostro atteggiamento dovrebbe essere di rispetto. Le parole e il tono di voce che usiamo dovrebbero riflettere tale impegno. Le parole che scegliamo e il tono che adottiamo parlano molto chiaramente. Riflettono il nostro atteggiamento.

Personalmente credo che noi, come comunità anabattista tradizionalista, abbiamo danneggiato molto la nostra «luce» e la nostra «testimonianza» rifiutandoci di indossare la mascherina nei luoghi pubblici in cui era obbligatoria. Ma Dio guarda più a fondo delle nostre azioni, e dovremmo farlo anche noi. Osservazioni come «nessuno mi dirà che devo indossare quella cosa», e altre simili, hanno origine in una «mancanza di rispetto». Dio ci dice chiaramente che, anche se non sempre possiamo obbedire in ogni situazione, il rispetto e l’onore devono sempre essere visibili e udibili nei nostri atteggiamenti e nelle nostre parole.

L’apostolo Paolo è un buon esempio di persona che aveva il cuore disposto a onorare chi era in autorità e che si pentì quando non lo fece. Quando Anania, il sommo sacerdote, ordinò a quelli che gli stavano accanto di colpirlo, Paolo chiamò il sommo sacerdote «muro imbiancato». Quando gli fu fatto notare che aveva insultato il sommo sacerdote, si affrettò a scusarsi per il suo errore, benché il sommo sacerdote avesse sbagliato a ordinare loro di colpirlo. Questo può ricordarci il detto: «Due torti non fanno una ragione».

Avere un atteggiamento negativo perché il governo prende decisioni che a nostro avviso sono sbagliate non porterà a nulla di buono! Mentre cerchiamo di orientarci fra queste disposizioni, assicuriamoci di non peccare contro chi è in autorità parlando di loro in modo irrispettoso. Pentiamoci di ogni atteggiamento negativo e assicuriamoci che il nostro cuore sia disposto a onorare; così anche le parole e il tono che usiamo esprimeranno lo stesso rispetto.

Un altro ambito a cui è estremamente difficile sapere come reagire riguarda tutte le informazioni negative che circolano sul Covid-19. Molti appartenenti alle comunità anabattiste tradizionaliste tendono a diffidare del modo in cui il governo sta gestendo la situazione. Per questo siamo pronti a credere alle informazioni negative e a diffonderle come se fossero fatti. Come facciamo a sapere che cosa è vero e che cosa non lo è? Dobbiamo essere molto cauti, anche quando le informazioni provengono da una fonte che riteniamo affidabile, perché più queste informazioni negative vengono diffuse, più le persone diffideranno del governo. Per esempio, ci sono stati numerosi decessi non direttamente collegati al Covid-19; tuttavia, è stato riferito che il Covid-19 era indicato sui certificati di morte come causa di quei decessi. Dopo aver verificato alcuni di questi presunti casi, si è scoperto che alcune di queste notizie non erano vere. Poiché diverse notizie sono state verificate e risultate false, ormai non so più a che cosa credere. Penso che tutti dovremmo fare molta attenzione a come trattiamo le informazioni che ci capitano e fare tutto il possibile per verificarle prima di diffonderle come fatti. Se qualcosa è difficile da credere, è tanto più importante verificarne i fatti o non diffonderla finché non sia stata provata.

In questo periodo, sembra che le teorie del complotto siano soltanto aumentate. Circolano molte speculazioni sull’origine del Covid-19, sui possibili motivi sottostanti e sui segreti del governo riguardo al modo in cui sta gestendo l’intera questione del Covid-19. Come facciamo a sapere se le tante teorie diffuse sono vere? Se lo sono, in che modo influiranno sul modo in cui vivo ora per l’altro regno? Cambierà il mio modo di vivere? Mi aiuterà in qualche modo a prepararmi alle presunte difficoltà in arrivo?

In Luca 21 troviamo un versetto che parla di eventi futuri: «Gli uomini verranno meno per la paura e per l’attesa di ciò che starà per accadere sulla terra». Affronteremo il futuro con fede o con paura? I media descrivono il Covid-19 come un virus molto pericoloso e contagioso. Questa percezione ha indotto molti nel nostro mondo a cominciare a comprare e ad accumulare scorte per paura di ciò che accadrà sulla terra. Ora molti diffondono articoli e teorie che apparentemente instilleranno paura del governo e di ciò che sta progettando di fare, e alla fine gli uomini verranno meno per la paura.

L’apostolo Pietro disse che …Dio non ci ha dato uno spirito di paura, ma di forza, di amore e di saggezza –2 Timoteo 1:7. Che queste affermazioni siano vere o no, la Bibbia ci esorta comunque, in Filippesi, a pensare a …tutte le cose vere, tutte le cose onorevoli, tutte le cose giuste, tutte le cose pure, tutte le cose amabili, tutte le cose di buona reputazione… –Filippesi 4:8. Anche dedicare poco tempo a seguire queste teorie avrà un effetto negativo e spiritualmente debilitante sulla nostra vita e su quella di chi ci sta intorno. Pensarci non solo alimenta la paura, ma rende anche più difficile rispettare e onorare il governo. In realtà, alcune o molte di queste cose potrebbero non essere affatto vere. Come cristiani cerchiamo di essere un popolo pacifico e fiducioso, eppure questo tende a renderci piuttosto creduloni. Siamo pronti a credere ad affermazioni, accuse e teorie negative senza verificare i fatti per capire se possano davvero essere vere. Il mio appello è di continuare a cercare le cose di lassù e a pensare a ciò che è nobile e virtuoso.

Come credenti, stiamo affrontando un’altra sfida. L’unità all’interno dei nostri gruppi è messa alla prova in modi mai visti prima. Abbiamo opinioni diverse su quanto il governo dovrebbe interferire nelle nostre funzioni religiose. Dovremmo celebrare il culto anche se il governatore preferirebbe che non lo facessimo? E che dire dell’uso delle mascherine durante le nostre funzioni? Alcuni la pensano in un modo, altri diversamente. Queste disposizioni e il modo in cui dovremmo reagire possono suscitare molte controversie! Ora, più che mai, mentre cerchiamo insieme di fare chiarezza su queste questioni, dobbiamo dimostrarci molta grazia a vicenda. Dobbiamo lasciare spazio l’uno all’altro per comprendere la situazione e rapportarci ad essa in modo un po’ diverso. Dobbiamo mostrarci molta grazia a vicenda e non dobbiamo permettere che queste questioni diventino motivo di contesa. Credo che Dio voglia servirsi di queste difficoltà per avvicinarci a Lui e gli uni agli altri, ma il nemico delle nostre anime sta facendo del suo meglio per far sì che esse distruggano il nostro amore e il nostro impegno reciproco. Cerchiamo la pace e perseguiamola!

Ramona* was a little girl who was very busy and active. Like other four-year-old’s, there were a lot of things Ramona could do. She could ride a bike, climb a tree, wash dishes, write her name, and ride her pony all by herself. One of Ramona’s favorite things to do was to ride horses. Her family had two horses and a pony. How fun those evenings were when they would hitch their pony, Tony, to the cart, and the whole family would take turns riding. Or when Ramona and three of her sisters would pack onto Tony’s back and go for a ride.

There were lots of things Ramona could do, but sometimes she thought she could do more than she really could. And sometimes she thought she was bigger than she really was.

One beautiful Summer evening, some guests came to Ramona’s house. When guests came, that usually meant a fun time.

On this particular evening, after supper, Ramona’s older siblings were riding horses with the guests. It looked like so much fun as they trotted around the pond and through the lawn. Ramona wanted to ride too, but she had to wait her turn. While she waited, she played on the lawn with Clifford, the dog. She soon tired of that and went for a spin on her bike. Then an idea popped into her mind. She ran off to the pasture entrance and climbed up the gate. She liked to pretend she was a monkey, swinging on the bars and climbing up and down. Then she tried balancing on a bar and taking her hands off the gate. Her siblings and their guests were riding nearby. Ramona threw her arms into the air, and while balancing on the gate, yelled to the riders, “Look at me! Look at me!” She felt very big to be balancing on the gate. Suddenly, her foot slipped and, down she went, into the dust. She blinked with surprise and quickly jumped up, brushing off her dress. She looked around, embarrassed, but no one seemed to notice. She climbed back up the side of the gate and began playing again. Ramona grew impatient, waiting for her ride. No one seemed to remember that she wanted to ride the horses. She thought it would be fun to see how high she could balance on the gate, so she climbed as high as she dared. She wanted others to see how brave she was, so waving her arms, she shouted, “Hey everyone! Look at me!” But again, her foot slipped off the gate. This time, however, she narrowly escaped falling to the ground. Ramona’s dad saw her and walked over to her. “Ramona,” he said, “I want you to stay off the gate.”

Ramona got down and tried to find something else to do. After playing for a while, her father’s command to stay off the gate seemed to slip from her mind, and she started climbing on the gate again. Then Ramona’s older sister, Elise, walked over, and quietly told her, “Ramona, you shouldn’t be showing off to our guests.” Ramona didn’t like that advice. Into one ear and out the other it went. She assured herself that she wasn’t showing off! She was just… well, just playing.

She climbed up just as high as she could, and once again, she waved her arms in the air, crying, “Look at me, everyone!” Suddenly, before she knew what was happening, she had landed on the ground with a thud and began to cry at the top of her lungs. Sure, she felt some pain, but mostly she was shocked and ashamed.

Ramona’s father came over to her and picked her up, making sure she wasn’t badly hurt, and carried her to the house. It was yet light outside, and still early in the evening, but he took her upstairs to her bed.

Before putting her to bed, he talked with her. Ramona was still crying, and Papa attempted to dry her tears. “Ramona, listen, can you be quiet for a bit? Why do you think you fell?” She sniffled and shrugged her shoulders. Papa continued, “If you would have obeyed me, and stayed off the gate like I told you to, you would not have fallen. Elise also told you to stop showing off, but you didn’t listen. Do you know that showing off is really pride? The Bible says, Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

Ramona nodded her head. “Are you sorry for disobeying me, Ramona?” Papa asked. “Yes, Papa, I am sorry” she replied tearfully. Papa decided to let her fall and going to bed early be her punishment this time. Ramona would have preferred a spanking instead of needing to go to bed early, which was a great grief to her little heart. But it was good for her because it caused her to repent.

Ramona never forgot this lesson, partly because of her fall, and partly because she was sent to bed early and missed the fun of riding horses. Not only had she been proud in showing off, she had also been willfully disobedient to Papa.

Elise had written a tune to the verse that Papa had mentioned to Ramona. From then on, whenever Ramona sang that song, she remembered how true that verse proved to be for her.

Рамона* была маленькой девочкой, очень занятой и активной. Как и другие дети четырёх лет, она многое умела. Она могла кататься на велосипеде, лазить по деревьям, мыть посуду, писать своё имя и самостоятельно ездить верхом на пони. Одним из любимых занятий Рамоны была верховая езда. В семье было две лошади и пони. Как весело проходили те вечера, когда они запрягали пони Тони в повозку и вся семья по очереди каталась! А бывало, Рамона и три её сестры усаживались на спину Тони и отправлялись в поездку.

Рамона многое умела, но иногда ей казалось, что она может больше, чем на самом деле. А порой она думала, что она больше, чем была на самом деле.

Однажды прекрасным летним вечером к Рамоне домой пришли гости. Когда приходили гости, это обычно означало, что будет весело.

В тот вечер, после ужина, старшие братья и сёстры Рамоны катались верхом вместе с гостями. Казалось, это так весело — они рысцой объезжали пруд и скакали по лужайке. Рамоне тоже хотелось покататься, но ей пришлось ждать своей очереди. Пока она ждала, она играла на лужайке с собакой Клиффордом. Вскоре ей это наскучило, и она отправилась прокатиться на велосипеде. Тут ей пришла в голову одна мысль. Она побежала к входу на пастбище и взобралась на ворота. Ей нравилось воображать себя обезьянкой: раскачиваться на перекладинах и лазить вверх и вниз. Потом она попробовала удержать равновесие на перекладине, отпустив руки. Её братья и сёстры с гостями катались неподалёку. Рамона вскинула руки и, балансируя на воротах, крикнула всадникам: «Посмотрите на меня! Посмотрите!» Она чувствовала себя такой большой, когда удерживала равновесие на воротах. Вдруг её нога соскользнула, и она шлёпнулась в пыль. Удивлённо моргнув, она быстро вскочила и отряхнула платье. Она смущённо огляделась, но, похоже, никто ничего не заметил. Она снова взобралась на ворота и принялась играть. Рамона начала терять терпение, ожидая своей очереди покататься. Казалось, никто не помнил, что ей тоже хотелось покататься на лошадях. Ей захотелось проверить, как высоко она сможет удержать равновесие на воротах, и она взобралась так высоко, как только осмелилась. Ей хотелось, чтобы остальные увидели, какая она храбрая, поэтому она замахала руками и крикнула: «Эй, все! Посмотрите на меня!» Но её нога снова соскользнула с ворот. На этот раз, однако, она едва не упала на землю. Папа увидел её и подошёл. «Рамона, — сказал он, — я хочу, чтобы ты не лазила на ворота».

Рамона слезла и попыталась найти себе другое занятие. Поиграв немного, она забыла о папином приказе не лазить на ворота и снова стала на них взбираться. Тут подошла её старшая сестра Элиз и тихо сказала ей: «Рамона, не надо выпендриваться перед нашими гостями». Рамоне не понравился этот совет. В одно ухо влетело, в другое вылетело. Она убеждала себя, что вовсе не выпендривается! Она просто… ну, просто играла.

Она забралась так высоко, как только могла, и снова замахала руками, крича: «Посмотрите на меня, все!» Вдруг, прежде чем она поняла, что происходит, она с грохотом приземлилась на землю и во всё горло разрыдалась. Да, ей было больно, но больше всего она была потрясена и пристыжена.

Папа подошёл к ней и поднял на руки, проверив, не сильно ли она ушиблась, а затем отнёс её в дом. На улице ещё было светло, и вечер только начинался, но он отвёл её наверх, в кровать.

Прежде чем уложить её спать, он поговорил с ней. Рамона всё ещё плакала, и папа попытался вытереть ей слёзы. «Рамона, послушай, помолчи немного, пожалуйста. Как ты думаешь, почему ты упала?» Она всхлипнула и пожала плечами. Папа продолжил: «Если бы ты послушалась меня и не лазила на ворота, как я тебе сказал, ты бы не упала. Элиз тоже велела тебе перестать выпендриваться, но ты её не послушала. Знаешь ли ты, что хвастовство на самом деле — это гордость? В Библии сказано: «Погибели предшествует гордость, и падению — надменный дух» — Притчи 16:18.

Рамона кивнула. «Ты сожалеешь, что ослушалась меня, Рамона?» — спросил папа. «Да, папа, сожалею», — со слезами ответила она. На этот раз папа решил, что её наказанием будет само падение и ранний отход ко сну. Рамона предпочла бы получить шлепок, а не ложиться спать так рано, и это было большим горем для её маленького сердечка. Но это пошло ей на пользу, потому что побудило её раскаяться.

Рамона никогда не забыла этот урок — отчасти из-за падения, а отчасти потому, что её отправили спать пораньше, и она пропустила весёлую верховую прогулку. Она не только гордилась, стараясь показать себя, но и сознательно ослушалась папу.

Элиз сочинила мелодию на стих, который папа прочитал Рамоне. С тех пор, когда бы Рамона ни пела эту песню, она вспоминала, насколько истинным оказался для неё этот стих.

Ramona got down and tried to find something else to do. After playing for a while, her father’s command to stay off the gate seemed to slip from her mind, and she started climbing on the gate again. Then Ramona’s older sister, Elise, walked over, and quietly told her, “Ramona, you shouldn’t be showing off to our guests.” Ramona didn’t like that advice. Into one ear and out the other it went. She assured herself that she wasn’t showing off! She was just… well, just playing.

She climbed up just as high as she could, and once again, she waved her arms in the air, crying, “Look at me, everyone!” Suddenly, before she knew what was happening, she had landed on the ground with a thud and began to cry at the top of her lungs. Sure, she felt some pain, but mostly she was shocked and ashamed.

Ramona’s father came over to her and picked her up, making sure she wasn’t badly hurt, and carried her to the house. It was yet light outside, and still early in the evening, but he took her upstairs to her bed.

Before putting her to bed, he talked with her. Ramona was still crying, and Papa attempted to dry her tears. “Ramona, listen, can you be quiet for a bit? Why do you think you fell?” She sniffled and shrugged her shoulders. Papa continued, “If you would have obeyed me, and stayed off the gate like I told you to, you would not have fallen. Elise also told you to stop showing off, but you didn’t listen. Do you know that showing off is really pride? The Bible says, Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

Ramona nodded her head. “Are you sorry for disobeying me, Ramona?” Papa asked. “Yes, Papa, I am sorry” she replied tearfully. Papa decided to let her fall and going to bed early be her punishment this time. Ramona would have preferred a spanking instead of needing to go to bed early, which was a great grief to her little heart. But it was good for her because it caused her to repent.

Ramona never forgot this lesson, partly because of her fall, and partly because she was sent to bed early and missed the fun of riding horses. Not only had she been proud in showing off, she had also been willfully disobedient to Papa.

Elise had written a tune to the verse that Papa had mentioned to Ramona. From then on, whenever Ramona sang that song, she remembered how true that verse proved to be for her.

라모나*는 늘 바쁘게 움직이며 활발한 어린 소녀였습니다. 다른 네 살 아이들처럼 라모나도 할 수 있는 일이 많았습니다. 자전거를 타고, 나무에 오르고, 설거지를 하고, 자기 이름을 쓰고, 조랑말을 혼자 탈 수 있었습니다. 라모나가 가장 좋아하는 일 가운데 하나는 말을 타는 것이었습니다. 가족은 말 두 마리와 조랑말 한 마리를 키웠습니다. 저녁이면 조랑말 토니를 수레에 매고 온 가족이 번갈아 타던 시간은 얼마나 즐거웠는지요. 라모나와 언니들 셋이 토니 등에 다 같이 올라타고 한 바퀴 타러 나갈 때도 그랬습니다.

라모나가 할 수 있는 일은 많았지만, 때로는 실제로 할 수 있는 것보다 더 많이 할 수 있다고 생각했습니다. 또 실제보다 자신이 더 큰 아이라고 생각할 때도 있었습니다.

어느 아름다운 여름 저녁, 손님들이 라모나의 집에 왔습니다. 손님이 오면 대개 즐거운 시간을 보내곤 했습니다.

그날 저녁 식사 후, 라모나의 손위 형제자매들은 손님들과 함께 말을 타고 있었습니다. 연못 주위를 돌고 잔디밭을 가로질러 말을 타는 모습은 무척 재미있어 보였습니다. 라모나도 타고 싶었지만 차례를 기다려야 했습니다. 기다리는 동안 개 클리퍼드와 잔디밭에서 놀았습니다. 이내 그 놀이가 싫증 나자 자전거를 타고 한 바퀴 돌았습니다. 그러다 문득 한 가지 생각이 떠올랐습니다. 목장 입구로 달려가 문 위로 올라갔습니다. 원숭이 흉내를 내며 문살을 잡고 흔들고 오르내리는 것을 좋아했습니다. 그러고는 문살 위에서 균형을 잡고 두 손을 놓아 보았습니다. 형제자매들과 손님들은 가까이에서 말을 타고 있었습니다. 라모나는 팔을 허공에 벌리고 문 위에서 균형을 잡은 채 말을 탄 사람들에게 소리쳤습니다. “나 좀 봐! 나 좀 봐!” 문 위에서 균형을 잡고 있으니 자신이 아주 큰 아이가 된 것 같았습니다. 갑자기 발이 미끄러져 먼지바닥으로 떨어졌습니다. 놀라 눈을 깜빡인 라모나는 얼른 일어나 옷에 묻은 먼지를 털었습니다. 부끄러워 주위를 둘러보았지만 아무도 눈치채지 못한 듯했습니다. 다시 문 옆으로 기어 올라가 놀이를 계속했습니다. 라모나는 차례를 기다리다 점점 조바심이 났습니다. 말을 타고 싶어 한다는 것을 아무도 기억하지 못하는 듯했습니다. 문 위에서 얼마나 높이까지 균형을 잡을 수 있는지 보는 것도 재미있을 것 같아, 용기를 낼 수 있는 데까지 올라갔습니다. 자신이 얼마나 용감한지 다른 사람들에게 보여 주고 싶어서 팔을 흔들며 소리쳤습니다. “얘들아, 나 좀 봐!” 하지만 이번에도 발이 문에서 미끄러졌습니다. 그러나 이번에는 간신히 땅에 떨어지는 것을 피했습니다. 라모나의 아빠가 그 모습을 보고 다가왔습니다. “라모나,” 아빠가 말했습니다. “문 위에 올라가지 말아라.”

라모나는 내려와 다른 할 일을 찾아보았습니다. 한동안 놀고 나자 문에 올라가지 말라는 아빠의 말이 머릿속에서 사라진 듯했고, 다시 문을 타고 오르기 시작했습니다. 그러자 언니 엘리스가 다가와 조용히 말했습니다. “라모나, 손님들 앞에서 잘난 체하면 안 돼.” 라모나는 그 충고가 마음에 들지 않았습니다. 한 귀로 듣고 한 귀로 흘려보냈습니다. 자기는 잘난 체하는 게 아니라고 스스로 다짐했습니다! 그저… 뭐랄까, 그냥 놀고 있을 뿐이었습니다.

라모나는 할 수 있는 한 가장 높이 올라가 다시 팔을 허공에 흔들며 외쳤습니다. “얘들아, 나 좀 봐!” 갑자기 무슨 일이 일어나는지 알아차리기도 전에 쿵 소리를 내며 땅에 떨어졌고, 목청껏 울기 시작했습니다. 물론 아프기도 했지만, 무엇보다도 놀라고 부끄러웠습니다.

라모나의 아빠가 다가와 라모나를 안아 올렸습니다. 크게 다치지 않았는지 살핀 뒤 집으로 데려갔습니다. 아직 밖은 밝았고 저녁도 이른 시간이었지만, 아빠는 라모나를 위층 침대로 데려갔습니다.

아빠는 라모나를 재우기 전에 이야기를 나누었습니다. 라모나는 여전히 울고 있었고, 아빠는 눈물을 닦아 주려 했습니다. “라모나, 잘 들어 보렴. 잠깐 조용히 할 수 있겠니? 왜 떨어졌다고 생각하니?” 라모나는 훌쩍이며 어깨를 으쓱했습니다. 아빠가 말을 이었습니다. “내 말을 듣고 내가 말한 대로 문에 올라가지 않았더라면 떨어지지 않았을 거야. 엘리스도 잘난 체하지 말라고 했지만, 넌 듣지 않았지. 잘난 체하는 것이 사실은 교만이라는 걸 아니? 성경에는 이렇게 쓰여 있단다. 교만은 패망에 앞서고, 거만한 마음은 넘어짐에 앞선다 –잠언 16:18.

라모나는 고개를 끄덕였습니다. “라모나, 아빠 말을 듣지 않은 걸 미안하게 생각하니?” 아빠가 물었습니다. “네, 아빠. 죄송해요.” 라모나가 눈물을 흘리며 대답했습니다. 아빠는 이번에는 라모나가 떨어진 일과 일찍 잠자리에 드는 일을 벌로 삼기로 했습니다. 라모나는 일찍 잠자리에 드는 대신 매를 맞는 편이 나았을 것입니다. 일찍 자야 한다는 것은 어린 라모나의 마음에 큰 슬픔이었기 때문입니다. 하지만 그 일은 라모나가 회개하게 했으므로 좋은 일이었습니다.

라모나는 이 교훈을 결코 잊지 않았습니다. 일부는 떨어졌기 때문이고, 일부는 일찍 잠자리에 들어 말을 타는 즐거움을 놓쳤기 때문이었습니다. 라모나는 잘난 체하며 교만했을 뿐 아니라, 아빠의 말을 고의로 듣지 않았습니다.

엘리스는 아빠가 라모나에게 들려준 구절에 곡을 붙였습니다. 그 뒤로 라모나는 그 노래를 부를 때마다 그 구절이 자기에게 얼마나 참된 말인지 떠올렸습니다.

라모나가 부른 노래는 이렇습니다.

It is August 2020, over four months since the coronavirus pandemic started, and it is still affecting our lives. People are still getting sick. The government and its decisions continue to be at the center of a lot of our conversations. The cause and cure are ongoing topics. The difference between those that believe the coronavirus to be a real threat and those that believe it to be primarily an agenda of political nature are becoming more distinct as this virus slowly makes its way through our communities, churches, and society as a whole.

The mandates being issued by the governors of many of our states are forcing God’s people to make decisions on issues we have not faced before. At what point does the government cross the line of interfering in our religious freedoms by putting in place mandates that will affect how we do church? How should we relate to the differences among us concerning the mandates? Should we or should we not follow them? What should our attitude be towards those in authority when we feel that they are doing things that are politically motivated? What should we do with all the “unbelievable things” that are being passed around, even from well-meaning Christians from what they would consider to be very valid and from legitimate sources? What should we do with the many, what seem to be, “conspiracy theories” that are being propagated and peddled from one person to another in such a manner that makes it hard to refute them? I, in no way, am going to attempt to answer how a church should relate to the specific mandates but would like to address some concerning attitudes and other responses that have been observed throughout our plain communities.

One of the most concerning issues is the attitude that people have had and are having toward the government. In 1 Peter, the apostle Peter calls us to “honor the king” and the Apostle Paul admonishes us in Romans 13 to be “subject to the higher Powers, for there is no power but of God”. The word honour, as used in 1 Peter 2, in reference to the king, means to “prize” or to “fix valuation upon.” A verse like this and others would indicate that when we speak of our government and, for that matter, others, our attitude should be one of respect. The words and the tone of voice we use should reflect that commitment. Our choice of words and the tone we use will speak volumes. They reflect our attitude.

I personally believe that we as the plain community have done a lot of damage to our “light” and “witness” by refusing to wear the mask in required public settings. But God looks deeper than our actions and we should too. The remarks like “no one will tell me I have to wear that thing” and others similar to that have their roots in a “lack of respect.” God clearly tells us, though we may not be able to always obey in every situation, respect and honor is always to be seen and heard in our attitudes and speech.

The apostle Paul is a good example of one who had a heart to honor those in authority and repented when he failed to do so. When Ananias the high priest asked the ones by him to smite him, he called the high priest a “whited wall”. When told that he had reviled the high priest, he was very quick to apologize for his wrong even though the high priest was wrong in asking them to hit him. It might remind us of the little saying, “Two wrongs do not make a right.”

Having a bad attitude because the government is making what we think are wrong decisions will not bring about right! As we find our way through these mandates, let’s make sure we do not sin against those in authority by speaking about them in a disrespectful manner. Let us repent of any bad attitudes and make sure our heart is in a position to honor and then the words and tone we use will convey the same.

Another area that is extremely hard to know how to respond to is that of all the negative information that is floating around surrounding Covid–19. Many of the plain community tend to distrust the government’s way of handling the situation. Because of this we are quick to believe and pass on negative information as fact. How do we know what is true and what is not? We need to be so careful, even when the information comes from what we believe to be a reliable source, because the more this negative information is passed along, the more folks will distrust the government. Case in point, there have been numerous deaths that were not directly connected to Covid–19; however, it was reported that Covid–19 was marked on the death certificate as being the cause of these deaths. After fact checking some of these supposed cases, it was found that some of these reports were not true. Since several reports have been verified as untrue, I no longer know what to believe. I think we should all be very careful what we do with the information we come across and do all we can to verify the information before passing it on as fact. If it is hard to believe, it is all the more important to check the facts or not pass it on until it has been proven.

Throughout this time period it seems that the conspiracy theories have just escalated. A lot of speculation surrounds the origin of Covid–19, the possible underlying motives, and secrecies the government has in how they are handling the whole Covid–19 dilemma. How do we know if the many propagated theories are true? If they are true, how will that affect the way I live for the other kingdom now? Will it change the way I live? Will it somehow help me prepare for these supposed difficulties that are coming?

In Luke 21, we have a verse talking about future events: “Men’s hearts failing them for fear of things that are coming on the earth.” Are we going to respond to the future in faith or in fear? The media proclaims Covid–19 to be a very dangerous, infectious virus. This perception has caused many in our world to start buying and hoarding for fear of things coming on the face of the earth. We now have articles and theories being peddled by many that seemingly will cause fear of the government and what they are planning to do and ultimately men’s hearts will fail for fear.

The Apostle Peter said that …God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7. Whether these claims are true or not, the Bible still calls us in Philippians to think on …whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report… –Philippians 4:8. To spend even a little time following these theories will have a negative and spiritually draining effect on our lives and the lives around us. Thinking about them not only promotes fear but also makes it even more difficult to respect and honor the government. In reality, some or many of these things may not even be true. As Christians we try to be a peaceful and trusting people, yet this tends to make us vulnerable to be quite gullible. We are quite willing to believe negative claims, allegations, and theories without checking the facts to see whether they could even be true or not. My appeal would be to continue to seek those things that are above, to think on the things that are noble and virtuous.

As believers, we are facing another challenge. The unity within our groups is being challenged in ways it has not been before. We differ in thought on how much the government should interfere in our services. Should we even be having church if the governor would rather that we would not? What about the wearing of masks in our services? Some feel one way and others think differently. These mandates and how we should respond to them can be quite controversial! Now, as much as ever before, we need to extend lots of grace as we sort these things through with each other. We must give some room to each other to understand and relate to it a bit differently. We need much grace with one another and dare not allow these things to become a point of contention. I believe God wants to use these difficulties to draw us closer to Him and each other, but the enemy of our souls is doing his best to have it destroy our love and commitment to each other. Let us seek peace and ensue it!

אוגוסט 2020. חלפו יותר מארבעה חודשים מאז שהחלה מגפת הקורונה, והיא עדיין משפיעה על חיינו. אנשים עדיין חולים. הממשלה והחלטותיה ממשיכות לעמוד במרכזן של רבות משיחותינו. הגורמים למחלה והתרופה לה ממשיכים להיות נושאים לדיון. ההבדל בין מי שמאמינים שהקורונה היא איום ממשי לבין מי שסבורים שהיא בעיקר חלק מאג׳נדה פוליטית הולך ומתחדד, בזמן שהנגיף מתפשט אט־אט בקהילותינו, בכנסיותינו ובחברה כולה.

ההנחיות שמוציאים מושלי רבות ממדינותינו מאלצות את עם אלוהים לקבל החלטות בסוגיות שלא נדרשנו להתמודד איתן בעבר. באיזה שלב חוצה הממשלה את הגבול ופוגעת בחירויות הדת שלנו, כשהיא קובעת הנחיות שישפיעו על האופן שבו אנו מקיימים את תפילותינו? כיצד עלינו להתייחס לחילוקי הדעות בינינו בנוגע להנחיות? האם עלינו לציית להן או לא? כיצד עלינו לנהוג כלפי בעלי הסמכות כשאנו מרגישים שמעשיהם מונעים משיקולים פוליטיים? מה עלינו לעשות עם כל אותם ״דברים שלא ייאמנו״ שמופצים, אפילו בידי נוצרים בעלי כוונות טובות, מתוך מקורות שהם מחשיבים לאמינים ולגיטימיים מאוד? מה עלינו לעשות עם שלל מה שנראה כ״תיאוריות קונספירציה״, המופצות ומועברות מאדם לאדם באופן שמקשה להפריך אותן? איני מתכוון כלל לנסות להשיב כיצד על כנסייה להתייחס להנחיות הספציפיות, אך ברצוני לדון בכמה גישות מדאיגות ובתגובות אחרות שנצפו בקהילותינו השמרניות.

אחד הנושאים המדאיגים ביותר הוא היחס של אנשים כלפי הממשלה, בעבר ובהווה. באיגרת פטרוס הראשונה קורא לנו השליח פטרוס ״לכבד את המלך״, והשליח פאולוס מזהיר אותנו ברומים י״ג להיות ״כפופים לשלטונות העליונים, כי אין שלטון אלא מאת אלוהים״. המילה ״כבוד״, כפי שהיא משמשת בפטרוס א׳ ב׳ בהתייחס למלך, פירושה ״להוקיר״ או ״לקבוע ערך״. פסוק כזה ואחרים מלמדים שכאשר אנו מדברים על ממשלתנו, ולמעשה גם על אחרים, עלינו לנהוג בכבוד. המילים והטון שבהם אנו משתמשים צריכים לשקף את המחויבות הזאת. לבחירת המילים שלנו ולטון שבו אנו מדברים יש משמעות רבה. הם משקפים את גישתנו.

אני אישית מאמין שאנחנו, בני הקהילה השמרנית, פגענו רבות ב״אור״ וב״עדות״ שלנו בכך שסירבנו לעטות מסכה במקומות ציבוריים שבהם הדבר נדרש. אך אלוהים מתבונן עמוק יותר ממעשינו, וגם אנחנו צריכים לעשות זאת. אמירות כמו ״אף אחד לא יגיד לי שאני חייב ללבוש את הדבר הזה״ ואמירות דומות נובעות מ״חוסר כבוד״. אלוהים אומר לנו בבירור, שאף כי לא תמיד נוכל לציית בכל מצב, עלינו תמיד להפגין כבוד ולנהוג בו הן בגישתנו והן בדיבורנו.

השליח פאולוס הוא דוגמה טובה לאדם שרצה בלבו לכבד את בעלי הסמכות, והתחרט כשלא עשה זאת. כשחנניה הכוהן הגדול ציווה על העומדים לידו להכות את פאולוס, הוא כינה את הכוהן הגדול ״קיר מסויד״. כשאמרו לו שהוא גידף את הכוהן הגדול, הוא מיהר להתנצל על עוול שעשה, אף שהכוהן הגדול טעה כשציווה להכות אותו. הדבר עשוי להזכיר לנו את האמרה: ״שתי עוולות אינן יוצרות צדק״.

גישה רעה מפני שהממשלה מקבלת החלטות שלדעתנו שגויות לא תביא לתוצאה נכונה! בעודנו מתמודדים עם ההנחיות האלה, נוודא שאיננו חוטאים נגד בעלי הסמכות בכך שאנו מדברים עליהם בחוסר כבוד. הבה נתחרט על כל גישה רעה ונוודא שלבנו נכון לכבד; אז גם המילים והטון שלנו ישקפו זאת.

תחום נוסף שקשה מאוד לדעת כיצד להגיב בו הוא כל המידע השלילי שמופץ סביב קוביד־19. רבים בקהילה השמרנית נוטים לחשוד באופן שבו הממשלה מטפלת במצב. בשל כך אנו ממהרים להאמין למידע שלילי ולהעבירו הלאה כאילו היה עובדה. כיצד נדע מה אמת ומה לא? עלינו להיזהר מאוד, גם כשהמידע מגיע ממקור שאנו מאמינים שהוא אמין, משום שככל שמפיצים את המידע השלילי הזה יותר, כך יותר אנשים יאבדו אמון בממשלה. דוגמה לכך: היו מקרי מוות רבים שלא היו קשורים ישירות לקוביד־19; עם זאת, דווח כי קוביד־19 צוין בתעודת הפטירה כסיבת המוות. לאחר בדיקת עובדות של כמה מהמקרים הנטענים האלה, התברר שחלק מהדיווחים אינם נכונים. מאחר שכמה מהדיווחים הוכחו כלא נכונים, איני יודע עוד למה להאמין. אני חושב שעל כולנו להיזהר מאוד במה שאנו עושים עם המידע שאנו נתקלים בו, ולעשות כל שביכולתנו כדי לאמתו לפני שאנו מעבירים אותו הלאה כעובדה. אם קשה להאמין לו, חשוב על אחת כמה וכמה לבדוק את העובדות או לא להעביר אותו הלאה עד שיוכח.

נדמה שבתקופה הזאת תיאוריות הקונספירציה רק הלכו והתרבו. יש ספקולציות רבות סביב מקורו של קוביד־19, מניעים אפשריים נסתרים, והסודות שהממשלה שומרת באשר לאופן שבו היא מטפלת בכל המשבר של קוביד־19. איך נדע אם התיאוריות הרבות שמופצות נכונות? אם הן נכונות, כיצד הדבר ישפיע על האופן שבו אחיה מעתה למען המלכות האחרת? האם הוא ישנה את אורח חיי? האם הוא יעזור לי איכשהו להתכונן לקשיים הנטענים שעומדים לבוא?

בלוקס כ״א יש פסוק המדבר על אירועים עתידיים: ״לבבות בני האדם ייכשלו מאימה מפני הדברים העתידים לבוא על העולם״. האם נגיב לעתיד באמונה או בפחד? אמצעי התקשורת מציגים את קוביד־19 כנגיף מסוכן ומדבק מאוד. תפיסה זו גרמה לרבים בעולמנו להתחיל לקנות ולאגור מתוך פחד מפני הדברים שעומדים לבוא על פני האדמה. כעת מופצים בידי רבים מאמרים ותיאוריות שלכאורה יגרמו לפחד מפני הממשלה ומפני מה שהיא מתכננת לעשות, ובסופו של דבר לבבות בני האדם ייכשלו מאימה.

השליח פטרוס אמר ש…אלוהים לא נתן לנו רוח של פחד, אלא של גבורה, אהבה ומשמעת – טימותיאוס ב׳ א׳ 7. בין אם הטענות האלה נכונות ובין אם לאו, התנ״ך עדיין קורא לנו באיגרת אל הפיליפים לחשוב על …כל אשר אמת, כל אשר נכבד, כל אשר צודק, כל אשר טהור, כל אשר נעים, כל אשר לשמו הטוב… – פיליפים ד׳ 8. אפילו זמן קצר של עיסוק בתיאוריות האלה ישפיע על חיינו ועל חיי הסובבים אותנו לרעה וירוקן אותנו מבחינה רוחנית. העיסוק בהן לא רק מעודד פחד, אלא גם מקשה עוד יותר לכבד את הממשלה. למעשה, ייתכן שחלק מהדברים האלה, או רבים מהם, כלל אינם נכונים. כנוצרים אנו משתדלים להיות עם של שלום ואמון, אך הדבר נוטה להפוך אותנו לפתי־מאמינים למדי. אנו מוכנים למדי להאמין לטענות שליליות, להאשמות ולתיאוריות בלי לבדוק את העובדות כדי לראות אם הן בכלל יכולות להיות נכונות. בקשתי היא שנמשיך לבקש את הדברים אשר למעלה, ולחשוב על הדברים הנעלים והטובים.

כמאמינים, אנו ניצבים בפני אתגר נוסף. האחדות בתוך הקבוצות שלנו עומדת למבחן בדרכים שלא חווינו בעבר. אנו חלוקים בדעתנו בשאלה עד כמה על הממשלה להתערב באספות התפילה שלנו. האם עלינו בכלל לקיים תפילות אם המושל מעדיף שלא נעשה זאת? ומה באשר לעטיית מסכות באספות שלנו? יש הסבורים כך ויש החושבים אחרת. ההנחיות האלה והדרך שבה עלינו להגיב להן עלולות להיות שנויות מאוד במחלוקת! כעת, יותר מאי־פעם, עלינו לנהוג זה בזה בחסד רב בעודנו מבררים את הדברים יחד. עלינו לאפשר זה לזה מרחב להבין אותם ולהתייחס אליהם מעט אחרת. עלינו לנהוג זה בזה בחסד רב, ואסור לנו להניח לדברים האלה להפוך לסלע מחלוקת. אני מאמין שאלוהים רוצה להשתמש בקשיים האלה כדי לקרב אותנו אליו ואיש לרעהו, אך אויב נשמותינו עושה ככל יכולתו כדי לגרום להם להרוס את אהבתנו ואת מחויבותנו זה לזה. הבה נבקש שלום ונרדוף אחריו!
