Molte persone chiedono: «Ascoltare musica secolare è un peccato? C’è qualcosa di sbagliato nella CCM (musica cristiana contemporanea)? È giusto che i cristiani ascoltino rap, rock, country, pop o rhythm and blues?». Ai fini di questo articolo, chiamerò tutta la musica elencata sopra musica “secolare”.

I cristiani dovrebbero ascoltare soltanto musica «a cappella»? La musica è coinvolgente e può influire in modo significativo sul modo in cui viviamo. La musica ci influenza in modo negativo o positivo. Dovremmo porci questa domanda: «La musica che ascolto mi avvicina a Dio oppure mi allontana da Lui e mi avvicina a Satana?»

Lo scopo principale della musica è adorare (esprimere reverenza e adorazione verso qualcosa o qualcuno). Eppure, a volte noi credenti continuiamo a non scegliere musica buona e sana da ascoltare. Questo è un problema, poiché la maggior parte della musica secolare è malvagia e promuove cose che Dio odia.

La musica secolare è molto orecchiabile e crea dipendenza. La carne preferirebbe ascoltare musica secolare anziché musica devota a Dio. Questo tipo di musica influenza negativamente la mente e non è vantaggioso. Se una canzone incoraggia il male, promuove la mondanità, ti induce pensieri cattivi, ti spinge ad agire in modo sbagliato e influenza negativamente il tuo modo di parlare, non dovremmo ascoltarla. Quando si tratta di musica, possiamo mentire a noi stessi con facilità in questo ambito. Ti sei mentito? Hai detto: «Dio approva questo tipo di musica», eppure, nel profondo del cuore, sai che Lui ti sta convincendo del contrario e che NON la approva?

La musica secolare è spesso sensuale. Il significato di sensuale è «che suscita gratificazione dei sensi e piacere fisico». La musica che ascoltiamo è sensuale? Ci porta in uno stato mentale in cui ci lasciamo semplicemente trasportare dal ritmo? Come vogliono reagire i nostri corpi quando ascoltiamo musica del genere? Se i nostri corpi ondeggiano al ritmo della musica, ciò non onora il Signore; non dà gloria al Suo nome; non dispone la nostra mente e il nostro corpo a adorare il Signore.

Quando ascoltiamo musica, adoriamo sempre qualcosa. Se ci concentriamo su musica che non viene da Dio, adoriamo la nostra carne, il mondo o persino il diavolo. Di solito, la musica come la CCM tende ad attirare l’attenzione su noi stessi e non su Dio. Una musica del genere è molto sensuale. Possiamo davvero adorare Dio ascoltando questo tipo di musica?

La CCM è un genere di musica popolare moderna i cui testi si concentrano su temi legati alla fede cristiana. Nacque quando coloro che furono influenzati dal risveglio del «Jesus movement» degli anni Sessanta iniziarono a esprimersi con uno stile musicale più contemporaneo. Prima di allora, nella chiesa dell’epoca erano diffusi gli inni e altri canti gospel. Che ce ne rendiamo conto o no, gran parte della CCM aggiunge un ritmo pulsante (sincope) in un punto in cui non dovrebbe trovarsi naturalmente. Il ritmo pulsante tipico della CCM non si rivolge allo spirito dell’uomo nell’adorazione, ma alla carne. Il tipo di musica che si rivolge alla carne non viene da Dio, ma dal diavolo. Oggi, il termine CCM si usa per indicare stili di ritmo e di battuta pop, rock o di lode e adorazione, purché i testi rientrino nella definizione di CCM.

La Lettera ai Filippesi ci dice che dovremmo pensare a … tutte le cose vere, tutte le cose onorevoli, tutte le cose giuste, tutte le cose pure, tutte le cose amabili, tutte le cose di buona reputazione; se c’è qualche virtù e qualche lode, pensate a queste cose –Filippesi 4:8.

La musica secolare non supera la prova di Filippesi 4:8. La maggior parte della musica secolare ha testi impuri, mentre tutta ha un ritmo o una battuta che contrasta con l’ordine di Dio. Il diavolo se ne serve per influenzare le persone a peccare o a pensare al peccato. Ti influenzerà in qualche modo. L’influenza della musica che ascoltiamo è buona o cattiva? Per esempio, se ci concentriamo su musica che influenza negativamente i nostri pensieri o il nostro stile di vita, allora si tratta di un’influenza negativa di cui dobbiamo liberarci.

Gli ebrei iniziarono la tradizione di usare musica senza accompagnamento dopo la caduta del secondo tempio, nel 70 d.C.; in quel periodo, dopo la caduta, non era consentito usare strumenti durante il lutto. Nel corso della storia, fino al Rinascimento, la musica strumentale fu per lo più associata alla danza e ai festeggiamenti. Poiché nei luoghi di culto non si poteva divertirsi troppo, questo tipo di musica giocosa non era popolare tra i capi religiosi.

A cappella è un’espressione italiana che significa «nello stile della cappella». Inizialmente si riferiva alla musica cantata in una cappella o in un piccolo spazio di culto senza accompagnamento strumentale, in contrapposizione a una grande chiesa, dove di solito un organo accompagnava il canto. Da allora il termine è arrivato a indicare qualsiasi musica cantata senza accompagnamento, sia sacra (religiosa) sia secolare (non religiosa). La musica a cappella può essere cantata da un grande coro, da un piccolo gruppo o da un solista.

Nelle congregazioni ebraiche ortodosse e conservatrici esiste ancora la tradizione di cantare per lo più a cappella. In queste sinagoghe, è consuetudine che un cantore reciti o canti un testo autorevole delle Scritture, al quale la congregazione risponde nello stesso modo. Gli unici strumenti utilizzati potrebbero essere un diapason per dare a tutti la nota iniziale oppure un corno d’ariete in un’occasione speciale o durante una festività.

La chiesa delle origini sviluppò la tradizione del canto a cappella a partire dalla tradizione ebraica degli ebrei: si cantavano salmi o altri passi delle Scritture e si usava un cantore come guida. Il canto gregoriano fu la forma dominante della musica ecclesiastica a partire circa dal 590 d.C. È una linea melodica unica e semplice, per metà parlata e per metà cantata, in uno stile ritmico libero. Nella chiesa delle origini, la musica strumentale era associata al mondo peccaminoso esterno ed era considerata un’influenza negativa.

La tradizione della musica vocale sacra senza accompagnamento continuò durante il Rinascimento. Anche se talvolta gli strumenti raddoppiavano o sostituivano una linea vocale, la musica vocale era per lo più autonoma. Il suono di un coro in una cappella dall’acustica eccellente produceva un effetto particolarmente etereo.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina fu uno dei compositori più importanti del Rinascimento in Italia e scrisse centinaia di messe e mottetti per la chiesa. Il «modo palestriniano», come viene chiamato, era una forma sofisticata di canto a cappella in cui molte voci cantavano musiche e testi diversi, entrando in momenti diversi. Si chiamava polifonia, in contrapposizione all’omofonia, che significa una sola linea melodica cantata insieme o con lo stesso ritmo.

L’apostolo Paolo scrive: Parlate tra voi con salmi, inni e cantici spirituali, cantando e inneggiando nel vostro cuore al Signore; –Efesini 5:19. Vi sembra che si parli di fare musica con strumenti? O sembra piuttosto che si tratti di cantare lodi a Dio con il cuore?

Verso la mezzanotte, Paolo e Sila pregavano e cantavano inni a Dio, e i prigionieri li udivano –Atti 16:25. Quando Paolo e Sila erano in prigione, incatenati ai ceppi e intenti a cantare a mezzanotte, non credo che cantassero per dare gloria a se stessi. Cantavano per dare gloria a Dio Padre. Il risultato del fatto che diedero gloria a Dio è davvero straordinario. Ci fu un terremoto, le fondamenta della prigione tremarono, le porte si spalancarono e a tutti si spezzarono le catene. Alla fine di questi avvenimenti, il carceriere si presentò tremando davanti a Paolo e Sila e chiese: «Che cosa devo fare per essere salvato?»

Anche la Lettera ai Colossesi ci dice che dovremmo La parola di Cristo abiti in voi abbondantemente, ammaestrandovi e ammonendovi gli uni gli altri con ogni sapienza, con salmi, inni e cantici spirituali, cantando con gratitudine nei vostri cuori a Dio –Colossesi 3:16. Lasciamo che i salmi, gli inni e i cantici spirituali ci istruiscano, ci ammoniscano e ci incoraggino?

Mi chiedo quale inno cantò Gesù con i suoi discepoli durante l’ultima cena, prima di uscire verso il monte degli Ulivi. Dubito che cantassero per se stessi. Credo che cantassero al loro Padre celeste.

La musica pura e santa è una benedizione del Signore. È qualcosa di così meravigliosamente potente che non dovremmo darla per scontata. A volte Dio se ne serve per parlarci. Credo fermamente che tutti i cristiani debbano ascoltare musica devota a Dio durante la settimana, non solo la domenica. Mi aiuta a mantenere la calma, a trovare incoraggiamento e a tenere la mente rivolta al Signore. Quando la mia mente è rivolta al Signore, posso affrontare la giornata benedetto.

Dobbiamo disciplinarci nelle cose di Dio. Dobbiamo anche liberarci delle cose della nostra vita che sappiamo non essere gradite a Dio. La musica devota a Dio (musica che rivolge il nostro spirito e la nostra mente alle cose che vengono da Dio) è il tipo di musica che i credenti dovrebbero ascoltare. In definitiva, si tratta di adorazione: adoriamo Dio o qualcos’altro?

Gesù dice: Ma l’ora viene, anzi è già venuta, in cui i veri adoratori adoreranno il Padre in spirito e verità; perché il Padre cerca tali adoratori –Giovanni 4:23.

Dunque, cantiamo in sincera adorazione al nostro Creatore, rendiamo gloria a Dio per le voci che ci ha dato e cantiamo e ascoltiamo canti devoti e puri al nostro Dio.

He was born in a stable, meant for beasts of the field.
It was from the beginning that His will He would yield.

He was never well-liked; despised by all men;
Laughed to scorn, reviled—again, and again.

Yes, His mission on this earth was unusual indeed,
Not seeking money and friends or trying to succeed.

He knew His purpose was to please His Father,
With the trifles of earth, He would not bother.

It surely wasn’t easy, to be the King of kings.
And suffer as a criminal, taking what that brings.

Ten thousand angels, He could have summoned south,
But the stricken Savior opened not His mouth.

With His eyes on the reward, He persevered the pain;
Was cruelly stripped and beaten, and ultimately slain.

But why would He suffer so willingly there;
Enduring the cross, all the pain He did bear?

Because He treasured us, an atonement for our sin
He made when He bled and died there to make us His kin!

I thank God now for that sacrifice so great;
Providing the Lamb and transforming my fate.

I say, “A wonderful Savior, is Jesus my Lord;”
Now the Father and I—a relationship restored!

–Barry Grant

Nasceu num estábulo, destinado aos animais do campo.
Desde o princípio, à vontade do Pai se submeteria.

Nunca foi bem-querido; todos o desprezavam;
Zombavam dele, insultavam-no — vez após vez.

Sim, sua missão nesta terra era mesmo incomum,
Não buscava dinheiro e amigos nem tentava vencer.

Sabia que seu propósito era agradar ao Pai,
E não se ocuparia com as ninharias terrenas.

Certamente não foi fácil ser o Rei dos reis
E sofrer como um criminoso, suportando o que isso traz.

Poderia ter convocado dez mil anjos para o sul,
Mas o Salvador ferido não abriu a boca.

Com os olhos fixos na recompensa, perseverou na dor;
Foi cruelmente despido e açoitado, e por fim morto.

Mas por que sofreria ali tão voluntariamente,
Suportando a cruz e toda aquela dor?

Porque nos tinha em grande estima, fez expiação pelo nosso pecado
Ao sangrar e morrer ali, para nos tornar sua família!

Agora agradeço a Deus por um sacrifício tão grandioso;
Ele proveu o Cordeiro e transformou meu destino.

Eu digo: “Que maravilhoso Salvador é Jesus, meu Senhor!”
Agora, entre o Pai e mim, o relacionamento foi restaurado!

–Barry Grant

That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace –Psalm 144:12.

The vision of every godly parent is to see their children grow into mature adulthood. We want our children to develop biblical convictions that will govern their lives and allow them to become independent of parental guidance.

This was the vision of every Jewish father. To celebrate their child’s transition to personal responsibility, a ceremony was held called bar mitzvah for boys, and bat mitzvah for girls. This was traditionally done at the age of thirteen. Bar mitzvah means “a son of the commandment” and bat mitzvah “a daughter of the commandment”. After bar mitzvah a son was considered to be “under the law” and responsible for his own actions. Prior to this event, his parents were accountable for his actions.

Most of us are not of Jewish descent; however, our Lord Jesus was. We find him at the age of twelve sitting in the temple visiting with the doctors, both hearing them and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. (see Luke 2:47) Jesus demonstrated an amazing level of maturity at the age of twelve. Even his parents were amazed. Yes, he was divine, yet as a human he demonstrated the potential for early maturity given the right set of values and disciplines.

The teen years are transitional years. Teens are transitioning from childhood to adulthood; from being dependent on parents to learning to be independent. This transition is a process that must be understood by both the parents and the child. Too much freedom too soon, can leave the child feeling insecure and can result in bad choices that can have life-long consequences. Too little freedom can squelch a child’s character growth and can become fertile ground for rebellion.

The teen years are growing years. Just as a plant needs diligent cultivation throughout its life cycle, so a child needs ongoing direction throughout his teen years. After Jesus’ episode in the temple we read, And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them… –Luke 2:51. We will look at some things that parents can do to nurture maturity in their children, but first we will consider several relationships that are foundational to healthy maturity.

Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the LORD –Psalm 144:15.

Parental relationship

The relationship between the parent and the child in the teen years is largely a reaping of what that relationship was throughout the formative years of childhood. Unless there is a major spiritual crisis that dynamically changes the relationship—such as an evangelical conversion on the part of either the parent or the child—we (as parents) reap during the child’s teen years that which we have sown during their childhood.

Raising teens is a rewarding experience if there has been a healthy foundational relationship established throughout childhood. If the parent has been physically and emotionally present; if the parent and child have been communicating openly and freely; and if the parent has lovingly maintained the role of authority and control, then a foundation has been laid for a more mature level of relating during the teen years.

In the absence of this kind of parental relationship, the child entering the teen years will try to fill this void with other relationships. Most often, if a parental relationship is lacking, a child will seek to fill that void through relationships with their peers. Peers are great friends but are a poor substitute for a parent. We have been created to be relational. Teens especially crave significance through relationship.

There are two things that every teen is looking for in parental relationship. One is identity and the other is affirmation. Two burning questions in the heart of every teen are “Who am I?” and “Am I OK?”.

The identity factor

When children are young, they assume their family identity. As children grow into adolescence and become more independent, they begin to view themselves as someone more than merely Dad’s son. They begin to develop an identity of their own. This movement toward “being my own person” becomes evident in many of the choices that they make such as:

  • How they dress
  • Their choice of music
  • Their choice of friends
  • Whether or not they choose to serve their parent’s God
  • Whether or not they choose to worship in the church of their upbringing

Admittedly, there are other influences that can affect a teen’s choices in these areas, but for the most part these choices reflect the relationship between the child and the parent. Where the parent has exerted a positive influence on the child, that child will be more inclined to adopt the values of the parent.

When the parental relationship has broken down or has never been nurtured, or if the relationship has been nothing more than a master/slave relationship, that child will seek to identify with someone other than the parent. This will manifest itself in choices of dress, music, friends, and activities that the parent will not approve of. This is often called “teenage rebellion”.

Is “teenage rebellion” always the fault of the parent? No, but if you are not actively involved in building and maintaining a relationship with your teen, it is likely to happen. It is important to note that there is a rebel in the heart of every person. In my last article I stressed the importance of confronting that rebel spirit when our children are young and impressionable.

This rebel spirit will not be fully conquered until it is surrendered to God through an evangelical conversion experience. Only a work of the grace of God upon the heart can subdue the inborn rebellion against God and parental authority.

Know the heart of your child and seek to lead them into loving submission to the Lord Jesus Christ. Only in a relationship with Jesus Christ can our children find their true and lasting identity. Parental authority has a place in shaping and controlling our children when they are young. As our children grow into adulthood, we come to realize that parental authority has limitations and our children need to be controlled by an influence beyond ourselves.

It is never too late to build a relational bridge. If you are feeling that you have failed in your relationship with your children, it’s never too late to call them to your side and humbly seek to restore what is missing. Even if your children are gone from home, I can assure you that they long for a relationship with mom and dad.

The affirmation factor

Every teen longs to be affirmed by their parents, especially their father. You can affirm your teen by looking for and acknowledging positive character traits. There is a place for corrective criticism from parent to child, but criticism that demeans is not constructive; it’s destructive. For every critical comment you should have several positive compliments. In other words, you earn the right to criticize what is wrong by blessing what is right.

You can affirm your teen by treating them with dignity and respect. You can ask, “How do you feel about…?” Or “What do you think we should do…?” You are not surrendering your parental responsibility by probing your son’s or daughter’s mind for their perspective. You are actually causing them to be “grown up in their youth” by forcing them to think as adults.

You can affirm your teen by treating him with common courtesy. Simple things like “please” and “thank you”,” I’m sorry”, “pardon me”, “good bye”, “have a good day”, “drive safely”, and “God bless you”, expresses worth and value to your teen. If these simple courtesies are common in your home your children will return them to you. Think about how you feel when someone says to you, “Oh, excuse me, I’m sorry.” You feel a sense of respect, value, and dignity. That is a simple gift that every parent can give to his child.

You can affirm your teen by entrusting him with responsibility. I grew up on a dairy farm. We had plenty of opportunity to develop character and skills. I remember one day when I was 16 years of age, my dad needed a concrete block wall built out in the barn. I volunteered for the job. Dad provided the blocks and the mortar and got me started. Then I was on my own. Did I build a professional-looking wall? No, but I was quite proud of the outcome and that wall lasted for many years. Dad trusted me to do a man’s job and I did it.

Affirming is not flattery. Flattery is praise that is not sincere and often is not true. Affirming is recognizing and encouraging the good that you see in another. I have encountered grown men who have wept bitterly because they had never received affirmation from their father. Even Jesus received affirmation from His Father when His Father said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

(2) Relationship with God

Our first responsibility in evangelization is to our children. If we cannot evangelize our children, how can we expect to win others to the Lord? We have a distinct advantage in relating our faith to our children in that we are living with our children. They can and do observe how our faith is lived out in everyday life. This should be the most convincing evidence for the validity of our faith.

Unfortunately, how parents live out their faith, or rather fail to live out their faith, can become a huge stumbling block to their children. Our children are keenly aware of any inconsistency in our Christian profession.

Conversely, if our children see that the power of God is evident in our lives, if they see their parents demonstrating faith in God that carries them through difficult times, if they see their parents demonstrating a graceful rest in the Lord, and if, in the home Jesus Christ is exalted and worshipped, they will be convinced to make their parents’ God, their God.

It is the reality of the gospel lived out in daily life that is the most convincing evidence for the validity of our faith. Our children should be our first witnesses to the transformational work of the gospel in our hearts.

How does a parent lead his child to salvation? Salvation is a work of God; however, God uses human instrumentality to accomplish His work. Parents play a major role in leading their children to Christ. Be aware of evidence of conviction. If a child is quiet and withdrawn, or irritable and restless, or belligerent and defiant, it may be that the spirit of God is working in their heart.

Hopefully, you have nurtured a relationship that allows you to probe their heart and gently lead them to Jesus for forgiveness and cleansing. Most of our children’s conversions were initiated by a parent. We recognized signs of conviction and lead them to brokenness and repentance and to receive salvation through faith in Christ.

The early teen years are an ideal time for a child to surrender his/her life to Jesus if he has not already done so. When active rebellion sets in, a teen often makes choices that lead to painful reaping and sometimes irrevocable consequences. A life of dedicated service to God is the only life of blessing and fulfilment.

Relationship with the church

There is one more relationship that dramatically affects the formation of a teen’s life and convictions and that is the local church. We gain both our sense of identity and our understanding of the reality of the Christian faith through our experience of worship and relationship within the local church. After parental relationship, this is the next most significant influence in a teen’s life.

It is important that we worship in a church that presents the gospel as a transformational relationship with God through faith in Jesus. It is also important that our church life consists of warm, loving relationships in a close–knit community.

The reason that I mention this is that some parents have the mistaken idea that they can provide all the spiritual direction and relationships that their children need. This may seem to work when the children are small and close at hand, but as our children grow into adulthood, they will seek a broader world of relationships. The local church and community of associated churches provides this broader base of fellowship.

It is important to worship in a church that you can support and that you can encourage your children to support. Many children have been lost to the faith because mom and dad were not supportive of the church where they were worshipping. It is far better to move on and find a church that you can support than to stay in a church and be in a state of constant opposition.

I am not encouraging church hopping. It is important to children, especially your teens, that there is stability in church life. Find a church that you are comfortable with, hopefully while your children are young, and stick with it. There are always logistical exceptions and your children will adapt to these, but for the most part a stable church life produces youth who have a strong sense of identity and purpose.

As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth –Psalm 127:4. This verse reminds us that our children are a mighty defense against the enemy. If properly honed (trained) and balanced (taught disciplines) our children will have the potential to outlive us both in years and in usefulness. When you release the arrow your children will go places both in time and in the world that you will never see. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate –Psalm 127:5.

Kiranya anak-anak lelaki kita seperti tanaman yang bertumbuh besar pada masa mudanya; kiranya anak-anak perempuan kita seperti batu penjuru, yang dipahat menyerupai istana –Mazmur 144:12.

Visi setiap orang tua yang saleh adalah melihat anak-anak mereka bertumbuh menjadi orang dewasa yang matang. Kita ingin anak-anak kita mengembangkan keyakinan alkitabiah yang akan menuntun hidup mereka dan memungkinkan mereka untuk tidak lagi bergantung pada bimbingan orang tua.

Inilah visi setiap ayah Yahudi. Untuk merayakan peralihan anak mereka menuju tanggung jawab pribadi, diadakan upacara yang disebut bar mitzvah bagi anak laki-laki dan bat mitzvah bagi anak perempuan. Secara tradisional, upacara ini dilakukan pada usia tiga belas tahun. Bar mitzvah berarti “anak laki-laki dari perintah” dan bat mitzvah berarti “anak perempuan dari perintah”. Setelah bar mitzvah, seorang anak laki-laki dianggap “di bawah hukum Taurat” dan bertanggung jawab atas tindakannya sendiri. Sebelum peristiwa ini, orang tuanyalah yang bertanggung jawab atas tindakannya.

Kebanyakan dari kita bukan keturunan Yahudi; namun, Tuhan kita Yesus adalah keturunan Yahudi. Kita mendapati Dia pada usia dua belas tahun duduk di Bait Allah, berbincang dengan para ahli, mendengarkan mereka dan mengajukan pertanyaan kepada mereka. Semua orang yang mendengar Dia takjub akan pengertian dan jawaban-Nya. (lihat Lukas 2:47) Yesus menunjukkan tingkat kematangan yang luar biasa pada usia dua belas tahun. Bahkan orang tua-Nya pun takjub. Ya, Dia ilahi, tetapi sebagai manusia, Dia menunjukkan potensi untuk menjadi matang sejak dini apabila dibekali nilai-nilai dan disiplin yang tepat.

Masa remaja adalah masa peralihan. Para remaja beralih dari masa kanak-kanak ke masa dewasa; dari bergantung pada orang tua menjadi belajar mandiri. Peralihan ini adalah suatu proses yang harus dipahami baik oleh orang tua maupun anak. Terlalu banyak kebebasan yang diberikan terlalu cepat dapat membuat anak merasa tidak aman dan dapat mengakibatkan pilihan buruk yang membawa akibat seumur hidup. Terlalu sedikit kebebasan dapat menghambat pertumbuhan karakter anak dan menjadi lahan subur bagi pemberontakan.

Masa remaja adalah masa pertumbuhan. Sebagaimana tanaman membutuhkan pemeliharaan yang tekun sepanjang siklus hidupnya, demikian pula seorang anak membutuhkan arahan yang berkelanjutan sepanjang masa remajanya. Setelah peristiwa Yesus di Bait Allah, kita membaca, Lalu Ia pulang bersama-sama mereka ke Nazaret, dan Ia tetap hidup dalam asuhan mereka… –Lukas 2:51. Kita akan melihat beberapa hal yang dapat dilakukan orang tua untuk memupuk kematangan anak-anak mereka, tetapi terlebih dahulu kita akan mempertimbangkan beberapa hubungan yang menjadi dasar bagi kematangan yang sehat.

Berbahagialah bangsa yang demikian keadaannya! Berbahagialah bangsa yang Allahnya ialah TUHAN! –Mazmur 144:15.

Hubungan dengan orang tua

Hubungan antara orang tua dan anak pada masa remaja sebagian besar merupakan hasil dari hubungan yang telah terjalin sepanjang tahun-tahun pembentukan pada masa kanak-kanak. Kecuali jika terjadi krisis rohani besar yang mengubah hubungan itu secara mendasar—seperti pertobatan injili pada pihak orang tua atau anak—kita (sebagai orang tua) menuai pada masa remaja anak apa yang telah kita tabur selama masa kanak-kanak mereka.

Membesarkan anak remaja merupakan pengalaman yang memuaskan jika hubungan mendasar yang sehat telah dibangun sepanjang masa kanak-kanak. Jika orang tua hadir secara fisik dan emosional; jika orang tua dan anak berkomunikasi secara terbuka dan leluasa; dan jika orang tua dengan penuh kasih mempertahankan peran sebagai pihak yang berwenang dan memegang kendali, maka landasan telah diletakkan bagi hubungan yang lebih matang pada masa remaja.

Jika hubungan orang tua seperti ini tidak ada, anak yang memasuki masa remaja akan berusaha mengisi kekosongan itu dengan hubungan lain. Paling sering, jika hubungan dengan orang tua kurang terjalin, anak akan berusaha mengisi kekosongan itu melalui hubungan dengan teman sebaya. Teman sebaya bisa menjadi sahabat yang baik, tetapi merupakan pengganti orang tua yang buruk. Kita diciptakan untuk menjalin hubungan. Terutama para remaja sangat mendambakan rasa berarti melalui hubungan.

Ada dua hal yang dicari setiap remaja dalam hubungan dengan orang tua. Yang pertama adalah jati diri dan yang kedua adalah peneguhan. Dua pertanyaan yang membara dalam hati setiap remaja adalah, “Siapakah aku?” dan “Apakah aku baik-baik saja?”.

Faktor jati diri

Ketika masih kecil, anak-anak menganggap jati diri keluarga sebagai jati diri mereka. Saat bertumbuh menuju masa remaja dan menjadi lebih mandiri, mereka mulai memandang diri sebagai seseorang yang lebih dari sekadar anak Ayah. Mereka mulai mengembangkan jati diri sendiri. Pergerakan menuju “menjadi diriku sendiri” tampak dalam banyak pilihan yang mereka buat, seperti:

  • Bagaimana mereka berpakaian
  • Pilihan musik mereka
  • Pilihan teman mereka
  • Apakah mereka memilih untuk melayani Allah orang tua mereka atau tidak
  • Apakah mereka memilih untuk beribadah di gereja tempat mereka dibesarkan atau tidak

Memang, ada pengaruh lain yang dapat memengaruhi pilihan remaja dalam bidang-bidang ini, tetapi pada umumnya pilihan-pilihan tersebut mencerminkan hubungan antara anak dan orang tua. Jika orang tua telah memberi pengaruh positif kepada anak, anak itu akan lebih cenderung menerima nilai-nilai orang tuanya.

Ketika hubungan dengan orang tua telah rusak atau tidak pernah dipupuk, atau jika hubungan itu tidak lebih dari hubungan tuan dan hamba, anak akan berusaha mengidentifikasi diri dengan orang lain selain orang tuanya. Hal ini akan tampak dalam pilihan pakaian, musik, teman, dan kegiatan yang tidak disetujui orang tua. Hal ini sering disebut “pemberontakan remaja”.

Apakah “pemberontakan remaja” selalu merupakan kesalahan orang tua? Tidak, tetapi jika Anda tidak secara aktif terlibat dalam membangun dan memelihara hubungan dengan anak remaja Anda, hal itu mungkin terjadi. Penting untuk diperhatikan bahwa ada pemberontak dalam hati setiap orang. Dalam artikel saya yang terakhir, saya menekankan pentingnya menghadapi roh pemberontak itu ketika anak-anak kita masih kecil dan mudah dibentuk.

Roh pemberontak ini tidak akan sepenuhnya ditaklukkan sampai diserahkan kepada Allah melalui pengalaman pertobatan injili. Hanya karya kasih karunia Allah dalam hati yang dapat menundukkan pemberontakan bawaan terhadap Allah dan wewenang orang tua.

Kenalilah hati anak Anda dan berusahalah menuntun mereka untuk tunduk dengan penuh kasih kepada Tuhan Yesus Kristus. Hanya dalam hubungan dengan Yesus Kristus anak-anak kita dapat menemukan jati diri mereka yang sejati dan kekal. Wewenang orang tua berperan dalam membentuk dan mengendalikan anak-anak kita ketika mereka masih kecil. Saat anak-anak kita bertumbuh menjadi dewasa, kita menyadari bahwa wewenang orang tua memiliki keterbatasan dan anak-anak kita perlu dikendalikan oleh pengaruh yang melampaui diri kita sendiri.

Tidak pernah terlambat untuk membangun jembatan hubungan. Jika Anda merasa telah gagal dalam hubungan dengan anak-anak Anda, tidak pernah terlambat untuk memanggil mereka ke sisi Anda dan dengan rendah hati berusaha memulihkan apa yang hilang. Sekalipun anak-anak Anda telah meninggalkan rumah, saya dapat meyakinkan Anda bahwa mereka merindukan hubungan dengan ibu dan ayah.

Faktor peneguhan

Setiap remaja rindu mendapat peneguhan dari orang tuanya, terutama ayahnya. Anda dapat meneguhkan anak remaja Anda dengan mencari dan mengakui sifat-sifat karakter yang positif. Ada tempat bagi kritik korektif dari orang tua kepada anak, tetapi kritik yang merendahkan bukanlah sesuatu yang membangun; itu merusak. Untuk setiap komentar kritis, hendaknya ada beberapa pujian positif. Dengan kata lain, Anda memperoleh hak untuk mengkritik hal yang salah dengan memberkati hal yang benar.

Anda dapat meneguhkan anak remaja Anda dengan memperlakukannya secara bermartabat dan hormat. Anda dapat bertanya, “Bagaimana perasaanmu tentang…?” atau “Menurutmu, apa yang sebaiknya kita lakukan…?” Anda tidak melepaskan tanggung jawab sebagai orang tua dengan menggali pandangan putra atau putri Anda. Sebenarnya, Anda membuat mereka “bertumbuh besar pada masa mudanya” dengan mendorong mereka berpikir seperti orang dewasa.

Anda dapat meneguhkan anak remaja Anda dengan memperlakukannya dengan sopan santun yang wajar. Hal-hal sederhana seperti “silakan” dan “terima kasih”, “maaf”, “permisi”, “sampai jumpa”, “semoga harimu menyenangkan”, “berhati-hatilah saat berkendara”, dan “Tuhan memberkatimu” menyampaikan kepada anak remaja Anda bahwa ia berharga dan bernilai. Jika kesopanan sederhana ini biasa dilakukan di rumah Anda, anak-anak Anda akan membalasnya kepada Anda. Pikirkan bagaimana perasaan Anda ketika seseorang berkata kepada Anda, “Oh, maaf, saya minta maaf.” Anda merasakan adanya penghormatan, penghargaan, dan martabat. Itulah hadiah sederhana yang dapat diberikan setiap orang tua kepada anaknya.

Anda dapat meneguhkan anak remaja Anda dengan memercayakan tanggung jawab kepadanya. Saya dibesarkan di sebuah peternakan sapi perah. Kami memiliki banyak kesempatan untuk mengembangkan karakter dan keterampilan. Saya ingat suatu hari ketika saya berusia 16 tahun, ayah saya membutuhkan tembok dari blok beton dibangun di lumbung. Saya menawarkan diri untuk mengerjakannya. Ayah menyediakan blok dan adukan semen, lalu memulai pekerjaan itu bersama saya. Setelah itu, saya mengerjakannya sendiri. Apakah saya membangun tembok yang tampak profesional? Tidak, tetapi saya cukup bangga dengan hasilnya dan tembok itu bertahan selama bertahun-tahun. Ayah memercayai saya untuk melakukan pekerjaan orang dewasa, dan saya melakukannya.

Meneguhkan bukanlah menjilat. Pujian yang menjilat tidak tulus dan sering kali tidak benar. Meneguhkan berarti mengakui dan mendorong hal baik yang Anda lihat dalam diri orang lain. Saya pernah bertemu pria dewasa yang menangis tersedu-sedu karena tidak pernah menerima peneguhan dari ayah mereka. Bahkan Yesus menerima peneguhan dari Bapa-Nya ketika Bapa-Nya berkata, “Inilah Anak-Ku yang Kukasihi, kepada-Nyalah Aku berkenan.”

(2) Hubungan dengan Allah

Tanggung jawab pertama kita dalam penginjilan adalah kepada anak-anak kita. Jika kita tidak dapat memberitakan Injil kepada anak-anak kita, bagaimana kita dapat berharap memenangkan orang lain bagi Tuhan? Kita memiliki keunggulan tersendiri dalam menyampaikan iman kita kepada anak-anak karena kita tinggal bersama mereka. Mereka dapat dan memang mengamati bagaimana iman kita dijalani dalam kehidupan sehari-hari. Inilah seharusnya bukti yang paling meyakinkan tentang kesahihan iman kita.

Sayangnya, cara orang tua menjalani iman mereka—atau lebih tepatnya, kegagalan mereka untuk menjalani iman itu—dapat menjadi batu sandungan besar bagi anak-anak mereka. Anak-anak kita sangat menyadari setiap ketidakkonsistenan dalam pengakuan iman Kristen kita.

Sebaliknya, jika anak-anak kita melihat kuasa Allah nyata dalam hidup kita, jika mereka melihat orang tua mereka menunjukkan iman kepada Allah yang menopang mereka melewati masa-masa sulit, jika mereka melihat orang tua mereka menunjukkan ketenangan penuh kasih karunia di dalam Tuhan, dan jika Yesus Kristus ditinggikan dan disembah di rumah, mereka akan diyakinkan untuk menjadikan Allah orang tua mereka sebagai Allah mereka.

Realitas Injil yang dijalani dalam kehidupan sehari-hari merupakan bukti paling meyakinkan tentang kesahihan iman kita. Anak-anak kita seharusnya menjadi saksi pertama atas karya Injil yang mengubahkan hati kita.

Bagaimana orang tua menuntun anaknya kepada keselamatan? Keselamatan adalah karya Allah; namun, Allah menggunakan manusia sebagai alat untuk melaksanakan karya-Nya. Orang tua memainkan peran besar dalam menuntun anak-anak mereka kepada Kristus. Waspadalah terhadap tanda-tanda adanya keyakinan akan dosa. Jika seorang anak pendiam dan menarik diri, mudah tersinggung dan gelisah, atau suka melawan dan membangkang, mungkin Roh Allah sedang bekerja dalam hatinya.

Kiranya Anda telah memupuk hubungan yang memungkinkan Anda menyelami hati mereka dan dengan lembut menuntun mereka kepada Yesus untuk memperoleh pengampunan dan penyucian. Pertobatan sebagian besar anak kami dimulai oleh orang tua. Kami mengenali tanda-tanda adanya keyakinan akan dosa dan menuntun mereka kepada kehancuran hati dan pertobatan, serta untuk menerima keselamatan melalui iman kepada Kristus.

Tahun-tahun awal masa remaja merupakan waktu yang ideal bagi seorang anak untuk menyerahkan hidupnya kepada Yesus jika ia belum melakukannya. Ketika pemberontakan aktif mulai muncul, seorang remaja sering membuat pilihan yang berujung pada akibat yang menyakitkan dan terkadang tidak dapat diperbaiki. Hidup yang dipersembahkan untuk melayani Allah adalah satu-satunya hidup yang penuh berkat dan pemenuhan.

Hubungan dengan gereja

Ada satu hubungan lagi yang sangat memengaruhi pembentukan kehidupan dan keyakinan seorang remaja, yaitu gereja lokal. Kita memperoleh rasa jati diri dan pemahaman tentang realitas iman Kristen melalui pengalaman beribadah dan menjalin hubungan dalam gereja lokal. Setelah hubungan dengan orang tua, inilah pengaruh paling penting berikutnya dalam kehidupan seorang remaja.

Penting bagi kita untuk beribadah di gereja yang menyampaikan Injil sebagai hubungan yang mengubahkan dengan Allah melalui iman kepada Yesus. Penting juga agar kehidupan gereja kita terdiri atas hubungan yang hangat dan penuh kasih dalam komunitas yang erat.

Saya menyebutkan hal ini karena beberapa orang tua keliru mengira bahwa mereka dapat menyediakan semua arahan rohani dan hubungan yang dibutuhkan anak-anak mereka. Hal ini mungkin tampak berhasil ketika anak-anak masih kecil dan berada dekat, tetapi saat mereka bertumbuh menjadi dewasa, mereka akan mencari lingkungan hubungan yang lebih luas. Gereja lokal dan komunitas gereja-gereja yang bersekutu menyediakan dasar persekutuan yang lebih luas ini.

Penting untuk beribadah di gereja yang dapat Anda dukung dan yang dapat Anda dorong untuk didukung oleh anak-anak Anda. Banyak anak meninggalkan iman karena ibu dan ayah tidak mendukung gereja tempat mereka beribadah. Jauh lebih baik untuk pindah dan mencari gereja yang dapat Anda dukung daripada tetap tinggal di sebuah gereja dan terus-menerus bersikap menentang.

Saya tidak menganjurkan kebiasaan berpindah-pindah gereja. Bagi anak-anak, terutama anak remaja Anda, kestabilan kehidupan bergereja itu penting. Temukan gereja yang membuat Anda nyaman, sedapat mungkin ketika anak-anak masih kecil, dan tetaplah di sana. Selalu ada pengecualian karena keadaan praktis, dan anak-anak Anda akan menyesuaikan diri, tetapi pada umumnya kehidupan bergereja yang stabil menghasilkan kaum muda yang memiliki rasa jati diri dan tujuan yang kuat.

Seperti anak-anak panah di tangan pahlawan, demikianlah anak-anak pada masa muda –Mazmur 127:4. Ayat ini mengingatkan kita bahwa anak-anak kita merupakan pertahanan yang kuat terhadap musuh. Jika diasah (dilatih) dengan tepat dan diseimbangkan (diajari disiplin), anak-anak kita berpotensi hidup lebih lama daripada kita, baik dalam usia maupun dalam manfaat yang mereka berikan. Ketika Anda melepaskan anak panah itu, anak-anak Anda akan pergi ke berbagai tempat, baik dalam perjalanan waktu maupun di dunia, yang tak akan pernah Anda lihat. Berbahagialah orang yang telah memenuhi tabung panahnya dengan semuanya itu. Ia tidak akan mendapat malu apabila berbicara dengan musuh-musuhnya di pintu gerbang –Mazmur 127:5.

Greetings in the name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. We are trusting that each of you as our readers are doing well and continuing to trust the Lord. The pandemic has created a bit of a backlog for us, along with some personal issues we have been working through, so this issue is coming to you somewhat behind schedule. Our apologies…. We plan to get the next issue printed within the next several months to get back on track.

In the last issue’s editorial, I wrote about an obscure news article which revealed that many folks across the world were surprised by the positive outcomes they were experiencing through the need to stay at home during the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic. They were enjoying family time. They were finding camaraderie in facing this challenge together. They were finding excitement in the adventure of discovering new ways to function and survive. And they were finding renewed vision and purpose in life.

However, as time has passed, this seems to have been short-lived by all who did not have a deeper level of stability in their lives. After a varying amount of time has elapsed for many folks, reality has begun to set in. Some have lost their jobs. Some have lost loved ones. Some have gone through a time of sickness. Many have been starved for fellowship with other human beings. For the elderly living in nursing homes and assisted-living facilities, and those requiring hospitalization, life has become a very lonely existence indeed, since most of these places have not allowed visitors to enter their doors.

The world is trying to find any way possible to cope and survive. There are phone conference lines. There are chat lines. There are webinars geared towards the issue. Many are doing their part to fill the gaps that this pandemic has created in the lives of the people around them.

As we step back to gain a clearer perspective of the unfolding events brought about by the pandemic, the last number of months have been a time of change and uncertainty for most. There’s the economic future, “Is my job secure?” “What about my bills?” “What about my housing?” Then there’s the greatly politicized nature of numerous issues—race inequality, conspiracy theories about the pandemic, and the government mandates regarding our response to the virus pandemic. Add to this the polarization in our country regarding politics—who is telling the truth on issues, and who will be the best option to lead the country after the upcoming election.

Despite everything else that is going on, the virus and its effects seem to be on everyone’s mind. On August 15, 2020 there was an article published by CNN, written by Ryan Prior, titled: “1 IN 4 YOUNG PEOPLE ARE REPORTING SUICIDAL THOUGHTS”. For those wanting to read the article, it can be found here:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

This article recognizes that there were positive effects during the onset of the pandemic and the resulting stay-at-home orders. This article goes on to say that as time has passed this event is different than most past events, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, and even the circumstances of 9/11. Most of these events have been localized and brief in their destructive effects, while the Covid-19 pandemic has dragged on for so long that it is becoming a way of life—with no end in sight, and its beginning is fading into our forgetful past.

According to the news article, the CDC has published data from a survey which was conducted to determine the outcome of the negative effects of the pandemic. Following are some facts as presented in the article:

  • Suicidal ideation is up among young people since last year
  • As many as one in four people ages 18 through 24 having seriously considered suicide in the 30 days preceding the survey (researchers surveyed 5,412 adults in the US between June 24 and 30.)
  • In the general US population … 11% of adults surveyed had seriously considered suicide in the past 30 days before they completed the survey.
  • The number of Americans reporting anxiety symptoms is three times the number at this same time last year, the CDC said.
  • The results reflect a nation increasingly on edge.

How sad it is to ponder this reality. As I read this news article, I had to wonder whether the percentages are the same for the church as they are for the world. A verse of scripture came to mind: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable –1 Corinthians 15:19. As Christians…

  • …we have HOPE!
  • …we have HOPE IN CHRIST!!
  • …we have HOPE both IN THIS LIFE and FOR ETERNITY!!!

Considering all this we should have a smile on our faces, hope in our hearts, and an encouraging word on our lips for all with whom we come in contact. Let’s be especially observant as we interact with the people around us—family, friend, and even the stranger. Who knows, maybe the neighbor next door is feeling all alone and discouraged. Or perhaps our best friend from church has been struggling with a burden that seems more than they can bear. As we pray, we can ask God to bring people to our minds that would be blessed by our assistance of one sort or another. We never know when our smile or encouraging word will help make a change in someone’s eternal welfare.

Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another. For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:1-5.

There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able… –1 Corinthians 10:13.

My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience –James 1:2-3.

In these verses, I see a number of things that God wants us to use to live by.

  1. God will not allow us to be tempted above that which we are able to endure. This is according to His fact, not according to our feeling.
  2. Each of us WILL fall into temptations, but as we see God’s sovereignty involved in our trials, we can rest as we “count it all joy”.
  3. When it seems that our faith is being tried and tested, sometimes seemingly almost to the breaking point, we can rest assured that God is in the middle of it and that He is up to something according to His will.
  4. God will allow burdens into each of our lives and He expects each of us to “bear our own burdens”.
  5. God will allow our fellow man to go through times of difficulty, during which God expects us to see our struggling brother or sister and do whatever we can to help ease the burden—through prayer, words of encouragement, or deeds of assistance.

In closing, I will leave you with several verses that Paul wrote to the church of Galatia. And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. –Galatians 6:9-10. As strangers and pilgrims here on this earth, let’s not lose sight of our Eternal Home, our Sympathetic Savior, our Sovereign God, and our Abba Father.

Groete in die Naam van ons Here en Verlosser, Jesus Christus. Ons vertrou dat dit goed gaan met elkeen van julle, ons lesers, en dat julle aanhou om op die Here te vertrou. Die pandemie het ’n effense agterstand vir ons veroorsaak, tesame met enkele persoonlike sake waardeur ons gewerk het, daarom bereik hierdie uitgawe julle ietwat later as beplan. Ons vra om verskoning…. Ons beplan om die volgende uitgawe binne die volgende paar maande te druk sodat ons weer op koers kan kom.

In die redaksionele artikel van die vorige uitgawe het ek geskryf oor ’n onbekende nuusberig wat aan die lig gebring het dat baie mense regoor die wêreld verras was deur die positiewe uitkomste wat hulle ervaar het omdat hulle aan die begin van die Covid-19-pandemie tuis moes bly. Hulle het gesinstyd geniet. Hulle het kameraadskap gevind daarin dat hulle hierdie uitdaging saam die hoof gebied het. Hulle het opgewondenheid gevind in die avontuur om nuwe maniere te ontdek om te funksioneer en te oorleef. En hulle het hernude visie en lewensdoel gevind.

Met verloop van tyd blyk dit egter dat dit van korte duur was vir almal wat nie ’n dieper vlak van stabiliteit in hulle lewens gehad het nie. Nadat daar vir baie mense ’n wisselende tyd verloop het, het die werklikheid begin insink. Party het hulle werk verloor. Party het geliefdes verloor. Party het ’n tyd van siekte deurgemaak. Baie het ’n groot behoefte aan gemeenskap met ander mense gehad. Vir bejaardes wat in verpleeginrigtings en fasiliteite vir begeleide sorg woon, en vir dié wat hospitalisasie benodig, het die lewe inderdaad ’n baie eensame bestaan geword, aangesien die meeste van hierdie plekke nie besoekers toegelaat het nie.

Die wêreld probeer enige moontlike manier vind om die hoof te bied en te oorleef. Daar is telefoniese konferensielyne. Daar is kletslyne. Daar is webinare wat op hierdie kwessie toegespits is. Baie mense doen hulle deel om die leemtes te vul wat hierdie pandemie in die lewens van die mense om hulle geskep het.

Wanneer ons ’n tree terugstaan om ’n duideliker perspektief te kry op die gebeure wat deur die pandemie aan die gang gesit is, sien ons dat die afgelope paar maande vir die meeste mense ’n tyd van verandering en onsekerheid was. Daar is die ekonomiese toekoms: “Is my werk veilig?” “Wat van my rekeninge?” “Wat van my behuising?” Dan is daar die sterk gepolitiseerde aard van talle kwessies—rasse-ongelykheid, samesweringsteorieë oor die pandemie en die regering se voorskrifte oor ons reaksie op die viruspandemie. Voeg hierby die polarisasie in ons land oor politiek—wie die waarheid oor sake vertel en wie die beste keuse sal wees om die land ná die komende verkiesing te lei.

Ten spyte van alles wat nog aan die gang is, lyk dit asof die virus en die gevolge daarvan almal se gedagtes besig hou. Op 15 Augustus 2020 is ’n artikel deur Ryan Prior in CNN gepubliseer met die titel: “1 UIT 4 JONGMENSE RAPPORTEER SELFMOORDGEDAGTES”. Vir dié wat die artikel wil lees, kan dit hier gevind word:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

Hierdie artikel erken dat daar positiewe gevolge was tydens die uitbreek van die pandemie en die daaropvolgende tuisblybevele. Die artikel sê verder dat hierdie gebeurtenis, namate die tyd verloop het, verskil van die meeste gebeure in die verlede, soos tornado’s, orkane, aardbewings en selfs die omstandighede van 9/11. Die meeste van hierdie gebeure was plaaslik en kortstondig wat hulle vernietigende uitwerking betref, terwyl die Covid-19-pandemie so lank voortduur dat dit ’n lewenswyse begin word—sonder dat die einde in sig is, en met die begin daarvan wat in ons vergeetagtige verlede vervaag.

Volgens die nuusartikel het die CDC data gepubliseer uit ’n opname wat gedoen is om die uitkoms van die negatiewe gevolge van die pandemie vas te stel. Hier volg enkele feite soos dit in die artikel aangebied word:

  • Selfmoordgedagtes onder jongmense het sedert verlede jaar toegeneem
  • Soveel as een uit elke vier mense tussen 18 en 24 jaar het dit in die 30 dae voor die opname ernstig oorweeg om selfmoord te pleeg (navorsers het tussen 24 en 30 Junie 5 412 volwassenes in die VSA ondervra.)
  • In die algemene bevolking van die VSA … het 11% van die volwassenes wat ondervra is, in die 30 dae voordat hulle die opname voltooi het, dit ernstig oorweeg om selfmoord te pleeg.
  • Die getal Amerikaners wat angssimptome rapporteer, is drie keer so groot as die getal op dieselfde tyd verlede jaar, het die CDC gesê.
  • Die resultate weerspieël ’n nasie wat toenemend gespanne is.

Hoe hartseer is dit om oor hierdie werklikheid na te dink. Toe ek hierdie nuusartikel lees, moes ek wonder of die persentasies vir die kerk dieselfde is as vir die wêreld. ’n Skrifvers het by my opgekom: As ons net in hierdie lewe op Christus hoop, is ons die ellendigste van alle mense –1 Korintiërs 15:19. As Christene…

  • …het ons HOOP!
  • …het ons HOOP IN CHRISTUS!!
  • …het ons HOOP in HIERDIE LEWE sowel as VIR DIE EWIGHEID!!!

As ons dit alles in ag neem, behoort ons ’n glimlag op ons gesigte, hoop in ons harte en ’n bemoedigende woord op ons lippe te hê vir almal met wie ons in aanraking kom. Laat ons veral oplettend wees wanneer ons met die mense om ons omgaan—familie, vriend en selfs die vreemdeling. Wie weet, dalk voel die buurman langsaan heeltemal alleen en mismoedig. Of miskien worstel ons beste vriend uit die kerk met ’n las wat meer lyk as wat hy of sy kan dra. Terwyl ons bid, kan ons God vra om mense in ons gedagtes te bring wat deur ons hulp op die een of ander manier geseën sal word. Ons weet nooit wanneer ons glimlag of bemoedigende woord ’n verandering in iemand se ewige welsyn sal help teweegbring nie.

Broeders, as iemand deur een of ander oortreding oorval word, moet julle wat geestelik is, so iemand in ’n gees van sagmoedigheid reghelp; let op jouself, dat jy nie ook versoek word nie. Dra mekaar se laste, en vervul so die wet van Christus. Want as iemand dink dat hy iets is, terwyl hy niks is nie, bedrieg hy homself. Maar laat elkeen sy eie werk toets; dan sal hy alleen in homself kan roem, en nie in ’n ander nie. Want elkeen sal sy eie las dra –Galasiërs 6:1-5.

Geen versoeking het oor julle gekom behalwe ’n menslike een nie; maar God is getrou, en Hy sal nie toelaat dat julle bo julle vermoë versoek word nie… –1 Korintiërs 10:13.

My broers, beskou dit as louter vreugde wanneer julle in allerhande versoekings beland; omdat julle weet dat die beproewing van julle geloof volharding bewerk –Jakobus 1:2-3.

In hierdie verse sien ek ’n aantal dinge wat God wil hê ons as lewensriglyn moet gebruik.

  1. God sal nie toelaat dat ons bo dit wat ons kan verduur, versoek word nie. Dit is volgens sy feit, nie volgens ons gevoel nie.
  2. Elkeen van ons SAL in versoekings beland, maar wanneer ons God se soewereiniteit in ons beproewinge raaksien, kan ons rus terwyl ons “dit alles as vreugde beskou”.
  3. Wanneer dit lyk asof ons geloof beproef en getoets word, soms skynbaar amper tot breekpunt, kan ons verseker wees dat God daar midde-in is en dat Hy volgens sy wil iets aan die werk is.
  4. God sal laste in elkeen van ons se lewens toelaat en Hy verwag dat elkeen van ons “ons eie laste dra”.
  5. God sal toelaat dat ons medemens deur moeilike tye gaan, waartydens God verwag dat ons ons sukkelende broer of suster raaksien en alles doen wat ons kan om die las te verlig—deur gebed, bemoedigende woorde of hulpvaardige dade.

Ten slotte laat ek julle met verskeie verse wat Paulus aan die gemeente in Galasië geskryf het. En laat ons nie moeg word om goed te doen nie, want op die regte tyd sal ons maai as ons nie verslap nie. Laat ons dan, terwyl ons die geleentheid het, aan almal goed doen, veral aan dié wat aan die huisgesin van die geloof behoort. –Galasiërs 6:9-10. As vreemdelinge en pelgrims hier op aarde, laat ons nie ons ewige tuiste, ons medelydende Verlosser, ons soewereine God en ons Abba-Vader uit die oog verloor nie.

Ramona* was a little girl who was very busy and active. Like other four-year-old’s, there were a lot of things Ramona could do. She could ride a bike, climb a tree, wash dishes, write her name, and ride her pony all by herself. One of Ramona’s favorite things to do was to ride horses. Her family had two horses and a pony. How fun those evenings were when they would hitch their pony, Tony, to the cart, and the whole family would take turns riding. Or when Ramona and three of her sisters would pack onto Tony’s back and go for a ride.

There were lots of things Ramona could do, but sometimes she thought she could do more than she really could. And sometimes she thought she was bigger than she really was.

One beautiful Summer evening, some guests came to Ramona’s house. When guests came, that usually meant a fun time.

On this particular evening, after supper, Ramona’s older siblings were riding horses with the guests. It looked like so much fun as they trotted around the pond and through the lawn. Ramona wanted to ride too, but she had to wait her turn. While she waited, she played on the lawn with Clifford, the dog. She soon tired of that and went for a spin on her bike. Then an idea popped into her mind. She ran off to the pasture entrance and climbed up the gate. She liked to pretend she was a monkey, swinging on the bars and climbing up and down. Then she tried balancing on a bar and taking her hands off the gate. Her siblings and their guests were riding nearby. Ramona threw her arms into the air, and while balancing on the gate, yelled to the riders, “Look at me! Look at me!” She felt very big to be balancing on the gate. Suddenly, her foot slipped and, down she went, into the dust. She blinked with surprise and quickly jumped up, brushing off her dress. She looked around, embarrassed, but no one seemed to notice. She climbed back up the side of the gate and began playing again. Ramona grew impatient, waiting for her ride. No one seemed to remember that she wanted to ride the horses. She thought it would be fun to see how high she could balance on the gate, so she climbed as high as she dared. She wanted others to see how brave she was, so waving her arms, she shouted, “Hey everyone! Look at me!” But again, her foot slipped off the gate. This time, however, she narrowly escaped falling to the ground. Ramona’s dad saw her and walked over to her. “Ramona,” he said, “I want you to stay off the gate.”

Ramona got down and tried to find something else to do. After playing for a while, her father’s command to stay off the gate seemed to slip from her mind, and she started climbing on the gate again. Then Ramona’s older sister, Elise, walked over, and quietly told her, “Ramona, you shouldn’t be showing off to our guests.” Ramona didn’t like that advice. Into one ear and out the other it went. She assured herself that she wasn’t showing off! She was just… well, just playing.

She climbed up just as high as she could, and once again, she waved her arms in the air, crying, “Look at me, everyone!” Suddenly, before she knew what was happening, she had landed on the ground with a thud and began to cry at the top of her lungs. Sure, she felt some pain, but mostly she was shocked and ashamed.

Ramona’s father came over to her and picked her up, making sure she wasn’t badly hurt, and carried her to the house. It was yet light outside, and still early in the evening, but he took her upstairs to her bed.

Before putting her to bed, he talked with her. Ramona was still crying, and Papa attempted to dry her tears. “Ramona, listen, can you be quiet for a bit? Why do you think you fell?” She sniffled and shrugged her shoulders. Papa continued, “If you would have obeyed me, and stayed off the gate like I told you to, you would not have fallen. Elise also told you to stop showing off, but you didn’t listen. Do you know that showing off is really pride? The Bible says, Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

Ramona nodded her head. “Are you sorry for disobeying me, Ramona?” Papa asked. “Yes, Papa, I am sorry” she replied tearfully. Papa decided to let her fall and going to bed early be her punishment this time. Ramona would have preferred a spanking instead of needing to go to bed early, which was a great grief to her little heart. But it was good for her because it caused her to repent.

Ramona never forgot this lesson, partly because of her fall, and partly because she was sent to bed early and missed the fun of riding horses. Not only had she been proud in showing off, she had also been willfully disobedient to Papa.

Elise had written a tune to the verse that Papa had mentioned to Ramona. From then on, whenever Ramona sang that song, she remembered how true that verse proved to be for her.

Ramona* was ’n klein dogtertjie wat baie besig en bedrywig was. Soos ander vierjariges kon Ramona baie dinge doen. Sy kon fiets ry, in ’n boom klim, skottelgoed was, haar naam skryf en heeltemal op haar eie op haar ponie ry. Een van Ramona se gunstelingdinge was om perd te ry. Haar gesin het twee perde en ’n ponie gehad. Hoe lekker was daardie aande wanneer hulle hul ponie, Tony, voor die karretjie ingespan het en die hele gesin beurte gemaak het om te ry. Of wanneer Ramona en drie van haar susters op Tony se rug geklim het en gaan ry het.

Daar was baie dinge wat Ramona kon doen, maar soms het sy gedink sy kan meer doen as wat sy werklik kon. En soms het sy gedink sy is groter as wat sy werklik was.

Een pragtige someraand het daar ’n paar gaste by Ramona se huis aangekom. Wanneer daar gaste gekom het, het dit gewoonlik ’n lekker tyd beteken.

Op hierdie besondere aand het Ramona se ouer broers en susters ná ete saam met die gaste perd gery. Dit het na soveel pret gelyk terwyl hulle om die dam en deur die grasperk gedraf het. Ramona wou ook ry, maar sy moes haar beurt afwag. Terwyl sy gewag het, het sy saam met Clifford, die hond, op die grasperk gespeel. Sy het gou moeg daarvoor geraak en ’n draai op haar fiets gaan ry. Toe skiet ’n idee haar te binne. Sy hardloop na die ingang van die weiding en klim op die hek. Sy het daarvan gehou om voor te gee dat sy ’n aap was, terwyl sy aan die tralies swaai en op en af klim. Toe probeer sy om op ’n dwarslat te balanseer en haar hande van die hek af te haal. Haar broers en susters en hul gaste het naby verby gery. Ramona gooi haar arms in die lug en roep vir die ruiters terwyl sy op die hek balanseer: “Kyk na my! Kyk na my!” Sy het baie groot gevoel terwyl sy op die hek balanseer. Skielik gly haar voet en daar val sy, in die stof. Sy knip verbaas haar oë en spring vinnig op terwyl sy haar rok afstof. Sy kyk verleë rond, maar dit lyk asof niemand dit agtergekom het nie. Sy klim weer teen die kant van die hek op en begin weer speel. Ramona raak ongeduldig terwyl sy wag vir haar rit. Dit het gelyk asof niemand onthou het dat sy perd wou ry nie. Sy het gedink dit sou pret wees om te sien hoe hoog sy op die hek kon balanseer, en daarom het sy so hoog geklim as wat sy durf. Sy wou hê die ander moes sien hoe dapper sy was, daarom het sy haar arms gewaai en geskree: “Haai almal! Kyk na my!” Maar weer gly haar voet van die hek af. Hierdie keer het sy egter net-net gekeer dat sy grond toe val. Ramona se pa het haar gesien en na haar toe gekom. “Ramona,” het hy gesê, “ek wil hê jy moet van die hek af bly.”

Ramona het afgeklim en iets anders probeer kry om te doen. Nadat sy ’n rukkie gespeel het, het haar pa se bevel om van die hek af te bly skynbaar uit haar gedagtes verdwyn, en sy het weer op die hek begin klim. Toe kom Ramona se ouer suster, Elise, nader en sê stilletjies vir haar: “Ramona, jy moenie voor ons gaste spog nie.” Ramona het nie van dié raad gehou nie. Dit het by die een oor ingegaan en by die ander een uitgegaan. Sy het haarself verseker dat sy nie gespog het nie! Sy het net… wel, net gespeel.

Sy het so hoog geklim as wat sy kon, en weer eens haar arms in die lug gewaai en uitgeroep: “Kyk na my, almal!” Skielik, voordat sy besef het wat gebeur, het sy met ’n doef op die grond beland en hard begin huil. Ja, sy het ’n bietjie pyn gevoel, maar meestal was sy geskok en skaam.

Ramona se pa het na haar toe gekom en haar opgetel. Hy het seker gemaak dat sy nie ernstig seergekry het nie en haar toe huis toe gedra. Dit was nog lig buite en dit was nog vroeg in die aand, maar hy het haar boontoe na haar bed geneem.

Voordat hy haar in die bed gesit het, het hy met haar gepraat. Ramona het steeds gehuil, en Pappa het probeer om haar trane af te droog. “Ramona, luister, kan jy vir ’n rukkie stil wees? Hoekom dink jy het jy geval?” Sy het gesnif en haar skouers opgetrek. Pappa het voortgegaan: “As jy my gehoorsaam het en van die hek af gebly het soos ek jou gesê het, sou jy nie geval het nie. Elise het ook vir jou gesê om op te hou spog, maar jy het nie geluister nie. Weet jy dat spog eintlik hoogmoed is? Die Bybel sê: Hoogmoed kom voor die verderf, en ’n hoogmoedige gees voor die val – Spreuke 16:18.

Ramona het haar kop geknik. “Is jy jammer dat jy my ongehoorsaam was, Ramona?” het Pappa gevra. “Ja, Pappa, ek is jammer,” het sy huilerig geantwoord. Pappa het besluit om haar val en die feit dat sy vroeg bed toe moes gaan, dié keer haar straf te laat wees. Ramona sou eerder ’n pak slae verkies het as om vroeg bed toe te moet gaan, wat vir haar klein hartjie ’n groot verdriet was. Maar dit was goed vir haar, want dit het haar tot bekering gebring.

Ramona het hierdie les nooit vergeet nie, deels weens haar val en deels omdat sy vroeg bed toe gestuur is en die pret van perdry misgeloop het. Sy was nie net hoogmoedig deur te spog nie; sy was ook moedswillig ongehoorsaam aan Pappa.

Elise het ’n wysie gemaak vir die vers wat Pappa vir Ramona genoem het. Van toe af, elke keer wanneer Ramona daardie liedjie gesing het, het sy onthou hoe waar daardie vers vir haar geblyk het te wees.

Many people ask, “Is listening to secular music a sin? Is there anything wrong with CCM (Christian Contemporary Music)? Is it okay for Christians to listen to rap, rock, country, pop, or rhythm and blues?” For the sake of this article, I am going to refer to all the music listed above as “secular” music.

Should Christians only listen to “A cappella” music? Music is compelling, and it can have a significant effect on how we live our lives. Music influences us negatively or positively. We should ask the question, “Does the music that I listen to draw me closer to God, or does it push me away from Him and closer to Satan?”

The primary purpose of music is to worship (the expression of reverence and adoration to something or someone). Yet at times we as believers still fail in listening to good wholesome music. This is a problem since most secular music is evil and promotes things that God hates.

Secular music is very catchy and addicting. The flesh would rather listen to secular music than to godly music. This type of music negatively influences the mind and is not profitable. If the song encourages evil, promotes worldliness, gives you bad thoughts, changes your actions for the wrong, and influences your speech for the wrong, we should not be listening to it. When it comes to music, we can comfortably lie to ourselves in this area. Have you lied to yourself? Have you said, “God is OK with this type of music,” yet deep down in your heart, you know He is convicting you, and that He is NOT OK with it?

Secular music is often sensual. The meaning of sensual is “of arousing gratification of the senses and physical.” Is the music that we listen to sensual? Does it put our mind in a state of just going with the beat? How do our bodies want to respond when we listen to such music? If our bodies swing with the rhythm of the music, it is not honoring to the Lord; it is not bringing glory to His name; it is not putting our mind and body in a position to worship the Lord.

We always worship something when we listen to music. If we are concentrating on music that is not of God, we are worshiping our flesh, the world, or even the devil. Usually, music like CCM tends to draw attention to ourselves and not to God. Music like this is very sensual. Can we truly worship God when we listen to this type of music?

CCM is a genre of modern popular music in which the lyrics are focused on matters concerned with the Christian faith. It formed as those affected by the 1960s’ “Jesus movement” revival began to express themselves with a more contemporary style of music. Before that, it was hymns and other gospel songs that were prevalent in the church at the time. Whether we know it or not, much of the CCM adds a pulsating beat (syncopation) at a place that it is not naturally supposed to be. The pulsating beat that is relevant in CCM does not appeal to the spirit of man in worship, rather, it appeals to the flesh. The type of music that appeals to the flesh is not of God but is of the devil. Today, CCM is a term that is used to refer to pop, rock, or praise & worship styles of rhythm and beat, so long as the lyrics fall under the definition of CCM.

Philippians tells us that we are supposed to think on … whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

Secular music does not pass the Philippians 4:8 test. Most secular music has lyrics that are impure, while all of it has a rhythm or beat that is against God’s order. The devil uses it all to influence people to sin or to think about sin. It will affect you in some way. Is the influence of the music that we listen to good or bad? For example, if we are concentrating on music that affects our thoughts or lifestyle in the wrong way, then it is a negative influence that we must put out of our lives.

The Hebrews started the tradition of using music without accompaniment after the fall of the second temple in 70 A.D., at which time instruments were not allowed during a period of mourning after the fall. Throughout history up until The Renaissance, instrumental music was mostly associated with dancing and merry making. As one could not have too much fun in places of worship, this kind of amusing music was not popular with religious leaders.

A cappella is an Italian phrase which means “in the style of the chapel”. It was initially used to refer to music that was sung in a chapel or small worship space without accompanying instruments, as opposed to a large church where an organ usually attended vocal music. The term has since come to mean any music sung without accompaniment, whether sacred (religious) or secular (non-religious). A cappella music can be sung by a large choir, a small group, or as a solo.

In Orthodox and Conservative Jewish congregations, the tradition of singing mostly A cappella still exists. In these synagogues, it is customary for a cantor to chant or sing an authoritative text from the scriptures which the congregation responds to in kind. The only instruments used might be a pitch pipe to give everyone a starting note or a ram’s horn on a special occasion or a holiday.

The early church developed the tradition of A cappella singing from the Hebrews’ Jewish tradition, chanting psalms, or other scriptures and using a cantor as a leader. Gregorian chant was the dominant form of church music starting around 590 A.D. It is a single, simple, melodic line half-spoken, half-sung in a free rhythmic style. In the early church, instrumental music was associated with the sinful outside world and was considered a negative influence.

The tradition of unaccompanied sacred vocal music continued during The Renaissance. Although instruments sometimes doubled or substituted for a vocal line, vocal music mostly stood on its own. The sound of a choir of voices in a chapel with excellent acoustics had a particularly ethereal effect.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was one of the most significant composers of The Renaissance in Italy, writing hundreds of masses and motets for the church. ‘The Palestrina Style,’ as it is called, was a sophisticated A cappella form using many voices singing with different music and text coming in at different times. This was called polyphonic, as opposed to homophonic, which means one melodic line sung together or in the same rhythm.

The Apostle Paul writes, Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; –Ephesians 5:19. Does that sound like making music with instruments? Or does it rather seem like singing praises to God from the heart?

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them –Acts 16:25. When Paul and Silas were in prison, and they were in stocks singing at midnight, I don’t believe that they were singing to bring glory to themselves. They were singing to bring glory to God the Father. The result of them giving God the glory is quite astounding. There was an earthquake, the foundations of the prison shook, the doors flew open, and everyone’s prison bands broke. At the end of this happening, the jailor came trembling before Paul and Silas and asked: “What must I do to be saved?”

Colossians also tells us that we should Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Do we let psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs teach us, admonish us, and encourage us?

I wonder what hymn Jesus sang with His disciples at the last supper before He went out to the Mount of Olives. I doubt that they were singing to themselves. I believe they were singing to their heavenly Father.

Pure and holy music is a blessing from the Lord. It is such a beautifully powerful thing that we should not take for granted. Sometimes God uses it to speak to us. I firmly believe that all Christians need to be listening to godly music throughout the week, not just on Sunday. It helps me stay calm, be encouraged, and keep my mind on the Lord. When my mind is on the Lord, I can go through the day blest.

We need to discipline ourselves with the things of God. We also need to get rid of things in our life that we know God is not pleased with. Godly music (music that draws our spirit and mind to the things that are from God) is the type of music that believers should listen to. Worship is what it boils down to, do we worship God or something else?

Jesus says, But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him –John 4:23.

So, let us sing in sincere worship to our Creator, let us give God the glory for the voices that He has given us, and let us sing and listen to godly, wholesome songs to our God.
