Greetings in the name of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. We are trusting that each of you as our readers are doing well and continuing to trust the Lord. The pandemic has created a bit of a backlog for us, along with some personal issues we have been working through, so this issue is coming to you somewhat behind schedule. Our apologies…. We plan to get the next issue printed within the next several months to get back on track.

In the last issue’s editorial, I wrote about an obscure news article which revealed that many folks across the world were surprised by the positive outcomes they were experiencing through the need to stay at home during the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic. They were enjoying family time. They were finding camaraderie in facing this challenge together. They were finding excitement in the adventure of discovering new ways to function and survive. And they were finding renewed vision and purpose in life.

However, as time has passed, this seems to have been short-lived by all who did not have a deeper level of stability in their lives. After a varying amount of time has elapsed for many folks, reality has begun to set in. Some have lost their jobs. Some have lost loved ones. Some have gone through a time of sickness. Many have been starved for fellowship with other human beings. For the elderly living in nursing homes and assisted-living facilities, and those requiring hospitalization, life has become a very lonely existence indeed, since most of these places have not allowed visitors to enter their doors.

The world is trying to find any way possible to cope and survive. There are phone conference lines. There are chat lines. There are webinars geared towards the issue. Many are doing their part to fill the gaps that this pandemic has created in the lives of the people around them.

As we step back to gain a clearer perspective of the unfolding events brought about by the pandemic, the last number of months have been a time of change and uncertainty for most. There’s the economic future, “Is my job secure?” “What about my bills?” “What about my housing?” Then there’s the greatly politicized nature of numerous issues—race inequality, conspiracy theories about the pandemic, and the government mandates regarding our response to the virus pandemic. Add to this the polarization in our country regarding politics—who is telling the truth on issues, and who will be the best option to lead the country after the upcoming election.

Despite everything else that is going on, the virus and its effects seem to be on everyone’s mind. On August 15, 2020 there was an article published by CNN, written by Ryan Prior, titled: “1 IN 4 YOUNG PEOPLE ARE REPORTING SUICIDAL THOUGHTS”. For those wanting to read the article, it can be found here:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

This article recognizes that there were positive effects during the onset of the pandemic and the resulting stay-at-home orders. This article goes on to say that as time has passed this event is different than most past events, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, and even the circumstances of 9/11. Most of these events have been localized and brief in their destructive effects, while the Covid-19 pandemic has dragged on for so long that it is becoming a way of life—with no end in sight, and its beginning is fading into our forgetful past.

According to the news article, the CDC has published data from a survey which was conducted to determine the outcome of the negative effects of the pandemic. Following are some facts as presented in the article:

  • Suicidal ideation is up among young people since last year
  • As many as one in four people ages 18 through 24 having seriously considered suicide in the 30 days preceding the survey (researchers surveyed 5,412 adults in the US between June 24 and 30.)
  • In the general US population … 11% of adults surveyed had seriously considered suicide in the past 30 days before they completed the survey.
  • The number of Americans reporting anxiety symptoms is three times the number at this same time last year, the CDC said.
  • The results reflect a nation increasingly on edge.

How sad it is to ponder this reality. As I read this news article, I had to wonder whether the percentages are the same for the church as they are for the world. A verse of scripture came to mind: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable –1 Corinthians 15:19. As Christians…

  • …we have HOPE!
  • …we have HOPE IN CHRIST!!
  • …we have HOPE both IN THIS LIFE and FOR ETERNITY!!!

Considering all this we should have a smile on our faces, hope in our hearts, and an encouraging word on our lips for all with whom we come in contact. Let’s be especially observant as we interact with the people around us—family, friend, and even the stranger. Who knows, maybe the neighbor next door is feeling all alone and discouraged. Or perhaps our best friend from church has been struggling with a burden that seems more than they can bear. As we pray, we can ask God to bring people to our minds that would be blessed by our assistance of one sort or another. We never know when our smile or encouraging word will help make a change in someone’s eternal welfare.

Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another. For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:1-5.

There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able… –1 Corinthians 10:13.

My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience –James 1:2-3.

In these verses, I see a number of things that God wants us to use to live by.

  1. God will not allow us to be tempted above that which we are able to endure. This is according to His fact, not according to our feeling.
  2. Each of us WILL fall into temptations, but as we see God’s sovereignty involved in our trials, we can rest as we “count it all joy”.
  3. When it seems that our faith is being tried and tested, sometimes seemingly almost to the breaking point, we can rest assured that God is in the middle of it and that He is up to something according to His will.
  4. God will allow burdens into each of our lives and He expects each of us to “bear our own burdens”.
  5. God will allow our fellow man to go through times of difficulty, during which God expects us to see our struggling brother or sister and do whatever we can to help ease the burden—through prayer, words of encouragement, or deeds of assistance.

In closing, I will leave you with several verses that Paul wrote to the church of Galatia. And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. –Galatians 6:9-10. As strangers and pilgrims here on this earth, let’s not lose sight of our Eternal Home, our Sympathetic Savior, our Sovereign God, and our Abba Father.

Salam dalam nama Tuhan dan Juruselamat kita, Yesus Kristus. Kami berharap Anda semua sebagai pembaca kami berada dalam keadaan baik dan terus percaya kepada Tuhan. Pandemi ini telah menyebabkan sedikit penumpukan pekerjaan bagi kami, ditambah beberapa persoalan pribadi yang sedang kami hadapi, sehingga edisi ini sampai kepada Anda agak terlambat dari jadwal. Kami mohon maaf…. Kami berencana mencetak edisi berikutnya dalam beberapa bulan mendatang agar kembali sesuai jadwal.

Dalam tajuk rencana edisi terakhir, saya menulis tentang sebuah artikel berita yang kurang dikenal, yang mengungkapkan bahwa banyak orang di seluruh dunia terkejut dengan hasil-hasil positif yang mereka alami karena harus tinggal di rumah pada awal pandemi Covid-19. Mereka menikmati waktu bersama keluarga. Mereka menemukan keakraban dalam menghadapi tantangan ini bersama-sama. Mereka merasakan kegembiraan dalam petualangan menemukan cara-cara baru untuk berfungsi dan bertahan hidup. Dan mereka menemukan kembali visi dan tujuan hidup.

Namun, seiring berjalannya waktu, hal ini tampaknya hanya berlangsung singkat bagi mereka yang tidak memiliki kestabilan hidup yang lebih mendalam. Setelah waktu yang berbeda-beda berlalu bagi banyak orang, kenyataan mulai terasa. Ada yang kehilangan pekerjaan. Ada yang kehilangan orang-orang terkasih. Ada yang jatuh sakit. Banyak yang sangat merindukan persekutuan dengan sesama manusia. Bagi para lansia yang tinggal di panti jompo dan fasilitas hunian berbantuan, serta mereka yang harus dirawat di rumah sakit, hidup benar-benar menjadi sangat sepi, karena kebanyakan tempat ini tidak mengizinkan pengunjung masuk.

Dunia sedang berusaha mencari segala cara untuk mengatasi keadaan dan bertahan hidup. Ada saluran konferensi telepon. Ada saluran obrolan. Ada webinar yang membahas persoalan ini. Banyak orang melakukan bagian mereka untuk mengisi kekosongan yang ditimbulkan pandemi ini dalam kehidupan orang-orang di sekitar mereka.

Saat kita mengambil jarak sejenak untuk memperoleh perspektif yang lebih jelas tentang peristiwa-peristiwa yang terus berkembang akibat pandemi ini, beberapa bulan terakhir telah menjadi masa perubahan dan ketidakpastian bagi kebanyakan orang. Ada masa depan ekonomi: “Apakah pekerjaan saya aman?” “Bagaimana dengan tagihan-tagihan saya?” “Bagaimana dengan tempat tinggal saya?” Lalu ada sifat berbagai persoalan yang sangat dipolitisasi—ketidaksetaraan rasial, teori konspirasi tentang pandemi, serta mandat pemerintah mengenai tanggapan kita terhadap pandemi virus ini. Tambahkan pula polarisasi politik di negara kita—siapa yang mengatakan kebenaran tentang berbagai persoalan, dan siapa yang menjadi pilihan terbaik untuk memimpin negara setelah pemilu mendatang.

Di tengah segala hal lain yang terjadi, virus dan dampaknya tampaknya ada dalam pikiran semua orang. Pada 15 Agustus 2020, CNN menerbitkan sebuah artikel yang ditulis Ryan Prior dengan judul: “1 DARI 4 ANAK MUDA MELAPORKAN PIKIRAN UNTUK BUNUH DIRI”. Bagi yang ingin membaca artikel tersebut, dapat menemukannya di sini:

https://www.cnn.com/2020/08/14/health/young-people-suicidal-ideation-wellness/index.html

Artikel ini mengakui bahwa ada dampak positif pada awal pandemi dan pemberlakuan perintah untuk tinggal di rumah yang menyusulnya. Artikel ini selanjutnya menyatakan bahwa seiring berjalannya waktu, peristiwa ini berbeda dari kebanyakan peristiwa di masa lalu, seperti tornado, badai topan, gempa bumi, bahkan keadaan pada 9/11. Kebanyakan peristiwa tersebut dampak kehancurannya bersifat setempat dan singkat, sementara pandemi Covid-19 telah berlangsung begitu lama sehingga menjadi bagian dari kehidupan—tanpa akhir yang terlihat, dan awal mulanya semakin memudar ke masa lalu yang kita lupakan.

Menurut artikel berita itu, CDC telah menerbitkan data dari sebuah survei yang dilakukan untuk mengetahui dampak negatif pandemi. Berikut beberapa fakta sebagaimana disajikan dalam artikel tersebut:

  • Pikiran untuk bunuh diri meningkat di kalangan anak muda sejak tahun lalu
  • Sebanyak satu dari empat orang berusia 18 hingga 24 tahun pernah serius mempertimbangkan bunuh diri dalam 30 hari sebelum survei (para peneliti menyurvei 5,412 orang dewasa di AS antara 24 dan 30 Juni.)
  • Di antara populasi umum AS … 11% orang dewasa yang disurvei pernah serius mempertimbangkan bunuh diri dalam 30 hari sebelum mereka menyelesaikan survei.
  • Jumlah warga Amerika yang melaporkan gejala kecemasan tiga kali lipat dibandingkan jumlah pada waktu yang sama tahun lalu, kata CDC.
  • Hasilnya mencerminkan suatu bangsa yang semakin diliputi ketegangan.

Betapa menyedihkan merenungkan kenyataan ini. Ketika membaca artikel berita ini, saya bertanya-tanya apakah persentasenya sama di gereja dan di dunia. Sebuah ayat Kitab Suci terlintas di benak saya: Jika hanya dalam hidup ini saja kita menaruh pengharapan pada Kristus, maka kita adalah orang-orang yang paling malang dari segala manusia –1 Korintus 15:19. Sebagai orang Kristen…

  • …kita memiliki PENGHARAPAN!
  • …kita memiliki PENGHARAPAN DI DALAM KRISTUS!!
  • …kita memiliki PENGHARAPAN baik DALAM HIDUP INI maupun UNTUK KEKEKALAN!!!

Mengingat semua ini, seharusnya kita tersenyum, menyimpan pengharapan di dalam hati, dan mengucapkan kata-kata yang menguatkan kepada setiap orang yang kita jumpai. Marilah kita sungguh-sungguh memperhatikan orang-orang di sekitar kita—keluarga, teman, bahkan orang asing. Siapa tahu, mungkin tetangga sebelah merasa benar-benar sendirian dan putus asa. Atau mungkin sahabat terbaik kita dari gereja sedang bergumul dengan beban yang terasa lebih berat daripada yang sanggup ditanggungnya. Saat berdoa, kita dapat meminta Allah menghadirkan dalam pikiran kita orang-orang yang akan diberkati oleh bantuan kita dalam satu dan lain cara. Kita tidak pernah tahu kapan senyuman atau kata-kata penguatan kita akan membantu mengubah keadaan kekal seseorang.

Saudara-saudara, kalaupun seseorang kedapatan melakukan suatu pelanggaran, maka kamu yang rohani harus memimpin orang itu ke jalan yang benar dalam roh lemah lembut, sambil menjaga dirimu sendiri, supaya kamu juga jangan kena pencobaan. Bertolong-tolonganlah menanggung bebanmu! Demikianlah kamu memenuhi hukum Kristus. Sebab kalau seseorang menyangka bahwa ia berarti, padahal ia sama sekali tidak berarti, ia menipu dirinya sendiri. Baiklah tiap-tiap orang menguji pekerjaannya sendiri; maka ia boleh bermegah melihat keadaannya sendiri dan bukan melihat keadaan orang lain. Sebab tiap-tiap orang akan memikul tanggungannya sendiri –Galatia 6:1-5.

Pencobaan-pencobaan yang kamu alami ialah pencobaan-pencobaan biasa, yang tidak melebihi kekuatan manusia. Sebab Allah setia dan karena itu Ia tidak akan membiarkan kamu dicobai melampaui kekuatanmu… –1 Korintus 10:13.

Saudara-saudaraku, anggaplah sebagai suatu kebahagiaan, apabila kamu jatuh ke dalam berbagai-bagai pencobaan, sebab kamu tahu, bahwa ujian terhadap imanmu itu menghasilkan ketekunan –Yakobus 1:2-3.

Dalam ayat-ayat ini, saya melihat beberapa hal yang Allah ingin kita jadikan pedoman hidup.

  1. Allah tidak akan membiarkan kita dicobai melampaui apa yang sanggup kita tanggung. Hal ini sesuai dengan fakta-Nya, bukan perasaan kita.
  2. Kita masing-masing PASTI akan jatuh ke dalam pencobaan, tetapi ketika kita melihat kedaulatan Allah bekerja dalam ujian-ujian kita, kita dapat beristirahat sambil “menganggap semuanya sebagai suatu kebahagiaan”.
  3. Ketika iman kita tampaknya sedang diuji dan dicobai, kadang-kadang seolah-olah hampir sampai pada titik hancur, kita dapat merasa yakin bahwa Allah ada di tengah-tengahnya dan sedang mengerjakan sesuatu sesuai dengan kehendak-Nya.
  4. Allah akan mengizinkan beban masuk ke dalam kehidupan kita masing-masing dan Ia mengharapkan kita masing-masing untuk “memikul tanggungan kita sendiri”.
  5. Allah akan mengizinkan sesama kita mengalami masa-masa sulit, dan selama masa itu Allah mengharapkan kita melihat saudara atau saudari kita yang sedang bergumul lalu melakukan apa pun yang mampu kita lakukan untuk meringankan bebannya—melalui doa, kata-kata penguatan, atau tindakan pertolongan.

Sebagai penutup, saya akan meninggalkan Anda dengan beberapa ayat yang ditulis Paulus kepada jemaat di Galatia. Janganlah kita jemu-jemu berbuat baik, karena apabila sudah datang waktunya, kita akan menuai, jika kita tidak menjadi lemah. Karena itu, selama masih ada kesempatan bagi kita, marilah kita berbuat baik kepada semua orang, tetapi terutama kepada kawan-kawan kita seiman. –Galatia 6:9-10. Sebagai orang asing dan pendatang di bumi ini, marilah kita tidak kehilangan pandangan akan Rumah Kekal kita, Juruselamat kita yang turut merasakan penderitaan kita, Allah kita yang berdaulat, dan Bapa kita, Abba.

As a young man I remember hearing a popular slogan about faith: “Faith begins when reason ends.” As a young Christian, I thought it was a great life slogan. As I mature in my walk with Jesus, I look back on this particular slogan and shake my head. I can think of no better way to misrepresent faith than by claiming it exists apart from reason.

One simple reason for rejecting this view is because it misrepresents faith. A quick search on Google turns up this definition of faith: “complete trust or confidence in someone or something.” We use this definition all the time. I might tell you I have faith in my wife, I have faith in my employer to give me a paycheck, or I have no faith in alcohol to give me a good time. This is the same way the Bible defines faith.

Hebrews 11:1 affirms that faith is “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” Biblical faith is simply a state of mind that has confidence and trust in the Lord. I have confidence that I will one day walk on the new Earth, and I have confidence that the Holy Spirit is working in the hearts of Christians. My confidence is based on, not apart from, reason. The more Jesus shows himself trustworthy, the more I trust (have confidence in) Him.

One aspect of Christ’s dependability is His word. The Old Testament was written by prophets and leaders who correctly predicted future events and ruled nations. The New Testament was written by Apostles or people that were closely associated with the apostles. We have more manuscripts of the Bible than any other work in antiquity. The Bible gives an honest portrayal of its heroes and correctly describes ancient leaders and places. In short, I trust in the Bible because it stands alone above all other books in terms of its authorship, preservation, honesty, and accuracy. The more I read it and read about it, the more my faith—and trust—increases.

Luke bases his whole Gospel on the premise that more knowledge gives more faith. He begins his book with this introduction: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled [or been surely believed] among us, just as they were handed down to us by those who from the first were eyewitnesses and servants of the word. With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught. –Luke 1:1-4. (NIV)

The apostle Paul argues that faith in God is so grounded in reality that no one has a legitimate claim against God’s existence. He writes, The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse –Romans 1:18-20. (NIV)

Knowledge of nature builds my faith in Jesus. Scripture teaches that God created all life in six days, that there was a global flood, and that animals produce after their own kind. All across our earth, the rocks cry out their testimony of the global flood. People have uncovered billions of fossils—mostly marine animals—in rock layers that were laid down by water. Animals too, live out what the Bible teaches about kinds. We can observe animals changing all around us. They change sizes, colors, and eating habits. Fish in caves lose their ability to see. Birds’ beaks adjust to the environment. In all this intricate change, all animals exist within the Biblical framework of their own kind. Sharks remain sharks; frogs remain frogs; iguanas remain iguanas; and gibbons remain gibbons. The more I learn and observe about nature, the more my faith (confidence) increases.

In some discussions of faith, it is natural for the words of Jesus to come up. After His resurrection, Jesus visits Thomas and tells him, …Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed –John 20:29. (ESV) From this, it is tempting to define faith as “believing without seeing.” That would be missing the point. I’m not claiming any superiority to Thomas, but he should have believed without seeing Jesus. All the evidence pointed to it. First, his good friends, who had proved themselves trustworthy, said Jesus was alive. Second, Jesus had plainly said He would be resurrected (see Matthew 16:21). Third, Jesus had already proven He was divine by His ability to raise the dead, control the weather, heal the sick, and multiply food. Thomas had all he needed to believe Jesus rose from the dead. Yet, he went against all reasoning and said he needed more evidence.

When confronted with the resurrected Christ, Thomas repented of his disbelief and followed Christ into martyrdom. Unfortunately, the spirit of disbelief in the face of evidence still lingers in our world. Atheists claim, in spite of all evidence to the contrary, that life can come from nothing. They claim, without any evidence, that fish turned into frogs. They blindly cling to various theories such as: The Big Bang, Punctuated Equilibrium, and Descent with Modification. They have NO workable evidence, yet they still claim to base all their thoughts on observable, repeatable reality. Christians, who with good intentions, tell them that faith begins where reason ends, unwittingly play right into their hands. This world does not need a social media definition of faith. They need to see faith for what it is: confidence in the living God based firmly in reason.

כשהייתי צעיר, אני זוכר ששמעתי סיסמה פופולרית על אמונה: „האמונה מתחילה כשההיגיון מסתיים.” כנוצרי צעיר, חשבתי שזו סיסמה נהדרת לחיים. ככל שאני מתבגר בדרכי עם ישוע, אני מביט לאחור על הסיסמה המסוימת הזאת ומניד בראשי. איני יכול לחשוב על דרך טובה יותר לסלף את משמעות האמונה מאשר לטעון שהיא מתקיימת בנפרד מן ההיגיון.

סיבה פשוטה אחת לדחות את ההשקפה הזאת היא שהיא מסלפת את משמעות האמונה. חיפוש מהיר בגוגל מעלה את ההגדרה הזאת לאמונה: „אמון מלא או ביטחון מלא במישהו או במשהו.” אנחנו משתמשים בהגדרה הזאת כל הזמן. אני עשוי לומר לך שיש לי אמונה באשתי, שיש לי אמונה במעסיק שלי שישלם לי משכורת, או שאין לי אמונה שאלכוהול יספק לי בילוי מהנה. כך בדיוק התנ״ך מגדיר אמונה.

בעברים י״א:1 נאמר שאמונה היא „ביטחון במה שאנו מקווים לו וודאות בדברים שאיננו רואים.” אמונה מקראית היא פשוט מצב נפשי של ביטחון ואמון באדון. יש לי ביטחון שיום אחד אתהלך בארץ החדשה, ויש לי ביטחון שרוח הקודש פועלת בלבם של המאמינים. הביטחון שלי מבוסס על ההיגיון, ולא בנפרד ממנו. ככל שישוע מוכיח את עצמו כאמין יותר, כך אני בוטח בו יותר (כלומר, בטוח בו יותר).

אחד ההיבטים של מהימנותו של המשיח הוא דברו. התנ״ך נכתב בידי נביאים ומנהיגים שחזו נכונה אירועים עתידיים ושלטו באומות. הברית החדשה נכתבה בידי שליחים או אנשים שהיו קשורים קשר הדוק לשליחים. יש לנו יותר כתבי יד של התנ״ך מכל יצירה אחרת מן העת העתיקה. התנ״ך מתאר בכנות את גיבוריו ומתאר במדויק מנהיגים ומקומות מן העת העתיקה. בקיצור, אני בוטח בתנ״ך מפני שהוא ניצב לבדו מעל לכל הספרים האחרים בכל הנוגע למחבריו, לשימורו, ליושרו ולדיוקו. ככל שאני קורא בו וקורא עליו יותר, כך אמונתי — ובטחוני — גדלים.

לוקס מבסס את כל הבשורה שלו על ההנחה שידע רב יותר מוביל לאמונה רבה יותר. הוא פותח את ספרו בהקדמה הזאת: רבים ניסו לערוך סיפור על הדברים שהתגשמו [או שהאמינו בהם בביטחון] בקרבנו, כפי שמסרו לנו אותם מי שהיו מראשית הדברים עדי ראייה ומשרתי הדבר. לכן, לאחר שחקרתי אני עצמי בדקדקנות את הכול מראשית הדברים, החלטתי גם אני לכתוב לך, תאופילוס הנכבד ביותר, תיאור מסודר, כדי שתדע בוודאות את הדברים שלמדת. –לוקס א׳:1-4. (NIV)

השליח פאולוס טוען שהאמונה באלוהים מעוגנת כל כך במציאות, שאין לאיש טענה מוצדקת נגד קיומו של אלוהים. הוא כותב: זעמו של אלוהים מתגלה מן השמים נגד כל רשעותם ועוולתם של בני אדם, המעכבים את האמת בעוולתם, שכן מה שאפשר לדעת על אלוהים גלוי להם, מפני שאלוהים גילה להם זאת. שהרי מאז בריאת העולם נראים בבירור תכונותיו הבלתי נראות של אלוהים — כוחו הנצחי וטבעו האלוהי — כשהן מובנות מתוך הדברים שנבראו, ולכן אין לבני האדם תירוץ –רומים א׳:18-20. (NIV)

הידע על הטבע מחזק את אמונתי בישוע. כתבי הקודש מלמדים שאלוהים ברא את כל החיים בשישה ימים, שהיה מבול עולמי, ושבעלי חיים מולידים לפי מינם. בכל רחבי הארץ, הסלעים משמיעים את עדותם על המבול העולמי. בני אדם חשפו מיליארדי מאובנים — רובם של בעלי חיים ימיים — בשכבות סלע שנוצרו משקיעת מים. גם בעלי החיים ממחישים את מה שהתנ״ך מלמד על מינים. אנחנו יכולים לראות בעלי חיים משתנים סביבנו. הם משתנים בגודל, בצבע ובהרגלי האכילה. דגים במערות מאבדים את יכולת הראייה. מקוריהם של ציפורים מסתגלים לסביבה. בתוך כל השינויים המורכבים האלה, כל בעלי החיים מתקיימים במסגרת המקראית של מינם. כרישים נשארים כרישים; צפרדעים נשארות צפרדעים; איגואנות נשארות איגואנות; וגיבונים נשארים גיבונים. ככל שאני לומד ומתבונן יותר בטבע, כך אמונתי (ביטחוני) גדלה.

בדיונים מסוימים על אמונה, טבעי שדבריו של ישוע יעלו. לאחר תחייתו, ישוע בא אל תומא ואומר לו: …האם האמנת מפני שראית אותי? אשרי מי שלא ראו ובכל זאת האמינו –יוחנן כ׳:29. (ESV) על סמך הדברים האלה, מפתה להגדיר אמונה כ„אמונה בלי לראות”. אבל זו תהיה החמצה של הנקודה. איני טוען שאני נעלה על תומא, אבל הוא היה צריך להאמין בלי לראות את ישוע. כל הראיות הצביעו על כך. ראשית, חבריו הטובים, שהוכיחו את עצמם כאמינים, אמרו שישוע חי. שנית, ישוע אמר בבירור שהוא יקום לתחייה (ראו מתי ט״ז:21). שלישית, ישוע כבר הוכיח שהוא אלוהי ביכולתו להקים מתים, לשלוט במזג האוויר, לרפא חולים ולהרבות מזון. כל מה שתומא היה זקוק לו כדי להאמין שישוע קם מן המתים כבר היה בידיו. ובכל זאת, הוא פעל בניגוד לכל היגיון ואמר שהוא זקוק לראיות נוספות.

כשעמד מול המשיח שקם לתחייה, תומא חזר בו מחוסר אמונתו והלך בעקבות המשיח עד למותו כמרטיר. למרבה הצער, רוח חוסר האמונה לנוכח ראיות עדיין שורה בעולמנו. אתאיסטים טוענים, למרות כל הראיות ההפוכות, שחיים יכולים להיווצר מכלום. הם טוענים, בלי שום ראיות, שדגים הפכו לצפרדעים. הם נאחזים בעיוורון בתיאוריות שונות, כגון: המפץ הגדול, שיווי משקל מקוטע, ומוצא עם שינויים. אין להם ראיות ישימות, כלל, ובכל זאת הם עדיין טוענים שכל מחשבותיהם מבוססות על מציאות נצפית וחוזרת. נוצרים שאומרים להם בכוונות טובות שהאמונה מתחילה במקום שבו ההיגיון מסתיים, משרתים אותם בבלי דעת. העולם הזה אינו זקוק להגדרה של אמונה מרשתות חברתיות. הוא צריך לראות את האמונה כפי שהיא: ביטחון באל החי, המבוסס היטב על ההיגיון.

Ramona* was a little girl who was very busy and active. Like other four-year-old’s, there were a lot of things Ramona could do. She could ride a bike, climb a tree, wash dishes, write her name, and ride her pony all by herself. One of Ramona’s favorite things to do was to ride horses. Her family had two horses and a pony. How fun those evenings were when they would hitch their pony, Tony, to the cart, and the whole family would take turns riding. Or when Ramona and three of her sisters would pack onto Tony’s back and go for a ride.

There were lots of things Ramona could do, but sometimes she thought she could do more than she really could. And sometimes she thought she was bigger than she really was.

One beautiful Summer evening, some guests came to Ramona’s house. When guests came, that usually meant a fun time.

On this particular evening, after supper, Ramona’s older siblings were riding horses with the guests. It looked like so much fun as they trotted around the pond and through the lawn. Ramona wanted to ride too, but she had to wait her turn. While she waited, she played on the lawn with Clifford, the dog. She soon tired of that and went for a spin on her bike. Then an idea popped into her mind. She ran off to the pasture entrance and climbed up the gate. She liked to pretend she was a monkey, swinging on the bars and climbing up and down. Then she tried balancing on a bar and taking her hands off the gate. Her siblings and their guests were riding nearby. Ramona threw her arms into the air, and while balancing on the gate, yelled to the riders, “Look at me! Look at me!” She felt very big to be balancing on the gate. Suddenly, her foot slipped and, down she went, into the dust. She blinked with surprise and quickly jumped up, brushing off her dress. She looked around, embarrassed, but no one seemed to notice. She climbed back up the side of the gate and began playing again. Ramona grew impatient, waiting for her ride. No one seemed to remember that she wanted to ride the horses. She thought it would be fun to see how high she could balance on the gate, so she climbed as high as she dared. She wanted others to see how brave she was, so waving her arms, she shouted, “Hey everyone! Look at me!” But again, her foot slipped off the gate. This time, however, she narrowly escaped falling to the ground. Ramona’s dad saw her and walked over to her. “Ramona,” he said, “I want you to stay off the gate.”

Ramona got down and tried to find something else to do. After playing for a while, her father’s command to stay off the gate seemed to slip from her mind, and she started climbing on the gate again. Then Ramona’s older sister, Elise, walked over, and quietly told her, “Ramona, you shouldn’t be showing off to our guests.” Ramona didn’t like that advice. Into one ear and out the other it went. She assured herself that she wasn’t showing off! She was just… well, just playing.

She climbed up just as high as she could, and once again, she waved her arms in the air, crying, “Look at me, everyone!” Suddenly, before she knew what was happening, she had landed on the ground with a thud and began to cry at the top of her lungs. Sure, she felt some pain, but mostly she was shocked and ashamed.

Ramona’s father came over to her and picked her up, making sure she wasn’t badly hurt, and carried her to the house. It was yet light outside, and still early in the evening, but he took her upstairs to her bed.

Before putting her to bed, he talked with her. Ramona was still crying, and Papa attempted to dry her tears. “Ramona, listen, can you be quiet for a bit? Why do you think you fell?” She sniffled and shrugged her shoulders. Papa continued, “If you would have obeyed me, and stayed off the gate like I told you to, you would not have fallen. Elise also told you to stop showing off, but you didn’t listen. Do you know that showing off is really pride? The Bible says, Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

Ramona nodded her head. “Are you sorry for disobeying me, Ramona?” Papa asked. “Yes, Papa, I am sorry” she replied tearfully. Papa decided to let her fall and going to bed early be her punishment this time. Ramona would have preferred a spanking instead of needing to go to bed early, which was a great grief to her little heart. But it was good for her because it caused her to repent.

Ramona never forgot this lesson, partly because of her fall, and partly because she was sent to bed early and missed the fun of riding horses. Not only had she been proud in showing off, she had also been willfully disobedient to Papa.

Elise had written a tune to the verse that Papa had mentioned to Ramona. From then on, whenever Ramona sang that song, she remembered how true that verse proved to be for her.

Ramona* was een klein meisje dat het erg druk had en heel actief was. Net als andere vierjarigen kon Ramona heel veel dingen. Ze kon fietsen, in een boom klimmen, afwassen, haar naam schrijven en helemaal zelf op haar pony rijden. Een van Ramona’s favoriete bezigheden was paardrijden. Haar gezin had twee paarden en een pony. Wat waren die avonden leuk wanneer ze hun pony Tony voor de kar spanden en het hele gezin om de beurt een ritje maakte. Of wanneer Ramona en drie van haar zusjes samen op Tony’s rug klommen en gingen rijden.

Er waren veel dingen die Ramona kon, maar soms dacht ze dat ze meer kon dan werkelijk het geval was. En soms dacht ze dat ze groter was dan ze werkelijk was.

Op een mooie zomeravond kwamen er gasten bij Ramona thuis. Als er gasten kwamen, betekende dat meestal dat het gezellig zou worden.

Die avond reden Ramona’s oudere broers en zussen na het avondeten samen met de gasten paard. Het zag er zo leuk uit terwijl ze rond de vijver en over het grasveld draafden. Ramona wilde ook rijden, maar ze moest op haar beurt wachten. Terwijl ze wachtte, speelde ze op het grasveld met Clifford, de hond. Daar kreeg ze al gauw genoeg van en ze ging een stukje fietsen. Toen kreeg ze een idee. Ze rende naar de ingang van de weide en klom op het hek. Ze deed graag alsof ze een aap was: ze slingerde aan de spijlen en klom op en neer. Toen probeerde ze haar evenwicht te bewaren op een spijl en haar handen van het hek te halen. Haar broers en zussen en de gasten reden vlakbij. Ramona gooide haar armen in de lucht en riep, terwijl ze haar evenwicht op het hek bewaarde, naar de ruiters: ‘Kijk eens naar mij! Kijk eens naar mij!’ Ze voelde zich heel groot terwijl ze op het hek haar evenwicht hield. Plotseling gleed haar voet weg en viel ze naar beneden, in het stof. Verbaasd knipperde ze met haar ogen en sprong snel overeind, terwijl ze haar jurk afklopte. Beschaamd keek ze om zich heen, maar niemand leek het te hebben gemerkt. Ze klom weer langs de zijkant van het hek omhoog en begon opnieuw te spelen. Ramona werd ongeduldig terwijl ze op haar ritje wachtte. Niemand leek eraan te denken dat ze graag paard wilde rijden. Ze dacht dat het leuk zou zijn om te zien hoe hoog ze haar evenwicht op het hek kon bewaren, dus klom ze zo hoog als ze durfde. Ze wilde dat anderen zouden zien hoe dapper ze was, dus zwaaide ze met haar armen en riep: ‘Hé, allemaal! Kijk eens naar mij!’ Maar opnieuw gleed haar voet van het hek. Deze keer ontsnapte ze echter ternauwernood aan een val op de grond. Ramona’s vader zag haar en liep naar haar toe. ‘Ramona,’ zei hij, ‘ik wil dat je van het hek af blijft.’

Ramona klom naar beneden en probeerde iets anders te bedenken om te doen. Nadat ze een poosje had gespeeld, leek haar vaders bevel om van het hek af te blijven uit haar gedachten te zijn verdwenen en begon ze weer op het hek te klimmen. Toen kwam Ramona’s oudere zus Elise naar haar toe en zei zachtjes: ‘Ramona, je moet niet opscheppen tegenover onze gasten.’ Ramona vond dat geen fijn advies. Het ging het ene oor in en het andere weer uit. Ze verzekerde zichzelf dat ze helemaal niet opschepte! Ze was gewoon… nou ja, gewoon aan het spelen.

Ze klom zo hoog als ze kon en zwaaide opnieuw met haar armen in de lucht, terwijl ze riep: ‘Kijk allemaal eens naar mij!’ Plotseling, voordat ze besefte wat er gebeurde, kwam ze met een dreun op de grond terecht en begon ze uit volle borst te huilen. Natuurlijk voelde ze pijn, maar vooral was ze geschokt en beschaamd.

Ramona’s vader kwam naar haar toe, tilde haar op en controleerde of ze niet ernstig gewond was. Daarna droeg hij haar naar huis. Het was buiten nog licht en het was nog vroeg op de avond, maar hij bracht haar naar boven, naar haar bed.

Voordat hij haar naar bed bracht, praatte hij met haar. Ramona huilde nog steeds en papa probeerde haar tranen te drogen. ‘Ramona, luister eens, kun je even stil zijn? Waarom denk je dat je gevallen bent?’ Ze snoof en haalde haar schouders op. Papa ging verder: ‘Als je me had gehoorzaamd en van het hek af was gebleven, zoals ik je had gezegd, was je niet gevallen. Elise zei ook dat je moest ophouden met opscheppen, maar je luisterde niet. Weet je dat opscheppen eigenlijk hoogmoed is? De Bijbel zegt: Hoogmoed komt vóór de ondergang, en een hoogmoedige geest vóór de val – Spreuken 16:18.

Ramona knikte. ‘Heb je er spijt van dat je me niet gehoorzaamd hebt, Ramona?’ vroeg papa. ‘Ja, papa, het spijt me,’ antwoordde ze met tranen in haar ogen. As a young man I remember hearing a popular slogan about faith: “Faith begins when reason ends.” As a young Christian, I thought it was a great life slogan. As I mature in my walk with Jesus, I look back on this particular slogan and shake my head. I can think of no better way to misrepresent faith than by claiming it exists apart from reason.

One simple reason for rejecting this view is because it misrepresents faith. A quick search on Google turns up this definition of faith: “complete trust or confidence in someone or something.” We use this definition all the time. I might tell you I have faith in my wife, I have faith in my employer to give me a paycheck, or I have no faith in alcohol to give me a good time. This is the same way the Bible defines faith.

Hebrews 11:1 affirms that faith is “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.” Biblical faith is simply a state of mind that has confidence and trust in the Lord. I have confidence that I will one day walk on the new Earth, and I have confidence that the Holy Spirit is working in the hearts of Christians. My confidence is based on, not apart from, reason. The more Jesus shows himself trustworthy, the more I trust (have confidence in) Him.

One aspect of Christ’s dependability is His word. The Old Testament was written by prophets and leaders who correctly predicted future events and ruled nations. The New Testament was written by Apostles or people that were closely associated with the apostles. We have more manuscripts of the Bible than any other work in antiquity. The Bible gives an honest portrayal of its heroes and correctly describes ancient leaders and places. In short, I trust in the Bible because it stands alone above all other books in terms of its authorship, preservation, honesty, and accuracy. The more I read it and read about it, the more my faith—and trust—increases.

Luke bases his whole Gospel on the premise that more knowledge gives more faith. He begins his book with this introduction: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the things that have been fulfilled [or been surely believed] among us, just as they were handed down to us by those who from the first were eyewitnesses and servants of the word. With this in mind, since I myself have carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I too decided to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught. –Luke 1:1-4. (NIV)

The apostle Paul argues that faith in God is so grounded in reality that no one has a legitimate claim against God’s existence. He writes, The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse –Romans 1:18-20. (NIV)

Knowledge of nature builds my faith in Jesus. Scripture teaches that God created all life in six days, that there was a global flood, and that animals produce after their own kind. All across our earth, the rocks cry out their testimony of the global flood. People have uncovered billions of fossils—mostly marine animals—in rock layers that were laid down by water. Animals too, live out what the Bible teaches about kinds. We can observe animals changing all around us. They change sizes, colors, and eating habits. Fish in caves lose their ability to see. Birds’ beaks adjust to the environment. In all this intricate change, all animals exist within the Biblical framework of their own kind. Sharks remain sharks; frogs remain frogs; iguanas remain iguanas; and gibbons remain gibbons. The more I learn and observe about nature, the more my faith (confidence) increases.

In some discussions of faith, it is natural for the words of Jesus to come up. After His resurrection, Jesus visits Thomas and tells him, …Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed –John 20:29. (ESV) From this, it is tempting to define faith as “believing without seeing.” That would be missing the point. I’m not claiming any superiority to Thomas, but he should have believed without seeing Jesus. All the evidence pointed to it. First, his good friends, who had proved themselves trustworthy, said Jesus was alive. Second, Jesus had plainly said He would be resurrected (see Matthew 16:21). Third, Jesus had already proven He was divine by His ability to raise the dead, control the weather, heal the sick, and multiply food. Thomas had all he needed to believe Jesus rose from the dead. Yet, he went against all reasoning and said he needed more evidence.

When confronted with the resurrected Christ, Thomas repented of his disbelief and followed Christ into martyrdom. Unfortunately, the spirit of disbelief in the face of evidence still lingers in our world. Atheists claim, in spite of all evidence to the contrary, that life can come from nothing. They claim, without any evidence, that fish turned into frogs. They blindly cling to various theories such as: The Big Bang, Punctuated Equilibrium, and Descent with Modification. They have NO workable evidence, yet they still claim to base all their thoughts on observable, repeatable reality. Christians, who with good intentions, tell them that faith begins where reason ends, unwittingly play right into their hands. This world does not need a social media definition of faith. They need to see faith for what it is: confidence in the living God based firmly in reason.

As jong man onthou ek dat ek ’n gewilde slagspreuk oor geloof gehoor het: “Geloof begin waar rede eindig.” As jong Christen het ek gedink dit is ’n wonderlike lewensleuse. Namate ek meer volwasse raak in my wandel met Jesus, kyk ek terug op hierdie spesifieke slagspreuk en skud my kop. Ek kan aan geen beter manier dink om geloof verkeerd voor te stel as om te beweer dat dit buite rede bestaan nie.

Een eenvoudige rede waarom ek hierdie beskouing verwerp, is dat dit geloof verkeerd voorstel. ’n Vinnige Google-soektog lewer hierdie definisie van geloof op: “volledige vertroue in iemand of iets.” Ons gebruik hierdie definisie die heeltyd. Ek kan vir jou sê dat ek vertroue in my vrou het, dat ek vertroue het dat my werkgewer my salaris sal betaal, of dat ek geen vertroue het dat alkohol my ’n lekker tyd sal besorg nie. Dit is dieselfde manier waarop die Bybel geloof definieer.

Hebreërs 11:1 bevestig dat geloof “vertroue is in wat ons hoop en sekerheid oor wat ons nie sien nie.” Bybelse geloof is bloot ’n gemoedstoestand van vertroue in die Here. Ek het vertroue dat ek eendag op die nuwe aarde sal wandel, en ek het vertroue dat die Heilige Gees in die harte van Christene werk. My vertroue is gegrond op, nie los van, rede nie. Hoe meer Jesus wys dat Hy vertrou kan word, hoe meer vertrou ek Hom (het ek vertroue in Hom).

Een aspek van Christus se betroubaarheid is sy woord. Die Ou Testament is geskryf deur profete en leiers wat toekomstige gebeure akkuraat voorspel en oor nasies regeer het. Die Nuwe Testament is geskryf deur apostels of mense wat nou met die apostels verbonde was. Ons het meer manuskripte van die Bybel as van enige ander werk uit die oudheid. Die Bybel gee ’n eerlike weergawe van sy helde en beskryf antieke leiers en plekke akkuraat. Kortom, ek vertrou op die Bybel omdat dit, wat outeurskap, bewaring, eerlikheid en akkuraatheid betref, uitsonderlik is bo alle ander boeke. Hoe meer ek dit lees en daaroor lees, hoe meer neem my geloof—en vertroue—toe.

Lukas grond sy hele Evangelie op die uitgangspunt dat meer kennis groter geloof meebring. Hy begin sy boek met hierdie inleiding: Baie het onderneem om ’n verslag op te stel van die dinge wat onder ons vervul is [of waarvan ons ten volle oortuig is], net soos dit aan ons oorgelewer is deur dié wat van die begin af ooggetuies en dienaars van die woord was. Daarom het ek ook, nadat ek alles van voor af noukeurig ondersoek het, besluit om ’n ordelike verslag vir u te skryf, hooggeagte Teofilus, sodat u sekerheid kan hê oor die dinge waarin u onderrig is. –Lukas 1:1-4. (NIV)

Die apostel Paulus voer aan dat geloof in God so stewig in die werklikheid gegrond is dat niemand ’n geldige rede het om God se bestaan te betwis nie. Hy skryf: God se toorn word uit die hemel geopenbaar oor al die goddeloosheid en ongeregtigheid van mense wat die waarheid deur hulle ongeregtigheid onderdruk, aangesien dit wat ’n mens van God kan weet, aan hulle bekend is, omdat God dit aan hulle bekend gemaak het. Want sedert die skepping van die wêreld is God se onsigbare eienskappe—sy ewige krag en goddelike natuur—duidelik waarneembaar, omdat dit verstaan word uit wat gemaak is, sodat mense geen verontskuldiging het nie –Romeine 1:18-20. (NIV)

Kennis van die natuur versterk my geloof in Jesus. Die Skrif leer dat God alle lewe in ses dae geskep het, dat daar ’n wêreldwye vloed was en dat diere volgens hulle eie soort voortplant. Oor die hele aarde getuig die rotse van die wêreldwye vloed. Mense het miljarde fossiele—meestal seediere—ontdek in rotslae wat deur water neergelê is. Diere leef ook uit wat die Bybel oor soorte leer. Ons kan oral om ons sien hoe diere verander. Hulle verander in grootte, kleur en eetgewoontes. Visse in grotte verloor hulle vermoë om te sien. Voëls se snawels pas by die omgewing aan. Te midde van al hierdie ingewikkelde veranderinge bly alle diere binne die Bybelse raamwerk van hulle eie soort. Haaie bly haaie; paddas bly paddas; iguanas bly iguanas; en gibbons bly gibbons. Hoe meer ek oor die natuur leer en dit waarneem, hoe meer neem my geloof (vertroue) toe.

Wanneer geloof bespreek word, kom Jesus se woorde natuurlik soms ter sprake. Ná sy opstanding besoek Jesus Tomas en sê vir hom: …Glo jy omdat jy My gesien het? Gelukkig is dié wat nie gesien het nie en tog geglo het –Johannes 20:29. (ESV) Hieruit is ’n mens geneig om geloof te definieer as “om te glo sonder om te sien”. Dit sou die punt mis. Ek maak nie daarop aanspraak dat ek beter as Tomas is nie, maar hy moes geglo het sonder om Jesus te sien. Al die bewyse het daarop gewys. Eerstens het sy goeie vriende, wat bewys het dat hulle vertrou kan word, gesê Jesus leef. Tweedens het Jesus duidelik gesê dat Hy opgewek sou word (sien Matteus 16:21). Derdens het Jesus reeds bewys dat Hy goddelik is deur sy vermoë om dooies op te wek, die weer te beheer, siekes te genees en kos te vermeerder. Tomas het alles gehad wat hy nodig gehad het om te glo dat Jesus uit die dood opgestaan het. Tog het hy alle redenasie geïgnoreer en gesê dat hy meer bewyse nodig het.

Toe Tomas met die opgestane Christus gekonfronteer is, het hy berou gehad oor sy ongeloof en Christus tot in die marteldood gevolg. Ongelukkig leef die gees van ongeloof ondanks bewyse steeds in ons wêreld voort. Ateïste beweer, ondanks al die bewyse van die teendeel, dat lewe uit niks kan ontstaan. Hulle beweer, sonder enige bewyse, dat visse in paddas verander het. Hulle klou blindelings vas aan verskeie teorieë soos die Oerknal, Punctuated Equilibrium en Afstamming met Verandering. Hulle het GEEN bruikbare bewyse nie, en tog beweer hulle steeds dat hulle al hulle denke op waarneembare, herhaalbare werklikheid grond. Christene wat met goeie bedoelings vir hulle sê dat geloof begin waar rede eindig, speel onbewustelik reg in hulle hande. Hierdie wêreld het nie ’n definisie van geloof van sosiale media nodig nie. Hulle moet geloof sien vir wat dit is: vertroue in die lewende God wat stewig in rede gegrond is.

Ramona* was a little girl who was very busy and active. Like other four-year-old’s, there were a lot of things Ramona could do. She could ride a bike, climb a tree, wash dishes, write her name, and ride her pony all by herself. One of Ramona’s favorite things to do was to ride horses. Her family had two horses and a pony. How fun those evenings were when they would hitch their pony, Tony, to the cart, and the whole family would take turns riding. Or when Ramona and three of her sisters would pack onto Tony’s back and go for a ride.

There were lots of things Ramona could do, but sometimes she thought she could do more than she really could. And sometimes she thought she was bigger than she really was.

One beautiful Summer evening, some guests came to Ramona’s house. When guests came, that usually meant a fun time.

On this particular evening, after supper, Ramona’s older siblings were riding horses with the guests. It looked like so much fun as they trotted around the pond and through the lawn. Ramona wanted to ride too, but she had to wait her turn. While she waited, she played on the lawn with Clifford, the dog. She soon tired of that and went for a spin on her bike. Then an idea popped into her mind. She ran off to the pasture entrance and climbed up the gate. She liked to pretend she was a monkey, swinging on the bars and climbing up and down. Then she tried balancing on a bar and taking her hands off the gate. Her siblings and their guests were riding nearby. Ramona threw her arms into the air, and while balancing on the gate, yelled to the riders, “Look at me! Look at me!” She felt very big to be balancing on the gate. Suddenly, her foot slipped and, down she went, into the dust. She blinked with surprise and quickly jumped up, brushing off her dress. She looked around, embarrassed, but no one seemed to notice. She climbed back up the side of the gate and began playing again. Ramona grew impatient, waiting for her ride. No one seemed to remember that she wanted to ride the horses. She thought it would be fun to see how high she could balance on the gate, so she climbed as high as she dared. She wanted others to see how brave she was, so waving her arms, she shouted, “Hey everyone! Look at me!” But again, her foot slipped off the gate. This time, however, she narrowly escaped falling to the ground. Ramona’s dad saw her and walked over to her. “Ramona,” he said, “I want you to stay off the gate.”

Ramona got down and tried to find something else to do. After playing for a while, her father’s command to stay off the gate seemed to slip from her mind, and she started climbing on the gate again. Then Ramona’s older sister, Elise, walked over, and quietly told her, “Ramona, you shouldn’t be showing off to our guests.” Ramona didn’t like that advice. Into one ear and out the other it went. She assured herself that she wasn’t showing off! She was just… well, just playing.

She climbed up just as high as she could, and once again, she waved her arms in the air, crying, “Look at me, everyone!” Suddenly, before she knew what was happening, she had landed on the ground with a thud and began to cry at the top of her lungs. Sure, she felt some pain, but mostly she was shocked and ashamed.

Ramona’s father came over to her and picked her up, making sure she wasn’t badly hurt, and carried her to the house. It was yet light outside, and still early in the evening, but he took her upstairs to her bed.

Before putting her to bed, he talked with her. Ramona was still crying, and Papa attempted to dry her tears. “Ramona, listen, can you be quiet for a bit? Why do you think you fell?” She sniffled and shrugged her shoulders. Papa continued, “If you would have obeyed me, and stayed off the gate like I told you to, you would not have fallen. Elise also told you to stop showing off, but you didn’t listen. Do you know that showing off is really pride? The Bible says, Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

Ramona nodded her head. “Are you sorry for disobeying me, Ramona?” Papa asked. “Yes, Papa, I am sorry” she replied tearfully. Papa decided to let her fall and going to bed early be her punishment this time. Ramona would have preferred a spanking instead of needing to go to bed early, which was a great grief to her little heart. But it was good for her because it caused her to repent.

Ramona never forgot this lesson, partly because of her fall, and partly because she was sent to bed early and missed the fun of riding horses. Not only had she been proud in showing off, she had also been willfully disobedient to Papa.

Elise had written a tune to the verse that Papa had mentioned to Ramona. From then on, whenever Ramona sang that song, she remembered how true that verse proved to be for her.

Ramona* alikuwa msichana mdogo mwenye shughuli nyingi na mchangamfu. Kama watoto wengine wa miaka minne, Ramona aliweza kufanya mambo mengi. Aliweza kuendesha baiskeli, kupanda mti, kuosha vyombo, kuandika jina lake, na kumpanda farasi wake mdogo peke yake. Mojawapo ya mambo aliyopenda sana Ramona kufanya ilikuwa kupanda farasi. Familia yao ilikuwa na farasi wawili na farasi mdogo mmoja. Jioni hizo zilikuwa za kufurahisha sana walipomfunga farasi wao mdogo, Tony, kwenye mkokoteni, kisha familia nzima ikapanda kwa zamu. Au Ramona na dada zake watatu walipopanda mgongoni mwa Tony na kwenda matembezini.

Ramona aliweza kufanya mambo mengi, lakini wakati mwingine alifikiri angeweza kufanya mengi zaidi ya yale aliyoweza kweli. Na wakati mwingine alifikiri alikuwa mkubwa zaidi kuliko alivyokuwa kweli.

Jioni moja nzuri ya kiangazi, wageni fulani walifika nyumbani kwa Ramona. Wageni walipokuja, kwa kawaida hiyo ilimaanisha wakati wa kufurahisha.

Jioni hiyo hasa, baada ya chakula cha jioni, ndugu na dada wakubwa wa Ramona walikuwa wakipanda farasi pamoja na wageni. Ilionekana kufurahisha sana walipokuwa wakizunguka bwawa kwa mwendo wa kunyata na kupita kwenye nyasi. Ramona alitaka kupanda pia, lakini ilimbidi asubiri zamu yake. Alipokuwa akisubiri, alicheza kwenye nyasi pamoja na Clifford, mbwa. Muda si muda alichoka na mchezo huo, akaenda kuzunguka kwa baiskeli yake. Kisha wazo likamjia ghafla. Alikimbilia kwenye lango la kuingilia malishoni na kupanda juu yake. Alipenda kujifanya tumbili, akining’inia kwenye vyuma vya lango na kupanda juu na chini. Kisha akajaribu kusimama kwenye chuma kimoja kwa mizani na kuondoa mikono yake langoni. Ndugu na dada zake pamoja na wageni wao walikuwa wakipanda farasi karibu na hapo. Ramona aliinua mikono juu, na huku akisawazisha mwili juu ya lango, akawapigia kelele wapandaji farasi, “Niangalieni! Niangalieni!” Alijihisi mkubwa sana kwa kusimama kwa mizani juu ya lango. Ghafla, mguu wake uliteleza, akaanguka chini kwenye vumbi. Alifumbua macho kwa mshangao na kuruka juu haraka, huku akipangusa vumbi kwenye gauni lake. Alitazama huku na huku kwa aibu, lakini ilionekana hakuna aliyegundua. Alipanda tena ubavuni mwa lango na kuanza kucheza. Ramona alizidi kukosa subira alipokuwa akisubiri zamu yake ya kupanda farasi. Ilionekana hakuna aliyekumbuka kwamba alitaka kupanda farasi. Alifikiri ingekuwa furaha kuona angeweza kusawazisha mwili juu kiasi gani kwenye lango, kwa hiyo alipanda juu kadiri alivyothubutu. Alitaka wengine waone jinsi alivyokuwa jasiri, kwa hiyo, huku akipunga mikono, akapaza sauti, “Jamani nyote! Niangalieni!” Lakini tena, mguu wake uliteleza kutoka kwenye lango. Hata hivyo, safari hii aliepuka kwa shida kuanguka chini. Baba yake Ramona alimwona na kumfuata. “Ramona,” alisema, “nataka usipande tena juu ya lango.”

Ramona alishuka na kujaribu kutafuta kitu kingine cha kufanya. Baada ya kucheza kwa muda, amri ya baba yake ya kutokupanda juu ya lango ilionekana kumponyoka akilini, akaanza tena kupanda lango. Kisha dada yake mkubwa, Elise, alimfuata na kumwambia kwa sauti ya chini, “Ramona, hupaswi kujionyesha mbele ya wageni wetu.” Ramona hakupenda ushauri huo. Uliingia sikio moja na kutoka lingine. Alijihakikishia kwamba hakuwa akijionyesha! Alikuwa tu… naam, alikuwa anacheza tu.

Alipanda juu kadiri alivyoweza, kisha tena akapunga mikono hewani, akipiga kelele, “Niangalieni, nyote!” Ghafla, kabla hajajua kilichokuwa kinatokea, alitua chini kwa kishindo na kuanza kulia kwa sauti kubwa. Bila shaka alihisi maumivu kiasi, lakini zaidi ya yote alishtuka na kuaibika.

Baba yake Ramona alimwendea na kumwinua, akihakikisha hakuwa ameumia vibaya, kisha akambeba hadi nyumbani. Kulikuwa bado na mwanga nje, na jioni ilikuwa bado changa, lakini alimpeleka ghorofani kitandani kwake.

Kabla ya kumlaza, alizungumza naye. Ramona alikuwa bado analia, na Baba alijaribu kumfuta machozi. “Ramona, sikiliza, unaweza kunyamaza kidogo? Unafikiri kwa nini ulianguka?” Alivuta kamasi na kuinua mabega. Baba akaendelea, “Kama ungenitii na kubaki mbali na lango kama nilivyokuambia, usingeanguka. Elise pia alikuambia uache kujionyesha, lakini hukumsikiliza. Je, unajua kwamba kujionyesha kwa kweli ni kiburi? Biblia inasema, Kiburi hutangulia uangamivu; na roho yenye majivuno hutangulia maanguko –Mithali 16:18.

Ramona aliitikia kwa kichwa. “Unajutia kuniasi, Ramona?” Baba akauliza. “Ndiyo, Baba, najutia,” akajibu huku akilia. Baba aliamua kwamba wakati huu adhabu yake iwe kuanguka na kulala mapema. Ramona angependelea kuchapwa viboko badala ya kulala mapema, jambo ambalo lilihuzunisha sana moyo wake mdogo. Lakini hilo lilikuwa jema kwake kwa sababu lilimfanya atubu.

Ramona hakusahau kamwe somo hilo, kwa sehemu kwa sababu ya kuanguka kwake, na kwa sehemu kwa sababu alipelekwa kulala mapema na akakosa furaha ya kupanda farasi. Hakuwa tu na kiburi kwa kujionyesha, bali pia alimwasi Baba kwa makusudi.

Elise alikuwa ametunga wimbo wa beti ambayo Baba alikuwa amemtajia Ramona. Tangu wakati huo, kila Ramona alipoimba wimbo huo, alikumbuka jinsi beti hiyo ilivyothibitika kuwa kweli kwake.

Many people ask, “Is listening to secular music a sin? Is there anything wrong with CCM (Christian Contemporary Music)? Is it okay for Christians to listen to rap, rock, country, pop, or rhythm and blues?” For the sake of this article, I am going to refer to all the music listed above as “secular” music.

Should Christians only listen to “A cappella” music? Music is compelling, and it can have a significant effect on how we live our lives. Music influences us negatively or positively. We should ask the question, “Does the music that I listen to draw me closer to God, or does it push me away from Him and closer to Satan?”

The primary purpose of music is to worship (the expression of reverence and adoration to something or someone). Yet at times we as believers still fail in listening to good wholesome music. This is a problem since most secular music is evil and promotes things that God hates.

Secular music is very catchy and addicting. The flesh would rather listen to secular music than to godly music. This type of music negatively influences the mind and is not profitable. If the song encourages evil, promotes worldliness, gives you bad thoughts, changes your actions for the wrong, and influences your speech for the wrong, we should not be listening to it. When it comes to music, we can comfortably lie to ourselves in this area. Have you lied to yourself? Have you said, “God is OK with this type of music,” yet deep down in your heart, you know He is convicting you, and that He is NOT OK with it?

Secular music is often sensual. The meaning of sensual is “of arousing gratification of the senses and physical.” Is the music that we listen to sensual? Does it put our mind in a state of just going with the beat? How do our bodies want to respond when we listen to such music? If our bodies swing with the rhythm of the music, it is not honoring to the Lord; it is not bringing glory to His name; it is not putting our mind and body in a position to worship the Lord.

We always worship something when we listen to music. If we are concentrating on music that is not of God, we are worshiping our flesh, the world, or even the devil. Usually, music like CCM tends to draw attention to ourselves and not to God. Music like this is very sensual. Can we truly worship God when we listen to this type of music?

CCM is a genre of modern popular music in which the lyrics are focused on matters concerned with the Christian faith. It formed as those affected by the 1960s’ “Jesus movement” revival began to express themselves with a more contemporary style of music. Before that, it was hymns and other gospel songs that were prevalent in the church at the time. Whether we know it or not, much of the CCM adds a pulsating beat (syncopation) at a place that it is not naturally supposed to be. The pulsating beat that is relevant in CCM does not appeal to the spirit of man in worship, rather, it appeals to the flesh. The type of music that appeals to the flesh is not of God but is of the devil. Today, CCM is a term that is used to refer to pop, rock, or praise & worship styles of rhythm and beat, so long as the lyrics fall under the definition of CCM.

Philippians tells us that we are supposed to think on … whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things –Philippians 4:8.

Secular music does not pass the Philippians 4:8 test. Most secular music has lyrics that are impure, while all of it has a rhythm or beat that is against God’s order. The devil uses it all to influence people to sin or to think about sin. It will affect you in some way. Is the influence of the music that we listen to good or bad? For example, if we are concentrating on music that affects our thoughts or lifestyle in the wrong way, then it is a negative influence that we must put out of our lives.

The Hebrews started the tradition of using music without accompaniment after the fall of the second temple in 70 A.D., at which time instruments were not allowed during a period of mourning after the fall. Throughout history up until The Renaissance, instrumental music was mostly associated with dancing and merry making. As one could not have too much fun in places of worship, this kind of amusing music was not popular with religious leaders.

A cappella is an Italian phrase which means “in the style of the chapel”. It was initially used to refer to music that was sung in a chapel or small worship space without accompanying instruments, as opposed to a large church where an organ usually attended vocal music. The term has since come to mean any music sung without accompaniment, whether sacred (religious) or secular (non-religious). A cappella music can be sung by a large choir, a small group, or as a solo.

In Orthodox and Conservative Jewish congregations, the tradition of singing mostly A cappella still exists. In these synagogues, it is customary for a cantor to chant or sing an authoritative text from the scriptures which the congregation responds to in kind. The only instruments used might be a pitch pipe to give everyone a starting note or a ram’s horn on a special occasion or a holiday.

The early church developed the tradition of A cappella singing from the Hebrews’ Jewish tradition, chanting psalms, or other scriptures and using a cantor as a leader. Gregorian chant was the dominant form of church music starting around 590 A.D. It is a single, simple, melodic line half-spoken, half-sung in a free rhythmic style. In the early church, instrumental music was associated with the sinful outside world and was considered a negative influence.

The tradition of unaccompanied sacred vocal music continued during The Renaissance. Although instruments sometimes doubled or substituted for a vocal line, vocal music mostly stood on its own. The sound of a choir of voices in a chapel with excellent acoustics had a particularly ethereal effect.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was one of the most significant composers of The Renaissance in Italy, writing hundreds of masses and motets for the church. ‘The Palestrina Style,’ as it is called, was a sophisticated A cappella form using many voices singing with different music and text coming in at different times. This was called polyphonic, as opposed to homophonic, which means one melodic line sung together or in the same rhythm.

The Apostle Paul writes, Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; –Ephesians 5:19. Does that sound like making music with instruments? Or does it rather seem like singing praises to God from the heart?

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them –Acts 16:25. When Paul and Silas were in prison, and they were in stocks singing at midnight, I don’t believe that they were singing to bring glory to themselves. They were singing to bring glory to God the Father. The result of them giving God the glory is quite astounding. There was an earthquake, the foundations of the prison shook, the doors flew open, and everyone’s prison bands broke. At the end of this happening, the jailor came trembling before Paul and Silas and asked: “What must I do to be saved?”

Colossians also tells us that we should Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Do we let psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs teach us, admonish us, and encourage us?

I wonder what hymn Jesus sang with His disciples at the last supper before He went out to the Mount of Olives. I doubt that they were singing to themselves. I believe they were singing to their heavenly Father.

Pure and holy music is a blessing from the Lord. It is such a beautifully powerful thing that we should not take for granted. Sometimes God uses it to speak to us. I firmly believe that all Christians need to be listening to godly music throughout the week, not just on Sunday. It helps me stay calm, be encouraged, and keep my mind on the Lord. When my mind is on the Lord, I can go through the day blest.

We need to discipline ourselves with the things of God. We also need to get rid of things in our life that we know God is not pleased with. Godly music (music that draws our spirit and mind to the things that are from God) is the type of music that believers should listen to. Worship is what it boils down to, do we worship God or something else?

Jesus says, But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him –John 4:23.

So, let us sing in sincere worship to our Creator, let us give God the glory for the voices that He has given us, and let us sing and listen to godly, wholesome songs to our God.

Många frågar: ”Är det synd att lyssna på sekulär musik? Är det något fel med CCM (kristen samtida musik)? Är det okej för kristna att lyssna på rap, rock, country, pop eller rhythm and blues?” För den här artikelns skull kommer jag att kalla all musik som räknats upp ovan för ”sekulär” musik.

Bör kristna bara lyssna på musik a cappella? Musik är fängslande, och den kan ha en betydande inverkan på hur vi lever våra liv. Musik påverkar oss negativt eller positivt. Vi bör ställa frågan: ”Drar musiken jag lyssnar på mig närmare Gud, eller driver den mig bort från honom och närmare Satan?”

Musikens främsta syfte är att tillbe (att uttrycka vördnad och tillbedjan för något eller någon). Ändå brister vi som troende ibland fortfarande i att lyssna på god och sund musik. Det är ett problem eftersom det mesta av den sekulära musiken är ond och främjar sådant som Gud hatar.

Sekulär musik är mycket medryckande och beroendeframkallande. Köttet lyssnar hellre på sekulär musik än på gudfruktig musik. Den här sortens musik påverkar sinnet negativt och är inte till någon nytta. Om en sång uppmuntrar till ondska, främjar världslighet, ger dig dåliga tankar, förändrar dina handlingar i fel riktning och påverkar ditt tal i fel riktning, bör vi inte lyssna på den. När det gäller musik kan vi lätt ljuga för oss själva på det här området. Har du ljugit för dig själv? Har du sagt: ”Gud har inget emot den här sortens musik”, fast du innerst inne vet att han överbevisar dig och att han INTE har något emot den?

Sekulär musik är ofta sinnlig. Sinnlig betyder ”något som väcker njutning genom sinnena och det fysiska”. Är musiken vi lyssnar på sinnlig? Får den vårt sinne att bara följa takten? Hur vill våra kroppar reagera när vi lyssnar på sådan musik? Om våra kroppar svänger med musikens rytm, är det inte till Herrens ära; det förhärligar inte hans namn; det försätter inte vårt sinne och vår kropp i en ställning där vi tillber Herren.

Vi tillber alltid något när vi lyssnar på musik. Om vi koncentrerar oss på musik som inte kommer från Gud, tillber vi vårt kött, världen eller till och med djävulen. Musik som CCM tenderar vanligtvis att dra uppmärksamheten till oss själva och inte till Gud. Sådan musik är mycket sinnlig. Kan vi verkligen tillbe Gud när vi lyssnar på den här sortens musik?

CCM är en genre inom modern populärmusik där texterna handlar om ämnen som rör den kristna tron. Den uppstod när personer som påverkades av väckelsen i ”Jesus-rörelsen” på 1960-talet började uttrycka sig med en mer samtida musikstil. Före det var det psalmer och andra gospelsånger som dominerade i kyrkan vid den tiden. Oavsett om vi vet om det eller inte lägger mycket av CCM till en pulserande takt (synkopering) på ett ställe där den inte naturligt hör hemma. Den pulserande takten som är vanlig i CCM tilltalar inte människans ande i tillbedjan, utan köttet. Den musik som tilltalar köttet kommer inte från Gud utan från djävulen. I dag används CCM som en beteckning för pop-, rock- eller lovsångs- och tillbedjansstilar med rytm och takt, så länge texterna faller inom definitionen av CCM.

Filipperbrevet säger att vi ska tänka på … allt som är sant, allt som är värdigt, allt som är rätt, allt som är rent, allt som är älskvärt, allt som är gott ansett, om det finns någon dygd och om det finns något som förtjänar beröm, tänk på detta –Filipperbrevet 4:8.

Sekulär musik klarar inte testet i Filipperbrevet 4:8. De flesta sekulära sånger har orena texter, medan all sådan musik har en rytm eller takt som strider mot Guds ordning. Djävulen använder allt detta för att påverka människor att synda eller tänka på synd. Det kommer att påverka dig på något sätt. Är påverkan från musiken vi lyssnar på god eller dålig? Om vi till exempel koncentrerar oss på musik som påverkar våra tankar eller vår livsstil i fel riktning, är det en negativ påverkan som vi måste avlägsna ur våra liv.

Hebréerna inledde traditionen att använda musik utan ackompanjemang efter det andra templets fall år 70 e.Kr., då instrument inte var tillåtna under en sorgperiod efter templets fall. Genom historien fram till renässansen förknippades instrumentalmusik mest med dans och festligheter. Eftersom man inte kunde roa sig alltför mycket på gudstjänstplatser var den här sortens underhållande musik inte populär bland religiösa ledare.

A cappella är ett italienskt uttryck som betyder ”i kapellstil”. Till en början användes det om musik som sjöngs i ett kapell eller ett litet gudstjänstrum utan instrumentackompanjemang, till skillnad från en stor kyrka där sången vanligtvis ackompanjerades av en orgel. Sedan dess har uttrycket kommit att beteckna all musik som sjungs utan ackompanjemang, oavsett om den är sakral (religiös) eller sekulär (icke-religiös). A cappella-musik kan framföras av en stor kör, en liten grupp eller som solo.

I ortodoxa och konservativa judiska församlingar finns traditionen att huvudsakligen sjunga a cappella fortfarande kvar. I dessa synagogor är det brukligt att en kantor reciterar eller sjunger en auktoritativ text ur skrifterna, och församlingen svarar på samma sätt. De enda instrument som används kan vara en stämtonspipa för att ge alla en startton eller ett vädurshorn vid ett särskilt tillfälle eller en högtid.

Den tidiga kyrkan utvecklade traditionen med a cappella-sång från hebréernas judiska tradition, med recitation av psalmer eller andra skrifter och en kantor som ledare. Den gregorianska sången var den dominerande formen av kyrkomusik från omkring år 590 e.Kr. Den består av en enda enkel melodisk linje, halvt talad och halvt sjungen i fri rytm. I den tidiga kyrkan förknippades instrumentalmusik med den syndiga världen utanför och ansågs vara ett negativt inflytande.

Traditionen med sakral vokalmusik utan ackompanjemang fortsatte under renässansen. Även om instrument ibland fördubblade eller ersatte en sångstämma stod vokalmusiken för det mesta på egna ben. Ljudet av en kör i ett kapell med utmärkt akustik hade en särskilt eterisk verkan.

Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina var en av renässansens mest betydelsefulla tonsättare i Italien och skrev hundratals mässor och motetter för kyrkan. ”Palestrinastilen”, som den kallas, var en sofistikerad a cappella-form där många röster sjöng olika musik och texter som kom in vid olika tidpunkter. Detta kallades polyfoni, till skillnad från homofoni, som innebär att en melodilinje sjungs tillsammans eller i samma rytm.

Aposteln Paulus skriver: Tala till varandra med psalmer, hymner och andliga sånger, sjung och spela i era hjärtan till Herren –Efesierbrevet 5:19. Låter det som att skapa musik med instrument? Eller verkar det snarare handla om att sjunga lovsånger till Gud ur hjärtat?

Vid midnatt bad Paulus och Silas och sjöng lovsånger till Gud, och fångarna hörde dem –Apostlagärningarna 16:25. När Paulus och Silas satt i fängelse, fastlåsta i stocken och sjöng vid midnatt, tror jag inte att de sjöng för att förhärliga sig själva. De sjöng för att förhärliga Gud Fadern. Resultatet av att de gav Gud äran är häpnadsväckande. Det blev en jordbävning, fängelsets grundvalar skakade, dörrarna flög upp och allas bojor lossnade. När detta hade hänt kom fångvaktaren darrande fram till Paulus och Silas och frågade: ”Vad måste jag göra för att bli frälst?”

Kolosserbrevet säger också att vi ska Låt Kristi ord bo rikligt hos er i all vishet; undervisa och förmana varandra med psalmer, hymner och andliga sånger, och sjung med tacksamhet i era hjärtan till Herren –Kolosserbrevet 3:16. Låter vi psalmer, hymner och andliga sånger undervisa, förmana och uppmuntra oss?

Jag undrar vilken hymn Jesus sjöng med sina lärjungar vid den sista måltiden innan han gick ut till Olivberget. Jag tvivlar på att de sjöng för sin egen skull. Jag tror att de sjöng till sin himmelske Fader.

Ren och helig musik är en välsignelse från Herren. Den är så vackert kraftfull att vi inte bör ta den för given. Ibland använder Gud den för att tala till oss. Jag är fast övertygad om att alla kristna behöver lyssna på gudfruktig musik under veckan, inte bara på söndagen. Den hjälper mig att hålla mig lugn, bli uppmuntrad och ha mitt sinne fäst vid Herren. När mitt sinne är fäst vid Herren kan jag gå välsignad genom dagen.

Vi behöver tukta oss själva med sådant som hör Gud till. Vi behöver också göra oss av med sådant i våra liv som vi vet att Gud inte tycker om. Gudfruktig musik (musik som drar vår ande och vårt sinne till sådant som kommer från Gud) är den sortens musik som troende bör lyssna på. I grund och botten handlar det om tillbedjan: tillber vi Gud eller något annat?

Jesus säger: Men den stund kommer, ja, den är redan här, då sanna tillbedjare ska tillbe Fadern i ande och sanning. Fadern söker sådana som tillber honom –Johannesevangeliet 4:23.

Låt oss därför sjunga i uppriktig tillbedjan till vår Skapare, ge Gud äran för de röster han har gett oss och sjunga och lyssna till gudfruktiga, sunda sånger till vår Gud.
