It is August 2020, over four months since the coronavirus pandemic started, and it is still affecting our lives. People are still getting sick. The government and its decisions continue to be at the center of a lot of our conversations. The cause and cure are ongoing topics. The difference between those that believe the coronavirus to be a real threat and those that believe it to be primarily an agenda of political nature are becoming more distinct as this virus slowly makes its way through our communities, churches, and society as a whole.

The mandates being issued by the governors of many of our states are forcing God’s people to make decisions on issues we have not faced before. At what point does the government cross the line of interfering in our religious freedoms by putting in place mandates that will affect how we do church? How should we relate to the differences among us concerning the mandates? Should we or should we not follow them? What should our attitude be towards those in authority when we feel that they are doing things that are politically motivated? What should we do with all the “unbelievable things” that are being passed around, even from well-meaning Christians from what they would consider to be very valid and from legitimate sources? What should we do with the many, what seem to be, “conspiracy theories” that are being propagated and peddled from one person to another in such a manner that makes it hard to refute them? I, in no way, am going to attempt to answer how a church should relate to the specific mandates but would like to address some concerning attitudes and other responses that have been observed throughout our plain communities.

One of the most concerning issues is the attitude that people have had and are having toward the government. In 1 Peter, the apostle Peter calls us to “honor the king” and the Apostle Paul admonishes us in Romans 13 to be “subject to the higher Powers, for there is no power but of God”. The word honour, as used in 1 Peter 2, in reference to the king, means to “prize” or to “fix valuation upon.” A verse like this and others would indicate that when we speak of our government and, for that matter, others, our attitude should be one of respect. The words and the tone of voice we use should reflect that commitment. Our choice of words and the tone we use will speak volumes. They reflect our attitude.

I personally believe that we as the plain community have done a lot of damage to our “light” and “witness” by refusing to wear the mask in required public settings. But God looks deeper than our actions and we should too. The remarks like “no one will tell me I have to wear that thing” and others similar to that have their roots in a “lack of respect.” God clearly tells us, though we may not be able to always obey in every situation, respect and honor is always to be seen and heard in our attitudes and speech.

The apostle Paul is a good example of one who had a heart to honor those in authority and repented when he failed to do so. When Ananias the high priest asked the ones by him to smite him, he called the high priest a “whited wall”. When told that he had reviled the high priest, he was very quick to apologize for his wrong even though the high priest was wrong in asking them to hit him. It might remind us of the little saying, “Two wrongs do not make a right.”

Having a bad attitude because the government is making what we think are wrong decisions will not bring about right! As we find our way through these mandates, let’s make sure we do not sin against those in authority by speaking about them in a disrespectful manner. Let us repent of any bad attitudes and make sure our heart is in a position to honor and then the words and tone we use will convey the same.

Another area that is extremely hard to know how to respond to is that of all the negative information that is floating around surrounding Covid–19. Many of the plain community tend to distrust the government’s way of handling the situation. Because of this we are quick to believe and pass on negative information as fact. How do we know what is true and what is not? We need to be so careful, even when the information comes from what we believe to be a reliable source, because the more this negative information is passed along, the more folks will distrust the government. Case in point, there have been numerous deaths that were not directly connected to Covid–19; however, it was reported that Covid–19 was marked on the death certificate as being the cause of these deaths. After fact checking some of these supposed cases, it was found that some of these reports were not true. Since several reports have been verified as untrue, I no longer know what to believe. I think we should all be very careful what we do with the information we come across and do all we can to verify the information before passing it on as fact. If it is hard to believe, it is all the more important to check the facts or not pass it on until it has been proven.

Throughout this time period it seems that the conspiracy theories have just escalated. A lot of speculation surrounds the origin of Covid–19, the possible underlying motives, and secrecies the government has in how they are handling the whole Covid–19 dilemma. How do we know if the many propagated theories are true? If they are true, how will that affect the way I live for the other kingdom now? Will it change the way I live? Will it somehow help me prepare for these supposed difficulties that are coming?

In Luke 21, we have a verse talking about future events: “Men’s hearts failing them for fear of things that are coming on the earth.” Are we going to respond to the future in faith or in fear? The media proclaims Covid–19 to be a very dangerous, infectious virus. This perception has caused many in our world to start buying and hoarding for fear of things coming on the face of the earth. We now have articles and theories being peddled by many that seemingly will cause fear of the government and what they are planning to do and ultimately men’s hearts will fail for fear.

The Apostle Peter said that …God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind –2 Timothy 1:7. Whether these claims are true or not, the Bible still calls us in Philippians to think on …whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report… –Philippians 4:8. To spend even a little time following these theories will have a negative and spiritually draining effect on our lives and the lives around us. Thinking about them not only promotes fear but also makes it even more difficult to respect and honor the government. In reality, some or many of these things may not even be true. As Christians we try to be a peaceful and trusting people, yet this tends to make us vulnerable to be quite gullible. We are quite willing to believe negative claims, allegations, and theories without checking the facts to see whether they could even be true or not. My appeal would be to continue to seek those things that are above, to think on the things that are noble and virtuous.

As believers, we are facing another challenge. The unity within our groups is being challenged in ways it has not been before. We differ in thought on how much the government should interfere in our services. Should we even be having church if the governor would rather that we would not? What about the wearing of masks in our services? Some feel one way and others think differently. These mandates and how we should respond to them can be quite controversial! Now, as much as ever before, we need to extend lots of grace as we sort these things through with each other. We must give some room to each other to understand and relate to it a bit differently. We need much grace with one another and dare not allow these things to become a point of contention. I believe God wants to use these difficulties to draw us closer to Him and each other, but the enemy of our souls is doing his best to have it destroy our love and commitment to each other. Let us seek peace and ensue it!

نحن في أغسطس 2020، وقد مضى أكثر من أربعة أشهر على بدء جائحة فيروس كورونا، وما زالت تؤثر في حياتنا. ولا يزال الناس يمرضون. وتواصل الحكومة وقراراتها احتلال مركز الصدارة في كثير من أحاديثنا. وما زال سبب الفيروس وعلاجه موضوعين مطروحين. كما أخذ يتضح أكثر فأكثر الفرق بين الذين يعتقدون أن فيروس كورونا تهديد حقيقي، والذين يعتقدون أنه في المقام الأول أجندة ذات طابع سياسي، فيما يشق هذا الفيروس طريقه ببطء عبر مجتمعاتنا وكنائسنا والمجتمع ككل.

إن الأوامر التي يصدرها حكام كثير من ولاياتنا تجبر شعب الله على اتخاذ قرارات بشأن أمور لم نواجهها من قبل. عند أي نقطة تتجاوز الحكومة الحد وتتدخل في حرياتنا الدينية، حين تضع أوامر تؤثر في كيفية إقامة الكنيسة؟ كيف ينبغي لنا أن نتعامل مع اختلافاتنا بشأن هذه الأوامر؟ هل ينبغي لنا اتباعها أم لا؟ وما موقفنا من أصحاب السلطة حين نشعر أنهم يفعلون أمورًا تحركها دوافع سياسية؟ ماذا نفعل بكل «الأمور التي لا تصدق» المتداولة، حتى على ألسنة مسيحيين حسني النية، ممن يرون أنها تستند إلى مصادر مشروعة وموثوقة جدًا؟ وماذا نفعل بنظريات «المؤامرة» الكثيرة، كما تبدو، التي يجري الترويج لها وتداولها من شخص إلى آخر على نحو يصعّب دحضها؟ لا أعتزم بأي حال أن أحاول الإجابة عن كيفية تعامل الكنيسة مع الأوامر المحددة، لكنني أود تناول بعض المواقف المثيرة للقلق وردود الفعل الأخرى التي لوحظت في مجتمعاتنا الأميشية.

من أكثر الأمور المثيرة للقلق الموقف الذي اتخذه الناس ويتخذونه تجاه الحكومة. ففي رسالة بطرس الأولى يدعونا الرسول بطرس إلى «إكرام الملك»، وفي رومية 13 يحثنا الرسول بولس على أن «تخضعوا للسلاطين الفائقة، لأنه ليس سلطان إلا من الله». وكلمة «أكرموا» الواردة في بطرس الأولى 2، في الإشارة إلى الملك، تعني «قدّروا» أو «أولوا قيمة». وتشير آية كهذه وغيرها إلى أن موقفنا ينبغي أن يتسم بالاحترام حين نتحدث عن حكومتنا، وعن الآخرين كذلك. وينبغي أن تعكس كلماتنا ونبرة صوتنا هذا الالتزام. فاختيارنا للكلمات ونبرة صوتنا يعبّران الكثير؛ إذ إنهما يعكسان موقفنا.

أعتقد شخصيًا أننا، نحن أبناء المجتمع الأميشي، قد ألحقنا ضررًا كبيرًا بـ«نورنا» و«شهادتنا» برفضنا ارتداء الكمامة في الأماكن العامة التي يُلزم فيها بارتدائها. لكن الله ينظر إلى ما هو أعمق من أفعالنا، وينبغي لنا نحن أيضًا أن نفعل ذلك. إن تعليقات مثل «لن يملي عليّ أحد أن أرتدي ذلك الشيء» وما شابهها، مصدرها «قلة الاحترام». ويخبرنا الله بوضوح أنه، حتى وإن لم نتمكن من الطاعة في كل موقف، ينبغي أن يظهر الاحترام والإكرام دائمًا في مواقفنا وكلامنا.

إن الرسول بولس مثال جيد لشخص امتلك قلبًا يكرم أصحاب السلطة، وتاب حين أخفق في ذلك. فعندما أمر حنانيا رئيس الكهنة الواقفين بجانبه أن يلطموه، وصف بولس رئيس الكهنة بأنه «حائط مبيّض». وحين أُخبر بأنه أهان رئيس الكهنة، سارع إلى الاعتذار عن خطئه، مع أن رئيس الكهنة أخطأ حين أمرهم بضربه. وقد يذكّرنا ذلك بالمقولة الصغيرة: «الخطآن لا يصنعان صوابًا».

إن اتخاذ موقف سيئ لأن الحكومة تتخذ قرارات نعتقد أنها خاطئة لن يجعل الأمور صائبة! وبينما نشق طريقنا عبر هذه الأوامر، لنتأكد من أننا لا نخطئ إلى أصحاب السلطة بالتحدث عنهم بطريقة تنم عن عدم الاحترام. لنتب عن أي مواقف سيئة، ولنتأكد من أن قلوبنا مهيأة للإكرام، وعندئذ ستعبّر كلماتنا ونبرتها عن ذلك أيضًا.

وثمة مجال آخر يصعب للغاية معرفة كيفية التعامل معه، وهو المعلومات السلبية المتداولة عن كوفيد-19. فكثيرون من أبناء المجتمع الأميشي يميلون إلى عدم الثقة بطريقة تعامل الحكومة مع الوضع. ولهذا نسارع إلى تصديق المعلومات السلبية وتناقلها على أنها حقائق. كيف نعرف ما هو صحيح وما هو غير صحيح؟ علينا أن نكون حذرين جدًا، حتى عندما تأتي المعلومات من مصدر نعتقد أنه موثوق، لأن ازدياد تداول هذه المعلومات السلبية سيزيد من عدم ثقة الناس بالحكومة. ومن الأمثلة على ذلك أن وفيات عديدة لم تكن مرتبطة مباشرة بكوفيد-19، ومع ذلك أفادت تقارير بأن كوفيد-19 سُجل سببًا لهذه الوفيات في شهادات الوفاة. وبعد التحقق من بعض هذه الحالات المزعومة، تبيّن أن بعض تلك التقارير غير صحيح. وبما أن عدة تقارير ثبت عدم صحتها، لم أعد أعرف ما الذي أصدقه. أعتقد أنه ينبغي لنا جميعًا أن نتحرى الحذر الشديد فيما نفعل بالمعلومات التي نصادفها، وأن نبذل كل ما في وسعنا للتحقق منها قبل تناقلها على أنها حقيقة. وإذا صعب تصديقها، فذلك يجعل التحقق من الوقائع أكثر أهمية، أو يقتضي عدم تناقلها إلى أن يثبت صحتها.

ويبدو أن نظريات المؤامرة تصاعدت خلال هذه الفترة. فهناك كثير من التكهنات بشأن منشأ كوفيد-19، والدوافع المحتملة الكامنة وراءه، وما تخفيه الحكومة في طريقة تعاملها مع معضلة كوفيد-19 برمتها. كيف نعرف إن كانت النظريات الكثيرة المتداولة صحيحة؟ وإذا كانت صحيحة، فكيف سيؤثر ذلك في الطريقة التي أعيش بها الآن من أجل الملكوت الآخر؟ هل سيغير طريقة عيشي؟ وهل سيساعدني بطريقة ما على الاستعداد لهذه الصعوبات المزعومة القادمة؟

لدينا في لوقا 21 آية تتحدث عن أحداث مستقبلية: «تخور قلوب الناس من خوف وانتظار ما يأتي على المسكونة». فهل سنواجه المستقبل بالإيمان أم بالخوف؟ تصف وسائل الإعلام كوفيد-19 بأنه فيروس شديد الخطورة ومعدٍ. وقد دفع هذا التصور كثيرين في عالمنا إلى البدء بشراء المؤن وتكديسها خوفًا مما يأتي على وجه الأرض. وأصبح لدينا الآن مقالات ونظريات يتداولها كثيرون، ويبدو أنها ستثير الخوف من الحكومة وما تخطط له، وفي نهاية المطاف تخور قلوب الناس من الخوف.

قال الرسول بطرس: …لأن الله لم يعطنا روح الفشل، بل روح القوة والمحبة والنصح. –2 تيموثاوس 1:7. سواء أكانت هذه الادعاءات صحيحة أم لا، فما زال الكتاب المقدس يدعونا في فيلبي إلى التفكير في …كل ما هو حق، وكل ما هو جليل، وكل ما هو عادل، وكل ما هو طاهر، وكل ما هو مسر، وكل ما صيته حسن… –فيلبي 4:8. إن قضاء ولو قليل من الوقت في تتبع هذه النظريات سيكون له أثر سلبي يستنزف روحيًا حياتنا وحياة من حولنا. فالتفكير فيها لا يشجع الخوف فحسب، بل يجعل أيضًا احترام الحكومة وإكرامها أصعب. والواقع أن بعض هذه الأمور، أو كثيرًا منها، قد لا يكون صحيحًا أصلًا. ونحن كمسيحيين نسعى إلى أن نكون شعبًا مسالمًا يثق بالله، إلا أن هذا يجعلنا عرضة لأن نكون سذّجًا إلى حد بعيد. فنحن مستعدون تمامًا لتصديق الادعاءات والاتهامات والنظريات السلبية من دون التحقق من الوقائع لمعرفة ما إذا كان يمكن أن تكون صحيحة أصلًا. وأود أن أحثكم على مواصلة طلب ما هو فوق، والتفكير في الأمور النبيلة والفاضلة.

ونحن المؤمنين نواجه تحديًا آخر. فالوحدة داخل جماعاتنا تتعرض لاختبار بطرق لم نعرفها من قبل. ونحن مختلفون في آرائنا بشأن مقدار تدخل الحكومة في اجتماعاتنا. فهل ينبغي أن نعقد اجتماعات الكنيسة أصلًا إذا كان الحاكم يفضل ألا نفعل ذلك؟ وماذا عن ارتداء الكمامات في اجتماعاتنا؟ فبعضنا له رأي، وآخرون يرون الأمر على نحو مختلف. وقد تكون هذه الأوامر وكيفية استجابتنا لها موضع خلاف شديد! والآن، أكثر من أي وقت مضى، علينا أن نبدي الكثير من النعمة بعضنا لبعض ونحن نتباحث في هذه الأمور. وينبغي أن نمنح بعضنا بعضًا فسحة لفهمها والتعامل معها بطرق مختلفة بعض الشيء. نحن بحاجة إلى الكثير من النعمة المتبادلة، ولا ينبغي لنا أن نسمح لهذه الأمور بأن تصبح موضع نزاع. أؤمن أن الله يريد أن يستخدم هذه الصعوبات ليقربنا إليه وإلى بعضنا بعضًا، لكن عدو نفوسنا يبذل قصارى جهده ليجعلها تدمر محبتنا والتزامنا بعضنا تجاه بعض. فلنسعَ إلى السلام ونتبعه!

Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it –Matthew 7:13-14.

Of all the word pictures painted by our Lord, it seems this one remains, for the most part, unexplored. On numerous occasions the disciples asked their Master to explain the parables he taught. The parable of the Wheat and Tares resulted in a detailed explanation that leaves little doubt to His intent. …He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man; The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels –Matthew 13:37-39. But in the picture presented as the strait gate, we receive few defining details and are even told that there be but few that will even find it.

The parable is followed by some intense teaching against false prophets, corrupt fruit, and empty words. Some souls will have a pretense of powerful prophecy while missing the gate. Others put forth a front of fruitful freedom but are foreigners to the strait gate. All professing words of goodness, grace, and godliness avail us nothing to the entrance into this gate. Those tramping through the broad gate are obviously more than just the world’s gross, hardened sinners. Rather, the two gates seem to be representative of those who have entered a religious pursuit of life.

Straight and Narrow, as ascribed by the early American revival movement, generally meant “a life of abstinence” from the vices of sin. This is certainly not an entirely wrong perception, yet it seems to differ from the profession of the broad group that had prophesied in thy name? And in thy name have cast out devils? And in thy name done many wonderful works? –Matthew 7:22. To free ourselves from the dregs of evil is quite indispensable to any good living, but he that would enter the strait gate will be he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. –Matthew 7:21. Also, to place asceticism, the doctrine that a person can attain a high spiritual and moral state by practicing self-denial, self-mortification, and the like. –dictionary.com, at the portal of the post seems to invite a works-based, monastic kingdom. Self-denial sings in perfect harmony with the Christian life but will never be found as the sole melody. The ordinances of this world, such as …Touch not; taste not; handle not [are] … after the commandments and doctrines of men. –Colossians 2:20-22. While we applaud the efforts of anyone who has denied himself of this world’s ease and enjoyment for the betterment of others, we cannot offer it as the prescription of the strait gate to the abundant life.

Some will attest that the gate is “Jesus” and all who will enter the kingdom must enter through Him. This certainly carries some merit, as well. In another parable, Christ described Himself as the door of the sheep –John 10:7. Who would care to deny Christ of such a preeminent position? Yet, we have noticed that the “Jesus only” movement has opened the gate so broadly that it can hardly be considered “strait”.

Regardless of our interpretation of what the gate may represent, the decided emphasis given here is upon the adjectives, straight and narrow, as opposed to wide and broad. Strait (Sten-os’) means narrow (from obstacles standing close about) –Strongs. Narrow (Thlee’-bo) means to crowd (literally or figuratively): afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble –Strongs. Here we find some solid definition to our entrance. We must endure an uncomfortable squeeze between two posts if we are to find life. Here we can behold the testimonies of those who have entered there.

  • …we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; (Thlee’-bo) –1 Thessalonians 3:4.
  • …they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted (Thlee’-bo), tormented –Hebrews 11:37.
  • We are troubled (Thlee’-bo) on every side, yet not distressed… –2 Corinthians 4:8.

Herein is an entrance beyond the discipline being taught by the scribes. …when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes –Matthew 7:28-29. The strait gate of Christ rested in a principle beyond word-worn profession. But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished! –Luke 12:50. This is where Christ got His authority: tenaciously doing the will of His Father in heaven by submitting Himself into the hands of men.

One Thing Needful

…The scribes came upon him with the elders, And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority? And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not? But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet. And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was. And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things –Luke 20:1-8.

If the scribes, priests, and elders could have answered this one question they could have understood the power source of His authority. There is an authority of heaven and an authority of men. These two make up the posts of a very strait gate. At times they may even conflict, leaving the conscientious Christian feeling stuck between a rock and a hard place. When earthly authorities overstep their bounds leaving no room to serve God in a Biblical manner, we must choose …to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29. It is here that we will experience the thlee’-bo of the gate.

There is a God-given authority vested in men by their position: government authorities, workplace authorities, parental authorities, and church authorities, to name a few. Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation –Romans 13:1-2. This is strong language that we dare not ignore. Yet the disciples answered such authorities …and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard –Acts 4:19-20. While the disciples carried no personal angst against the rulers, there was a narrow way that they were walking in. Narrow, not because they served God alone, but because they had duel posts to submit to. Patriotism wants to serve man to the exclusion of God. Modern Christianity wants to serve God to the exclusion of man. Both paths are broad, for in either case, we move the opposite post to a position that is less hurtful to our humanity and more pleasing to our palate.

Submission Activates Power.

The authority ushered in by Christ Jesus left His followers astonished and amazed—But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men –Matthew 9:8. Their experience with authority was a mere social, hierarchical subordination that left them oppressed, pushed down, and forced into subservience. Christ exemplified a new and narrow way. It was not a casting away of civil authority but an empowerment of it. It was a strait gate that respected the authorities enough to volunteer to transport a soldier’s pack the second mile. Today, it is an inner authority that empowers us to respond respectfully and to glorify God while doing it. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13:5. To embrace our authorities in our heart is ultimately the inner channel to freedom and a deterrent to legalism, for it takes to task the issue of sin, sulking, and selfishness, while replacing it with righteousness, well-being, and peace. While many disdain these earthly authorities and remove them as far as possible from their hearts’ compliance, they only succeed to broaden the posts and thus forfeit the life that the strait gate brings. There are a mere few who will find the blessedness within the posts.

These will find life within the confinements of the strait and narrow provided by God and…

…Governments

The humble request of the centurion of Capernaum made Jesus marvel—…Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. He was a man with authority… and under authority. He seemed to understand the correlation in subjection to earthly authority and the exercising of it, for he entreated Christ not to come under his roof but to …speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed –Matthew 8:8. The gate formed by his overseers and the sincere love of his servants under him often left but little room for personal preferences. Yet, the power entwined in his speech was such that the Son of God readily complied with his request!

Joseph repeatedly found himself in tight places between God and the people he served. This resulted in being raised to the second ruling power in the most prominent nation on the earth. Esther and Daniel experienced similar plights. At times, the posts were so narrow that they wondered if they might perish, but the end result was always power… power to live in holiness, power to respond in righteousness, power to overcome victoriously, and power to endure faithfully unto the end.

…Masters

While slavery has been predominantly eradicated in our modern world, the relationship to a master still exists. Employers exercise authority over their servants and greater responsibility is ultimately given to those who submit wholeheartedly to it. The authority given to Eleazer is amazing and inspiring. Abraham trusted him to secure a wife for Isaac; He was even permitted to determine the rules. This colossal commitment left the indentured servant in a tight squeeze between the Master God and his master Abraham. And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham s–Genesis 24:12.

The American workforce has grown very accustomed to refusing anything they esteem as an unreasonable mandate from their employers. In faithless defiance they readily strike and kick the posts further apart to their broad preferences. This attitude has left them spiritually anemic and powerless. The Ethiopian eunuch served God while also serving under Queen Candace. Though his world was narrowed beyond what most of us could ever imagine, …he went on his way rejoicing –Acts 8:39, His life stands as a stellar testimony to Isaiah’s prophecy …neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree –Isaiah 56:3.

…Parents

Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth –Ephesians 6:1-3. This one should be obvious to any spiritually awakened individual. Children, who have parents, have an evident advantage in life and those who respect them, fare even better. Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live? –Hebrews 12:9. Life is found by those who can embrace their earthly fathers and the “Father of spirits”. Those who claim God as their Father while viewing their parents as a mere obstruction to the path they wish to walk in, will sooner or later be walking through the broad gate to destruction.

…Husbands

As Jesus entered into dialogue with the Samaritan woman at Jacob’s well, he began to describe a life that she desperately wanted—… Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come hither to draw. Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither –John 4:16. Christ was seeking to convince her that the abundant life will be found between the two posts. She had previously had five husbands and undoubtedly had not found contentment with any of them. Women who stand up for their rights kick at the narrowness of the gate and forfeit their God-ordained dignity. A woman at rest within the confines of her authorities is not oppressed but is actually liberated and empowered. For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head… –1 Corinthians 11:10. The headship veiling is not just a symbol of submission, nor is it merely a form of protection, it is spiritual power. Her wholehearted subjection fuels a dynamic marriage as she embraces her husband as “lord”, and in doing so, she becomes a faithful vessel of liberty, power, strength, and delegated influence.

…Church Leaders

These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee –Titus 2:15. Many self-proclaimed believers reject any outward display of authority in the Church. To the western mind, church authority is negatively associated with legalism, communism, bondage, and heaviness. But just as a disregard for spiritual authorities stripped Saul of his kingship, so likewise this attitude robs the believer of true authoritative power and nobility. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry… –1 Samuel 15:23. Efforts to choose …a way which seemeth right unto a man… –Proverbs 14:12, leads to bondage, but choosing to walk in surrender and subjection leads to liberation and life. Satan promised Jesus the entire world if He would only throw off the “yoke” of obedience to God. Instead, He set His face like a flint, endured the constraint of subordination, and ultimately liberated the entire world.

Subjection Produces Spiritual Authority

God’s authority and earthly authorities are rooted within the opposing posts of the strait gate. Those fully subject unto them both experience a living authority found within the gate. It brings power unto people rather than power over people. It produces liberty in Christ… the right to the tree of life… freedom from fear… health to our bones… power over unclean spirits… grace to train children… strength to preach and convert souls… and it is the ultimate deterrent to legalism. Faith that comes through wholehearted and humble subjection is the most suspect and under-estimated power available to mankind. Few there be that find it. Why? Because it is fastidiously founded and formulated between the posts of the strait gate and the narrow way.

Ingieni kwa kupitia lango jembamba; kwa maana lango ni pana, na njia ni kubwa iendayo upotevuni, nao ni wengi waingiao kwa hiyo; kwa sababu lango ni jembamba, na njia imesonga iendayo uzimani, nao waipatao ni wachache –Mathayo 7:13-14.

Katika picha zote za maneno zilizochorwa na Bwana wetu, inaonekana kuwa hii, kwa sehemu kubwa, bado haijachunguzwa. Mara nyingi wanafunzi walimwomba Mwalimu wao awaeleze mifano aliyofundisha. Mfano wa Ngano na Magugu ulipata maelezo ya kina yasiyoacha shaka kuhusu nia yake. …Apandaye mbegu njema ni Mwana wa Adamu; shamba ni ulimwengu; mbegu njema ni wana wa ufalme; magugu ni wana wa yule mwovu; adui aliyepanda hayo ni Ibilisi; mavuno ni mwisho wa dunia; na wavunaji ni malaika –Mathayo 13:37-39. Lakini katika picha inayowasilishwa kama lango jembamba, tunapokea maelezo machache ya ufafanuzi, na hata tunaambiwa kwamba ni wachache tu watakaolipata.

Mfano huo unafuatwa na mafundisho makali dhidi ya manabii wa uongo, matunda yaliyoharibika, na maneno matupu. Baadhi ya watu watakuwa na mwonekano wa unabii wenye nguvu huku wakilikosa lango. Wengine hujifanya kuwa na uhuru wenye kuzaa matunda, lakini ni wageni kwa lango jembamba. Kukiri maneno ya wema, neema, na utauwa hakutatusaidia hata kidogo kuingia langoni hapa. Wanaopita katika lango pana ni zaidi tu ya wenye dhambi wakubwa na wagumu wa dunia hii. Badala yake, milango hii miwili yaonekana kuwakilisha wale walioingia katika jitihada za kidini maishani.

Njia Iliyo Nyooka na Nyembamba, kama ilivyohusishwa na vuguvugu la uamsho la awali la Marekani, kwa ujumla ilimaanisha “maisha ya kujiepusha” na maovu ya dhambi. Hakika hii si mtazamo usio sahihi kabisa, lakini yaonekana kutofautiana na kauli ya kundi pana lililokuwa limetabiri kwa jina lako? Na kwa jina lako kutoa pepo? Na kwa jina lako kufanya miujiza mingi? –Mathayo 7:22. Kujiondoa katika mabaki ya uovu ni jambo lisiloweza kukosekana katika maisha mema, lakini yeye atakayeingia katika lango jembamba atakuwa yeye atendaye mapenzi ya Baba yangu aliye mbinguni. –Mathayo 7:21. Pia, kuweka kujinyima, fundisho kwamba mtu anaweza kufikia hali ya juu ya kiroho na maadili kwa kujizoeza kujikana nafsi, kujitesa, na mambo kama hayo. –dictionary.com, kwenye lango la kuingilia kunaonekana kualika ufalme wa utawa unaotegemea matendo. Kujikana nafsi huimba kwa upatanifu kamili na maisha ya Kikristo, lakini kamwe hakutakuwa wimbo pekee. Amri za ulimwengu huu, kama vile …Usiguse; usionje; usishike [ni] … kwa kufuata maagizo na mafundisho ya wanadamu. –Wakolosai 2:20-22. Ingawa tunapongeza juhudi za yeyote aliyejinyima raha na anasa za ulimwengu huu kwa ajili ya kuwafaidi wengine, hatuwezi kuitoa kama agizo la lango jembamba linaloelekea kwenye uzima tele.

Wengine watathibitisha kwamba lango ni “Yesu” na kwamba wote watakaoingia ufalme lazima waingie kupitia kwake. Bila shaka, jambo hili lina msingi fulani pia. Katika mfano mwingine, Kristo alijieleza kuwa mlango wa kondoo –Yohana 10:7. Nani angependa kumnyima Kristo nafasi hiyo ya ukuu? Hata hivyo, tumeona kwamba vuguvugu la “Yesu pekee” limefungua lango kwa upana kiasi kwamba haliwezi tena kuitwa “jembamba”.

Bila kujali tafsiri yetu ya kile ambacho lango linaweza kuwakilisha, mkazo uliowekwa hapa bila shaka ni juu ya vivumishi, nyoofu na nyembamba, kinyume na pana na kubwa. Jembamba (Sten-os’) humaanisha finyu (kwa sababu ya vizuizi vilivyo karibu) –Strongs. Imesonga (Thlee’-bo) humaanisha kubana (kihalisi au kitamathali): kutesa, kufanya nyembamba, kusonga, kuteseka dhiki, taabu –Strongs. Hapa tunapata ufafanuzi thabiti kuhusu kuingia kwetu. Ni lazima tuvumilie kubanwa kusikofurahisha kati ya nguzo mbili ili tupate uzima. Hapa tunaweza kutazama ushuhuda wa wale walioingia humo.

  • …tuliwaambia hapo awali kwamba tutapata dhiki; (Thlee’-bo) –1 Wathesalonike 3:4.
  • …walizunguka huku wakiwa wamevaa ngozi za kondoo na mbuzi; wakiwa wahitaji, wenye dhiki (Thlee’-bo), wakiteswa –Waebrania 11:37.
  • Tunasongwa (Thlee’-bo) pande zote, lakini hatushindwi… –2 Wakorintho 4:8.

Hapa kuna kuingia kunakozidi nidhamu inayofundishwa na waandishi. …Yesu alipomaliza maneno hayo, makutano walishangaa kwa mafundisho yake; kwa maana alikuwa akiwafundisha kama mtu mwenye mamlaka, wala si kama waandishi –Mathayo 7:28-29. Lango jembamba la Kristo liliegemea katika kanuni iliyozidi ungamo lililozoeleka kwa maneno. Lakini nina ubatizo unipasao kubatizwa nao; nami ninataabika kama nini hata utimizwe! –Luka 12:50. Hapa ndipo Kristo alipopata mamlaka yake: kwa kufanya kwa uthabiti mapenzi ya Baba yake aliye mbinguni, kwa kujikabidhi mikononi mwa watu.

Jambo Moja Linalohitajika

…Waandishi walimjia pamoja na wazee, wakamwambia, Tuambie, unafanya mambo haya kwa mamlaka gani? Au ni nani aliyekupa mamlaka hii? Akajibu akawaambia, Nami nitawauliza neno moja; nanyi niambieni: Ubatizo wa Yohana ulitoka mbinguni, au kwa wanadamu? Wakajadiliana wao kwa wao, wakisema, Tukisema, Ulitoka mbinguni; atasema, Kwa nini basi hamkumwamini? Lakini tukisema, Kwa wanadamu; watu wote watatupiga kwa mawe; kwa maana wameshawishika kwamba Yohana alikuwa nabii. Wakajibu kwamba hawakujua ulipotoka. Yesu akawaambia, Wala mimi siwaambii ni kwa mamlaka gani ninayafanya haya –Luka 20:1-8.

Kama waandishi, makuhani, na wazee wangeweza kujibu swali hili moja, wangeweza kuelewa chanzo cha nguvu ya mamlaka yake. Kuna mamlaka ya mbinguni na mamlaka ya wanadamu. Mamlaka hizi mbili ndizo nguzo za lango jembamba sana. Nyakati nyingine zinaweza hata kupingana, na kumfanya Mkristo mwenye dhamiri ajihisi amekwama kati ya mwamba na mahali pagumu. Mamlaka za duniani zinapovuka mipaka yake na kutuacha bila nafasi ya kumtumikia Mungu kwa namna ya kibiblia, ni lazima tuchague …kumtii Mungu kuliko wanadamu –Matendo 5:29. Hapo ndipo tutakapopitia thlee’-bo ya lango.

Kuna mamlaka iliyotolewa na Mungu kwa watu kutokana na nafasi zao: mamlaka za serikali, za mahali pa kazi, za wazazi, na za kanisa, kwa kutaja baadhi tu. Kila mtu na aitii mamlaka iliyo kuu. Kwa maana hakuna mamlaka isipokuwa kwa Mungu; na zile zilizopo zimewekwa na Mungu. Basi yeye apingaye mamlaka hushindana na agizo la Mungu; nao washindanao watapata hukumu juu yao wenyewe –Warumi 13:1-2. Haya ni maneno yenye nguvu tusiyothubutu kuyapuuza. Hata hivyo, wanafunzi waliwajibu wenye mamlaka hao …wakawaambia, Kama ni haki mbele za Mungu kuwasikiliza ninyi kuliko Mungu, hukumuni ninyi wenyewe; maana sisi hatuwezi kuacha kuyanena mambo tuliyoyaona na kuyasikia –Matendo 4:19-20. Ingawa wanafunzi hawakuwa na chuki binafsi dhidi ya watawala, walikuwa wakitembea katika njia nyembamba. Nyembamba, si kwa sababu walimtumikia Mungu pekee, bali kwa sababu walipaswa kujitiisha chini ya nguzo zote mbili. Uzalendo hutaka kumtumikia mwanadamu na kumwacha Mungu. Ukristo wa kisasa hutaka kumtumikia Mungu na kumwacha mwanadamu. Njia zote mbili ni pana, kwa maana katika kila hali tunaisogeza nguzo iliyo kinyume ili iwe karibu na ubinadamu wetu na ipendeze zaidi kaakaa letu.

Kujitiisha Huamilisha Nguvu.

Mamlaka yaliyoletwa na Kristo Yesu yaliwaacha wafuasi wake wakishangaa na kustaajabu—Makutano walipoona hayo, walishangaa, wakamtukuza Mungu aliyewapa wanadamu mamlaka ya namna hii –Mathayo 9:8. Uzoefu wao kuhusu mamlaka ulikuwa tu utiifu wa kijamii na wa ngazi za vyeo uliowaacha wameonewa, wamesukumwa chini, na kulazimishwa kutumikishwa. Kristo alionyesha njia mpya na nyembamba. Haikuwa kutupa kando mamlaka ya kiraia, bali ilikuwa kuyawezesha. Lilikuwa lango jembamba lililoheshimu mamlaka kiasi cha kujitolea kubeba mzigo wa askari maili ya pili. Leo, ni mamlaka ya ndani inayotuwezesha kuitikia kwa heshima na kumtukuza Mungu tunapofanya hivyo. Kwa sababu hiyo hamna budi kunyenyekea, si kwa sababu ya ghadhabu tu, bali na kwa sababu ya dhamiri –Warumi 13:5. Kuzikumbatia mamlaka zetu mioyoni mwetu hatimaye ndiyo njia ya ndani ya uhuru na kizuizi dhidi ya ushupavu wa sheria, kwa maana hushughulikia dhambi, kununa, na ubinafsi, na badala yake huleta haki, ustawi, na amani. Ingawa wengi huyadharau mamlaka haya ya duniani na kuyaweka mbali kadiri wawezavyo na utiifu wa mioyo yao, wanafanikiwa tu kuyatenganisha zaidi na hivyo kupoteza uzima unaoletwa na lango jembamba. Ni wachache sana watakaopata baraka zilizo ndani ya nguzo hizo.

Hawa watapata uzima ndani ya mipaka ya jembamba na nyembamba iliyowekwa na Mungu na…

…Serikali

Ombi la unyenyekevu la jemadari wa Kapernaumu lilimshangaza Yesu—…Amin, nawaambia, sijaona imani kubwa namna hii, hata katika Israeli –Mathayo 8:10. Alikuwa mtu mwenye mamlaka… na chini ya mamlaka. Alionekana kuelewa uhusiano kati ya kujitiisha chini ya mamlaka ya duniani na kuitumia, kwa maana alimwomba Kristo asiingie chini ya paa lake, bali …sema neno tu, na mtumishi wangu atapona –Mathayo 8:8. Lango lililoundwa na wasimamizi wake na upendo wa dhati wa watumishi walio chini yake mara nyingi liliacha nafasi ndogo tu kwa mapendeleo binafsi. Hata hivyo, nguvu iliyofungamana na maneno yake ilikuwa ya namna ambayo Mwana wa Mungu alikubali ombi lake mara moja!

Yusufu alijikuta tena na tena katika hali ngumu kati ya Mungu na watu aliowatumikia. Hilo lilimfanya ainuliwe kuwa mtawala wa pili katika taifa mashuhuri zaidi duniani. Esta na Danieli walikabili hali kama hizo. Nyakati nyingine, nguzo zilikuwa nyembamba sana hivi kwamba walijiuliza kama wangekufa, lakini matokeo yalikuwa daima nguvu… nguvu ya kuishi katika utakatifu, nguvu ya kuitikia kwa haki, nguvu ya kushinda kwa ushindi, na nguvu ya kuvumilia kwa uaminifu hadi mwisho.

…Mabwana

Ingawa utumwa umekomeshwa kwa kiasi kikubwa katika ulimwengu wetu wa kisasa, uhusiano na bwana bado upo. Waajiri hutumia mamlaka juu ya watumishi wao, na hatimaye wajibu mkubwa zaidi hupewa wale wanaojitiisha chini yake kwa moyo wote. Mamlaka aliyopewa Eleazeri yanastaajabisha na kutia moyo. Abrahamu alimwamini atafute mke wa Isaka; aliruhusiwa hata kuamua masharti. Ahadi hii kubwa ilimwacha mtumishi aliyefungwa kwa mkataba katika hali ngumu kati ya Bwana Mungu na bwana wake Abrahamu. Akasema, Ee BWANA, Mungu wa bwana wangu Abrahamu, nakusihi, unifanikishe leo, umfanyie fadhili bwana wangu Abrahamu –Mwanzo 24:12.

Wafanyakazi wa Marekani wamezoea sana kukataa jambo lolote wanaloona kuwa agizo lisilo na sababu kutoka kwa waajiri wao. Kwa ukaidi usio na imani, wanagoma kwa urahisi na kuzisukuma nguzo zitengane zaidi, ili ziendane na mapendeleo yao mapana. Mtazamo huu umewaacha wakiwa dhaifu kiroho na wasio na nguvu. Towashi Mwethiopia alimtumikia Mungu huku pia akimtumikia chini ya Malkia Kandake. Ingawa ulimwengu wake ulifanywa mwembamba zaidi ya vile wengi wetu tunavyoweza kufikiria, …aliendelea na safari yake akifurahi –Matendo 8:39, Maisha yake ni ushuhuda wa pekee wa unabii wa Isaya …wala towashi asiseme, Mimi ni mti mkavu –Isaya 56:3.

…Wazazi

Enyi watoto, watiini wazazi wenu katika Bwana, maana hii ndiyo haki. Waheshimu baba yako na mama yako; (amri hii ndiyo ya kwanza yenye ahadi;) upate heri, ukae siku nyingi katika dunia –Waefeso 6:1-3. Hili lapaswa kuwa dhahiri kwa kila mtu aliyeamshwa kiroho. Watoto walio na wazazi wana faida iliyo wazi maishani, na wale wanaowaheshimu hufanikiwa zaidi. Tena, tulikuwa na baba zetu wa mwili waliotuadhibu, nasi tukawastahi; je, si zaidi sana kujitiisha chini ya Baba wa roho zetu na kuishi? –Waebrania 12:9. Uzima hupatikana na wale wanaoweza kuwakumbatia baba zao wa duniani na “Baba wa roho”. Wale wanaodai kuwa na Mungu kama Baba yao huku wakiwaona wazazi wao kuwa kizuizi tu katika njia wanayotaka kuifuata, mapema au baadaye watapita katika lango pana linaloelekea upotevuni.

…Waume

Yesu alipoanza mazungumzo na mwanamke Msamaria kwenye kisima cha Yakobo, alianza kueleza maisha aliyoyatamani sana—…Bwana, nipe maji haya, nisipate kiu, wala nisije hapa kuteka. Yesu akamwambia, Nenda ukamwite mumeo, urudi hapa –Yohana 4:16. Kristo alikuwa akijaribu kumshawishi kwamba uzima tele utapatikana kati ya nguzo hizo mbili. Hapo awali alikuwa na waume watano na bila shaka hakupata uridhisho kwa yeyote kati yao. Wanawake wanaosimamia haki zao huipiga teke nafasi finyu ya lango na kupoteza heshima waliyoamriwa na Mungu. Mwanamke aliyetulia ndani ya mipaka ya mamlaka yake hakandamizwi, bali kwa kweli amefunguliwa na kuwezeshwa. Kwa sababu hiyo imempasa mwanamke awe na mamlaka juu ya kichwa chake… –1 Wakorintho 11:10. Kufunika kichwa si ishara tu ya kujitiisha, wala si aina tu ya ulinzi; ni nguvu ya kiroho. Kujitiisha kwake kwa moyo wote huimarisha ndoa yenye nguvu anapomkumbatia mumewe kama “bwana”, na kwa kufanya hivyo anakuwa chombo mwaminifu cha uhuru, nguvu, uthabiti, na ushawishi aliopewa.

…Viongozi wa Kanisa

Maneno haya yanene, na kuonya, na kukaripia, kwa mamlaka yote. Mtu awaye yote asikudharau –Tito 2:15. Waumini wengi wanaojitangaza hukataa udhihirisho wowote wa nje wa mamlaka Kanisani. Kwa mtazamo wa Magharibi, mamlaka ya kanisa huhusishwa kwa njia hasi na ushupavu wa sheria, ukomunisti, utumwa, na ukali. Lakini kama vile kupuuza mamlaka ya kiroho kulimnyang’anya Sauli ufalme wake, vivyo hivyo mtazamo huu humwibia mwamini nguvu na heshima ya kweli ya mamlaka. Kwa maana kuasi ni kama dhambi ya uchawi, na ukaidi ni kama uovu na ibada ya sanamu… –1 Samweli 15:23. Jitihada za kuchagua …njia ionekanayo kuwa sawa machoni pa mtu… –Mithali 14:12, huongoza kwenye utumwa, lakini kuchagua kutembea katika kujisalimisha na kujitiisha huongoza kwenye kuwekwa huru na uzima. Shetani alimwahidi Yesu ulimwengu wote kama tu angeitupa mbali “nira” ya kumtii Mungu. Badala yake, aliukaza uso wake kama jiwe gumu, akastahimili kizuizi cha kujitiisha, na hatimaye akauweka ulimwengu wote huru.

Kujitiisha Huzaa Mamlaka ya Kiroho

Mamlaka ya Mungu na mamlaka za duniani ziko katika nguzo pinzani za lango jembamba. Wale wanaojitiisha kikamilifu chini ya zote mbili hupitia mamlaka hai inayopatikana ndani ya lango. Huleta nguvu kwa ajili ya watu badala ya nguvu juu ya watu. Huzaa uhuru katika Kristo… haki ya kuufikia mti wa uzima… uhuru dhidi ya hofu… afya katika mifupa yetu… nguvu juu ya pepo wachafu… neema ya kuwalea watoto… nguvu ya kuhubiri na kugeuza roho… na ndicho kizuizi cha mwisho dhidi ya ushupavu wa sheria. Imani inayopatikana kwa kujitiisha kwa moyo wote na kwa unyenyekevu ndiyo nguvu inayotiliwa shaka na kudharauliwa zaidi kuliko inavyostahili kati ya zile zinazopatikana kwa wanadamu. Ni wachache wanaoipata. Kwa nini? Kwa sababu inajengwa na kuumbwa kwa uangalifu kati ya nguzo za lango jembamba na njia nyembamba.

That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace –Psalm 144:12.

The vision of every godly parent is to see their children grow into mature adulthood. We want our children to develop biblical convictions that will govern their lives and allow them to become independent of parental guidance.

This was the vision of every Jewish father. To celebrate their child’s transition to personal responsibility, a ceremony was held called bar mitzvah for boys, and bat mitzvah for girls. This was traditionally done at the age of thirteen. Bar mitzvah means “a son of the commandment” and bat mitzvah “a daughter of the commandment”. After bar mitzvah a son was considered to be “under the law” and responsible for his own actions. Prior to this event, his parents were accountable for his actions.

Most of us are not of Jewish descent; however, our Lord Jesus was. We find him at the age of twelve sitting in the temple visiting with the doctors, both hearing them and asking them questions. And all that heard him were astonished at his understanding and answers. (see Luke 2:47) Jesus demonstrated an amazing level of maturity at the age of twelve. Even his parents were amazed. Yes, he was divine, yet as a human he demonstrated the potential for early maturity given the right set of values and disciplines.

The teen years are transitional years. Teens are transitioning from childhood to adulthood; from being dependent on parents to learning to be independent. This transition is a process that must be understood by both the parents and the child. Too much freedom too soon, can leave the child feeling insecure and can result in bad choices that can have life-long consequences. Too little freedom can squelch a child’s character growth and can become fertile ground for rebellion.

The teen years are growing years. Just as a plant needs diligent cultivation throughout its life cycle, so a child needs ongoing direction throughout his teen years. After Jesus’ episode in the temple we read, And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them… –Luke 2:51. We will look at some things that parents can do to nurture maturity in their children, but first we will consider several relationships that are foundational to healthy maturity.

Happy is that people, that is in such a case: yea, happy is that people, whose God is the LORD –Psalm 144:15.

Parental relationship

The relationship between the parent and the child in the teen years is largely a reaping of what that relationship was throughout the formative years of childhood. Unless there is a major spiritual crisis that dynamically changes the relationship—such as an evangelical conversion on the part of either the parent or the child—we (as parents) reap during the child’s teen years that which we have sown during their childhood.

Raising teens is a rewarding experience if there has been a healthy foundational relationship established throughout childhood. If the parent has been physically and emotionally present; if the parent and child have been communicating openly and freely; and if the parent has lovingly maintained the role of authority and control, then a foundation has been laid for a more mature level of relating during the teen years.

In the absence of this kind of parental relationship, the child entering the teen years will try to fill this void with other relationships. Most often, if a parental relationship is lacking, a child will seek to fill that void through relationships with their peers. Peers are great friends but are a poor substitute for a parent. We have been created to be relational. Teens especially crave significance through relationship.

There are two things that every teen is looking for in parental relationship. One is identity and the other is affirmation. Two burning questions in the heart of every teen are “Who am I?” and “Am I OK?”.

The identity factor

When children are young, they assume their family identity. As children grow into adolescence and become more independent, they begin to view themselves as someone more than merely Dad’s son. They begin to develop an identity of their own. This movement toward “being my own person” becomes evident in many of the choices that they make such as:

  • How they dress
  • Their choice of music
  • Their choice of friends
  • Whether or not they choose to serve their parent’s God
  • Whether or not they choose to worship in the church of their upbringing

Admittedly, there are other influences that can affect a teen’s choices in these areas, but for the most part these choices reflect the relationship between the child and the parent. Where the parent has exerted a positive influence on the child, that child will be more inclined to adopt the values of the parent.

When the parental relationship has broken down or has never been nurtured, or if the relationship has been nothing more than a master/slave relationship, that child will seek to identify with someone other than the parent. This will manifest itself in choices of dress, music, friends, and activities that the parent will not approve of. This is often called “teenage rebellion”.

Is “teenage rebellion” always the fault of the parent? No, but if you are not actively involved in building and maintaining a relationship with your teen, it is likely to happen. It is important to note that there is a rebel in the heart of every person. In my last article I stressed the importance of confronting that rebel spirit when our children are young and impressionable.

This rebel spirit will not be fully conquered until it is surrendered to God through an evangelical conversion experience. Only a work of the grace of God upon the heart can subdue the inborn rebellion against God and parental authority.

Know the heart of your child and seek to lead them into loving submission to the Lord Jesus Christ. Only in a relationship with Jesus Christ can our children find their true and lasting identity. Parental authority has a place in shaping and controlling our children when they are young. As our children grow into adulthood, we come to realize that parental authority has limitations and our children need to be controlled by an influence beyond ourselves.

It is never too late to build a relational bridge. If you are feeling that you have failed in your relationship with your children, it’s never too late to call them to your side and humbly seek to restore what is missing. Even if your children are gone from home, I can assure you that they long for a relationship with mom and dad.

The affirmation factor

Every teen longs to be affirmed by their parents, especially their father. You can affirm your teen by looking for and acknowledging positive character traits. There is a place for corrective criticism from parent to child, but criticism that demeans is not constructive; it’s destructive. For every critical comment you should have several positive compliments. In other words, you earn the right to criticize what is wrong by blessing what is right.

You can affirm your teen by treating them with dignity and respect. You can ask, “How do you feel about…?” Or “What do you think we should do…?” You are not surrendering your parental responsibility by probing your son’s or daughter’s mind for their perspective. You are actually causing them to be “grown up in their youth” by forcing them to think as adults.

You can affirm your teen by treating him with common courtesy. Simple things like “please” and “thank you”,” I’m sorry”, “pardon me”, “good bye”, “have a good day”, “drive safely”, and “God bless you”, expresses worth and value to your teen. If these simple courtesies are common in your home your children will return them to you. Think about how you feel when someone says to you, “Oh, excuse me, I’m sorry.” You feel a sense of respect, value, and dignity. That is a simple gift that every parent can give to his child.

You can affirm your teen by entrusting him with responsibility. I grew up on a dairy farm. We had plenty of opportunity to develop character and skills. I remember one day when I was 16 years of age, my dad needed a concrete block wall built out in the barn. I volunteered for the job. Dad provided the blocks and the mortar and got me started. Then I was on my own. Did I build a professional-looking wall? No, but I was quite proud of the outcome and that wall lasted for many years. Dad trusted me to do a man’s job and I did it.

Affirming is not flattery. Flattery is praise that is not sincere and often is not true. Affirming is recognizing and encouraging the good that you see in another. I have encountered grown men who have wept bitterly because they had never received affirmation from their father. Even Jesus received affirmation from His Father when His Father said, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

(2) Relationship with God

Our first responsibility in evangelization is to our children. If we cannot evangelize our children, how can we expect to win others to the Lord? We have a distinct advantage in relating our faith to our children in that we are living with our children. They can and do observe how our faith is lived out in everyday life. This should be the most convincing evidence for the validity of our faith.

Unfortunately, how parents live out their faith, or rather fail to live out their faith, can become a huge stumbling block to their children. Our children are keenly aware of any inconsistency in our Christian profession.

Conversely, if our children see that the power of God is evident in our lives, if they see their parents demonstrating faith in God that carries them through difficult times, if they see their parents demonstrating a graceful rest in the Lord, and if, in the home Jesus Christ is exalted and worshipped, they will be convinced to make their parents’ God, their God.

It is the reality of the gospel lived out in daily life that is the most convincing evidence for the validity of our faith. Our children should be our first witnesses to the transformational work of the gospel in our hearts.

How does a parent lead his child to salvation? Salvation is a work of God; however, God uses human instrumentality to accomplish His work. Parents play a major role in leading their children to Christ. Be aware of evidence of conviction. If a child is quiet and withdrawn, or irritable and restless, or belligerent and defiant, it may be that the spirit of God is working in their heart.

Hopefully, you have nurtured a relationship that allows you to probe their heart and gently lead them to Jesus for forgiveness and cleansing. Most of our children’s conversions were initiated by a parent. We recognized signs of conviction and lead them to brokenness and repentance and to receive salvation through faith in Christ.

The early teen years are an ideal time for a child to surrender his/her life to Jesus if he has not already done so. When active rebellion sets in, a teen often makes choices that lead to painful reaping and sometimes irrevocable consequences. A life of dedicated service to God is the only life of blessing and fulfilment.

Relationship with the church

There is one more relationship that dramatically affects the formation of a teen’s life and convictions and that is the local church. We gain both our sense of identity and our understanding of the reality of the Christian faith through our experience of worship and relationship within the local church. After parental relationship, this is the next most significant influence in a teen’s life.

It is important that we worship in a church that presents the gospel as a transformational relationship with God through faith in Jesus. It is also important that our church life consists of warm, loving relationships in a close–knit community.

The reason that I mention this is that some parents have the mistaken idea that they can provide all the spiritual direction and relationships that their children need. This may seem to work when the children are small and close at hand, but as our children grow into adulthood, they will seek a broader world of relationships. The local church and community of associated churches provides this broader base of fellowship.

It is important to worship in a church that you can support and that you can encourage your children to support. Many children have been lost to the faith because mom and dad were not supportive of the church where they were worshipping. It is far better to move on and find a church that you can support than to stay in a church and be in a state of constant opposition.

I am not encouraging church hopping. It is important to children, especially your teens, that there is stability in church life. Find a church that you are comfortable with, hopefully while your children are young, and stick with it. There are always logistical exceptions and your children will adapt to these, but for the most part a stable church life produces youth who have a strong sense of identity and purpose.

As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth –Psalm 127:4. This verse reminds us that our children are a mighty defense against the enemy. If properly honed (trained) and balanced (taught disciplines) our children will have the potential to outlive us both in years and in usefulness. When you release the arrow your children will go places both in time and in the world that you will never see. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate –Psalm 127:5.

愿我们的儿子在幼年时如茁壮成长的植物；愿我们的女儿如宫殿式样雕琢而成的房角石——诗篇 144:12。

每一位敬虔父母的愿景，都是看着儿女成长为成熟的成年人。我们希望儿女建立合乎圣经的信念，使他们在人生中有所遵循，并能够不再依赖父母的指导。

这也是每一位犹太父亲的愿景。为了庆祝孩子开始承担个人责任，人们会举行一种仪式：男孩举行成年礼（bar mitzvah），女孩举行成年礼（bat mitzvah）。按照传统，仪式在十三岁时举行。Bar mitzvah意为“诫命之子”，bat mitzvah意为“诫命之女”。举行bar mitzvah之后，儿子便被视为“在律法之下”，要为自己的行为负责。在此之前，他的行为由父母负责。

我们大多数人并非犹太人；然而，我们的主耶稣是犹太人。我们看到他十二岁时坐在圣殿里，与教师交谈，既听他们讲解，也向他们提问。凡听见他的人，都因他的聪明和应对而惊奇。（见路加福音 2:47）耶稣十二岁时就显出惊人的成熟。连他的父母也感到惊讶。不错，他是神；然而，作为一个人，他显明了：若有正确的价值观和操练，人就有可能早早成熟。

青少年时期是一个过渡阶段。青少年正从童年迈向成年，从依赖父母转向学习独立。这种转变是一个过程，父母和孩子都必须理解。过早给予太多自由，可能让孩子感到不安，也可能导致错误的选择，并造成终身的后果。自由太少，则可能压制孩子品格的成长，为叛逆提供滋生的土壤。

青少年时期也是成长的时期。植物在整个生长周期中都需要悉心培育，孩子在整个青少年时期也需要持续的引导。耶稣在圣殿里的那件事之后，我们读到：他就同他们下去，回到拿撒勒，并且顺从他们……——路加福音 2:51。我们将探讨父母可以做些什么来培育儿女的成熟；但首先，我们要思考几种对健康成熟至关重要的关系。

处在这样的光景中的百姓有福了！以耶和华为神的百姓有福了！——诗篇 144:15。

与父母的关系

青少年时期父母与孩子之间的关系，很大程度上是童年成长阶段所建立关系的收成。除非发生重大的属灵危机，使关系彻底改变——例如父母或孩子一方经历福音性的归信——否则，在孩子的青少年时期，我们（作为父母）收获的，正是我们在他们童年时所播下的。

如果童年时期已经建立了健康的关系，那么养育青少年会是令人欣慰的经历。如果父母在身体和情感上都陪伴孩子；如果父母与孩子能够坦诚、自由地沟通；如果父母以爱心维持权威和管教的角色，那么就为青少年时期更成熟的相处方式打下了基础。

如果缺少这样的亲子关系，进入青少年时期的孩子就会试图通过其他关系来填补空缺。父母关系不足时，孩子最常会寻求同辈关系来填补这个空缺。同辈可以是好朋友，却无法很好地替代父母。我们受造是为了建立关系。青少年尤其渴望通过关系感受到自己有价值。

每个青少年都希望从父母那里得到两样东西：一是身份认同，二是肯定。每个青少年心中都有两个迫切的问题：“我是谁？”“我还好吗？”

身份认同的因素

孩子年幼时，会认同自己的家庭。随着孩子进入青春期、变得更加独立，他们开始不再只把自己看作“爸爸的儿子”或“爸爸的女儿”，而是开始建立自己的身份认同。这种“做我自己”的倾向，会在他们做出的许多选择中显现出来，例如：

  • 他们如何穿衣
  • 他们选择什么音乐
  • 他们选择什么朋友
  • 他们是否选择事奉父母的神
  • 他们是否选择在自己成长过程中所属的教会敬拜

诚然，其他因素也会影响青少年在这些方面的选择；但总的来说，这些选择反映了孩子与父母之间的关系。如果父母对孩子产生了积极的影响，孩子就更倾向于接受父母的价值观。

如果亲子关系已经破裂、从未得到培育，或者这种关系不过是主人与奴仆的关系，孩子就会寻求认同父母以外的人。这会体现在穿着、音乐、朋友和活动等选择上，而这些往往不为父母所认可。这通常被称为“青少年叛逆”。

“青少年叛逆”总是父母的错吗？不是；但如果你没有积极地与你的青少年子女建立并维系关系，叛逆很可能发生。值得注意的是，每个人心中都有一个悖逆者。在我上一篇文章中，我强调了当孩子年幼、容易受影响时，就要面对他们里面悖逆的灵。

唯有通过福音性的归信，将这种悖逆的灵降服于神，才能彻底胜过它。唯有神的恩典在心中动工，才能制服人与生俱来对神和父母权柄的悖逆。

要了解孩子的内心，并设法引导他们甘心顺服主耶稣基督。唯有与耶稣基督建立关系，我们的儿女才能找到真正且持久的身份认同。孩子年幼时，父母的权柄在塑造和管教他们方面发挥作用。随着儿女成长为成年人，我们会逐渐明白，父母的权柄有其限度，而儿女需要受一种超越我们自身的影响所引导。

建立关系的桥梁永远不嫌晚。如果你觉得自己在与儿女的关系上失败了，叫他们来到你身边，谦卑地设法修复缺失之处，永远不嫌晚。即使儿女已经离家，我也可以向你保证，他们仍渴望与父母建立关系。

肯定的因素

每个青少年都渴望得到父母的肯定，尤其是父亲的肯定。你可以留意并肯定孩子积极的品格特质，从而肯定他们。父母确实需要纠正孩子，但贬低人的批评并无建设性，反而具有破坏性。每一句批评的话，都应当配上几句正面的赞美。换句话说，先肯定做得对的地方，才赢得指出错误的机会。

你可以尊重孩子，以有尊严的方式对待他们，从而肯定他们。你可以问：“你对……有什么感受？”或者“你觉得我们应该怎么做……？”探问儿子或女儿的想法，并不表示你放弃了父母的责任。实际上，这会促使他们像成年人一样思考，从而使他们“在幼年时就茁壮成长”。

你可以用基本的礼貌对待孩子，从而肯定他们。简单的话语，如“请”、“谢谢”、“对不起”、“劳驾”、“再见”、“祝你今天愉快”、“开车小心”和“愿神祝福你”，都能让孩子感受到自身的价值。如果这些基本礼貌在你家中很常见，孩子也会以同样的礼貌对待你。想想别人对你说“噢，抱歉，真对不起。”时，你有什么感受。你会感到自己受到尊重、被重视，也有尊严。这是每位父母都能送给孩子的一份简单礼物。

你可以把责任托付给孩子，从而肯定他们。我在一个奶牛场长大。我们有很多机会培养品格和技能。我记得十六岁那年，有一天爸爸需要在谷仓里砌一堵混凝土砌块墙。我主动揽下了这项工作。爸爸提供了砌块和砂浆，帮我起了个头。之后就由我自己完成。我砌出的墙看起来像专业工匠的手艺吗？没有，但我对结果相当满意，那堵墙也用了很多年。爸爸信任我去做一件成年男子该做的工作，而我做到了。

肯定不是奉承。奉承是不真诚的赞美，往往也不符合事实。肯定则是看见并鼓励他人身上的美善。我遇见过一些成年男子，他们因为从未得到父亲的肯定而痛哭不已。就连耶稣也得到天父的肯定，天父说：“这是我的爱子，我所喜悦的。”

（2）与神的关系

我们在传福音方面，首先要对自己的儿女尽责。如果我们不能向自己的儿女传福音，又怎能指望把别人带到主面前？我们向儿女传递信仰有一个明显的优势：我们与儿女共同生活。他们能够、也确实会观察我们的信仰如何体现在日常生活中。这应当是我们信仰真实可信的最有力证据。

遗憾的是，父母活出信仰的方式，或者说未能活出信仰的情形，可能成为儿女极大的绊脚石。儿女对我们基督信仰告白中的任何不一致都非常敏锐。

相反，如果儿女看见神的大能在我们生命中彰显；如果他们看见父母对神的信心使他们能够度过艰难时刻；如果他们看见父母在主里安然安息；并且如果耶稣基督在家中被尊崇、受敬拜，他们就会确信要以父母的神为自己的神。

在日常生活中活出福音的真实，是我们信仰真实可信的最有力证据。我们的儿女应当首先见证福音在我们心中带来的转变。

父母如何引导孩子得救？救恩是神的工作；然而，神使用人作为工具来成就他的工作。父母在引导儿女归向基督的过程中扮演重要角色。要留意孩子知罪的迹象。如果孩子沉默退缩、易怒烦躁，或好争辩、抗拒不从，可能是神的灵正在他们心中动工。

希望你已经培育了一种关系，使你能够探问他们的内心，并温柔地引导他们到耶稣面前，求得赦免和洁净。我们大多数孩子的归信都是由父母引发的。我们察觉到知罪的迹象，便带领他们忧伤悔改，并凭着信心接受基督所赐的救恩。

如果孩子还没有将生命交给耶稣，青少年初期是他们这样做的理想时期。一旦主动悖逆的行为开始，青少年往往会作出一些选择，导致痛苦的后果，有时甚至造成无法挽回的后果。献身事奉神的人生，才是蒙福且充实的人生。

与教会的关系

还有一种关系会显著影响青少年生命和信念的形成，那就是地方教会。我们通过在地方教会中的敬拜经历和人际关系，获得身份认同，也认识基督教信仰的真实。父母关系之后，这是对青少年影响最重大的因素。

我们敬拜的教会应当宣讲这样的福音：人借着信靠耶稣，与神建立能改变生命的关系。我们的教会生活也应当充满温暖、友爱的关系，形成紧密相连的群体。

我之所以提这一点，是因为有些父母误以为自己可以提供儿女所需的一切属灵引导和关系。孩子年幼、常在身边时，这或许行得通；但儿女长大成人后，会寻求更广阔的人际关系。地方教会以及彼此联系的众教会所组成的群体，能提供这样更广阔的团契基础。

重要的是，要在一间你能够支持、也能鼓励儿女支持的教会中敬拜。许多孩子失去了信仰，是因为父母不支持他们敬拜的教会。与其留在一间不断反对的教会里，不如离开，寻找一间你能够支持的教会。

我并不是鼓励人频繁更换教会。教会生活的稳定对孩子，尤其是青少年，非常重要。找一间你感到合适的教会——最好在孩子年幼时就找到——并持守下去。总会有一些实际情况上的例外，孩子也会适应这些情况；但总的来说，稳定的教会生活能培养出具有强烈身份认同和目标感的年轻人。

箭袋充满了箭的勇士，少年时所生的儿女也是这样——诗篇 127:4。这节经文提醒我们，儿女是抵御仇敌的强大防线。如果得到适当的磨砺（训练）和平衡（教导操练），儿女就有潜力在寿命和效用上都超过我们。当你放出这支箭时，儿女将在时间和世界中去到你永远无法看见的地方。箭袋充满了箭的人便为有福；他们在城门口和仇敌说话的时候，必不至于羞愧——诗篇 127:5。

He was born in a stable, meant for beasts of the field.
It was from the beginning that His will He would yield.

He was never well-liked; despised by all men;
Laughed to scorn, reviled—again, and again.

Yes, His mission on this earth was unusual indeed,
Not seeking money and friends or trying to succeed.

He knew His purpose was to please His Father,
With the trifles of earth, He would not bother.

It surely wasn’t easy, to be the King of kings.
And suffer as a criminal, taking what that brings.

Ten thousand angels, He could have summoned south,
But the stricken Savior opened not His mouth.

With His eyes on the reward, He persevered the pain;
Was cruelly stripped and beaten, and ultimately slain.

But why would He suffer so willingly there;
Enduring the cross, all the pain He did bear?

Because He treasured us, an atonement for our sin
He made when He bled and died there to make us His kin!

I thank God now for that sacrifice so great;
Providing the Lamb and transforming my fate.

I say, “A wonderful Savior, is Jesus my Lord;”
Now the Father and I—a relationship restored!

–Barry Grant

জন্মেছিলেন তিনি আস্তাবলে, মাঠের পশুদের জন্য নির্দিষ্ট স্থানে।
শুরু থেকেই তিনি সমর্পণ করেছিলেন নিজের ইচ্ছাকে পিতার ইচ্ছায়।

কেউ তাঁকে কখনো ভালোবাসেনি; সবাই করত অবজ্ঞা;
উপহাস, নিন্দা—বারবার, নিরন্তর, ছিল তাঁর ভাগ্য।

হ্যাঁ, এ পৃথিবীতে তাঁর মিশন ছিল সত্যিই অসাধারণ,
অর্থ-বন্ধু খোঁজা কিংবা সফল হওয়ার চেষ্টা—কিছুই নয় তাঁর সাধন।

তিনি জানতেন, তাঁর উদ্দেশ্য পিতাকে সন্তুষ্ট করা,
পৃথিবীর তুচ্ছ বিষয় নিয়ে তিনি চাইতেন না মাথা ঘামাতে।

রাজাধিরাজ হওয়া নিশ্চয়ই সহজ ছিল না তাঁর,
অপরাধীর মতো দুঃখভোগ, তার সব পরিণাম বয়ে নেওয়া ছিল ভার।

দশ হাজার স্বর্গদূতকে তিনি ডাকতে পারতেন কাছে,
কিন্তু ক্ষতবিক্ষত ত্রাণকর্তা মুখ খুললেন না পাছে।

পুরস্কারের দিকে চোখ রেখে, যন্ত্রণা সহ্য করে গেলেন তিনি;
নিষ্ঠুরভাবে বস্ত্রহীন ও প্রহৃত, শেষে নিহত হলেন তিনি।

কিন্তু কেন তিনি স্বেচ্ছায় সেখানে এত দুঃখ সইবেন;
ক্রুশের যন্ত্রণা, সব কষ্ট কেনই বা বয়ে নেবেন?

কারণ তিনি আমাদের অতি প্রিয়—আমাদের পাপের প্রায়শ্চিত্ত
করলেন, যখন রক্ত ঝরিয়ে সেখানে প্রাণ দিলেন, আমাদের আপনজন করতে!

এখন ঈশ্বরকে ধন্যবাদ জানাই সেই মহৎ আত্মত্যাগের জন্য;
মেষশাবক জুগিয়ে আমার ভাগ্য বদলে দেওয়ার জন্য।

আমি বলি, “কী মহান ত্রাণকর্তা, যিশু আমার প্রভু;”
এখন পিতার সঙ্গে আমার—সম্পর্ক আবার হলো নতুন!

–ব্যারি গ্রান্ট
